body.translated_text:
1.1.1: We shall explain the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice).
1.1.2: It [belongs] to three <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).
1.1.3: Of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and the <s>Vaiśya</s>.
1.1.4: That which is prescribed without being conjoined [with a specific class] is common [to all].
1.1.5: It is differentiated by conjunction.
1.1.6: Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), one performs rites for the gods.
1.1.7: Wearing the thread over the right shoulder (<s>prācīnāvīta</s>), [one performs] rites for the ancestors.
1.1.8: Beginning from the sipping of water (<s>ācamana</s>), with whatever ritual context one is conjoined, one should not deviate from it.
1.1.9: Nor should one leave [it].
1.1.10: This is the characteristic of a recurrent [rite].
1.1.11: [This was] the enumeration.
1.1.12: The detailed procedure [follows] hereafter.
1.1.13: Rites for the gods follow the northward direction.
1.1.14: Rites for the ancestors follow the southward direction.
1.1.15: The <s>bāhvṛcya</s> (Ṛgvedic recitation) follows the seated position.
1.1.16: Standing up is [required only] by explicit instruction.
1.1.17: The <s>Hotṛ</s> (priest) should also perform what has not been specifically directed.
1.1.18: In groups of <s>ṛcs</s> (Ṛgvedic verses) beginning from three, the first and last are recited three times, except in <s>japas</s> (silent recitations).
1.1.19: After the last metrical [verse], above the initial consonant, in its place, the <s>Oṃkāra</s> is [pronounced] — prolonged (<s>pluta</s>), of three <s>mātrās</s> (morae), pure.
1.1.20: Or ending with the <s>ma</s>-sound.
1.1.21: That they call the <s>praṇava</s>.
1.1.22: At the conclusion, [the <s>praṇava</s>] ending with the <s>ma</s>-sound [occurs] in all groups of <s>ṛcs</s> that have <s>puronuvākyās</s> (invitatory verses).
1.1.23: By joining a half-verse of the subsequent [<s>ṛc</s>] with it, one concludes with a <s>pāda</s> (quarter-verse) — that they call <s>saṃtata</s> (continuous).
1.1.24: That is the rule for all groups of <s>ṛcs</s> which are enjoined by connection with a ritual action.
1.1.25: Even in widely separated rituals, between the first and the concluding (<s>paridhānīyā</s>) [verses], the half-verse serves the purpose of <s>saṃtāna</s> (continuity).
1.1.26: The <s>ṛcs</s> follow the half-verse rule.
1.1.27: Anything different [is done only] by explicit instruction.
1.1.28: The <s>Ṛgveda</s> follows the loud-voice rule.
1.1.29: Soft utterance (<s>upāṃśu</s>) [is done only] by explicit instruction.
1.1.30: Sounds follow the rule of having [proper] resonance.
1.1.31: And [there should be] uniform pitch (<s>aikasvaryam</s>).
1.1.32: The <s>praṇava</s> of the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) is louder [than the rest].
1.1.33: The <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) is louder than the <s>praṇava</s>.
1.1.34: The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (exclamation) is the loudest.
1.1.35: Or [they may be] of equal [volume].
1.1.36: The <s>praṇava</s>, the "<s>ye yajāmahe</s>" (formula), the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, the <s>saṃpraiṣas</s> (full directions), and the <s>praiṣas</s> (directions) — [these are] loud; [the rest is] <s>upāṃśu</s> (soft) in the <s>havis</s> (oblation) offerings.
1.1.37: The name of the deity is [recited] softly at the places of <s>nigama</s> (Vedic citation).
1.1.38: "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ</s>" is a <s>japa</s> (murmured recitation) before [the main recitation].
1.1.39: "<s>Ye yajāmahe</s>, <s>vauṣaṭ</s>, <s>ojaḥ</s>, <s>sahaḥ</s>, <s>saha</s>, <s>ojaḥ</s>, <s>svar</s>" — this is the fourfold [formula recited] at the end, in all <s>yājyās</s> (offering verses).
1.1.40: But in the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings), "<s>ye yajāmahe</s>" does not occur.
1.1.41: Nor in the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (supplementary exclamation).
1.1.42: The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is joined to the prolonged ending of the <s>yājyā</s>.
1.1.43: Or with a non-prolonged [ending].
1.1.44: In the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (silent offering), that [joining] does not occur.

body.translated_text:
1.2.1: One should prolong the <s>ā</s>-sound of the invocation (<s>āvāhana</s>).
1.2.2: "<s>Ye yajāmahaḥ</s>" has a prolonged beginning, placed before the <s>yājyās</s> (offering verses).
1.2.3: The sacrificial prolongation (<s>pluti</s>) is of four <s>mātrās</s> (morae).
1.2.4: Of the <s>sandhi</s> (junction) syllables, at the palatal position, they become <s>ā-i</s>-sounds.
1.2.5: At the labial position, they become <s>ā-u</s>-sounds.
1.2.6: Other syllables [remain] in their natural form.
1.2.7: The <s>e</s>-sound and <s>o</s>-sound are <s>pragṛhya</s> (retained without sandhi)
1.2.8: at the end of a <s>yājyā</s>.
1.2.9: The <s>visarjanīya</s> (visarga), when followed by <s>r</s>, becomes <s>repha</s> (the consonant <s>r</s>).
1.2.10: When not followed by <s>r</s>, it is elided.
1.2.11: <s>Anusvāra</s> [becomes] the <s>ma</s>-sound.
1.2.12: Other consonants [remain] in their natural form.
1.2.13: The <s>au</s>-sound in the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is of four <s>mātrās</s>.
1.2.14: And the <s>a</s>-sound following the <s>ṣa</s>-sound [also receives special treatment].
1.2.15: Or both [remain] in their natural form.
1.2.16: Or the former [remains] in its natural form.
1.2.17: The <s>a</s>-sound [remains] in its natural form — thus <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>.
1.2.18: One should pronounce the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> in the <s>Bārhatarāthantara</s> [manner] — long at the beginning, short at the end.
1.2.19: After "<s>ye yajāmahe</s>," the designation of the deity [follows] at the end, in [rites] that have an invitatory verse.
1.2.20: But in one that has a <s>praiṣa</s> (direction), it does not occur.
1.2.21: When "he offers" is said, one should be gratified by the ghee.
1.2.22: The <s>svāhākāra</s> (exclamation "<s>svāhā</s>") [comes] at the end of <s>homa</s> (oblation) <s>mantras</s>.
1.2.23: And of the <s>samidādhāna</s> (fuel-placing) <s>mantras</s>.
1.2.24: From the separateness of the <s>mantras</s>, the separateness of the ritual actions [follows].
1.2.25: The word <s>iti</s> and the ritual act [come] at the end of the <s>mantra</s>.
1.2.26: The ritual action coincides with the end of the <s>mantra</s> in the ritual performances.
1.2.27: Having been directed, [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] recites.
1.2.28: Likewise, [the <s>Adhvaryu</s>] makes the offering.
1.2.29: Thus this is the universal rule for all sacrifices (<s>sārvayajñika</s>).

body.translated_text:
1.3.1: Having fasted, one sacrifices with the full-moon (<s>paurṇamāsa</s>) oblation.
1.3.2: Likewise with the new-moon (<s>amāvāsya</s>) [oblation].
1.3.3: There are two full-moon [days].
1.3.4: And [two] new-moon [days].
1.3.5: [The day] on which [the moon] rises full around sunset, and [the day] on which [it rises full] after sunset — those are the two full-moon [days].
1.3.6: The day [on which one says] "tomorrow [the moon] will not be seen," and the day on which it is not seen — those are the two new-moon [days].
1.3.7: Regarding the performance on either [day], one may choose as one wishes.
1.3.8: "On the full-moon day" and "on the new-moon day" — by these instructions they are differentiated.
1.3.9: The words "and" (<s>ca</s>) are connected with that [instruction].
1.3.10: The rest is the same.
1.3.11: In both [sacrifices], there is a <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) for <s>Agni</s>.
1.3.12: The <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (silent offering) is for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>.
1.3.13: Or for <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
1.3.15: For one who does not prepare [curds], the second [offering] at the new moon is for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
1.3.16: The <s>sāmnāyya</s> (mixed milk offering) is for <s>Indra</s>, for one who prepares [curds].
1.3.17: Or for <s>Mahendra</s> (Great <s>Indra</s>).
1.3.18: But the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> for <s>Viṣṇu</s> [is offered by] one who does not prepare [curds].

body.translated_text:
1.4.1: Having been invited, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (priest), passing between the rubbish heap (<s>utkara</s>) and the <s>praṇītā</s> (sacred waters), steps upon the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) with the right forefoot.
1.4.2: [His] heel at the back is level with the edge of the <s>vedi</s> (altar).
1.4.3: Having stepped forward, [he takes his] standing position.
1.4.4: He is directed: "For <s>Agni</s> being kindled" [begin the recitation].
1.4.5: [He recites:] "Whom do I seek refuge in? Him I seek refuge in. Whatever is your shelter, O <s>Prajāpati</s>, that metrical protection I seek refuge in. As far as I know you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so far will I act for you. Impelled by the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, I shall perform the priestly office. Homage to <s>Agni</s> the witness; homage to <s>Vāyu</s> the listener; homage to <s>Āditya</s> the approver. Today I shall speak speech pleasing to the gods, worthy of being heard by men, rich in nourishment for the ancestors, a foundation for every being. With a well-governed self, with progeny, with cattle, I seek refuge in <s>Prajāpati</s>. May there be fearlessness for us. I shall recite what belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>. Speech shall perform the priestly office. I seek refuge in Speech." Having murmured "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>,"
1.4.6: having pronounced <s>hiṃ</s> three times,
1.4.7: he begins with "<s>Pra vo vājāḥ</s>" (Forth, O prizes!) in a middle voice.
1.4.8: "<s>Agna ā yāhi vītaye</s>" (O <s>Agni</s>, come to the feast) and "<s>Īḷenya</s>" (O praiseworthy one) — two triplets.
1.4.9: "<s>Agnim dūtam vṛṇīmahe</s>" (We choose <s>Agni</s> as messenger) — one [verse].
1.4.10: "<s>Samidhyamāno adhvare</s>" (Being kindled at the sacrifice) — one [verse].
1.4.11: Three [verses are used] in the <s>sāptadaśya</s> (seventeen-versed <s>stotra</s>).
1.4.12: That [applies] at all [times] except the two evening <s>Darśa-pūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon sacrifices).
1.4.13: "<s>Samiddho agna āhuta</s>" (O <s>Agni</s>, kindled and offered into) — two [verses].
1.4.14: "<s>Agne mahān asi brāhmaṇa bhārata</s>" (O <s>Agni</s>, you are great, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>) — joined with the <s>praṇava</s>.
1.4.15: From the remote [ancestor] down to the present <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer), he pronounces the three <s>ārṣeyas</s> (seer lineages).
1.4.16: But six for one belonging to two <s>gotras</s> (lineages).
1.4.17: For a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [the lineage recitation follows] the <s>pravara</s> (lineage declaration) of the <s>purohita</s> (family priest).
1.4.18: Or [the lineage] of <s>Manu</s> for all.
1.4.19: [He recites:] "Kindled by the gods, kindled by <s>Manu</s>, praised by the <s>ṛṣis</s>, approved by the inspired sages, lauded by the poets, sharpened by <s>Brahman</s>, [you are] the offering of ghee" — and concludes.
1.4.20: "Leader of sacrifices, charioteer of rites, unhurried <s>Hotṛ</s>, swift bearer of oblations" — and concludes.
1.4.21: "The <s>juhū</s> (ladle) is the vessel of the gods, the cup the divine drinking-bowl; like the felly of a wheel, O <s>Agni</s>, you encompass the gods" — and concludes.
1.4.22: Concluding thus, he invokes the deities.

body.translated_text: 1.5.1: 'Bring the gods for the sacrificer.' 1.5.2: '<s>Agni</s>, bring <s>Agni</s>; bring <s>Soma</s>' — these are the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions). 1.5.3: 'Bring <s>Agni</s>; bring <s>Agnīṣomau</s> (Agni-and-Soma); or bring <s>Viṣṇu</s>; bring <s>Agnīṣomau</s>; bring <s>Indrāgnī</s> (Indra-and-Agni); bring <s>Indra</s>; or <s>Mahendra</s> (Great Indra).' 1.5.4: 'Bring the gods who drink the ghee.' 1.5.5: 'Bring <s>Agni</s> for the office of <s>Hotṛ</s>.' 1.5.6: 'Bring his own greatness.' 1.5.7: 'And bring, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, and sacrifice well' — having thus invoked, 1.5.8: he sits down with knees raised, touches the ground with his right span, and mutters: 1.5.9: 'May I not be cut off from this firm ground. O Mother Earth, do not harm me, do not scorch me. I shall obtain sweetness, I shall win sweetness, I shall produce sweetness. Today I shall speak a honey-sweet speech to the gods, [and a] pleasant [one] to humans. With this fifteen-fold <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) I drive away the sinful rival' — or with the seventeen-fold one.

body.translated_text: 1.6.1: He is addressed as 'human.' 1.6.2: 'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, they choose you together with the father <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. O <s>Indra</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, proclaim and sacrifice. May we be in the gift of the <s>Vasus</s>, in the favor of the <s>Rudras</s>, in the grace of the <s>Ādityas</s>. Whatever in this office of the <s>Hotṛ</s> may have gone crooked, whatever went astray — may <s>Agni</s> <s>Jātavedas</s>, the far-seeing, bring that back' — thus he mutters after being initiated. 1.6.3: Having risen, he touches the right shoulder of the <s>Adhvaryu</s> with his right span, and the right shoulder of the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> with his left, muttering: 'We depend on <s>Indra</s> in the office of the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the one placed in front. By whom the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, the gods, went to the highest heaven, to the sky. The <s>yashṭi</s> (sacrificial pole) of the <s>Adhvaryus</s> and the ninety fetters are spread between heaven and earth. They bind the simple one; I, the wise, go above. May these two, heaven and earth, be comfortable for me.' 1.6.4: 'May six broad [spaces] protect me from distress: heaven and earth, day and night, the waters and the plants' — thus releasing. 1.6.5: 'I have turned the turning of <s>Indra</s>; I have followed the turning of <s>Āditya</s>' — turning around the right arm. 1.6.6: 'Cast away is the defeated one; whoever hates us and whomever we hate — along with him' — cutting dry grass on both sides from the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s seat, casting it away to the south in an intermediate direction. 1.6.7: He sips water. 1.6.8: He places a fresh [blade of grass] with its tip pointing north. 1.6.9: 'I now sit in the seat of the near one' — sitting down. 1.6.10: Making his lap face south-north, extending his hands forward, he mutters: 1.6.11: 'Homage to heaven and earth, to the two <s>Hotṛs</s>, the primeval creators, the two all-makers, the two body-protectors: you are my body-protectors; protect my body. Do not harm me; do not scorch me' — looking at the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fires. 1.6.12: Moving northward, he says: 'This is your space.' 1.6.13: 'All gods, instruct; to that speech today, homage to the great ones' — having muttered thus. 1.6.14: '<s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s>, let him know; <s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s>, let him know the offering. May the impelling [priest] be good. May the deity bless you, O sacrificer' — concluding thus. 1.6.15: 'You who have chosen <s>Agni</s> as <s>Hotṛ</s>' — in a low voice. 1.6.16: 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, fill the ghee-laden ladle; the god-seeking, all-choosing one — we invoke the gods; I praise some, I bow to those worthy of homage, I sacrifice to those worthy of sacrifice' — having the two ladles taken up, he performs the five <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings).

body.translated_text: 1.7.1: 'O <s>Agni</s>, may the kindling sticks, the kindling sticks approve of the ghee' — this is the first [<s>prayāja</s>]. 1.7.2: 'May he approve of the ghee' — this is the second. 1.7.3: 'O <s>Agni</s>, may <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> approve of the ghee' — this is the second [<s>prayāja</s>] for the <s>Vasiṣṭha-Śunakas</s>, the <s>Atri-Vadhryaśvas</s>, the <s>Kaṇva-Saṃkṛtis</s>, for <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and for those desiring offspring. 1.7.4: 'O <s>Agni</s>, may <s>Iḷā</s> approve of the ghee' — this is the third. 1.7.5: 'O <s>Agni</s>, may the sacred grass approve of the ghee' — this is the fourth. 1.7.6: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Agnīṣomau</s> — or to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Agnīṣomau</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Indrāgnī</s>, <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Indra</s> — or to <s>Mahendra</s> — O <s>Agni</s>, may the gods who drink the ghee, being pleased, approve of the ghee offering' — these are the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verses) for the <s>prayājas</s>.

body.translated_text: 1.8.1: '<s>Agni</s> [slays] the enemies; you, O <s>Soma</s>, are the lord of truth' — these are the <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion) [verses], destructive of enemies, at the full-moon [sacrifice]. 1.8.2: '<s>Agni</s> by ancient [ways]; <s>Soma</s>, by hymns' — at the new-moon [sacrifice], the enriching ones. 1.8.3: 'May <s>Agni</s>, being pleased, approve of the ghee offering; may <s>Soma</s>, being pleased, approve of the ghee offering' — these are the <s>yājyā</s> verses. 1.8.4: '<s>Agni</s> is the head' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) for the <s>Āgneya</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s>). 1.8.5: 'You have become [the lord] of the sacrifice' — this is the <s>yājyā</s>. 1.8.6: '<s>Agnīṣomau</s>, this [offering]' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> for the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (low-voiced offering). 1.8.8: 'May <s>Agnīṣomau</s>, being pleased, partake of the ghee offering' — this is the <s>yājyā</s>. 1.8.8: 'This <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode; <s>vaṣaṭ</s> to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — for the offering to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. 1.8.9: Or 'being pleased.' 1.8.10: 'O <s>Agnīṣomā</s>, of common knowledge; you two, these' — for the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> offering. 1.8.11: 'O <s>Indrāgnī</s>, with your help; forth among the peoples' — for the <s>Aindrāgna</s> offering. 1.8.12: 'O <s>Indra</s>, the conquering; you have prevailed' — for the <s>Sāmnāyya</s> offering. 1.8.13: 'Great is <s>Indra</s> who by might; great is <s>Indra</s> with heroes' — for the <s>Māhendra</s> offering. 1.8.14: '<s>Indra</s>, you from all sides; rejoice with the bay horses' — for [the offering to] <s>Indra</s> without substitute.

body.translated_text: 1.9.1: 'Gratify the gods' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (making-good-of-the-offering). 1.9.2: '<s>Agni</s> has gone to <s>Agni</s>'s dear abodes; he has gone to <s>Soma</s>'s dear abodes; he has gone to <s>Agni</s>'s dear abodes; he has gone to the dear abodes of <s>Agnīṣomau</s> — or of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — he has gone to the dear abodes of <s>Agnīṣomau</s>; he has gone to the dear abodes of <s>Indrāgnī</s>; he has gone to the dear abodes of <s>Indra</s> — or of <s>Mahendra</s> — he has gone to the dear abodes of the gods who drink the ghee. May he sacrifice at the dear abodes of <s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s>. May he sacrifice at his own greatness. May he obtain offering and refreshment. May <s>Jātavedas</s> be pleased with the oblation. O <s>Agni</s>, whatever [was done] today by the people [belonging to] the sacrifice' — this is the <s>yājyā</s>. 1.9.3: After the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call, there is the touching [of water].

body.translated_text: 1.10.1: For the one about to invoke the <s>Iḍā</s>, he anoints the index finger of the right hand at the topmost and middle joints. 1.10.2: 'By the lord of speech I taste of your offering — for sustenance, for the <s>prāṇa</s> (in-breath)' — the first anointing is smeared on the lower lip. 'By the lord of mind I taste of your offering — for nourishment, for the <s>udāna</s> (up-breath)' — the second [anointing is smeared] on the upper lip. 1.10.3: He sips water. 1.10.4: With the right [hand] he holds the <s>Iḍā</s> in the north. 1.10.5: With fingers not extended, not clenched into a fist. 1.10.6: Taking [a portion] himself as the fifth. 1.10.7: Holding [it] measured to the mouth, or measured to the heart.

ŚŚS_1.11.1a: upahūtam.bṛhat.saha.divā.saha.sūryeṇa.saha.cakṣuṣā.upa.mām.bṛhat.saha.divā.saha.sūryeṇa.saha.cakṣuṣā.hvayatām.|.upahūtam.vāmadevyam.saha.antarikṣeṇa.saha.vāyunā.saha.prāṇena.upa.mām.vāmadevyam.saha.antarikṣeṇa.saha.vāyunā.saha.prāṇena.hvayatām /

ŚŚS_1.11.1g: upahūtā.iḷā.vṛṣṭir.upa.mām.iḷā.vṛṣṭir.hvayatām.|.upahūtā.iḷā.taturir.upa.mām.iḷā.taturir.hvayatām.|.upahūtā.he.sā.asi.juṣasva.mā.iḷa.iti.japitvā.iḷām.upahvayate /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 1.11.1a: 'Invoked is <s>Bṛhat</s> (the great chant), together with heaven, together with <s>Sūrya</s>, together with sight — may <s>Bṛhat</s>, together with heaven, together with <s>Sūrya</s>, together with sight, invoke me.' 'Invoked is <s>Vāmadevya</s> (the Vāmadeva chant), together with the atmosphere, together with <s>Vāyu</s>, together with breath — may <s>Vāmadevya</s>, together with the atmosphere, together with <s>Vāyu</s>, together with breath, invoke me.'
ŚŚS 1.11.1b: 'Invoked is <s>Rathantara</s> (the chariot chant), together with the earth, together with <s>Agni</s>, together with speech, together with cattle — may <s>Rathantara</s>, together with the earth, together with <s>Agni</s>, together with speech, together with cattle, invoke me.'
ŚŚS 1.11.1c: 'Invoked is the stationary world — may the stationary world invoke me.'
ŚŚS 1.11.1d: 'Invoked is the moving world — may the moving world invoke me.' 'Invoked is the companion, the portion — may the companion, the portion, invoke me.'
ŚŚS 1.11.1e: 'Invoked are the seven <s>hotrās</s> (priestly offices) — may the seven <s>hotrās</s> invoke me.' 'Invoked are the cows together with the mixed [milk] — may my cows together with the mixed [milk] invoke me.'
ŚŚS 1.11.1f: 'Invoked is speech together with breath — may speech together with breath invoke me.' 'Invoked is speech together with mind — may speech together with mind invoke me.'
ŚŚS 1.11.1g: 'Invoked is <s>Iḍā</s> (the libation goddess) as rain — may <s>Iḍā</s> as rain invoke me.' 'Invoked is <s>Iḍā</s> as swift-crossing — may <s>Iḍā</s> as swift-crossing invoke me.' Having murmured 'Invoked — you are [<s>Iḍā</s>]; accept me, O <s>Iḍā</s>,' he invokes <s>Iḍā</s>.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 1.12.1a: '<s>Iḍā</s> is invoked; invoked is <s>Iḍā</s>. May <s>Iḍā</s> invoke us. <s>Iḍā</s> is invoked — the daughter of <s>Manu</s>, whose track is ghee, belonging to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.'
ŚŚS 1.12.1b: 'The <s>brahman</s> (sacred utterance) fashioned by the gods is invoked. The divine <s>adhvaryus</s> (priests) are invoked. Invoked are the human [priests] who attend this sacrifice and who increase the lord of the sacrifice. Invoked are heaven and earth, the first-born, upholders of truth (<s>ṛta</s>), divine, daughters of the gods.'
ŚŚS 1.12.1c: 'Invoked is this sacrificer for a further divine worship; invoked for a greater offering. May the gods enjoy this my oblation' — thus, having invoked with the formula 'invoked,' at that [point] he invokes.
ŚŚS 1.12.2: Having pressed down [the remnant].
ŚŚS 1.12.3: He makes four divisions within the <s>Iḍā</s> portion.
ŚŚS 1.12.4: Or the fourth [portion] at the end.
ŚŚS 1.12.5: 'You are <s>Iḍā</s>; you are pleasant; you are the maker of pleasantness. Place us in the state of good offspring and the increase of dominion. May I attain the cherished state of your cherished [gift]. Being invoked, may I obtain your invocation. For the splendor of your mouth, for the fragrance of your palate, I partake [of you]' — having thus eaten the upper <s>Iḍā</s> portion.
ŚŚS 1.12.6: The other [portions are eaten by] the sacrificer and those who are fifth [in rank], having partaken.
ŚŚS 1.12.7: Restraint of speech [is maintained] until the purification.
ŚŚS 1.12.8: With the <s>tṛca</s> (triplet of verses) beginning 'These waters' (<s>idam āpaḥ</s>), they purify themselves within the <s>vedi</s> (altar) with the purifying [grass].
ŚŚS 1.12.9: After setting aside the <s>brahman</s>'s share, they bring forward the <s>anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering).
ŚŚS 1.12.10: This is the time for the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee) in all <s>iṣṭis</s> (offerings).
ŚŚS 1.12.11: There is no <s>anvāhārya</s> in [offerings] where the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is [already] prescribed.
ŚŚS 1.12.12: 'This is your fuel-stick, O <s>Agni</s>; by it may you grow and be nourished. And may we also grow and be nourished' — having thus consecrated the fuel-stick with this <s>mantra</s>.
ŚŚS 1.12.13: He offers three after-offerings (<s>anuyājas</s>).

body.text:
ŚŚS_1.13.1: devam.barhir.vasuvane.vasu.dheyasya.vetu /
ŚŚS_1.13.2: devo.narāśaṃso.vasuvane.vasu.dheyasya.vetu /
ŚŚS_1.13.3: devo.agniḥ.sviṣṭakṛt.sudraviṇā.mandraḥ.kaviḥ.satya.manmā.āyajī.hotā.hotur.hotur.āyajīyān.agne.yān.devān.ayāḍ.yān.apiprer.ye.te.hotre.amatsata.ity.avasāya /
ŚŚS_1.13.4: tām.sasanuṣīm.hotrām.devam.gamām.divi.deveṣu.yajñam.eraya.imam.sviṣṭakṛc.ca.agne.hotā.bhūr.vasuvane.vasu.dheyasya.namo.vāke.vīhi.ity.anuyāja.yājyāḥ /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 1.13.1: 'May the divine <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) go to the winning of <s>Vasus</s>, to the bestowal of wealth.'
ŚŚS 1.13.2: 'May the divine <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> go to the winning of <s>Vasus</s>, to the bestowal of wealth.'
ŚŚS 1.13.3: 'The divine <s>Agni</s> <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings), possessing excellent riches, the gladdening one, the poet, of true inspiration, the offerer, the <s>Hotṛ</s> — more worthy of offering than [any other] <s>Hotṛ</s>. O <s>Agni</s>, whatever gods you have worshipped, whomever you have satisfied, who have delighted in your <s>hotra</s> (priestly office)' — thus concluding.
ŚŚS 1.13.4: 'That unfailing <s>hotrā</s> (priestly function), going to the gods, going to heaven, to the gods — send forth this sacrifice. And O <s>Agni</s> <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, may the <s>Hotṛ</s> go to the winning of <s>Vasus</s>, to the bestowal of wealth. Homage! O <s>Vāk</s> (Speech), pronounce!' — these are the <s>yājyā</s> (offering) verses for the after-offerings (<s>anuyājas</s>).

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 1.14.1: When told 'Recite the <s>sūktavāka</s> (well-spoken word)' —
ŚŚS 1.14.2: 'This auspicious thing has come to be for heaven and earth; we have accomplished the well-spoken word and also the word of homage. May we succeed in the well-spoken utterance. O <s>Agni</s>, you are the one of well-spoken words' — thus concluding.
ŚŚS 1.14.3: 'O <s>Upaśruti</s> (fame), of heaven and earth, gracious one — be you in this sacrifice [favorable] to the sacrificer, O heaven and earth, let them be' — thus concluding.
ŚŚS 1.14.3: 'Auspicious, swift-giving, fearless, not to be found out, having wide pastures, creating freedom from fear' — thus concluding.
ŚŚS 1.14.5: 'Heaven of rain, waters of flowing, the two beneficent ones, the two delightful ones, full of nourishment, full of milk, of good approach and good management — their favor [be ours]' — thus concluding.
ŚŚS 1.14.6: <s>Agni</s> has accepted the oblation; he has increased; he has made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.7: <s>Soma</s> has accepted the oblation; he has increased; he has made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.8: <s>Agni</s> has accepted the oblation; he has increased; he has made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.9: <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> have accepted the oblation; they have increased; they have made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.10: Or <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
ŚŚS 1.14.11: <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> have accepted the oblation; they have increased; they have made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.12: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> have accepted the oblation; they have increased; they have made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.13: <s>Indra</s> has accepted the oblation; he has increased; he has made [it] a great and greater [offering]. Or Great <s>Indra</s>.
ŚŚS 1.14.14: The gods who drink the ghee have accepted the ghee; they have increased; they have made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.15: <s>Agni</s> has accepted the oblation through the <s>hotra</s> (priestly function); he has increased; he has made [it] a great and greater [offering].
ŚŚS 1.14.16: In this successful <s>hotrā</s>, going to the gods, this sacrificer aspires:
ŚŚS 1.14.17: Having uttered the two names of the sacrificer as 'So-and-so, So-and-so,' he aspires to a further divine worship; he aspires to a greater offering; he aspires to life; he aspires to good offspring; he aspires to the heavenly abode.
ŚŚS 1.14.18: 'What he aspires to with this oblation, may he obtain it; may he succeed in it; may the gods grant it to him; may <s>Agni</s>, the divine, obtain it from the gods for him. We [are] human beings dependent on <s>Agni</s>.'
ŚŚS 1.14.19: 'The offered and the distributed have come to be; may both heaven and earth protect him (or 'not [let him fall]') from distress. Here is the path for both of you; and homage to the gods.'
ŚŚS 1.14.20: Having placed a handful [of grass] on the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass) with [the word] 'homage,' he mutters.
ŚŚS 1.14.21: When told 'Recite the <s>śaṃyuvāka</s> (benediction),' having uttered 'That <s>śaṃyu</s>' — having spoken the <s>śaṃyu</s> word, he touches [water].
ŚŚS 1.14.22: From the taking up of the ladles up to the share of the <s>mandra</s> (soft-voiced) offering verse.
ŚŚS 1.14.23: The next [portion is recited] with the middle [voice].
ŚŚS 1.14.24: From the after-offerings onward, with the highest [voice].

body.translated_text:
1.15.1: They perform the <s>patnī-samyājas</s> (wife's offerings) in a low voice at the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire.
1.15.2: He offers to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, to the wives of the gods, and to <s>Agni Gṛhapati</s> (Agni as lord of the house).
1.15.3: <s>Rākā</s> and <s>Sinīvālī</s> [are offered to] before <s>Gṛhapati</s>, for one desiring offspring.
1.15.4: [The mantras are:] 'ā pyāyasva sam te payāṃsi' (Swell up, may thy milks), 'iha tvaṣṭāram' (Here Tvaṣṭṛ), 'tan nas turīpam' (That swiftness for us), 'devānām patnīr uta gnā vyantu' (May the wives of the gods and the divine women come), 'rākām aham' (I invoke Rākā), 'yās te rāke' (Those of thine, O Rākā), 'sinīvāli' (O Sinīvālī), 'yāsu bāhur' (In whom the arm), 'agnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ' (Agni the invoker, lord of the house), 'vayam u tvā gṛhapata' (We indeed, O lord of the house).
1.15.5: Having recited 'yathā ha tyad vasava' (As indeed, O Vasus), he invokes <s>Iḍā</s>.
1.15.6: The modification [of the formula] is 'upahūtā iyam yajamānī' (Invoked is this sacrificer's wife).
1.15.7: The <s>patnī-samyājas</s> end with <s>Iḍā</s>.
1.15.8: Or they end with the <s>śamyā</s> (measuring rod).
1.15.9: [Reciting] 'pra tvā muñcāmi' (I release thee), he releases the <s>veda</s> (grass bundle) and its binding cord.
1.15.10: Having placed the <s>veda</s> and its released [cord] in the wife's cupped hands.
1.15.11: Sprinkling the <s>veda</s> and cord with water, he recites:
1.15.12: 'kāmāya tvā vedo 'si' (For desire thou art, O Veda; by which thou, O Veda, became the Veda for the gods, by that be the Veda for us. Thou art the Veda, thou art attainment; may I know. Thou art the deed, thou art the instrument; may I accomplish. Thou art the winning, thou art the winner; may I win).
1.15.13: 'ghṛtavantaṃ kulāyinam rāyas poṣaṃ sahasriṇam | vedo dadātu vājinam' (May the Veda give [us] a nest rich in ghee, increase of wealth, thousandfold, vigorous) — with this, the <s>veda</s> makes the wife recite.
1.15.14: He, having grasped grass, places it between the thighs.
1.15.15: [Reciting] 'tantum tanvan' (Weaving the thread), he spreads [it] north of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire up to the sacred grass seat.
1.15.16: [Reciting] 'āpṛṇo 'si sampṛṇaḥ prajayā mā paśubhir ā pṛṇa' (Thou art filling, thou fillest fully; fill me with offspring and cattle) — he reverences the remainder of the <s>veda</s>.
1.15.17: [Reciting] 'etena agne brahmaṇā' (With this sacred formula, O Agni) — 'ayāḍ yajñaṃ jātavedā antaraḥ pūrvo 'smin niṣadya | sanvan saniṃ suvimucā vi muñca dhehy asmabhyaṃ draviṇaṃ jātavedaḥ' (Jātavedas has entered the sacrifice; sitting first within, winning the reward, release with good release, bestow wealth upon us, O Jātavedas) — he reverences the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
1.15.18: Having touched water, [the sacrifice] is concluded.

body.translated_text:
1.16.1: The new-moon and full-moon sacrifices have been explained; [they are] the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) of <s>iṣṭi</s> (offerings) and <s>paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifices).
1.16.2: [This] archetype is designated as [governing] what follows (<s>anvaya</s>).
1.16.3: What is offered between the two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions) and the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to Agni for what was properly offered) — that they call the <s>āvāpa</s> (the main insertion); that is the principal [offering].
1.16.4: The other [rites] are its subsidiary parts (<s>aṅga</s>).
1.16.5: When they share the same time, then [there is] capacity [for combination].
1.16.6: That is the characteristic of <s>tantra</s> (shared performance).
1.16.7: The offering is prescribed in conjunction with various deities, higher and lower.
1.16.8: In a modification of the deity, the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) and <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) belong to that deity.
1.16.9: And that deity is identified in the <s>nigama-sthānas</s> (places where the deity is mentioned by name).
1.16.10: In the invocation, in the last <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary offering), in the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, in the <s>nigada</s> (recitation), and in the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn-speech) — the deity being worshipped is mentioned; therefore these are the <s>nigama-sthānas</s>.
1.16.11: And proceeding sequentially, we shall explain the modifications.
1.16.12: When a modification of the full-moon [sacrifice] is stated, one should understand the <s>Vārtraghnī</s> [offerings].
1.16.13: When a modification of the new-moon [sacrifice] is stated, [one should understand] the <s>Vṛdhanvat</s> [offerings].
1.16.14: When there is no specific instruction, [they are] optional alternatives.
1.16.15: Based on the deity.
1.16.16: Or based on the oblation material.
1.16.17: When there is a convergence [of both], [the rule is determined] by the oblation material.
1.16.18: From the general, [comes] the restrictive rule.
1.16.19: And the seventeen-fold [number] of <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses.
1.16.20: [There is something] different from what is stated in <s>iṣṭi</s> and <s>paśubandha</s> [rites].
1.16.21: In rites performed for a specific desire (<s>kāmya</s>), the oblation materials [are offered] in a low voice.
1.16.22: And proceeding sequentially, we shall explain [them].

body.translated_text:
1.17.1: In the injunctive passage, the mention of the opening words (<s>pratīka</s>) of the oblation materials [serves to identify] the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>puronuvākyā</s> [verses], unless there is a connection with another meaning.
1.17.2: When there are two or more [oblations], [the verses are assigned] in sequence according to the injunction.
1.17.3: [Or assigned] by the deity.
1.17.4: And by the characteristic mark (<s>liṅga</s>).
1.17.5: When deities are mentioned in combination, if one cannot find [specific verses], one should be content with [a verse having] that deity's characteristic mark.
1.17.6: But combined [deities] are mentioned [in the nigama-sthānas].
1.17.7: And when an oblation to one and the same deity is repeatedly enjoined, the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>puronuvākyā</s> first prescribed should be understood as applying everywhere.
1.17.8: It is not possible to enumerate the <s>iṣṭis</s> separately [for each case].
1.17.9: When <s>yājyā</s> and <s>puronuvākyā</s> are not prescribed, one should select [verses in] <s>Gāyatrī</s> and <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meters addressed to that deity.
1.17.10: Or [in] <s>Uṣṇih</s> and <s>Bṛhatī</s> meters, excluding [the others].
1.17.11: The <s>yājyā</s> should be in the longer [meter].
1.17.12: Or they may be equal.
1.17.13: [This applies] where any of these characteristics is present.
1.17.14: 'I invoke,' 'we call,' 'hear,' 'come,' 'come here,' 'sit on this sacred grass,' the deity's name — these are the characteristics of the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse).
1.17.15: 'Eat,' 'drink,' 'enjoy,' 'be gladdened,' 'be aroused,' 'convey,' 'grant,' the deity's name — these are the characteristics of the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse).
1.17.16: The <s>puronuvākyā</s> has its characteristic marks at the beginning.
1.17.17: The <s>yājyā</s> has its characteristic marks at the end.
1.17.18: If one cannot find [verses] addressed to that deity, one should sacrifice with the two general-purpose [verses].
1.17.19: 'imam ā śṛṇudhī havam' (Hear this invocation here), 'yat tvā gīrbhir havāmahe' (When we invoke thee with songs), 'ā idam barhir niṣīda naḥ' (Sit here on this our sacred grass), 'stīrṇam barhir ānuṣag ā sadeta' (Seated in order on the spread grass), 'upa iḍānā iha no adya gaccha' (Praised, come hither to us today), 'aheḍanā manasā idam juṣasva' (Without anger, enjoy this with thy mind), 'vīhi havyam prayatam āhutam naḥ' (Convey the offered and cast oblation of ours) — thus one should adapt [these] for dual-deity and multi-deity [offerings].
1.17.20: Or one should revert to the archetypal [verses]; or one should revert to the archetypal [verses].

body.translated_text:
2.1.1: In spring, the setting up of the sacred fires (<s>agnyādhāna</s>) for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
2.1.2: In summer, for a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
2.1.3: In the rainy season, for a <s>vaiśya</s>.
2.1.4: Or in autumn.
2.1.5: Winter [is suitable] for all <s>varṇas</s> (classes).
2.1.6: [The choice of] seasons is according to wish for one who is about to perform the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice.
2.1.7: One should establish [the fires] on the new-moon day or the full-moon day.
2.1.8: Or in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion).
2.1.9: [The auspicious nakṣatras are] the three beginning with <s>Kṛttikā</s> and those beginning with <s>Phalgunī</s>.

body.translated_text:
2.2.1: Now [the rules regarding] the times for <s>iṣṭi</s> (offerings).
2.2.2: Immediately, on the twelfth day, in a month, in a season, or in a year.
2.2.3: [There is] an <s>iṣṭi</s> to <s>Agni Pavamāna</s> (Agni the Purifier).
2.2.4: [This is] a modification of the full-moon [sacrifice].
2.2.5: [The mantras are:] 'agna āyūṃṣi' (O Agni, lifespans) and 'agne pavasva' (O Agni, purify).
2.2.6: 'tam hi śaśvanta īḍate' (Him indeed they praise perpetually) and 'te syāma ye agnaya' (May we be those whom the fires [protect]) — these are for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
2.2.7: The second [iṣṭi is] to <s>Agni Pāvaka</s> (Agni the Pure) and <s>Agni Śuci</s> (Agni the Bright).
2.2.8: [This is] a modification of the new-moon [sacrifice].
2.2.9: [The mantras are:] 'agne pāvaka' (O Agni the Pure) and 'sa naḥ pāvaka' (That pure one for us).
2.2.10: [And:] 'agniḥ śuci vartatama' (Agni, the most bright, revolving) and 'ud agne śucayaḥ' (Up, O Agni, the bright ones).
2.2.11: 'agnim agnim havīmabhiḥ' (Agni, Agni, with oblations) and 'agninā aṅgiḥ samidhyata' (By Agni, Aṅgi was kindled) — these are for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
2.2.12: The third [iṣṭi is] to <s>Aditi</s>.
2.2.13: 'tvam agne saprathāḥ' (Thou, O Agni, widely spread) and 'soma yās ta' (O Soma, those of thine) — these two, containing [the word] 'sat,' are the <s>ājyabhāgas</s>.
2.2.14: [The mantras are:] 'uta tvām adite mahi' (Also thee, O great Aditi), 'mahīm ū ṣu mātaram suvratānāṃ ṛtasya patnīm avase huvema | tuvi-kṣatrāṃ ajarantīm urūcīṃ suśarmāṇam aditim supraṇītim' (We invoke for aid the great mother of those of good vows, the wife of <s>Ṛta</s>, of mighty dominion, unaging, wide-reaching, <s>Aditi</s> of good shelter and good guidance).
2.2.15: 'pra iddho agna' (Forth, O kindled Agni) and 'imo agna' (These, O Agni) — these two in <s>Virāj</s> meter are for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
2.2.16: [Some] make four [iṣṭis], with the first to <s>Agni</s>.
2.2.17: [The mantras are:] 'agne dyumnena' (O Agni, with splendor) and 'upa tvā juhvaḥ' (To thee, with oblations).
2.2.18: 'arcantas tvā' (Praising thee) and 'agniṃ stomena' (Agni, with a hymn) — these are for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>.

body.translated_text: 2.3.1: [It may be performed] in the first [pressing], as part of the same ritual procedure, 2.3.2: or in the middle [pressing], 2.3.3: or with two oblations. 2.3.4: [The offering] to <s>Āditya</s>; the second is the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (to Indra-and-Agni), for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. 2.3.5: Or the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> (to Agni-and-Soma). 2.3.6: The <s>Aindra</s> (to Indra) for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>. 2.3.7: The <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (to the All-Gods) for a <s>Vaiśya</s>. 2.3.8: 'All gods, upon the strewn sacred grass.' 2.3.9: Or for both, the <s>Āgneyī</s> (to Agni) comes first. 2.3.10: With ghee, the deities of the self — before the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake), [the verses to] <s>Agni Pavamāna</s> (purifying Agni), <s>Pāvaka</s> (the purifier), and <s>Śuci</s> (the bright) — [and] after it. 2.3.11: 'O <s>Agni</s>, with all <s>Agnis</s>; O <s>Agni</s>, with all <s>Agnis</s>' — for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. 2.3.12: The second [offering] is to <s>Aditi</s>. 2.3.13: The new-moon [sacrifice] is a modification [of the full-moon one]. 2.3.14: For the <s>Tākṣṇis</s>: with the deity-of-the-self [verses], a single-oblation [rite] for three days; then with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (to Viṣṇu) as second [for another period]; then with the <s>Āditya</s> (to Āditya) as third [for another period]; the tenth day is unmodified, [being] the <s>Āgneyī</s>. 2.3.15: In all [these], the <s>upāṃśu</s> (low-voiced) oblation is offered. 2.3.16: And [the number of] <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling verses) is fifteen. 2.3.17: Seventeen on the <s>Āditya</s> [day]. 2.3.18: The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) is twenty-four. 2.3.19: [Or] twelve. 2.3.20: Or six. 2.3.21: [Or] a horse. 2.3.22: Or a <s>śatamāna</s> (a gold piece of a hundred [units]), a chariot, a garment, and goats. 2.3.23: For twelve nights he should maintain his own fire-offering. 2.3.24: And truthful speech. 2.3.25: And giving to guests. 2.3.26: One who has established the [sacred] fires, while under the vow, should not eat meat without having sacrificed with a <s>paśu</s> (animal offering), nor [eat] the fruits of new plants without having sacrificed with the <s>āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering).

body.translated_text: 2.4.1: Prior to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon sacrifices) is the <s>anvārambhaṇīyā iṣṭi</s> (initiatory offering). 2.4.2: [It consists of offerings] to <s>Agni-and-Viṣṇu</s> (<s>Āgnāvaiṣṇava</s>), and to <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Sarasvat</s>. 2.4.3: 'O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, great is that your greatness; protect the secret names of the ghee. In every house, the well-recited praise going forth to you, your tongue has licked the ghee. O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, great abode, dear to you, partaking of the secret [offerings] of the ghee, being pleased — in every house bestowing the seven treasures, your tongue has raised the ghee.' 2.4.4: 'May <s>Sarasvatī</s> [who is] purifying' and 'invoking.' 2.4.5: 'Being born, he increased.' 2.4.6: Some [prescribe] five oblations — to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Bhaga</s> (the apportioner), and to <s>Vratapati</s> (lord of the vow). 2.4.7: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, [grant] glory with heroes'; 'you [are] our <s>Bhaga</s>.' 2.4.8: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, protector of vows'; 'whatever we [have vowed].' 2.4.9: The full-moon [sacrifice] is a modification [of the basic form]. 2.4.10: And a milch cow is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee).

body.translated_text: 2.5.1: The re-establishment of fires is optional, for one who does not know [the proper procedure]. 2.5.2: [The offerings are] to <s>Agni</s> and to <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, for one about to remove [the old fires]. 2.5.3: 'May <s>Vaiśvānara</s> come hither for our help, from afar. May <s>Agni</s> [come to] our well-recited praises. Asked in heaven.' 2.5.4: The mid-rainy season is the time for re-establishment of fires. 2.5.5: And the <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) <s>Punarvasu</s>. 2.5.6: Or the new-moon day after <s>Āṣāḍhā</s>. 2.5.7: And midday is the time. 2.5.8: And the <s>Āgneya</s> (offering to Agni) is on five potsherds. 2.5.9: And the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling verses) are fifteen. 2.5.10: And in three <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings) the word '<s>Agni</s>' is modified: 2.5.11: '<s>Tanūnapāt</s>, <s>Agni</s>; <s>Iḷā</s>, <s>Agni</s>; the sacred grass, <s>Agni</s>.' 2.5.12: The first <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion) is the enemy-destroying one. 2.5.13: 'Awaken <s>Agni</s> with praise' — or for <s>Agni Buddhimat</s> (Agni of intelligence). 2.5.14: 'O <s>Agni</s>, [grant] long lives' — the latter [verse] is for <s>Agni Pavamāna</s> (purifying Agni). 2.5.15: 'Come now, let me speak' — or for [Agni] who possesses the <s>Indu</s> (Soma drop). 2.5.16: '<s>Agni</s> is the head' — or for [Agni] who possesses seed. 2.5.17: He sacrifices as prescribed. 2.5.18: 'O <s>Agni</s>, you today' — the first [verse serves as] the second [verse] of the third oblation; and the fourth [verses are] for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. 2.5.19: 'The divine sacred grass, for the wealth-winning of <s>Agni</s>; the divine <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>, for the wealth-winning of <s>Agni</s>.' 2.5.20: They say the word '<s>Agni</s>' is distributed across the four earlier <s>prayājas</s> and the <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings). 2.5.21: And these are [recited] in a low voice (<s>upāṃśu</s>). 2.5.22: And the latter <s>ājyabhāga</s> (ghee-portion). 2.5.23: And the oblation. 2.5.24: Or everything, together with the first two <s>anuyājas</s>. 2.5.25: Or up to and including the oblation. 2.5.26: Or the oblation alone. 2.5.27: The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) is an unsewn [cloth], or a worn-out blanket re-prepared, or a decrepit cart-ox, or gold. 2.5.28: The second [offering] is to <s>Aditi</s>. 2.5.29: The new-moon [sacrifice] is a modification. 2.5.30: Or it is <s>Āgnivāruṇī</s> (to Agni-and-Varuṇa). 2.5.31: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, who are nearest'; 'you, O <s>Agni</s>, knowing <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [ways].'

body.translated_text: 2.6.1: He offers the <s>Agnihotra</s> in the evening and in the morning. 2.6.2: Before the shadows merge, he transfers [the fire] from the <s>Gārhapatya</s> to the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. 2.6.3: When the night is shining [with stars]. 2.6.4: Making it visible is [the duty of] one who maintains it constantly. 2.6.5: [This is for] one whose prosperity has departed — a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a village chief, [or] a <s>Kṣatriya</s>. 2.6.6: While transferring [the fire]: 'Lift me up from sin — both what I did unknowingly and what I did knowingly. Whatever sin we have committed here by day — from all that, being lifted up, protect me.' 2.6.7: 'I offer the immortal oblation in the immortal [fire]; <s>Agni</s> on the earth, for the conquest of immortality. By that may I win the endless world which <s>Prajāpati</s> first conquered.' 2.6.8: [The word] 'of the night' is the morning modification. 2.6.9: Having swept around [the altar], he prepares to offer. 2.6.10: 'I sprinkle you with <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) through <s>Satya</s> (truth)' — sprinkling three times three, one by one, and after offering. 2.6.11: 'I sprinkle you with <s>Satya</s> (truth) through <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order)' — in the morning. 2.6.12: 'You are the continuity of the sacrifice; I lead you for the continuity of the sacrifice' — [he draws] a continuous stream from the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and a flowing stream from the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. 2.6.13: 'Spinning the thread' — [he recites this] in between, when a wild animal has passed.

body.translated_text: 2.7.1: He offers when the [sun] has first set. 2.7.2: Or when a star is visible. 2.7.3: Near sunrise, when [the sky] has brightened. 2.7.4: Or when [the sun] has risen. 2.7.5: But he should set his mind on [offering] before the [proper] time. 2.7.6: For the transgression of that, there is an expiation. 2.7.7: Having lifted [the fire], having sat from sunset until darkness, having offered, having given a gift, he should pronounce the blessing with '<s>bhūḥ</s>.' 2.7.8: Or, without having offered, having milked [the cow], having conveyed another [fire] to the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he should offer. 2.7.9: Milk, rice gruel, curds, and ghee are the <s>Agnihotra</s> oblations. 2.7.10: He does not heat the curds. 2.7.11: He does not pour water back into the ghee. 2.7.12: Having strained [it] through a fresh <s>kuśa</s> grass [blade], he lifts up the ghee. 2.7.13: Behind the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern fire), the sacrificer, standing facing west, worships <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun): 'I lead the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> for you who are truth-and-order (<s>satyaṛta</s>)' — in the evening. 2.7.14: 'I lead the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> for you who are order-and-truth (<s>ṛtasatya</s>)' — toward the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, in the morning. 2.7.15: The sacrificer's passage is to the north of the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern fire). 2.7.16: The seat is to the south, behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. 2.7.17: Likewise [the seat] of the wife is [placed relative to] the <s>Gārhapatya</s>. 2.7.18: 'You are rain; cut away my sin. You are knowledge; know my sin' — he sips water [with this mantra]. 2.7.19: And he restrains his speech.

body.translated_text:
2.8.1: They release the <s>Agnihotrī</s> (fire-offering cow) to the south.
2.8.2: And they should not pass between [the fires and the cow].
2.8.3: Nor should one have her milked by a <s>Śūdra</s>.
2.8.4: In the evening he murmurs: "Milk for <s>Agni</s>, for the gods."
2.8.5: In the morning: "Milk for <s>Sūrya</s>, for the gods."
2.8.6: [He recites:] "Hunger and thirst — women indeed oppress a woman; with a woman I oppress you two, with the <s>Agnihotrī</s> cow, with the calf, with a hero" — in the evening and morning.
2.8.7: "With the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern fire) as a hero" — when [the cow] has a female calf.
2.8.8: [Reciting] "O maker of well-being, make well-being for us," sitting down, having brought out embers northward from the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, he places [the vessel] on [the fire] — the variation is: "with hunger and thirst, with the <s>Agnihotra</s> vessel, with the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire], with a hero."
2.8.9: [Saying] "With the eye of <s>Agni</s> I look upon you," he lights a firebrand and illuminates.
2.8.10: [Saying] "Together with the waters, with the sap of herbs," with the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) he brings back waters.
2.8.11: Having heated [the ladle], silently he again illuminates.
2.8.12: He removes [the vessel] northward, three times toward the place of deposit.
2.8.13: As if not cutting off [the stream].
2.8.14: [Saying] "Homage to the gods," he touches the embers on the south.
2.8.15: [Saying] "For well-being," having scraped back [the embers] well-heaped.
2.8.16: Having heated the <s>sruva</s> and the <s>sruc</s> (offering ladle), he draws up [the milk] — the variation is: "with hunger and thirst, with the <s>sruc</s>, with the <s>sruva</s>, with a hero."
2.8.17: Four or five times.
2.8.18: And a <s>mantra</s> at each ladling.
2.8.19: When drawn up, he wipes the <s>sruc</s>.
2.8.20: In the evening he murmurs: "Together with the gods, to the evening barley-drinks."
2.8.21: In the morning: "Together with the gods, to the morning barley-drinks."
2.8.22: Having placed the <s>sruc</s> north of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, taking a <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) firebrand of one span's length, and carrying the <s>sruc</s> past the <s>Gārhapatya</s> by the same [path], having placed the <s>sruc</s> on the tips of <s>kuśa</s> grass north-west of the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he places on [the fire] the firebrand — the variation is: "with hunger and thirst, with the firebrand, with the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, with a hero."
2.8.23: Having carried [the milk] past the firebrand by two finger-breadths, he makes the oblation.

ŚŚS_2.9.15: etad.eka.home.karma /
ŚŚS_2.9.16: sarveṣu.tu.juhvaty.ūrṇām.srucam.uttareṇa.gārhapatyam.nidhāya /
body.translated_text:
2.9.1: In the evening [he recites]: "<s>Agni</s> is light, light is <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>."
2.9.2: In the morning: "<s>Sūrya</s> is light, light is <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>svāhā</s>."
2.9.3: Bending the right knee, [he offers] without <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> [exclamations].
2.9.4: Having placed [the second oblation], a greater portion than the first, he [pours] silently the later [oblation] without mixing.
2.9.5: He should make the greater portion [remain] in the <s>sruc</s> (ladle).
2.9.6: Having touched the embers with the bottom of the <s>sruc</s>, twice lifting the <s>sruc</s> northward, he places it down.
2.9.7: The <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) breathes after the first oblation: "<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) has gone to the heavenly world; I conquer in the conquered; may there be no fear for me from worldlessness, sonlessness, cattlelessness."
2.9.8: He breathes after the second [oblation]: "<s>Apāna</s> (downward breath) has come; I completely conquer in the completely conquered; may there be no fear for me from worldlessness, sonlessness, cattlelessness."
2.9.9: "May the blessing of the well-accomplished sacrifice be fulfilled for me."
2.9.10: After both offerings, to the north, facing west, in the evening he wipes twice.
2.9.11: [Wiping] upward, to the south, in the morning.
2.9.12: The first wiping he smears on the <s>kuśa</s> grass, mentally [reciting]: "I gratify the herbs."
2.9.13: The second [wiping] — to the south, he places [his] palm face-up, mentally [reciting]: "I gratify the ancestors."
2.9.14: Having tasted twice with the forefinger, having turned around northward making a sound, having eaten with the ladle-handle pointing east, having turned the ladle-handle eastward, having licked [it] clean, having washed, having sipped water, having poured out the water to the north-east, he points to the north-east.
2.9.15: This is the procedure for a single oblation.
2.9.16: But in all offerings, he lays down the <s>sruc</s> with its wool covering north of the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.

ŚŚS_2.10.1: iha.puṣṭim.puṣṭi.patir.dadhātv.iha.prajām.janayatu.prajāpatiḥ.|.agnaye.rayimate.paśumate.puṣṭi.pataye.svāhā.|.agnaye.gṛha.pataye.svāhā.|.agnaye.svāhā.|.tūṣṇīm.caturthī.gārhapatye /

ŚŚS_2.10.4: avikṛtā.caturthī /
ŚŚS_2.10.5: yāḥ.srucy.āpas.traidham.tāḥ.karoty.agnihotra.sthālyām.gārhapatyasya.paścād.añjalau.ca.patnyāḥ /
ŚŚS_2.10.6: sam.tvā.sṛjāmi.prajayā.dhanena.ity.añjalau /
ŚŚS_2.10.7: pratitapya.srucam.nidadhāti /
body.translated_text:
2.10.1: [He offers four oblations in the <s>Gārhapatya</s>:] "May <s>Puṣṭipati</s> (lord of nourishment) bestow nourishment here; may <s>Prajāpati</s> generate offspring here. To <s>Agni</s> the wealthy, lord of cattle, lord of nourishment, <s>svāhā</s>. To <s>Agni</s> the lord of the household, <s>svāhā</s>. To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>." The fourth [oblation is made] silently in the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
2.10.2: [He offers in the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire:] "That excellent [glory] of <s>Savitṛ</s> — <s>Bhūḥ</s>, Speech — much, may much be mine, <s>svāhā</s>. The radiance of the god we meditate upon — <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) — more, may more be mine, <s>svāhā</s>. Who may inspire our thoughts — <s>Svar</s>, name, all — may all be mine, <s>svāhā</s>. To <s>Agni</s> the food-eater, lord of food, <s>svāhā</s>" — the fourth [oblation is made] in the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire.
2.10.3: Three [oblations] with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances) for one desiring the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
2.10.4: The fourth is without modification.
2.10.5: The waters that are in the <s>sruc</s> he divides threefold — into the <s>Agnihotra</s> vessel, behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and into the cupped hands of the wife.
2.10.6: [He says] "I unite you with offspring, with wealth" into the cupped hands.
2.10.7: Having heated the <s>sruc</s>, he lays it down.

body.translated_text:
2.11.1: The [procedure] that concerns the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) [follows the] southward rule.
2.11.2: "<s>Upa prayanto adhvaram</s>" (Approaching the sacrifice), "<s>Ayam agniḥ sahasriṇaḥ</s>" (This <s>Agni</s> of thousandfold [power]), "<s>Ubhā vām</s>" (Both of you), "<s>Ayam te yoniḥ</s>" (This is your womb), "<s>Ayam iha</s>" (This here), "<s>Asya pratnām</s>" (His ancient) — of these six, the first and last are [recited] three times each.
2.11.3: [He murmurs:] "O <s>Agni</s>, giver of life, give me life; O <s>Agni</s>, giver of splendor, give me splendor; O <s>Agni</s>, protector of the body, protect my body; O <s>Agni</s>, whatever is deficient in my body, fill that for me. Kindling you for a hundred winters, we kindle you the brilliant one, the one made of vigor, full of vigor, the one made of strength, full of strength. O <s>Agni</s>, destroyer of enemies, unconquered, undeceivable" — having murmured this,
2.11.4: [He recites] "<s>Citrāvaso svasti te pāram aśīya</s>" (O possessor of brilliant wealth, may I safely reach the other shore) three times.
2.11.5: [He sits down reciting:] "You, O <s>Agni</s>, have come together with the splendor of <s>Sūrya</s>, with the praise of the <s>ṛṣis</s>, with the praise of the <s>ṛṣis</s>, with the beloved abode, together with lifespan, with splendor, with offspring, with the beloved abode, with the increase of wealth — may I [attain]" — and sits down.
2.11.6: [He approaches the cow reciting:] "You are the waters; may I partake of you. You are greatness; may I partake of your greatness. You are nourishment; may I partake of your nourishment. You are the increase of wealth; may I partake of your increase of wealth. O rich ones, delight in this womb, in this world, in this cow-pen, in this dwelling, in this abode, in this blessing, in this foundation. Be here; do not depart from here" — thus he approaches the cow.

ŚŚS_2.12.1: saṃhitā.asi.viśva.rūpy.ūjā.mā.āviśa.gaupatyena.ity.asyā.lalāṭam.upaspṛśya /

ŚŚS_2.12.3: iḷa.ehy.adita.ehi.sūnṛta.ehi.iti.gām.abhyeti /
ŚŚS_2.12.5: somānam.svaraṇam.iti.tṛcena.uttarato.anvāhārya.pacanam /

ŚŚS_2.12.9: daivas.tantur.asy.anu.tvā.rabhe.mā.aham.tvad.vyavacchitsi.ity.āhavanīyasya.dakṣiṇato.aṅgārān.upaspṛśya /
ŚŚS_2.12.10: tato.asi.tantur.asy.anu.mā.saṃtanuhi.prajayā.paśubhī.rāyas.poṣeṇa.suprajās.tvena.suvīryeṇa.mānuṣas.tantur.asy.anu.mā.rabhasva.mā.tvam.mad.vyavacchitthā.asāv.iti.jyeṣṭhasya.putrasya.nāma.abhivyāhṛtya.yāvanto.vā.bhavanti /
ŚŚS_2.12.11: ātmano.ajāta.putraḥ /
ŚŚS_2.12.12: satyena.avabhṛtham.abhyavaimy.apsu.vratam.ity.ācamya.vācam.visṛjate /
body.translated_text:
2.12.1: [He says] "You are the composite, all-formed; may nourishment enter me through the lordship of cattle" — touching her forehead.
2.12.2: With the triplet "<s>Upa tvā agna</s>" (To you, O <s>Agni</s>) and the two-footed [verse] "<s>Agne tvam na</s>" (O <s>Agni</s>, you for us), [he approaches] the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
2.12.3: [He says] "Come, O <s>Iḍā</s>; come, O <s>Aditi</s>; come, O <s>Sūnṛtā</s>" — thus he approaches the cow.
2.12.5: With the triplet "<s>Somānāṃ svaraṇam</s>" (The self-moving of the <s>Somas</s>), [he approaches] the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire from the north.
2.12.6: Having murmured the <s>Māhitra</s> [formula] between the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he reverences the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
2.12.7: "<s>Tat savitur vareṇyam</s>" (That excellent [glory] of <s>Savitṛ</s>), "<s>Kadā cana starīr asi</s>" (Never are you barren), "<s>Pari te dūlabha</s>" (Around you, O hard to attain) — this [last verse] three times.
2.12.8: But in all offerings, the one who offers a single oblation places three firebrands each in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances).
2.12.9: [He says] "You are the divine thread; I attach myself to you; may I not be cut off from you" — touching the embers south of the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
2.12.10: [He says] "You are that thread; continue me with offspring, with cattle, with increase of wealth, with good progeny, with good heroism. You are the human thread; attach yourself to me; may you not be cut off from me" — [saying] the name of the eldest son, or of as many [sons] as there are.
2.12.11: [He speaks] of himself if he has no son yet born.
2.12.12: [He says] "By truth I descend to the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath); in the waters is the vow" — having sipped water, he releases speech.

ŚŚS_2.13.5: abhayam.te.abhayam.no.astu.prāṇena.tvā.upatiṣṭhe.vyānam.upaimy.āyuś.ca.ity.anvāhārya.pacanam /
ŚŚS_2.13.6: abhayam.vo.abhayam.no.astu.kāmena.va.upatiṣṭhate.vittim.upaimi.bhūtim.ca.iti.sarvān /
ŚŚS_2.13.7: samānam.samit.prabhṛtyā.vratasya.visarjanāt /

ŚŚS_2.13.9: anupasthānam.vā.prātaḥ /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 2.13.1: Now, in the morning:
ŚŚS 2.13.2: '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>! May I be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in nourishment through nourishments, rich in heroes through heroes. May there be fearlessness for you, fearlessness for us. With mind I attend upon you; I attain the world and heaven' — [thus addressing] the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire).
ŚŚS 2.13.3: Standing at that very spot, [he addresses] the other two [fires].
ŚŚS 2.13.4: 'May there be fearlessness for you, fearlessness for us. With speech I attend upon you; I attain offspring and cattle' — [thus addressing] the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (householder's fire).
ŚŚS 2.13.5: 'May there be fearlessness for you, fearlessness for us. With breath I attend upon you; I attain the diffused breath (<s>vyāna</s>) and life' — [thus addressing] the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern fire).
ŚŚS 2.13.6: 'May there be fearlessness for you, fearlessness for us. With desire I attend upon you all; I attain wealth and prosperity' — [thus addressing] all [the fires].
ŚŚS 2.13.7: The [procedure] is the same from the offering of the fuel-stick up to the release of the observance.
ŚŚS 2.13.8: By this very same [procedure], evening and morning.
ŚŚS 2.13.9: Or [there is] no [separate] attendance in the morning.

ŚŚS_2.14.8: anapetam.hi.kāraṇam /
ŚŚS_2.14.9: saṃdhi.velayor.vā.ācamya.vācam.yatvā.punar.ācamya.mahā.vyāhṛtibhir.visargaḥ /
ŚŚS_2.14.10: cakṣur.viṣaye.agnīnām.vācam.yacchet.|.proṣyāyan /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 2.14.1: One who is about to go on a journey looks at the fires [saying] 'May there be fearlessness for you, fearlessness for us.'
ŚŚS 2.14.2: 'O manly one, protect my offspring; protect the human ones from fear' — [thus addressing] the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
ŚŚS 2.14.3: 'O <s>Atharya</s> (?), protect my food; protect the ancestral ones from fear' — [thus addressing] the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s>.
ŚŚS 2.14.4: Having gone to the north of that [fire], 'O praiseworthy one, protect my cattle; protect the divine ones from fear' — [thus addressing] the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
ŚŚS 2.14.7: Having lifted up three words [saying] 'Food, food' — restraint of speech from that point onward.
ŚŚS 2.14.8: For the cause (i.e., the fire) has not departed.
ŚŚS 2.14.9: Or, at the two juncture times (dawn and dusk), having sipped water, having restrained speech, sipping water again, the release [of speech] is with the great <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances).
ŚŚS 2.14.10: He should restrain speech within the range of sight of the fires, when about to go on a journey.

body.text:
ŚŚS_2.15.1: tathā.caiva.samīkṣaṇam /
ŚŚS_2.15.2: āganma.vṛtra.hantamam.asmabhyam.vasuvittamam.|.agne.saṃrāḷ.abhi.dyumnam.abhi.saha.ā.yacchasva.|.śaṃsya.paśūn.me.ajugupas.tān.me.pāhy.eva.daivān.mā.bhayād.ajugupas.tasmān.mā.pāhy.eva.ity.āhavanīyam /
ŚŚS_2.15.3: tṛṇa.apacayanam.samid.ādhānam.ca.sarveṣu /
ŚŚS_2.15.4: ayam.agniḥ.purīṣyo.rayimān.puṣṭi.vardhanaḥ.|.agne.purīṣyā.abhi.dyumnam.abhi.saha.ā.yacchasva.|.atharya.pitum.me.ajugupsas.tam.me.pāhy.eva.pitryān.mā.bhayād.ajugupas.tasmān.mā.pāhy.eva.ity.anvāhārya.pacanam /
ŚŚS_2.15.5: ayam.agnir.gṛha.patir.gārhapatyāt.prajāyā.vasuvittamaḥ.|.agne.gṛha.pate.abhi.dyumnam.abhi.saha.ā.yacchasva.|.narya.prajām.me.ajugupas.tām.me.pāhy.eva.mānuṣān.mā.bhayād.ajugupas.tan.mān.mā.pāhy.eva.iti.gārhapatyam /
ŚŚS_2.15.6: vyaveto.agnīn.pravasati /
ŚŚS_2.15.7: tena.ca.eva.utsṛjyate /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 2.15.1: Similarly [there is] the looking at [the fires upon return].
ŚŚS 2.15.2: 'We have come to the greatest slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the best winner of wealth for us. O <s>Agni</s>, sovereign lord, bestow upon [us] splendor, bestow strength. O praiseworthy one, you have guarded my cattle — do guard them; likewise the divine ones — you have guarded from fear — from that do guard me likewise' — [thus addressing] the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
ŚŚS 2.15.3: Clearing away the grass and placing a fuel-stick — [this is done] at all [fires].
ŚŚS 2.15.4: 'This <s>Agni</s> is rich in soil (<s>purīṣya</s>), wealthy, increaser of nourishment. O <s>Agni</s>, rich in soil, bestow upon [us] splendor, bestow strength. O <s>Atharya</s>, you have guarded my food — do guard it; likewise the ancestral ones — you have guarded from fear — from that do guard me likewise' — [thus addressing] the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s>.
ŚŚS 2.15.5: 'This <s>Agni</s> is the lord of the household (<s>gṛhapati</s>), born from the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, the best winner of wealth for offspring. O <s>Agni</s>, lord of the household, bestow upon [us] splendor, bestow strength. O manly one, you have guarded my offspring — do guard them; likewise the human ones — you have guarded from fear — from that do guard me likewise' — [thus addressing] the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
ŚŚS 2.15.6: Having taken leave of the fires, he goes on his journey.
ŚŚS 2.15.7: [End of section.]

body.text:
ŚŚS_2.16.1: vāstoṣ.patīyam.dhrauvye.daśarātra.avara.ardhe.samprayāteṣu /
ŚŚS_2.16.2: agniṣṭhasya.dakṣiṇe.yukta.upohya.cīvaram.vāstoṣ.pate.pratijānīhi.ity.anūcya.vāstoṣ.pate.śagmaya.iti.yajati /
ŚŚS_2.16.3: hute.ca.anāhitam.tyajet /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 2.16.1: The <s>Vāstoṣpatīya</s> (offering to the Lord of the Dwelling) [is performed] on the permanent [fire], in the latter half of a ten-night [period], when [the fires] have been sent forth.
ŚŚS 2.16.2: Having brought the covering (<s>cīvara</s>) and placed it on the right side of the <s>Agniṣṭha</s> (fire-place), having recited 'O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, accept,' he offers with [the verse] 'O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, the auspicious one.'
ŚŚS 2.16.3: After the offering, he should abandon [the fire that was] not established.

body.text:
ŚŚS_2.17.1: samārohayamāṇo.gārhapatye.pāṇī.pratitapya.prāṇān.sammṛśaty.ehi.me.prāṇān.āroha.iti /
ŚŚS_2.17.2: sakṛt.sakṛn.mantreṇa.dvir.dvis.tūṣṇīm /
ŚŚS_2.17.3: ayam.te.yonir.iti.vāraṇī.pratitapati /
ŚŚS_2.17.4: sakṛt.sakṛn.mantreṇa.dvir.dvis.tūṣṇīm /
ŚŚS_2.17.5: evam.āhavanīyāt /
ŚŚS_2.17.6: nitya.dhṛtād.anyasmin /
ŚŚS_2.17.7: anastamite.ca.manthanam /
ŚŚS_2.17.8: upāvaroha.jāta.vedaḥ.punas.tvam.devebhyo.havyam.vaha.naḥ.prajānan.|.āyuḥ.prajām.rayim.asmāsu.dhehy.ariṣṭo.dīdihi.no.duroṇe.|.ity.ātmano.araṇyor.upāvarohya.manthanam /
ŚŚS_2.17.9: laukike.vā.laukike.vā /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 2.17.1: When placing [the fires] back together, having warmed his hands at the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, he touches his vital breaths [saying] 'Come to me; ascend my vital breaths.'
ŚŚS 2.17.2: Once each [time] with the <s>mantra</s>; twice each [time] silently.
ŚŚS 2.17.3: 'This is your womb' — thus he warms the fire-sticks (<s>araṇī</s>).
ŚŚS 2.17.4: Once each with the <s>mantra</s>; twice each silently.
ŚŚS 2.17.5: Likewise from the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
ŚŚS 2.17.6: From the permanently maintained [fire] into another.
ŚŚS 2.17.7: And the churning [of fire should be done] before sunset.
ŚŚS 2.17.8: 'Descend again, O <s>Jātavedas</s>; carry the oblation to the gods again, knowing. Bestow upon us life, offspring, and wealth; shine undamaged in our dwelling' — thus, having [symbolically] descended into one's own fire-sticks (<s>araṇis</s>), [he performs] the churning.
ŚŚS 2.17.9: Or from an ordinary [household] fire — or from an ordinary fire.

body.text:
ŚŚS_3.1.1: saṃsthitāyām.paurṇamāsyām.indrāya.iṣṭir.vimṛdhe /
ŚŚS_3.1.2: amāvāsyā.vikāraḥ /
ŚŚS_3.1.3: indra.kṣatram.mṛgo.na.bhīmaḥ /
ŚŚS_3.1.4: juṣṭo.damūnā.agne.śardha.iti.sviṣṭakṛtaḥ /
ŚŚS_3.1.5: aditaye.amāvāsyāyām.saṃsthitāyām /
ŚŚS_3.1.6: paurṇamāsī.vikāraḥ /
ŚŚS_3.1.7: ye.vaimṛdhasya.te.sviṣṭakṛtaḥ /
ŚŚS_3.1.8: yāvaj.jīvam.ca /
ŚŚS_3.1.9: prayoga.āntāt /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 3.1.1: When the full-moon [offering] is completed, [there follows] the <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) to <s>Indra</s> for overcoming hostility (<s>vimṛdha</s>).
ŚŚS 3.1.2: [It is] a modification of the new-moon [offering].
ŚŚS 3.1.3: '<s>Indra</s>, the lordship — terrible like a wild beast.'
ŚŚS 3.1.4: 'Favored, dwelling in the home' and 'O <s>Agni</s>, be strong' — [these are the verses] for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the maker of good offerings).
ŚŚS 3.1.5: [The offering] to <s>Aditi</s> when the new-moon [offering] is completed.
ŚŚS 3.1.6: [It is] a modification of the full-moon [offering].
ŚŚS 3.1.7: Those of the <s>Vaimṛdha</s> [serve as verses] for the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
ŚŚS 3.1.8: And [this is to be performed] as long as one lives.
ŚŚS 3.1.9: Up to the end of the [sacrificial] practice.

body.text:
ŚŚS_3.2.1: anāgate.parvaṇy.amāvāsye.pravṛtte.abhyudita.iṣṭiḥ /
ŚŚS_3.2.2: agnaye.dātra.indrāya.pradātre.viṣṇave.śipiviṣṭāya.iti /
ŚŚS_3.2.3: nirupte.jānaṃs.tān.eva.vibhajet /
ŚŚS_3.2.4: agne.dādāno.agne.bṛhataḥ /
ŚŚS_3.2.5: sahasrā.te.śatā.tū.bhara /
ŚŚS_3.2.6: amāvāsyā.vikāraḥ /
ŚŚS_3.2.7: dhanuś.ca.trīṣu.dakṣiṇā /
ŚŚS_3.2.8: kāle.ca.amāvāsyam /
ŚŚS_3.2.9: na.abhyāvṛttiḥ.piṇḍa.pitṛ.yajñasya.asti /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 3.2.1: When the new-moon day has not yet arrived but the full moon is in progress, [that is] the <s>Abhyudita-iṣṭi</s> (offering when [the sun] has risen [with the moon still visible]).
ŚŚS 3.2.2: [The deities are] <s>Agni</s> the giver, <s>Indra</s> the bestower, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s> (pervading all).
ŚŚS 3.2.3: When the [offerings] have been poured, he should divide them knowing [the deities].
ŚŚS 3.2.4: 'O <s>Agni</s>, giving' [and] 'O <s>Agni</s>, of the great.'
ŚŚS 3.2.5: 'Bring a thousand and a hundred for you.'
ŚŚS 3.2.6: [It is] a modification of the new-moon [offering].
ŚŚS 3.2.7: And a bow is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee) in the three [offerings].
ŚŚS 3.2.8: And the new-moon [offering should be performed] at the proper time.
ŚŚS 3.2.9: There is no repetition of the <s>Piṇḍa-pitṛ-yajña</s> (ball-offering to the ancestors).

body.text:
ŚŚS_3.3.1: atīte.parvaṇy.amāvāsye.pravṛtte.abhyuddṛṣṭa.iṣṭi /
ŚŚS_3.3.2: agnaye.pathikṛta.indrāya.vṛtraghne.vaiśvānarāya /
ŚŚS_3.3.3: vetthā.hi.vedha.ā.devānām /
ŚŚS_3.3.4: vārtrahatyāya.sahadānum /
ŚŚS_3.3.5: ṛtāvānam.vaiśvānaram.ṛtasya.jyotiṣas.patim.|.ajasram.bhānum.īmahe.|.nābhim.yajñānām /
ŚŚS_3.3.6: amāvāsyā.vikāraḥ /
ŚŚS_3.3.7: daṇḍa.upānaham.dakṣiṇā /
ŚŚS_3.3.8: saṃsthitāyām.ca.amāvāsyam /
ŚŚS_3.3.9: nābhy.āvṛttiḥ.piṇḍa.pitṛ.yajñasya.asti /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 3.3.1: When the new-moon day has passed and the full-moon is in progress, [that is] the <s>Abhyuddṛṣṭa-iṣṭi</s> (offering when [the moon] has been seen [after the new moon]).
ŚŚS 3.3.2: [The deities are] <s>Agni</s> the path-maker, <s>Indra</s> the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, and <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
ŚŚS 3.3.3: 'You know indeed, O dispenser, [the ways] of the gods.'
ŚŚS 3.3.4: 'For the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>, [the one] together with <s>Dānu</s>.'
ŚŚS 3.3.5: '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>, upholder of truth (<s>ṛta</s>), lord of the light of truth — we seek the unquenchable flame, the center of sacrifices.'
ŚŚS 3.3.6: [It is] a modification of the new-moon [offering].
ŚŚS 3.3.7: A staff and a pair of sandals [is] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee).
ŚŚS 3.3.8: And the new-moon [offering is performed] when [the regular time] is completed.
ŚŚS 3.3.9: There is no repetition of the <s>Piṇḍa-pitṛ-yajña</s>.

body.text:
ŚŚS_3.4.1: agnaye.agnimate.agnāv.agnāv.abhyuddhṛte /
ŚŚS_3.4.2: pathi.kṛte.antareṇa.vihāram.cakrīvati.vṛtte.niyata.atipattau.ca /
ŚŚS_3.4.3: vītaye.mithaḥ.saṃsṛṣṭeṣu /
ŚŚS_3.4.4: vivicaye.grāmyeṇa /
ŚŚS_3.4.5: saṃvargāya.pradāvyena /
ŚŚS_3.4.6: śucaye.kravyeṇa /
ŚŚS_3.4.7: apsumate.vaidyutena /
ŚŚS_3.4.8: vyādhi.plāye.rudrāya /
ŚŚS_3.4.9: adhvānam.gamiṣyan.pūṣṇe.pathi.kṛte /
ŚŚS_3.4.10: sārvakāmiky.agnaye.kāmāya /
ŚŚS_3.4.11: vrata.pataye.vratya.velām.proṣyā.vratyam.vā.caritvā /
ŚŚS_3.4.12: vratabhṛte.aśru.kṛtvā /
ŚŚS_3.4.13: gṛha.dāhe.kṣāmavate /
ŚŚS_3.4.14: marudbhyo.yamau.prajātāyām /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 3.4.1: To <s>Agni</s> <s>Agnimat</s> (possessing fire), when [the fire has been] placed in fire upon fire.
ŚŚS 3.4.2: To [<s>Agni</s>] the path-maker, when [fire from] a cart with wheels has been brought in between during a journey, when transgression of the rule has occurred.
ŚŚS 3.4.3: To [<s>Agni</s> for] going forth, when [fires] have been mixed together.
ŚŚS 3.4.4: To [<s>Agni</s> for] separating, [when mixed] with a village fire.
ŚŚS 3.4.5: To [<s>Agni</s> for] gathering up, when there has been a rush [of fire].
ŚŚS 3.4.6: To [<s>Agni</s>] the purifier, when [contaminated] by cremation fire.
ŚŚS 3.4.7: To [<s>Agni</s>] possessing water, when [affected] by lightning.
ŚŚS 3.4.8: In case of disease or plague — to <s>Rudra</s>.
ŚŚS 3.4.9: When about to go on a journey — to <s>Pūṣan</s> the path-maker.
ŚŚS 3.4.10: For all desires — to <s>Agni</s> <s>Kāma</s> (desire).
ŚŚS 3.4.11: To the lord of observances, when one has gone beyond the time of the vow, or after having performed the <s>vrātya</s> observance.
ŚŚS 3.4.12: To the bearer of observances, when one has made [a ritual] error.
ŚŚS 3.4.13: In case of a house fire — to [<s>Agni</s>] possessing the earth (<s>kṣāmavat</s>).
ŚŚS 3.4.14: To the <s>Maruts</s>, when twins are born.

body.text:
ŚŚS_3.5.1: agnim.agnim.havīmabhir.agninā.agniḥ.samidhyate /
ŚŚS_3.5.2: agna.ā.yāhi.vītaye.yo.agnim.deva.vītaye /
ŚŚS_3.5.3: kayā.no.agne.vivasas.tvām.agne.mānuṣīḥ /
ŚŚS_3.5.4: kuvit.su.no.mā.no.asmin.mahā.dhane /
ŚŚS_3.5.5: apsv.agna.urau.mahān /
ŚŚS_3.5.6: kad.rudrāya.aśyāma.te /
ŚŚS_3.5.7: vayam.u.tvā.pathas.pate.pathas.pathaḥ /
ŚŚS_3.5.8: agniḥ.pareṣu.dhāmasu.kāmo.bhūtasya.bhavyasya.|.saṃrāḷ.eko.vi.rājati.|.aśyāma.tam /
ŚŚS_3.5.9: tvam.agne.vratabhṛt.śucir.agne.devān.iha.ā.vaha.|.upa.yajñam.haviś.ca.naḥ.|.vratāni.bibhrad.vratapā.adābhyo.bhavā.no.dūto.ajaraḥ.suvīraḥ.|.dadhar.ratnāni.sumṛlīko.agne.gopāya.no.jīvase.jāta.vedaḥ /
ŚŚS_3.5.10: kṛṣṇā.rajāṃsi.patsutas.tve.vasūni.purvaṇīka.hotaḥ /
ŚŚS_3.5.11: marutas.tveṣa.sadṛśa.ā.yāta.yamāv.iva.|.śubhrā.hiraṇya.khādayaḥ.|.vāta.tviṣo.marutaḥ.śriye.kam.iti.vā /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 3.5.1: [The <s>yājyā</s> verses are:] '<s>Agni</s>, <s>Agni</s> with oblations'; '<s>Agni</s> is kindled by <s>Agni</s>.'
ŚŚS 3.5.2: 'O <s>Agni</s>, come forth to the feast'; 'He who [worships] <s>Agni</s>, for the divine feast.'
ŚŚS 3.5.3: 'With what [aid], O <s>Agni</s>, do you shine for us?'; 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, [are worshipped] by the human ones.'
ŚŚS 3.5.4: 'Perhaps indeed for us'; 'Do not [forsake us] in this great contest.'
ŚŚS 3.5.5: 'In the waters, O <s>Agni</s>, the great one in the wide [realm].'
ŚŚS 3.5.6: 'What [shall we offer] to <s>Rudra</s>?'; 'May we attain those.'
ŚŚS 3.5.7: 'We indeed [attend] you, O lord of the path'; 'O lord of each path.'
ŚŚS 3.5.8: '<s>Agni</s> in the highest abodes'; '<s>Kāma</s> (desire) of what has been and what will be; the sole sovereign shines forth; may we attain that.'
ŚŚS 3.5.9: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the bearer of observances, O pure one'; 'O <s>Agni</s>, bring the gods here to our sacrifice and our oblation'; 'Bearing the observances, protector of vows, inviolable, be our ageless messenger, rich in heroes'; 'He has borne the treasures; O gracious <s>Agni</s>, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, protect us for [a long] life.'
ŚŚS 3.5.10: 'The dark spaces [he traverses] going forth'; 'In you the riches, O <s>Hotṛ</s> of the vanguard.'
ŚŚS 3.5.11: 'O <s>Maruts</s>, brilliant, equal — come here; like the two <s>Yamas</s> (twins); bright, with golden ornaments'; 'O <s>Maruts</s>, having the brilliance of the wind, shining...'

body.text:
ŚŚS_3.6.1: jñātayo.asaṃvidānā.bahu.devatām.iṣṭim.nirvaperan /
ŚŚS_3.6.2: agniḥ.prathamo.vasubhir.no.avyāt.somo.rudrair.abhi.rakṣatu.tmanā.|.indro.ṃrudbhir.ṛtuthā.kṛṣotv.ādityair.no.varuṇaḥ.śarma.yaṃsat.|.sam.agnir.vasubhir.no.avyāt.sam.somo.rudriyābhis.tanūbhiḥ.|.sam.indro.rāta.havyo.marudbhiḥ.sam.ādityair.varuṇo.viśva.vedāḥ /
ŚŚS_3.6.3: saṃjñānam.iti.ca.japeran /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 3.6.1: Kinsmen who are not in agreement should offer a multi-deity <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering).
ŚŚS 3.6.2: [The mantras are:] 'May <s>Agni</s> as the first protect us with the <s>Vasus</s>; may <s>Soma</s> with the <s>Rudras</s> guard us by himself; may <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s> cultivate [for us] according to the seasons; may <s>Varuṇa</s> with the <s>Ādityas</s> grant us shelter. May <s>Agni</s> with the <s>Vasus</s> protect us; may <s>Soma</s> with the <s>Rudra</s>-like bodies [protect us]; may <s>Indra</s>, to whom oblations are given, [protect us] with the <s>Maruts</s>; may <s>Varuṇa</s> with the <s>Ādityas</s>, the all-knowing one.'
ŚŚS 3.6.3: And they should mutter the [hymn beginning with] '<s>Saṃjñānam</s>' (mutual understanding).

body.text:
ŚŚS_3.7.1: mitra.vindāyāḥ /
ŚŚS_3.7.2: pañcadaśa.sāmidhenīḥ /
ŚŚS_3.7.3: agninā.rayim.gayasphāna.ity.ājya.bhāgau /

body.translated_text: 3.7.1: Of the <s>Mitravindā</s> [offering]. 3.7.2: [There are] fifteen <s>sāmidhenīs</s> (kindling verses). 3.7.3: 'By <s>Agni</s>, wealth' and '<s>gayasphāna</s> (household-increasing)' — these are the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions). 3.7.4: '<s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s> who gives a thousandfold — may <s>Pūṣan</s> [protect] us with cattle, with help; may <s>Sarasvatī</s> [and] <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> anoint the forms with sacrifices. <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> bestowing forms, <s>Sarasvatī</s> — may <s>Pūṣan</s> [give] fortune, may <s>Savitṛ</s> give to me; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> give, may <s>Indra</s> [give] strength to me — <s>Mitra</s>, dominion, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Agni</s>.' 3.7.5: 'Now bestow upon us a thousandfold; and, O <s>Brahman</s>, help us' — for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. 3.7.6: A thousand [is] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). 3.7.7: The order of deities is [stated] with the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) pattern in the <s>nigamas</s> (citations). 3.7.8: With the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) pattern in the directives. 3.7.9: Or as directed [by the Adhvaryu].
