body.translated_text: 3.8.1: On the full-moon day of <s>Phālgunī</s>, in the performance [of those] whose session has not been initiated. 3.8.2: Of the <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> sacrifice, on the new-moon day, and of the <s>Sākaprasthāyya</s>. 3.8.3: Fifteen years [is the duration] of the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice. 3.8.4: Or [performed once] each year, for all [sacrificers]. 3.8.5: The regular new-moon and full-moon [sacrifices] do not continue for one who is performing [the Dākṣāyaṇa]. 3.8.6: Of the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice: 3.8.7: The full-moon [offerings are performed] on the preceding day. 3.8.8: Or the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [is offered]. 3.8.9: The <s>Āgneya</s> (to Agni), the <s>Sāmnāyya</s>, and the <s>Aindra</s> (to Indra) [are offered] at the full moon. 3.8.10: During the dark fortnight, one who has the vow of the initiated gives to guests. 3.8.11: Or one who has the vow of truth. 3.8.12: He does not wear [garments that are] anointed, washed, woolen, or refined. 3.8.13: He eats the remnants of the oblation. 3.8.14: He should not attain satiety. 3.8.15: Meditating in his mind, 'I eat King <s>Soma</s>, the moon,' he eats. 3.8.16: The new-moon [offerings are performed] on the preceding day. 3.8.17: Or the <s>Aindrāgna</s> (to Indra-and-Agni). 3.8.18: The <s>Āgneya</s> (to Agni), the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> (to Mitra-and-Varuṇa), and the <s>Payasyā</s> (milk offering) [are offered] at the new moon. 3.8.19: 'By <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), she who' and 'among your peoples.' 3.8.20: Before the <s>Śamyorvāka</s> (benediction), or after, without invoking, he sacrifices to the <s>Vājins</s> (coursers). 3.8.21: They converge at the last <s>prayāja</s> (fore-offering), and according to purpose in the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn-recitation). 3.8.22: 'The <s>Vājins</s>, the gods, will enjoy the oblation, will increase, will make [us] greater than the great.' 3.8.23: 'May the <s>Vājins</s> be auspicious to us; in vigor, vigor' — with knees raised, he sacrifices without interruption. 3.8.24: 'O <s>Agni</s>, partake of the <s>Vājin</s>' — [this is] the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> (subsidiary vaṣaṭ call). 3.8.25: The sacrificer, the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, and the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, having been summoned together, partake. 3.8.26: The sacrificer [partakes] first and last. 3.8.27: 'Whatever seed of mine flows forth, or whatever poured out is produced — by King <s>Soma</s>, we retain that within ourselves. You are vigor; you are vigorous; place vigor in me' — this is the <s>bhakṣa</s> (partaking) <s>mantra</s>.

body.translated_text: 3.9.1: Of the <s>Iḷādadha</s> [offering]. 3.9.2: [The offerings are] to <s>Agni</s> and to <s>Sarasvatī</s>. 3.9.3: The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> (to Agni-and-Soma), together with the <s>upāṃśuyāja</s> (low-voiced offering), the <s>Sāmnāyya</s>, and the <s>Aindra</s> (to Indra) [are offered] at the full moon. 3.9.4: And the vows are those of the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice. 3.9.5: [The offerings are] to <s>Agni</s> and to <s>Sarasvat</s>. 3.9.6: The <s>Aindrāgna</s> (to Indra-and-Agni), the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> (to Mitra-and-Varuṇa), and the <s>Payasyā</s> (milk offering) [are offered] at the new moon. 3.9.7: The <s>Vājin</s> [offering] is the same [as before].

body.translated_text: 3.10.1: In the <s>Sārvaseni</s> sacrifice. 3.10.2: Both [sets of] oblations [are offered] in a single <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering). 3.10.3: The full-moon [oblations come] first. 3.10.4: 'Honoring our sacrifice, O <s>Agni</s>' — for the latter <s>Āgneya</s> (offering to Agni). 3.10.5: He does not sacrifice at the new moon. 3.10.6: But he performs the <s>piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (ball-offering to the ancestors). 3.10.7: In the <s>Śaunaka</s> sacrifice and the <s>Sākaprasthāyya</s>, there is no modification for the <s>Hotṛ</s>.

body.translated_text: 3.11.1: By the <s>Sārvaseni</s> sacrifice, the <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> sacrifice is explained. 3.11.2: But the new-moon [oblations come] first. 3.11.3: He does not sacrifice at the full moon. 3.11.4: Thus [end] the new-moon and full-moon sessions (<s>ayana</s>s). 3.11.5: [Now] the optional [offerings]. 3.11.6: And [there are] fifteen <s>sāmidhenīs</s> (kindling verses). 3.11.7: [The offerings are] to <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Āgnāvaiṣṇava</s> (to Agni-and-Viṣṇu). 3.11.8: The full-moon [sacrifice] is a modification. 3.11.9: He sacrifices always, except on the <s>parvan</s> (junction day). 3.11.10: They call this the <s>munyayana</s> (the sage's session). 3.11.11: [The offerings are] to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Viśvedeva</s> (All-Gods). 3.11.12: The new-moon [sacrifice] is a modification. 3.11.13: He sacrifices always, except on the <s>parvan</s>. 3.11.14: One who is not initiated puts on a black antelope skin. 3.11.15: They call this the <s>turāyaṇa</s> (the swift session). 3.11.16: And [it lasts] for one year in performance.

body.translated_text: 3.12.1: The <s>Saumī</s> offering with <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet). 3.12.2: And the <s>Vaiṇuyavī</s> (with bamboo rice). 3.12.3: The <s>Aindrāgna</s> (to Indra-and-Agni), or the <s>Āgnendra</s> (to Agni-and-Indra), the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (to the All-Gods), and the <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s> (to Heaven-and-Earth) — [these are] for rice and barley [offerings]. 3.12.4: The <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee-portions) are as in the [basic] form. 3.12.5: 'This sacrifice of yours' [and] 'your abodes in heaven.' 3.12.6: The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee) for the <s>Saumya</s> (to Soma) is a <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture reception). 3.12.7: 'This of yours' [and] 'the pure one, indeed.' 3.12.8: 'O those of good deeds, of good brightness.' 3.12.9: 'Great heaven, broad earth.' 3.12.10: The <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s> [offerings are performed] in a low voice (<s>upāṃśu</s>). 3.12.11: The <s>Virāj</s> [verses are used] for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. 3.12.12: A calf is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee) for the first-born. 3.12.13: Or [it is performed] as part of the same ritual procedure with the new-moon and full-moon [sacrifices]. 3.12.14: Or the new-moon and full-moon [sacrifices serve as] the first-fruits [offering]. 3.12.15: Or the <s>Agnihotra</s> with rice gruel, in the evening and morning. 3.12.16: Or, having made the <s>Agnihotrī</s> cow eat the new [grain], with her milk he should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> in the evening and morning. 3.12.17: Or, having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering) on the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, he should offer it in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> with the <s>svāhā</s> call to the <s>āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits) deities, with the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> as the fourth.

body.translated_text:
3.13.1: The performance of the <s>cāturmāsyas</s> (four-monthly sacrifices) [begins] on the full-moon day of <s>Phālgunī</s>.
3.13.2: Or on [the full-moon of] <s>Caitra</s>.
3.13.3: The <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> (offering to Agni Vaiśvānara) and <s>Pārjanya</s> (offering to Parjanya) <s>iṣṭi</s> [are performed] on the first full-moon day.
3.13.4: [The mantra] to <s>Parjanya</s>: 'yasya vrate' (In whose ordinance).
3.13.5: On the latter [full-moon day, is] the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to all gods).
3.13.6: [The first offering is] to <s>Agni</s>.
3.13.7: [Then] to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s>.
3.13.8: [Then] to <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>.
3.13.9: To the <s>Maruts</s> who possess their own power (<s>svatavadbhyaḥ</s>).
3.13.10: [Then] the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (offering to all gods).
3.13.11: And [the offering] to <s>Dyāvā-Pṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth).
3.13.12: [The mantras are:] 'hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye' (The golden-handed one for aid) and 'udīraya' (Rouse up).
3.13.13: 'pūṣan tava' (O Pūṣan, thine) and 'śukraṃ te' (Thy bright [offering]).
3.13.14: 'iha iha vaḥ' (Here, here to you) and 'pra citram' (Forth the wondrous).
3.13.15: And the fire-churning [mantras are used] when the oblations are near at hand.
3.13.17: 'abhi tvā deva savituḥ' (Unto thee, O divine Savitṛ), 'mahī dyauḥ' (Great heaven), 'tvām agne puṣkarāt' (Thee, O Agni, from the lotus) — these three. 'uta bruvantu jantavaḥ' (Let the creatures declare) — for [the fire] when born. 'ā yaṃ haste na khādinam' (As one bears a ring upon the hand) — for [the fire] while being held in the hand. The latter [two mantras are used] while [the fire is] being carried forward. 'agninā agniḥ samidhyate' (By fire is fire kindled), 'tvam hy agne agninā' (For thou, O Agni, by fire), 'tam marjayanta' (They polish him) — these are the fire-churning mantras.
3.13.18: And nine <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings).
3.13.19: Four [additional ones are inserted] between the fourth and the last.
3.13.20: 'duro agna ājyasya vyantu' (May the doors [partake] of Agni's ghee), 'uṣāsānaktā agna ājyasya vītām' (May Dawn and Night partake of Agni's ghee), 'daivyā hotārā agna ājyasya vītām' (May the two divine invokers partake of Agni's ghee), 'tisro devīr agna ājyasya vyantu' (May the three goddesses partake of Agni's ghee).
3.13.21: The two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions) contain [the word] 'sat.'
3.13.22: And the <s>Sāvitra</s> and <s>Dyāvā-Pṛthivīya</s> [offerings are made] in a low voice.
3.13.23: [The verses for] the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> are in <s>Virāj</s> meter.
3.13.24: A calf as the first-born [is given as] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee).
3.13.25: Nine <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings).
3.13.26: But six [additional ones are inserted] between the first and second.
3.13.27: 'devīr dvāro vasuvane vasudheyasya vyantu' (May the divine doors [partake] in the wealth-winning, in the wealth-giving), 'devī uṣāsānaktā...' (May the divine Dawn and Night...), 'devī joṣṭrī...' (May the divine Approver...), 'devī ūrja āhutī...' (May the divine oblations of nourishment...), 'devī uṣāsānaktā...' (May the divine Dawn and Night...), 'devī joṣṭrī...' (May the divine Approver...), 'devīs tisras tisro devīr vasuvane vasudheyasya vyantu' (May the three goddesses [partake] in the wealth-winning, in the wealth-giving).
3.13.28: The <s>vājina</s> (vitality formula) is the same [as in the archetype].
3.13.29: When [the full-moon sacrifice] is concluded, [one performs] the full-moon [rite].
3.13.30: Abstinence from meat, celibacy, sleeping on the ground — or approaching one's wife at the proper season — and truthful speech: these are the observances for the intermediate periods.

body.translated_text:
3.14.1: The <s>Varuṇa-praghāsas</s> (offerings associated with Varuṇa) [are performed] on the full-moon of <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>, for the <s>Phālgunī</s> commencement.
3.14.2: On <s>Śravaṇī</s>, for the <s>Caitrī</s> commencement.
3.14.3: The <s>Vaiśvadevika</s> [portions] end with [the offering to] <s>Pūṣan</s>.
3.14.4: [The offerings are:] <s>Aindrāgna</s> (to Indra and Agni), <s>Vāruṇī</s> (to Varuṇa), <s>Payasyā</s> (milk offering), <s>Mārutī</s> (to the Maruts), and <s>Kāya</s> (to Ka/Prajāpati).
3.14.5: [The mantras are:] 'imam me varuṇa' (This to me, O Varuṇa) and 'tat tvā yāmi' (That I request of thee).
3.14.6: 'maruto yadd ha' (O Maruts, when indeed) and 'yūyam asmān' (You [protect] us).
3.14.7: 'hiraṇyagarbho yaḥ prāṇata' (The golden embryo who gave breath).
3.14.8: And they carry fire forward from the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
3.14.9: [Reciting] 'pra devam devyā' (Forth the god through the divine) — of the three [verses], [he recites] the first while seated.
3.14.10: The latter two while proceeding forward.
3.14.11: [Reciting] 'iḍāyās tvā' (Of Iḍā, thee) — while the two fire-sticks are being set down.
3.14.12: 'agne viśvebhiḥ' (O Agni, with all), 'svanīka' (Of beautiful appearance), 'sīda' (Sit), 'hotar' (O invoker), 'ni' (Down), 'hotā' (The invoker), 'tvam dūtaḥ' (Thou the messenger) —
3.14.13: these are the fire-carrying mantras.
3.14.14: And where, while seated, he recited the first [verse], there, standing up, [the fire] is released.
3.14.15: On the latter [altar], the <s>hotṛ</s>'s (invoker's) ritual action [is performed] at the <s>vedi</s>.
3.14.16: The <s>Kāya</s> (offering to Ka) [is made] in a low voice.
3.14.17: A pair of cattle (cow and bull) [is given as] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.
3.14.18: The <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) spreads the <s>veda</s> (sacred grass).
3.14.19: After the <s>Vāruṇī</s> [offering], with the concluding rite (<s>niṣkāsa</s>), he proceeds to the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) as in the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice].
3.14.20: [The mantras are:] 'urum hi rājā' (Wide indeed, O king) and 'śataṃ te' (A hundred for thee).
3.14.21: The rest is the same as the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.

body.translated_text:
3.15.1: The <s>Sākamedhas</s> (common offerings) [are performed] on the full-moon of <s>Kārttikī</s>, for the <s>Phālgunī</s> commencement.
3.15.2: On <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s>, for the <s>Caitrī</s> commencement.
3.15.3: An <s>iṣṭi</s> to <s>Agni Anīkavat</s> (Agni of the vanguard) [is performed] on the first full-moon day, in the forenoon.
3.15.4: [The mantras are:] 'anīkair dveṣo ardaya agne viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ | rayiṃ no dehi jīvase' (With thy vanguards crush enmity, O Agni, with all protections; give us wealth for living). [The dakṣiṇā is] an army commander (<s>sainānīka</s>).
3.15.5: At midday, [an offering] to the <s>Maruts Sāṃtapana</s> (the scorching Maruts).
3.15.8: 'agninā rayim' (Through Agni, wealth) and 'gayasphāna' (Increasing the household) — these are the <s>ājyabhāgas</s>.
3.15.9: [The mantras are:] 'gṛhamedhāsa ā gata' (Come, O lords of the house-sacrifice) and 'pra budhnyā vaḥ' (Forth from the depth to you).
3.15.10: 'tvāṃ citraśravastama' (Thee, O most famously glorious) and 'yad vāhiṣṭham' (What is best to convey) — these are for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
3.15.11: He does not recite the <s>nigada</s> (recitation formula).
3.15.12: He does not recite the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses.
3.15.13: The sacrificial acts from the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> onwards [are performed] ending with <s>Iḍā</s>.
3.15.14: Its concluding rite: in the morning, having offered a full ladle, [he performs] an <s>iṣṭi</s> to the <s>Maruts Krīḍin</s> (the playful Maruts).
3.15.15: [The mantra is:] 'krīḍaṃ vaḥ parvatāścit' (Your play [shakes] even mountains).
3.15.16: [This is] a <s>mahāhavis</s> (great oblation).
3.15.17: The <s>Varuṇa-praghāsa</s> procedures [apply] up to and including the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [offering].
3.15.18: [Then offerings] to <s>Mahendra</s> and to <s>Viśvakarman</s>.
3.15.19: [The mantras are:] 'vācas patim' (The lord of speech) and 'yā te dhāmāni paramāṇi' (Those highest abodes of thine).
3.15.18: The <s>Vaiśvakarmaṇa</s> (offering to Viśvakarman) [is also made] in a low voice.
3.15.21: And one fire is carried forward.
3.15.22: A bull [is given as] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.
3.15.23: There is no <s>vājina</s> (vitality formula) and no <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath).
3.15.24: The rest is the same as the <s>Varuṇa-praghāsas</s>.

body.translated_text:
3.16.1: In the afternoon, the ancestral (<s>pitrya</s>) three-oblation <s>iṣṭi</s>.
3.16.2: To <s>Soma Pitṛmat</s> (Soma associated with the fathers), or to the fathers who have Soma, to the fathers who sit on the sacred grass (<s>barhiṣad</s>), [and] to the fathers who are fire-consumed (<s>agniṣvātta</s>).
3.16.3: And <s>Agni Kavyavāhana</s> (Agni who conveys offerings to the ancestors) becomes the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> deity.
3.16.4: 'tvam soma pra cikitaḥ' (Thou, O Soma, hast perceived), 'somo dhenum' (Soma, the cow), 'tvam soma pitṛbhiḥ' (Thou, O Soma, with the fathers) — these are for <s>Soma Pitṛmat</s>.
3.16.5: 'udīratām aṅgiraso' (Let the Aṅgirasas arise) and 'ye naḥ pūrve' (Those who [came] before us) — for the fathers who have Soma.
3.16.6: 'upahūtā āhaṃ pitṝn barhiṣada' (Invoked have I the fathers who sit on the sacred grass) — for the <s>Barhiṣads</s>.
3.16.7: 'ava sṛja' (Release) and 'ye ca iha agniṣvāttāḥ' (And those fire-consumed ones here) — for the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>.
3.16.8: One <s>yājyā</s> each, and two <s>puronuvākyās</s> each [for the first two].
3.16.9: When [the offerings are] not continuous, [there are] separate <s>praṇavas</s> (oṃ recitations).
3.16.10: 'ye tātṛṣuḥ' (Those who thirsted) and 'tvam agna īḍitaḥ' (Thou, O Agni, art praised) — for <s>Agni Kavyavāhana</s>.
3.16.11: Wearing the sacred thread in the reversed manner (<s>prācīnāvītī</s>), he offers to these deities.
3.16.12: And he maintains [this arrangement] at the <s>nigama-sthānas</s> (places where the deity is named).
3.16.13: Omitting [the formula containing the word] 'pitṛmat' (associated with the fathers).
3.16.14: [But one should wear it as] <s>yajñopavītī</s> (in the normal sacrificial manner) — according to <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>.
3.16.15: In the directives (<s>sampraiṣa</s>), when the word <s>svadhā</s> is used, [one says] 'ye svadhāmahe svadhā namaḥ' (We who are svadhā; svadhā, homage) in place of 'ye yajāmahe' (we who sacrifice) and the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call.
3.16.16: They perform [the rite] in the enclosure south of the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern) fire.
3.16.17: The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> stands south of the altar, in front.
3.16.18: And [the priest] does not step upon the sacred grass.
3.16.19: The <s>japas</s> (whispered recitations) are [performed with] release.
3.16.20: The ritual acts [involving mantras are performed] silently, [as] whispered-mantra rites.
3.16.21: And [this applies] at the <s>upasad</s> (preliminary rite) also — according to the teachers.
3.16.22: But [silent performance for] the ritual act is the proper procedure.
3.16.23: Having recited 'uśanas tvā' (Uśanas, thee) — a single <s>sāmidhenī</s> verse thrice — he does not recite the <s>ārṣeya</s> (lineage formula).
3.16.24: Having performed the <s>prayājas</s> without sacred grass, [with the mantras:] 'iṣṭvā no agne sucetunā' (Having sacrificed, O Agni, with good thought) and 'tvam soma mahe bhagam' (Thou, O Soma, for great fortune) — these two, containing [the word for] 'living,' are the <s>ājyabhāgas</s>.
3.16.25: Having invoked <s>Iḍā</s>, they do not partake [of the offering].
3.16.26: Having smelled the portions, they cast them [away].
3.16.27: [The offering] is given to the fathers.

body.translated_text:
3.17.1: Murmuring "<s>Ayā viṣṭhā</s> — By this pervasion, generating deeds of praise, for he, the radiant one, [is] broad, the way for the chooser. He raised the foundation, the foremost of sweetness, when he set in motion his own body" — they go north of the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire.
3.17.2: [Reciting] "<s>Susaṃdṛśam tvā</s>" (You of beautiful appearance, we have seen; they delighted) and "<s>Upa ū ṣu śṛṇuhi</s>" (Now indeed listen), he reverences the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
3.17.3: With the triplet "<s>Mano nv ā huvāmahe</s>" (Now we invoke the mind), [he reverences] the southern fire.
3.17.4: They should say: "May the mind come back to me."
3.17.5: With the triplet "<s>Agnim tam manya</s>" (I consider that <s>Agni</s>) and the two-footed [verse] "<s>Agne tvam na</s>" (O <s>Agni</s>, you for us), [he reverences] the <s>Gārhapatya</s>.
3.17.6: Having reverenced <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) with "<s>Tat cakṣuḥ</s>" (That eye).
3.17.7: Having offered the two <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings) without the sacred grass.
3.17.8: In the <s>sūktavāka</s> (hymn of praise), he does not pronounce the name of the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer).
3.17.9: And [the rite concludes] with the <s>śamyā</s> (wooden pin).
3.17.10: Having concluded the <s>Tryambaka</s> [offerings], [there follows] the <s>caru</s> (cooked grain offering) for <s>Mitra</s>.
3.17.11: Or for <s>Aditi</s>.
3.17.12: "<s>Mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ</s>" — the great <s>Āditya</s>, upholder of peoples.
3.17.13: When [the sacrifice] is completed, [it is] the full-moon [rite].

body.translated_text:
3.18.1: Regarding the <s>Śunāsīrya</s> [rite].
3.18.2: The <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (all-gods) [offerings] end with [the offering] to <s>Pūṣan</s>.
3.18.3: In the <s>Śunāsīrya</s>, [there is] a milk offering for <s>Vāyu</s> and one for <s>Sūrya</s>.
3.18.4: [The verses are:] "<s>Śunā sīrāv imām</s>" (O <s>Śuna</s> and <s>Sīra</s>, [accept] this) and "<s>Śunam naḥ phālāḥ</s>" (May the ploughshares [bring] happiness to us).
3.18.5: [And:] "<s>Tava Vāyav ṛtaspate</s>" (Yours, O <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of <s>ṛta</s>) and "<s>Adhvaryavaś cakṛvāṃsaḥ</s>" (The <s>Adhvaryus</s> who have performed).
3.18.6: "<s>Taraṇir viśvadarśataḥ</s>" (The all-seeing crosser) and "<s>Divo rukma</s>" (The golden ornament of heaven).
3.18.7: The offering for <s>Sūrya</s> is [made] in a low voice (<s>upāṃśu</s>).
3.18.8: A white horse is the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).
3.18.9: Or a cow.
3.18.10: Or a plough with twelve yoke-animals.
3.18.11: Not a prize stallion.
3.18.12: The rest is the same as in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [rite].
3.18.13: It is a full-moon [rite], but [performed] when [the fire] is being churned.
3.18.14: [The verses are:] "May <s>Indra</s> and <s>Śunāsīrā</s> enrich this sacrifice for us; bestow embryos for our welfare. Into whom this entire world has entered, in whom delight and greatness are deposited — O <s>Śunāsīrā</s>, in accord with the seasons, accompanied by <s>Indra</s>, enjoy this oblation."
3.18.15: "Offer the oblation with the ladle to <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Śunāsīra</s>; may the wise one be pleased. Bring forward the ghee-rich oblations to him of bay horses, united; O <s>Indra</s>, in accord with the <s>Ṛbhus</s> and <s>Brahman</s>, O <s>Śunāsīrin</s>, enjoy this oblation."
3.18.16: "We invoke <s>Śuna</s>, [we who are] desiring horses."
3.18.17: Having sacrificed with the <s>Sākamedha</s> [rites], immediately [follows] the <s>Śunāsīrya</s>.
3.18.18: Or on the full-moon day of the month of <s>Māgha</s>.
3.18.19: The conclusion is with <s>Soma</s>, with an animal [offering], or with an <s>iṣṭi</s> (oblation).
3.18.20: Once in five years — on the first day the <s>Śunāsīrya</s>, on the second day the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.

body.translated_text:
3.19.1: For a procedural error, [there is] expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>).
3.19.2: For loss of the substance, [there is] substitution (<s>pratinidhi</s>).
3.19.3: [The expiatory oblations are:] "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>. O <s>Agni</s>, you are the <s>ayā</s> (uninjured) and the blameless; truth indeed are you, the <s>ayā</s>. Made with uninjured mind, being uninjured, you carry the oblation. Make a remedy for us with the <s>ayā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>" — these are the expiatory oblations for all errors.
3.19.4: The <s>Āhavanīya</s> [is the fire] for all oblations.
3.19.5: And the <s>juhū</s> (ladle) is the vessel.
3.19.6: Four ladlings (<s>caturgṛhīta</s>) in expiations.
3.19.7: The expiation [should follow] immediately after the error, for there is no proceeding to the next [act] when the error has not been removed.
3.19.8: And when a specific expiation is prescribed for certain errors, one should perform both — the general expiation and the specific one.
3.19.9: If the <s>Āhavanīya</s> goes out without having been removed [to safety], it should be re-established by a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; gold tied to <s>kuśa</s> grass is carried in front; silver [is given] when [the sun] has risen; a chosen gift is the sacrificial fee.
3.19.10: When the <s>Āhavanīya</s> follows [the <s>Gārhapatya</s> in going out], the re-establishment [is done] from the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and an <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering) to <s>Agni Jyotiṣmat</s> (the luminous).
3.19.11: [The verses are:] "<s>Ud agne śucayaḥ</s>" (Arise, O <s>Agni</s>, with flames) and "<s>Vi jyotiṣā</s>" (With light).
3.19.12: When the <s>Gārhapatya</s> follows [in going out], having first resolved upon the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, one should carry another [fire] forward and offer.
3.19.13: Or having placed [the fires] together, one should remove [them] northward.
3.19.14: When both follow [in going out], churning [of new fire is done] with the upper fire-drill from the <s>Gārhapatya</s> firebrand.
3.19.15: When no firebrand exists, having touched the fire-drills with ash, an <s>iṣṭi</s> to <s>Agni Tapasvat</s> (the austere), <s>Janadvat</s> (the people-possessing), and <s>Pāvakavat</s> (the purifying).
3.19.16: [The verses are:] "Come to us with austerity, O <s>Agni</s>, the purifier, among the people, with flame; to this well-praised [prayer] of mine. Come to us with austerity, O <s>Agni</s>, the purifying, shining among the people; placing our offerings among the gods."
3.19.17: Thus, when both [fires] have risen [gone out?] or both have set, or been lost by some other cause, one should produce [them] by the <s>agnyādheya</s> (fire-establishment) [procedure].

body.translated_text:
3.20.1: If the released <s>Agnihotrī</s> cow bellows, he should offer a handful of barley, [reciting] "<s>Sūyavasāt</s>" (from pasture).
3.20.2: If she sits down: [reciting] "From whatever fear you sit down, make us free from that fear; be gracious to all offspring; homage to <s>Rudra</s> the bountiful" — having raised her with a wet stick — [then] "The divine <s>Aditi</s> has risen; she has placed life in the lord of sacrifice, making a portion for <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Mitra</s>, and for <s>Varuṇa</s>" — thus he addresses [her] with the <s>mantra</s>.
3.20.3: Or he may give her to an enemy.
3.20.4: When the oblation is spilled: [reciting] "<s>Acchāyam vaḥ</s> — You by whose power the realms were fixed, most heroic by [your] heroisms, most mighty — who go unchecked by strength — O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, come, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, invoked first" — having brought [it] back with waters — [and] "The sacrifice has gone to heaven, to the gods, as a third; may wealth come to me from there. The sacrifice has gone to the atmosphere, to the ancestors, as a third; may wealth come to me from there. The sacrifice has gone to the earth, to humans, as a third; may wealth come to me from there" — thus he addresses [it] with the <s>mantra</s>.
3.20.5: What a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would refuse to eat — that is the mark of the spoiled [oblation].
3.20.6: Its remedy is water.
3.20.7: When a remainder exists, the completion [is done] with that.
3.20.8: In the absence of a remainder, one should produce another [oblation].
3.20.9: When that substance is unavailable, whatever one considers most similar, one should substitute that.
3.20.10: This is the rule for substitutions.
3.20.11: And there is no change of the words [of the mantras in case of substitution].
3.20.12: When the offering substance is spoiled before being given to the deity, there is no repetition of the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s [recitation]; having consecrated another oblation, one should offer it to the deity.
3.20.13: When the error [occurs] after the offering, there is no repetition; the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s>), the <s>Iḍā</s> (invocation), and the partaking portions are omitted.
3.20.14: Ghee [is used] for the subsequent [offerings].
3.20.15: When other deities have been offered to, or when [the offering is] spoiled, with a remainder in the ritual system, the offering is repeated.
3.20.16: The entire offering [is repeated] when there is no remainder.
3.20.17: What has been done is not repeated when there is loss of a subsidiary element.

body.translated_text:
3.21.1: In <s>iṣṭi</s> (oblation) offerings, <s>paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice), and <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], the <s>Brahmā</s> (priest) makes the expiatory oblation.
3.21.2: If the error is in the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, [he offers] "<s>Bhūḥ svāhā</s>" in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire.
3.21.3: If in the <s>Yajurveda</s>, "<s>Bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>" in the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire.
3.21.4: But in the <s>Soma</s> [sacrifice], in the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> fire.
3.21.5: If in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, "<s>Svaḥ svāhā</s>" in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
3.21.6: "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>" when the error is not identifiable.
3.21.7: When one has not reverenced [the fires] at the release [of the rite], one should reverence [them] in each direction.
3.21.8: When one has reverenced [them] but not at the release, [one does] as when returning from a journey.
3.21.9: When [the fires] have been placed together but not released, churning [of new fire is required].
3.21.10: There is no reverencing of the fire-drills.
3.21.11: One should not abandon the fires without offering or without performing a sacrifice.
3.21.12: But having performed the expiation, one should substitute for the rites that have been missed — one should substitute.

4.1.2: They should eat before the driving away of the calves.
4.1.3: [They may eat] anything other than meat, salt, sexual intercourse, and <s>māṣa</s> beans — and [they should not consume] the substance with which one is about to sacrifice.

body.translated_text:
4.2.1: One should add fuel to the fires (<s>anvādadhīta</s>) in <s>iṣṭi</s> (oblation) and <s>paśubandha</s> (animal-binding) rites on the previous day.
4.2.2: In the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, with the last of the great utterances (<s>mahāvyāhṛti</s>).
4.2.3: In the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, with the first [<s>mahāvyāhṛti</s>].
4.2.4: In the southern fire (<s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>), with the middle one.
4.2.5: And two [fuel-sticks] each, silently.
4.2.6: A tenth [fuel-stick] in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, with all [three <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>] combined.
4.2.7: Or, in place of the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>, four [verses] of <s>Vihavya</s> in sequence.
4.2.8: And the <s>upasthāna</s> (reverential approach) with the remainder.
4.2.9: With the seven [verses] beginning 'Drive away from us the burning sin' (<s>apa naḥ śośucad agham</s>), or with the ten [verses] 'O <s>Agni</s>, lead,' 'You who with heart,' 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, from below.'
4.2.10: And the <s>upasthāna</s> with the two <s>sūktas</s> (hymns) 'Forth for <s>Agni</s> [send] the voice' and 'This hymn.'
4.2.11: The <s>Prāgahīya</s> [procedure is performed] silently.
4.2.12: The <s>Paiṅgya</s> [procedure is performed] with the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>.
4.2.13: The <s>Kauṣītaka</s> [procedure is performed] with the <s>Vihavya</s> [verses].
4.2.14: The <s>Āruṇa</s> [procedure uses] the last [<s>mahāvyāhṛti</s>].

body.translated_text:
4.3.1: The <s>piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> (ancestral cake-offering) [is performed] in the afternoon on the new-moon day (<s>amāvāsyā</s>).
4.3.2: In front of the southern fire (<s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>), one arranges the winnowing basket (<s>śūrpa</s>), the pot (<s>sthālī</s>), the sacrificial sword (<s>sphya</s>), the ladle (<s>pātrī</s>), and the mortar and pestle (<s>ulūkhala-musala</s>).
4.3.3: Behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, one places the sacrificial sword on the southern sacred grass (<s>kuśa</s>).
4.3.4: Above, [one places] the rice grains in the ladle.
4.3.5: In front, [one places] the pot on the winnowing basket.
4.3.6: Bending the left knee, with lowered fist, he grasps the rice grains while meditating on the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>).
4.3.8: So that it should be cooked from below — having the wife hull [the grains] once, having cooked them in the southern fire, having sprinkled ghee, having removed [the pot] westward, having swept the offering area (<s>avasavi</s>), having strewn [grass] around, having sprinkled [water] around, bending the right knee, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (<s>yajñopavītī</s>), sitting facing north, he offers with the stirring spoon (<s>mekṣaṇa</s>).
4.4.1: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s> the bearer of offerings to the ancestors (<s>Kavyavāhana</s>); <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Soma</s> accompanied by the ancestors; <s>svāhā</s> to <s>Yama</s> accompanied by the <s>Aṅgirases</s> and the ancestors.'
4.4.2a: Having extended the stirring spoon, to the south of the southern fire [he recites]: 'Driven away are the <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Rakṣases</s> who sit on the <s>vedi</s>.' Having cleaned with the sacrificial sword and sprinkled [water]: 'Those who, assuming forms, being <s>Asuras</s>, roam about with <s>svadhā</s> (ancestral offerings); those who carry away [oblations] from the settlements and from the habitations — may <s>Agni</s> drive them away from this world.'
4.4.2b: Having thus placed the firebrand on the southern half of the cleaned [area], having placed once-cut <s>kuśa</s> grasses at the base on the cleaned [area], addressing the father by name: 'O so-and-so, wash yourself, and [wash] those who follow you here' — he pours water on the <s>kuśa</s> grasses with downward-turned palm.
4.4.3: Likewise, to the south, for the grandfather (<s>pitāmaha</s>).
4.4.4: And for the great-grandfather (<s>prapitāmaha</s>).
4.4.5: 'O so-and-so, this is for you, and for those who follow you here' — having thus placed the <s>piṇḍas</s> (rice-balls) as [water was] poured for washing.
4.4.6: Both [<s>piṇḍas</s>] on one [grass-bed] when there is a division of ancestors.
4.4.7: There is none for a living father.
4.4.8: Nor for one who has gone [but is still] living.
4.4.9: Either from those [ancestors] the father, [or] from those the son [inherits the rite].
4.4.10: Or [the rite extends] up to the end of the oblation.
4.4.11: 'Here, O ancestors, delight yourselves; according to your share, O ancestors, nourish yourselves.'
4.4.12: Turning around to the north.
4.4.13: Not touching [the <s>piṇḍas</s>] three times.
4.4.14: 'The ancestors have been delighted; according to their share, they have been nourished' — turning back.
4.4.15: Washing in the same manner.
4.5.1a: 'Homage to you, O Ancestors, for life; homage to you, O Ancestors, for heat; homage to you, O Ancestors, for fierceness; homage to you, O Ancestors, for essence; homage to you, O Ancestors, for strength; homage to you, O Ancestors, for death.'
4.5.1b: 'Homage to you, O Ancestors, for wrath; homage to you, O Ancestors, for <s>svadhā</s> (the ancestral offering). Homage to you, O Ancestors, O Ancestors, homage to you. You who are Ancestors of Ancestors here — may you be the best of those.'
4.5.1c: 'We who are the human Ancestors here — may we be the best of those. Whatever <s>svadhā</s> is yours, O Ancestors, may it be [ours]. Whatever nourishment is here for the Ancestors, may it be ours. O Ancestors, give us homes.'
4.5.2: 'This is your garment, O Ancestors; clothe yourselves, O Ancestors' — having laid down three threads.
4.5.3: 'Carrying nourishment, immortality, ghee, milk, sweet drink, filtered [<s>Soma</s>] — you are <s>svadhā</s>; satisfy our ancestors' — having poured out the remaining water.
4.5.4: Having smelled the <s>piṇḍas</s>.
4.5.5: Having set [them] down, one should eat.
4.5.6: Or one should give [them] to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
4.5.7: Or one should immerse [them] in water.
4.5.8: The wife desiring a son should eat the middle <s>piṇḍa</s>: 'O Ancestors, place the embryo, the boy wearing a lotus garland, so that here may be a man' — thus.
4.5.9: Having placed the firebrand in the fire.
4.5.10: Having offered the once-cut [grasses].
4.5.11: The <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-offering) is indeed rice gruel (<s>yavāgū</s>), [offered] evening and morning.
4.5.12: And the self-performed oblation on the <s>parvan</s> (juncture day).
4.5.13: By this very rule, the <s>piṇḍapitṛyajña</s> should be performed for one who has not established the [sacred] fires.

body.translated_text:
4.6.1: To the south is the regular [place for] the <s>Brahman</s> priest's ritual action.
4.6.2: But behind [the altar] in ancestral rites (<s>pitryā</s>).
4.6.3: The reversal is determined by the sacrificer.
4.6.4: The seat is in front of the sacrificer.
4.6.5: The removal of grass is the same as for the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
4.6.6: Likewise the sitting down.
4.6.7: At the beginning of a ritual and when there is a change of place.
4.6.8: The modification is [to face] eastward first.
4.6.9: '<s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the <s>Brahman</s>; may he protect the sacrifice, may he protect the lord of the sacrifice, may he protect me. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the divine <s>Brahman</s>; I am the human one. <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>, <s>oṃ</s>' — having thus sat down.
4.6.10: And he is the witness of all ritual actions.
4.6.11: Restraint of speech [is maintained] during [rites involving] <s>mantras</s>.
4.6.12: In all movements, they return by the same [path] as they went; otherwise, they return differently.
4.6.13: He follows along when the fire is being led forward.
4.6.14: The sitting down [is performed] together with the fuel-stick.
4.6.15: A horse [is the fee] for the <s>Brahman</s> at the establishment of the sacred fires (<s>Agnyādheya</s>).
4.6.16: Or [it applies] for all [priests].
4.6.17: Having been addressed for the authorization of the ritual act, having said '<s>oṃ</s>,' he authorizes [the continuation of] the ritual as appropriate.

body.translated_text:
4.7.1: Restraint of speech [is maintained] at the time of the <s>praṇītā</s> (sacred waters).
4.7.2: Release [from silence comes] at the <s>haviṣkṛt</s> (preparation of oblations).
4.7.3: And in the <s>iṣṭi</s> (oblation), release [comes] with the authorization of the after-offering (<s>anuyāja</s>) following the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (making-good-of-the-offering).
4.7.4: 'With the eye of <s>Mitra</s> I behold you' — having thus looked at the <s>prāśitra</s> (Brahman's portion).
4.7.5: 'By the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I receive [you]' — having thus received [it].
4.7.6: 'I seat you on the navel of the earth, in the lap of <s>Aditi</s>' — having placed the staff with its tip pointing east on the ground.
4.7.7: Having taken the <s>prāśitra</s> with the ring finger and thumb.
4.7.8: 'With the mouth of <s>Agni</s> I eat you' — having eaten without chewing.
4.7.9: 'You are peace (<s>śānti</s>)' — having sipped water.
4.7.10: He touches the sense organs.
4.7.11: 'You are the protector of <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath); protect my <s>prāṇa</s>' — [touching] the nostrils and mouth.
4.7.12: 'You are the protector of sight; protect my sight' — [touching] the eyes.
4.7.13: 'You are the protector of hearing; protect my hearing' — [touching] the ears.
4.7.14: 'I seat you in the belly of <s>Indra</s>' — [touching] the navel.
4.7.13: 'You are the protector of hearing; protect my hearing' — [touching] the ears.
4.7.14: 'I seat you in the belly of <s>Indra</s>' — [touching] the navel.
4.7.15: 'Who gave? To whom did he give? Desire (<s>Kāma</s>) gave; to Desire he gave. <s>Kāma</s> is the giver; <s>Kāma</s> is the receiver. O <s>Kāma</s>, this is yours' — having thus received the <s>anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering).
4.7.16: He is addressed: 'O <s>Brahman</s>, I shall depart.'
4.7.17: 'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, they declare this sacrifice of yours for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the <s>Brahman</s>. By that, protect the sacrifice; by that, protect the lord of the sacrifice; by that, protect me. Impelled by the god <s>Savitṛ</s>' — having murmured [this], he authorizes: '<s>Oṃ</s>, proceed.'
4.7.18: The release of the <s>Brahman</s> [occurs] when the <s>praṇītā</s> waters are released.
4.7.19: And the eating of the <s>Brahman</s>'s share.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 4.8.1: 'With undeceived eye I look upon you, for the increase of wealth, for having good offspring, for having good heroes. You are the tongue of <s>Agni</s>, a good invoker. Be for me abode after abode for the gods, sacrifice after sacrifice' — thus the wife looks upon the ghee (<s>ājya</s>).
ŚŚS 4.8.2: 'You are radiance; you are brightness; you are immortality; you are belonging to all the gods' — [thus says] the sacrificer when [the offerings] have been placed on the <s>vedi</s> (altar).
ŚŚS 4.8.3a: 'They have sat firm in the womb of truth (<s>ṛta</s>), in the world of merit. O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, protect — protect the sacrifice, protect the lord of the sacrifice' — having touched the offerings that have been placed nearby. 'Protect me, the sacrificing one' — [touching] himself.
ŚŚS 4.8.3: 'You are the rain; cut away my sins. You are knowledge; know my sin' — having sipped water. 'O <s>Agni</s>, lord of observances, I shall perform the observance; may I be able to do it; may it succeed for me. Herewith I go from untruth to truth' — having placed a fuel-stick on the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, he restrains his speech.

body.text:
ŚŚS_4.8.5: yat.kāmo.vā.syāt /
ŚŚS_4.8.6: anupadasyam.anna.adyam.āpnavāni.ity.ākāśam.samudram.vā /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 4.8.5: Or whatever [other] desire he may have.
ŚŚS 4.8.6: 'May I obtain food that does not fall away' — [gazing at] the sky or the ocean.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 4.9.1: 'May <s>Indra</s> bestow this great power (<s>indriya</s>) upon us; may the bountiful lords accompany us with wealth. May our blessings be [fulfilled]; may our blessings be true' — [this is recited] when the <s>Iḍā</s> is being invoked.
ŚŚS 4.9.2: 'O <s>Bradhna</s> (tawny one, the sun), swell forth! Protect my breath; protect my offspring; protect my cattle. Yield for me the sacred power (<s>brahman</s>); yield for me the ruling power (<s>kṣatra</s>); yield for me the people (<s>viś</s>). You are the arrangement of the quarters; may the quarters be arranged for me; may the quarters be arranged — in those arranged [quarters] may I prosper. Here, O ancestors, delight yourselves; according to your share, O ancestors, be satisfied' — having touched the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) placed on the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass).
ŚŚS 4.9.3: 'The ancestors have been delighted; according to their share they have been satisfied' — having placed [it] back.
ŚŚS 4.9.4: 'You are the share of <s>Prajāpati</s>; you are full of nourishment, full of milk; you are imperishable — do not perish for me, in the other world and here' — having touched the <s>anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering).
ŚŚS 4.9.5: When the after-offerings (<s>anuyājas</s>) have been offered, having separated the two ladles: 'I have followed the success of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Agni-Soma</s>; by the impulse of <s>Vāja</s> (strength) I push forward' — with the right hand face-up, [he pushes] the <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) forward; 'May <s>Agni</s> and <s>Agni-Soma</s> push away him who hates us and whom we hate; by the impulse of <s>Vāja</s> I push him away' — with the left hand face-down, [he pushes] the <s>upabhṛt</s> (under-ladle) backward.
ŚŚS 4.9.6: According to the deity in other [cases].
ŚŚS 4.9.7: When [the offering] is not for the householder, [he offers] in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> with the <s>sruva</s> (small ladle).

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 4.10.1a: 'That share of nourishment which the gods have arranged for you two, O hundred-powered ones — with that I gratify you two; be satisfied with it. <s>Ahāha</s>, <s>Ahuhū</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>! To the two <s>Gandharvas</s>, the two <s>Nārīṣṭā</s> goddesses, <s>Ahāha</s> and <s>Ahuhū</s> — <s>Svāhā</s>!'
ŚŚS 4.10.1b: 'O <s>Agni</s>, lord of the earth; O <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of the atmosphere; O <s>Savitṛ</s>, lord of impulses; O <s>Sūrya</s>, lord of the stars; O <s>Soma</s>, lord of the plants; O <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, lord of the forms of the fuel-sticks; O <s>Mitra</s>, lord of truths; O <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of ordinances; O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the foremost — O <s>Prajāpati</s>, lord of creatures — O gods, stride forth among the gods!'
ŚŚS 4.10.2: 'Stride forth among the second ones' — thus, increasing by one each time, for eleven [repetitions].
ŚŚS 4.10.3: 'All the gods, thirty-three...'

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 4.11.1: 'May the <s>Dhruvā</s> (the permanent ladle) swell with the oblation of ghee, sacrifice after sacrifice, for the divine worship. The udder of the sun-goddess, the lap of <s>Aditi</s>, the broad stream, the earth — in this sacrifice' — thus he fills the <s>Dhruvā</s>.
ŚŚS 4.11.2: He holds on [to the ladle] while the <s>samiṣṭayajus</s> (concluding formula) is being offered.
ŚŚS 4.11.3: 'Being [present] in the assembly, may you be for me. You are the whole; may you be the whole for me. You are fullness; may you be fullness for me. You are imperishable; do not perish for me, in the other world and here' — having touched the full vessel, he shakes [drops] toward the quarters.
ŚŚS 4.11.4: 'With the eastern quarter, together with the gods, may the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) purify. With the southern quarter, together with the months, may the ancestors purify. With the western quarter, together with the houses, may the cattle purify. With the upward quarter, together with the sacrifice, the year, and the lord of the sacrifice, may they purify...'

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 4.12.1: From the southern hip-area of the <s>vedi</s>, [facing] the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
ŚŚS 4.12.2: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth in heaven with the <s>Jagatī</s> meter — I stride forth following him. From that may he who hates us and whom we hate be excluded' — having lifted the right foot first, [placing] the left foot lower.
ŚŚS 4.12.3: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth in the atmosphere with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter' — the second [stride].
ŚŚS 4.12.4: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth on the earth with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter' — the third [stride].
ŚŚS 4.12.5: '<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode forth in the quarters with the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter' — he strides sideways.
ŚŚS 4.12.6: The conclusion is the same [for all].
ŚŚS 4.12.7: 'We have gone to the sun (heaven)' — he looks toward the east.
ŚŚS 4.12.8: 'We have become united with the light' — [facing] the <s>Āhavanīya</s>.
ŚŚS 4.12.9: [He continues] thus...

body.translated_text: 4.13.1a: 'He who hates us from afar, he who hates us from near, whether a kinsman or a stranger, O <s>Agni</s> — of him, blazing like kindling wood, do not leave any remainder' — having placed the coals of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> together while they are scattering. 4.13.1b: He mutters the <s>tṛca</s> (triplet of verses) 'O <s>Agni</s>, rich in cattle.' 4.13.1c: 'Upward [we look]; that eye; may I not be cut off from your sight; whatever is your splendor (<s>tapas</s>), may I not be cut off from that' — having worshipped <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), turning back in the same way, sitting down with a leftward turn. 4.13.1d: 'May this oblation be my procreation, with ten heroes, with the entire group, for well-being — [may there be] attainment of self, attainment of offspring, attainment of freedom from fear, attainment of cattle, attainment of worlds. May <s>Agni</s> make abundant offspring for me; place food, milk, and seed in us' — thus one desiring progeny partakes of the milk offering. 4.13.2: 'Of <s>Dadhikrāvan</s> I have sung' — or, one desiring prosperity [partakes of] the curd offering. 4.13.3: 'May the lord of the sacrifice [be united] with blessings' — he eats the sacrificer's portion. 4.13.4: Together with the concluding <s>yajus</s> formula, he offers while departing.

body.translated_text: 4.14.1: [These are] the rites for [one who has] died. 4.14.2: If [he dies] while [a sacrifice] is incomplete, [with the intention of] departing — with death as the end — in one-day [rites] there is no completion of that. 4.14.3: Having offered all the oblations in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire. 4.14.4: Having collected the hair and nails of the deceased. 4.14.5: Having bathed [the body] and adorned it. 4.14.6: In the southern direction, on ground sloping southward, or on ground sloping south-eastward. 4.14.7: 'Depart, go away' — wiping [the ground] with a <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) branch. 4.14.8: Scraping with the wooden sword (<s>sphya</s>) and sprinkling. 4.14.9: Having made the funeral pyre facing east-southward. 4.14.10: Placing the <s>Āhavanīya</s> in front, the <s>Gārhapatya</s> behind, and the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) to the south. 4.14.11: Having carried [the body] between the <s>Gārhapatya</s> and the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>. 4.14.12: Laying [the body] face-up on the pyre. 4.14.13: To the south or behind, tying a cow for strewing (<s>anustaraṇī</s>), or a reddish she-goat, facing south. 4.14.14: From a living or slaughtered [animal], extracting the two kidneys from the back. 4.14.15: Having warmed them on the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern fire), 'Run over!' — with the two <s>ṛc</s> verses, placing [them] in the hands. 4.14.16: Placing gold fragments at the seats of the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>). 4.14.17: 'The armor of <s>Agni</s>' — covering the face with the omentum (<s>vapā</s>). 4.14.18: The <s>juhū</s> (offering ladle) in the right hand. 4.14.19: The <s>upabhṛt</s> (secondary ladle) in the left. 4.14.20: The <s>dhruvā</s> (fixed ladle) on the chest. 4.14.21: The <s>Agnihotra</s> ladle at the throat. 4.14.22: The two <s>sruvas</s> (small ladles) at the nostrils. 4.14.23: The <s>prāśitraharaṇa</s> (vessel for the fore-portion) at the right ear. 4.14.24: The <s>praṇītāpraṇayana</s> (vessel for the consecrated waters) at the left. 4.14.25: The potsherds (<s>kapāla</s>) on the head. 4.14.26: The pressing stones (<s>grāvāṇas</s>) in the water [vessel]. 4.14.27: The <s>samavattadhānī</s> (storage vessel) on the belly. 4.14.28: The two dishes (<s>pātryau</s>) at the sides. 4.14.29: The wooden sword (<s>sphya</s>) at the right side. 4.14.30: The black antelope skin at the left. 4.14.31: The fire-sticks (<s>araṇī</s>) on the lap. 4.14.32: The mortar and pestle on the thighs and knees. 4.14.33: The winnowing basket and cart at the feet. 4.14.34: Around [are placed] the <s>Agnihotra</s> vessels. 4.14.35: Having filled those with ghee and mixed ghee (<s>pṛṣadājya</s>). 4.14.36: 'This one is indeed from you; you are from this one; this is your womb, you are his womb. O <s>Jātavedas</s>, carry him to where is the world of the meritorious. This one indeed begot you; may he be born again from you. To him, <s>svāhā</s>' — they pile up with the fires.

body.translated_text: 4.15.1: 'O <s>Agni</s>, do not [burn] him' — when it is well-kindled, having muttered ten [verses], turning leftward, not looking back, they walk away northward-eastward. 4.15.2: 'The step of death' — he pronounces the blessing with the two [verses]. 4.15.3: 'O waters, you indeed' [and] 'pure, and <s>Soma</s>' — they touch water with the two hymns, not submerging, not washing. 4.15.4: 'O so-and-so, this is yours' — having offered one handful of water. 'O waters, [protect] us' — stepping out. Having put on a new garment. 'That eye' — having worshipped <s>Āditya</s>. The youngest first, they return. 4.15.5: Having placed <s>dūrvā</s> grass, barley, and mustard seeds in a water vessel, placing [them] on moist cow-dung, they touch 'with stones' — the anointed stone, the fire, and the water vessel. 4.15.6: Sleeping on the ground, eating sacrificial food, and reversing [the order of] rites except for the fire-ritual — for one night, three nights, or nine nights, or until the bone-gathering — these are the observances. 4.15.7: 'One should not extend the days of impurity' — thus <s>Kauṣītaki</s> used to say. 4.15.8a: In the dark fortnight, having piled [the bones], on odd-numbered nights — 'you whom, O <s>Agni</s>' — with the two [verses], having cooled the bones with water mixed with milk. Having placed the bodily remains in an old pot. 4.15.8: 'I prop you up' — covering with a clod of earth. 'Rise up' — burying in a pit. 'Rising up' — placing in a measured [spot]. They bury [it] in the wilderness. 4.15.9: When the bodily remains are not visible, [they use] three hundred and sixty <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) leaf-stalks. 4.15.10: Their placement is [as follows]: 4.15.11: Forty on the head. 4.15.12: Ten on the neck. 4.15.13: A hundred on the shoulders and arms. 4.15.14: Thirty on the chest. 4.15.15: Twenty on the belly. 4.15.16: Six on the testicles. 4.15.17: Four on the penis. 4.15.18: A hundred on the thighs. 4.15.19: Thirty on the knees, shins, and kneecaps. 4.15.20: Twenty on the toes. 4.15.21: Thus there are three hundred and sixty. 4.15.22: Having made [them] in the shape of a person, wrapping with woolen threads, coating with barley flour, anointing with ghee, they perform [the rites] with the fires. 4.15.23: If desired, having cremated a previously deceased wife with the fires — or with the <s>sāṃtapana</s> [fire] — having brought another [wife], he should then re-establish the fires.

body.translated_text: 4.16.1: Upon the completion of the observance, [there is] the <s>paridhi</s> rite (enclosure ceremony). 4.16.2: Having spread a bull's hide, reddish, with neck facing north or east, with hair upward, behind the fire — they sit down; or [on] <s>kuśa</s> grasses arranged with tips in the same way. 4.16.3: Between the fire and these [persons], having placed an anointed stone — having made the <s>śamī</s> (Prosopis) wood [into] enclosing sticks, and <s>śamī</s> or <s>palāśa</s> wood [as] fuel — he offers with a <s>vāraṇa</s> (warding) ladle, or a bronze one. 4.16.4: [The ladle is] placed on the lap, while they are holding onto [each other]. 4.16.5: 'This [rite is] for the living. May death depart; may immortality come to me. May <s>Vaivasvata</s> (Yama) make freedom from fear for us. Like the leaf of a tree, may wealth fall upon us. May the lord of <s>Śacī</s> (Indra) be with us. And those ten in the dawn-colored [flames]' — [the verses for] the re-establishment. 4.16.6: Having offered twelve [oblations]. 4.16.6: 'As the days' — looking at the right shoulder with the two [verses]. Having mixed collyrium with ghee. With <s>kuśa</s> grasses he anoints the eyes of the women: 'Come, O women' — once with each <s>mantra</s>, twice silently. 4.16.7: 'Arise, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>' — with the two [verses], he pronounces the blessing as they rise, holding the right arm of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. 4.16.8: Or [they hold] the tail of a bull. 4.16.9: A bull, a new garment, and a bronze [vessel] are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). 4.16.10: 'Turn back your wealth from the south' — with the hymn, going around from left to right three times against [the direction of the funeral]. 4.16.11: In [the ceremony for one who dies] away from home, [the same] <s>paridhi</s> rite [applies].

body.translated_text:
4.17.1: One sacrifices to <s>Rudra</s> with a cow for well-being.
4.17.2: They call it <s>Śūlagava</s> (the impaled bull).
4.17.3: Having fasted during the bright fortnight, under the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation, in the northeast direction.
4.17.4: Having churned fire, he carries it forward eastward.
4.17.5: He plants a branch of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) with its leaves to the east.
4.17.6: He stations the animal to the north of that [branch].
4.17.7: "I prepare you, pleasing to <s>Rudra</s>."
4.17.8: "I sprinkle you, pleasing to <s>Rudra</s>."
4.17.9: "I yoke you, pleasing to <s>Rudra</s>."
4.17.10: Having carried [the animal] around the fire, they lead it northward.
4.17.11: They suffocate it with its head facing east, feet facing north — or with its head facing west, feet facing north — while it is not bellowing.
4.17.12: "If the animal made a cry, or struck [its] chest with [its] feet — may <s>Agni Jātavedas</s> release me from that sin, <s>svāhā</s>" — he offers [this] when [the animal] bellows.
4.17.13: Having extracted the omentum, washed it, cooked it on the first fire, anointed it with ghee, removed it, and sprinkled [it] three times [saying] "<s>Śivam śivam</s>" (Auspicious, auspicious), he offers the ghee oblations.

body.translated_text:
4.18.1: [First oblation:] "She who crosswise does not fall — I [am] the supporter. I yoke her, the contestant, with a stream of ghee. <s>Svāhā</s>."
4.18.2: "He whose is all this — him we invoke. May he, the lord of desires, grant me my wishes. <s>Svāhā</s>" — the second [oblation].
4.18.3: "O <s>Agni</s>, lord of the earth" — the third.
4.18.4: "O <s>Prajāpati</s>" — the fourth.
4.18.5a: Having pierced three middle leaves of <s>palāśa</s> and spread [them as a bed], having placed the omentum and anointed it: "Over as many as I rule, as many as are my ministers — for them I venerate you, O god; for them be gracious to us, O god."
4.18.5: "I know your father, I know your mother — heaven is your father, earth your mother. To you, O god, to <s>Bhava</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Paśupati</s>, to the fierce god, to the great god, to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Īśāna</s>, to the thunderbolt, <s>svāhā</s>" — having offered the omentum, he casts in the <s>palāśa</s> leaves.
4.18.6: And the two omentum-cooking [sticks].
4.18.7: Having offered the subsequent ghee oblation [saying] "To the visible one, to the reflected one, <s>svāhā</s>," he sprinkles in the same way.
4.18.8: He cooks a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked porridge) on the western fire.
4.18.9: The cut portions [are placed] to the north.
4.18.10: Having combined the <s>sthālīpāka</s>, broth, meat, and ghee, having sprinkled three times [saying] "<s>Śamyoḥ śamyoḥ</s>" (For peace, for peace), he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_4.19.1: bhavāya.svāhā.śarvāya.svāhā.rudrāya.svāhā.īśānāya.svāhā.agnaye.sviṣṭakṛte.svāhā.iti /

ŚŚS_4.19.8: āghoṣiṇyaḥ.pratighoṣiṇyaḥ.saṃghośiṇyo.vicinvatyaḥ.śvasanāḥ.kravyāda.eṣa.vo.bhāgas.tam.juṣadhvam.svāhā.iti /
ŚŚS_4.19.9: yajamānaś.ca.upatiṣṭhate /
body.translated_text:
4.19.1: [He offers:] "To <s>Bhava</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Śarva</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Rudra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, <s>svāhā</s>."
4.19.2: He sprinkles in the same manner.
4.19.3: Combining those same [substances].
4.19.4: In the western fire.
4.19.5: [He offers:] "To <s>Bhavānī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Śarvāṇī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Rudrāṇī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Īśānānī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Agnāyī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>."
4.19.6: The sprinkling is the same.
4.19.7: Having cut six <s>palāśa</s> leaves and placed them northeast, having placed on them refuse mixed with blood, he dedicates [them] to the hosts of <s>Rudra</s>.
4.19.8: [He says:] "O clamoring ones, responding ones, resounding ones, seeking ones, sighing ones, flesh-eating ones — this is your share; enjoy it, <s>svāhā</s>."
4.19.9: And the <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer) reverences [the fire].

ŚŚS_4.20.5: palāśa.śākhā.iti.devatāyai.vapām.devatāyai.haviḥ.sviṣṭakṛte.ca.anyeṣām.paśūnām /
ŚŚS_4.20.6: āgneyaḥ.saumyaś.ca.ājya.bhāgau.devatāyai.vapām.devatāyai.haviḥ.sviṣṭakṛte.ca.ājya.āhutiś.ca.anumataye.sthālī.pākānām /
body.translated_text:
4.20.1a: [He recites:] "O lord of beings, lord of existence, lord of the world, lord of creatures, lord of all creatures, lord of the great being, be gracious to us, to our two-footed and four-footed cattle; be gracious to us, to both the two-footed and the four-footed. He who hates us and whom we hate — you are hard to fill, [yet] you are a shade, by your own authority."
4.20.1: "Your bow is [your] heart, [your] mind is [your] arrows, [your] eye is [your] discharge. I know you thus. Homage to you. May <s>Soma</s> protect you. Do not harm me. Like two wolves that roam in the forest, snapping their jaws — homage to the two sons of <s>Mahādeva</s>, to <s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>."
4.20.2: [He recites] the hymns "<s>Kad Rudrāya</s>" (What to <s>Rudra</s>), "<s>Imā Rudrāya</s>" (These to <s>Rudra</s>), "<s>Te pitar</s>" (O father), "<s>Imā Rudrāya sthiradhanvane</s>" (These to <s>Rudra</s> of the firm bow).
4.20.3: A chosen [item] is the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).
4.20.4: The preparatory offering, the sprinkling, and the carrying of fire around — these are the recurrent [procedures] from the <s>Paśubandha</s> (animal sacrifice).
4.20.5: The <s>palāśa</s> branch, the omentum for the deity, the oblation for the deity, and [the offering] for <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> — [this applies] for other animals.
4.20.6: The ghee portions for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, the omentum for the deity, the oblation for the deity, the [offering] for <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, and a ghee oblation for <s>Anumatī</s> — [this is the rule] for the <s>sthālīpāka</s> offerings.

ŚŚS_4.21.25: kūrcaḥ.pādyam.arghyam.ācamanīyam.madhu.parko.gaur.iti.vedayeta.vedayeta /
body.translated_text:
4.21.1: Six [persons] are worthy of the <s>arghya</s> (honorific reception): the teacher, the officiating priest, the father-in-law, the king, the <s>snātaka</s> (one who has completed Vedic study), and a dear [person].
4.21.2: Facing north or east, [he recites:] "I [am like] the sun among those of equal stature, like lightning. I stand upon this one who attacks us" — he sits or stands on the <s>kūrca</s> (grass bundle).
4.21.3: Having received the foot-washing water, [he says:] "You are the milking of <s>Virāj</s>; may I obtain the milking of <s>Virāj</s>; may the milking of <s>Virāj</s> come to me."
4.21.4: Being told "<s>Arghya</s>" (the honor-water), he accepts the water.
4.21.5: Being told "<s>Ācamanīya</s>" (sipping water), he sips three times, once with each of the three [verses beginning] "<s>Āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>" (You are indeed the waters).
4.21.6: Being told "<s>Madhuparka</s>" (honey-mixture), he waits as for the tasting portion.
4.21.7: He accepts it thus; the variation is: "for fame, for the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>."
4.21.8: Having accepted [the <s>madhuparka</s>], placing it in the left hand, with the thumb and ring finger, having scooped from the front half, he smears [it] on the front half of the bronze [vessel, saying:] "May the <s>Vasus</s> with <s>Agni</s> as king partake of you."
4.21.9: "May the ancestors with <s>Yama</s> as king partake of you" — from the right half, onto the right half.
4.21.10: "May the <s>Ādityas</s> with <s>Varuṇa</s> as king partake of you" — from the rear half, with the rear half.
4.21.11: "May the <s>Rudras</s> with <s>Indra</s> as king partake of you" — from the front half, onto the front half.
4.21.12: "May the <s>Viśvedevas</s> with <s>Prajāpati</s> as king partake of you" — from the middle, upward.
4.21.13: Once each with the <s>mantra</s>, twice each silently.
4.21.14: Having tasted with the three <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances), one at a time.
4.21.15: The fourth without tasting.
4.21.16: The remainder is given to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
4.21.17: Or [the guest may] drink it all.
4.21.18: [Then] the swallowing down of water.
4.21.19: Having touched the chest with the four [verses beginning] "<s>Śam no devī</s>" (May the divine [waters] be auspicious for us).
4.21.20: The touching of the breath [organs] is the same.
4.21.21: And the wiping of the face.
4.21.22: Silence until the mention of the cow.
4.21.23: When told "[Here is] a cow," he assents with "<s>Om</s>."
4.21.24: Having murmured "<s>Mātā Rudrāṇām</s>" (Mother of the <s>Rudras</s>), [he says] "Release [her]; let her eat grass."
4.21.25: The <s>kūrca</s>, the foot-washing, the <s>arghya</s>, the sipping water, the <s>madhuparka</s>, the cow — thus he announces, thus he announces.

body.translated_text:
5.1.1: One who is about to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s> selects as his officiating priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) young men of known seer-lineage who are learned [in the Vedas].
5.1.2: Four, or all [of them].
5.1.3: "The moon is my divine <s>Brahmā</s> (priest)" — softly; "you are the human [one]" — aloud.
5.1.4: Similarly for all.
5.1.5: "<s>Āditya</s> is my divine <s>Udgātṛ</s>; you are the human [one]."
5.1.6: "<s>Agni</s> is my divine <s>Hotṛ</s>; you are the human [one]."
5.1.7: "<s>Vāyu</s> is my divine <s>Adhvaryu</s>; you are the human [one]."
5.1.8: "<s>Prajāpati</s> is my divine <s>Sadasya</s> (assembly member); you are the human [one]."
5.1.9: "The seasons are my divine <s>Hotrāśaṃsins</s> (assistant chanters); you are the human [ones]."
5.1.10: "Speak splendor for me, speak blessedness for me, speak prosperity for me, speak beauty for me, speak fame for me. In me [may there be] splendor, in me blessedness, in me prosperity, in me beauty, in me fame" — having murmured this upon being chosen, having asked "Are you perhaps one who has abandoned a day-sequence sacrifice, one dismissed [from priestly office], or one whose sacrificial fee has been taken away?" — he accepts or declines.

body.text:
ŚŚS_5.2.1: prācīna.pravaṇam.deva.yajanam /
ŚŚS_5.2.2: prāg.udak.pravaṇam.yajña.kāmasya /

ŚŚS_5.2.4: śuddha.pakṣe.dīkṣā.puṇye.nakṣatre.samāpanam.ca /
body.translated_text:
5.2.1: The place of worship of the gods should slope toward the east.
5.2.2: For one desiring [success in] sacrifice, [the ground should slope] toward the east and north.
5.2.3: Where the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker), while reciting, can see the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, the sun, and the waters — that [place is suitable] for one desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>).
5.2.4: The consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) [should be] in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), and the completion [should also be on such a day].

body.translated_text:
5.3.1: In the afternoon, the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration) <s>iṣṭi</s> — a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> (offering to Viṣṇu).
5.3.2: [This is] a modification of the full-moon [sacrifice].
5.3.3: With fifteen <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses.
5.3.4: The oblation [is offered] in a low voice.
5.3.5: [The verses for] the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> are in <s>Virāj</s> meter.
5.3.6: Or the regular ones [are used].
5.3.7: [The formula is:] 'upahūto 'yam yajamāno 'sya yajñasya āgura udṛcam aśīya' (Invoked is this sacrificer; may I partake of the surplus and overflow of this sacrifice) — thus he wishes. 'āśāsta' (he wished) — this [formula] replaces the [regular formula] at the <s>Iḷā</s>, the <s>sūktavāka</s>, and before the third-pressing rites.

body.text:
ŚŚS_5.4.1: adhvayurm.anvārabhya.udagrabhaṇāni.juhvatam.yajamānam.mano.me.manasā.dīkṣatām.vān.me.vācā.dīkṣatām.prāṇo.me.prāṇena.dīkṣatām.cakṣur.me.cakṣuṣā.dīkṣatām.śrotram.me.śrotreṇa.dīkṣatām.iti /
ŚŚS_5.4.2: āhutīr.vā.juhuyāt /
ŚŚS_5.4.3: eka.dīkṣe.ca.upasthānam /
ŚŚS_5.4.4: mano.dīkṣām.upaimi.ity.āhavanīyam /
ŚŚS_5.4.5: vācam.dīkṣām.upaimi.iti.gārhapatyam /
ŚŚS_5.4.6: prāṇam.dīkṣām.upaimi.iti.dakṣiṇa.agnim /
ŚŚS_5.4.7: aparimitā.dīkṣās.tāsām.apavarge.prāyaṇīyā.iṣṭiḥ /
body.translated_text:
5.4.1: The <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest), having the sacrificer hold on [to him] while offering oblations taken with upward scooping [speaks]: 'mano me manasā dīkṣatām' (May my mind be consecrated through mind), 'vān me vācā dīkṣatām' (May my speech be consecrated through speech), 'prāṇo me prāṇena dīkṣatām' (May my breath be consecrated through breath), 'cakṣur me cakṣuṣā dīkṣatām' (May my sight be consecrated through sight), 'śrotraṃ me śrotreṇa dīkṣatām' (May my hearing be consecrated through hearing).
5.4.2: Or he may offer [these as individual] oblations.
5.4.3: And [there is] a reverencing [of the fires] at each [individual] consecration.
5.4.4: 'mano dīkṣām upaimi' (I approach the consecration of mind) — [reverencing] the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
5.4.5: 'vācaṃ dīkṣām upaimi' (I approach the consecration of speech) — [reverencing] the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire.
5.4.6: 'prāṇaṃ dīkṣām upaimi' (I approach the consecration of breath) — [reverencing] the <s>Dakṣiṇa</s> fire.

body.translated_text:
5.5.1: [He offers] to <s>Pathyā Svasti</s> (Auspicious Path), <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Savitṛ</s> with ghee; and to <s>Aditi</s> with a rice dish (<s>caru</s>).
5.5.2: [The mantras are:] 'svasti naḥ pathyāsu' (Welfare for us on the paths) and 'svastir iddhi' (May there be welfare). 'agne naya' (O Agni, lead) and 'agne tvam pāraya' (O Agni, carry across). 'tvam soma pra cikitaḥ' (Thou, O Soma, hast perceived) and 'yā te dhāmāni haviṣā' (Those abodes of thine, with an oblation). 'tat savitur vareṇyam' (That choiceworthy [splendor] of Savitṛ) and 'ya imā viśvā jātāni' (He who [created] all these beings). 'sutrāmāṇam' (The good protector) and 'mahīm ū ṣu' (The great one, indeed).
5.5.3: With fifteen <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses.
5.5.4: The oblation [is offered] in a low voice.
5.5.5: There are no <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (ghee portions).
5.5.6: 'tvāṃ citraśravastama' (Thee, O most famously glorious) and 'yad vāhiṣṭham' (What is best to convey) [are for the sviṣṭakṛt].

body.translated_text:
5.6.1: Having purchased the king [Soma] and placed [him] on the cart — [the formula] 'somāya paryuhyamāṇāya' (To Soma being conveyed around) has been stated.
5.6.2: [Reciting] 'bhadrād abhi śreyaḥ prehi' (From the auspicious, go forth to the better), 'bṛhaspatiḥ pura etā te astu' (May Bṛhaspati be thy foremost guide), 'atha īm avasya vara ā pṛthivyāḥ' (Then [acquire] the choicest on the broad earth), 'āre śatrūn kṛṇuhi sarvavīraḥ' (Keep enemies far away, O all-heroic one) — standing between the two cart-tracks, having recited [these].
5.6.3: [Reciting] 'imāṃ dhiyam' (This meditation), 'śikṣamāṇasya' (Of the striving one), 'vaneṣu' (In the forests), 'vyantarikṣam' (Through the atmosphere), 'soma yāsi' (O Soma, thou goest) — these four [he recites] while walking between the two cart-tracks.
5.6.4: Having stationed the cart in front of the hall...

body.translated_text:
5.7.1: The <s>Ātithya</s> (hospitality) <s>iṣṭi</s> is a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> (offering to Viṣṇu).
5.7.2: [This is] a modification of the full-moon [sacrifice].
5.7.3: [The mantras are:] 'viṣṇor nu kam' (Of Viṣṇu indeed) and 'pra tad viṣṇuḥ' (Forth that Viṣṇu).
5.7.4: 'hotāram citraratham' (The invoker of the brilliant chariot) and 'yas tvā svaśva' (He who, with good horses, [approaches] thee) — these are for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
5.7.5: And the fire-churning mantras [are used] when the oblation is near at hand.
5.7.6: The oblation [is offered] in a low voice.
5.7.7: [The rite] ends with <s>Iḍā</s>.

body.translated_text:
5.8.1: All [the priests] touch water.
5.8.2: [Reciting] 'anādhṛṣṭam asy anādhṛṣyam devānām ojo 'nabhiśasty abhiśastipāḥ | anabhiśastenyam añjasā satyam upageṣam suvite mā dhāḥ' (Thou art unassailable, the inviolable vigor of the gods, free from reproach, protector from reproach; may I directly and truly attain that which is beyond reproach; place me in well-being) — touching together [the following items:] the golden <s>dhruva</s> (constant) ladle of ghee, standing in the <s>pātrī</s> vessel, placed on the sacred grass, [and] the <s>Tānūnaptra</s> (self-oath offering).
5.8.3a: Having touched water, passing around the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire in front, touching the [Soma] shoots, they invigorate the king [Soma].
5.8.3b: [Reciting] 'aṃśur aṃśuṣ ṭe deva soma ā pyāyatām indrāya ekadhanavide' (Shoot by shoot, may thy [essence], O divine Soma, swell for <s>Indra</s>, the winner of sole wealth).

body.translated_text:
5.9.1: The first sacrifice [is performed] without the <s>Pravargya</s> (hot-milk ceremony).
5.9.2: [Its performance] is optional for a learned Vedic scholar.
5.9.3: North of the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire.
5.9.4: When the <s>Mahāvīra</s> (great hero) vessels are being set down, [the priest] enters the hall through the front door, goes north of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> to the clod, the vessels, and [then] sits down behind them. When told 'O <s>hotṛ</s>, praise,' he praises [with] each [verse] one by one, without interruption, with the <s>praṇava</s> (oṃ).
5.9.5: [He begins:] 'brahma jajñānam prathamaṃ purastād vi sīmataḥ suruco vena āvaḥ' (The sacred word was born first in the east; from the boundary the shining one brought it forth)...

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 5.10.1: [He recites] 'Invoke!' when the cow is being called.
ŚŚS 5.10.2: [He recites] 'She lows' when [the cow] is approaching.
ŚŚS 5.10.3: [He recites] 'O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, over you...' when [the cow] is being addressed.
ŚŚS 5.10.4: [He recites] 'Together with the calf, like a calf...' when [the calf] is being released [to its mother].
ŚŚS 5.10.5: [He recites] 'Your teat...' when the calf is taking hold of the teat.
ŚŚS 5.10.6: [He recites] 'The cow has lowed...' when [the milk] is being drawn upward.
ŚŚS 5.10.7: [He recites] 'With homage sit down, being of one mind' — thus he sits down.
ŚŚS 5.10.8: [He recites] 'They milk the cow with the milking — the seventeen, possessing a self. <s>Agni</s> is kindled; O <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>gharma</s> (hot milk offering) is heated — come! The cows are milked, the powerful milch-cows here; the wondrous ones, the makers delight. That is the most excellent of gifts' — when [the cow] is being milked.
ŚŚS 5.10.9: [He recites] 'He has milked' [and] 'Arise, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>' — he rises.
ŚŚS 5.10.10: 'Bring near the milk — O milking one, among the cow-milkers! Pour the <s>gharma</s> for me, the milk of the dawn-cow. <s>Savitṛ</s>, dwelling at home, has opened the sky; follow, O heaven and earth, O well-guided ones!' — when the two [vessels of] milk are being brought.
ŚŚS 5.10.11: 'Pour splendor into the pressed [Soma]' [and] 'Now the seer of the <s>Aśvins</s>...' — when [the milks] are being poured in.
ŚŚS 5.10.12: 'Up there the divine <s>Savitṛ</s> with the golden [arms]...' — when [the vessel] is being lifted up.
ŚŚS 5.10.13: If the actions are reversed, [the mantras follow] according to the action.
ŚŚS 5.10.14: [He recites] 'Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth' — when [the priests] go forth.
ŚŚS 5.10.15: [He recites] 'The eagle in heaven (<s>nāke suparṇam</s>)' — following along.
ŚŚS 5.10.16: Having sat down on the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s seat.
ŚŚS 5.10.17: When told 'Offer the <s>gharma</s>!'
ŚŚS 5.10.18: 'Drink both! The heated <s>gharma</s> approaches you; the <s>Hotṛ</s> [offers], the <s>Adhvaryu</s> proceeds rich in offerings. Of the sweet, milked [drink], O <s>Aśvins</s>, of the extension — drink at the feast the milk of the dawn-cow!' — having pronounced the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call with both [verses] together.
ŚŚS 5.10.19: [He recites] 'O <s>Agni</s>, proclaim the <s>gharma</s>!' — he makes the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> (response call). Thus in the forenoon.
ŚŚS 5.10.20: Now in the afternoon:
ŚŚS 5.10.21: 'Drink of this! The ghee and milk offered in the dawn-cows — this excellent share is yours, O <s>Aśvins</s>; come! The two sweet supporters, lords of the assembly, the true ones — drink the heated <s>gharma</s> in the light of heaven!' — having pronounced the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call with both [verses] together.
ŚŚS 5.10.22: Likewise, having made the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> call.
ŚŚS 5.10.23: 'The <s>gharma</s>, made pure among the gods with the <s>Svāhā</s> call — the cup of the <s>Aśvins</s>, the divine drink — all the immortals, delighting, lick the cheek of the <s>Gandharva</s>' — having praised [with this verse].

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 5.11.1: For the <s>Upasad</s> (approach rite), in the forenoon he recites three <s>Sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses, each individually, with the <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>), three times each, without the <s>Anavāna</s> [verse].
ŚŚS 5.11.2: [He recites] 'O <s>Agni</s>, this fuel-stick of mine...' — three [verses] in the afternoon.
ŚŚS 5.11.3: With the third recitation of the former [verse], joining [it with] the next, he completes.
ŚŚS 5.11.4: 'Bring <s>Agni</s>; bring <s>Soma</s>; bring <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — joining with the <s>praṇava</s>.
ŚŚS 5.11.5: Having taken up the ladles with the ladle-taking [mantra].
ŚŚS 5.11.6: He offers in a low voice.
ŚŚS 5.11.7: [The verses are:] '<s>Agni</s> [conquers] obstacles, fierce like a hero'; 'You, O <s>Soma</s>, unconquered in battles by your powers'; 'Who [is] for the ancient one' [and] 'Him the praisers [invoke]'.
ŚŚS 5.11.8: As far as prescribed.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 5.12.1: The leading forth of the fire (<s>Agni-praṇayana</s>) [is performed] when there is no <s>Pravargya</s>.
ŚŚS 5.12.2: The removal of the great hero vessel (<s>Mahāvīra-pātra</s>) [is performed] when there is a <s>Pravargya</s>.
ŚŚS 5.12.3: There the <s>Prastotṛ</s> (the leader of the chant) sings a <s>Sāman</s>.
ŚŚS 5.12.4: There is the approaching of the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s final note (<s>nidhana</s>).
ŚŚS 5.12.5: The leading forth of the fire has been explained.

ŚŚS 5.13.1: When addressed for the rolling forth of the oblation carts (<s>Havirdhāna</s>).
ŚŚS 5.13.2: Standing between the southern track of the southern oblation cart and the northern track of the northern one — when told [to proceed] as the oblation carts are being rolled forward:
ŚŚS 5.13.3: 'Away with the fear from kinsmen and away with the fear from strangers, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>! The wheels have turned away' — with the right foot-tip, having swept away the clod backward.
ŚŚS 5.13.4: [He recites] 'Go forth to the sacrifice!' — standing, having recited.
ŚŚS 5.13.5: 'May heaven and earth [protect] us in this' [and] 'Of those two, the ghee-rich one, like <s>Yama</s>' — having taken position near the northern track of the southern [cart], following along.

body.translated_text: 5.19.1: Having been invited for the animal offering and the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake), they go north of the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> [fireplace] and of the <s>Hotṛ</s>, and sit down at their respective <s>dhiṣṇya</s> (fire-hearths). 5.19.2: They accomplish the purposes pertaining to the animal [offering] from available resources. 5.19.3: The <s>puroḍāśa</s> [has its own] <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, even in conjunction. 5.19.4: For unequal [offerings], by inference (<s>anūha</s>). 5.19.5: There are no <s>nigama</s> citations for those directed in the animal-offering procedure. 5.19.6: '<s>Agnīṣomā</s>, who today' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) for the <s>puroḍāśa</s>. 5.19.7: 'May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agnīṣomau</s>' — this is the directive (<s>praiṣa</s>). 5.19.8: '<s>Agnīṣomā</s>, the most abundantly nourishing' — this is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse). 5.19.9: '<s>Iḷā</s>, O <s>Agni</s>' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. 5.19.10: 'May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s> of the <s>puroḍāśa</s>' — this is the directive. 5.19.11: '<s>Agni</s>, the well-shining' — this is the <s>yājyā</s>. 5.19.12: Having invoked <s>Iḍā</s>, they proceed with the animal [offering]. 5.19.13: When told 'for the <s>Manotā</s> oblation,' he recites the <s>Manotā</s> hymn: 'For you, O <s>Agni</s>, are the first <s>Manotā</s> (approver).' 5.19.14: '<s>Agnīṣomā</s>, who [receive] what is offered' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> for the animal. 5.19.15: 'May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agnīṣomau</s>' — this is the directive. 5.19.16: '<s>Agnīṣomā</s>, with the oblation' — at the half-verse of the <s>yājyā</s>, he pauses, [awaiting] the omentum offering (<s>vasāhoma</s>). 5.19.17: When [the omentum] has been offered, he makes the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call. 5.19.18: 'For the gods, O lord of the forest (<s>Vanaspati</s>)' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> for <s>Vanaspati</s> (the sacrificial post). 5.19.19: 'May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Vanaspati</s>' — this is the directive. 5.19.20: 'O <s>Vanaspati</s>, with the rope' — this is the <s>yājyā</s>. 5.19.21: 'Gratify the gods' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. 5.19.22: 'May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s> <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>' — this is the directive. 5.19.23: The <s>yājyā</s> is without a <s>nigada</s> (citation). 5.19.24: Having invoked <s>Iḍā</s>, he performs the eleven <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings).

body.translated_text: 5.20.1: 'The divine sacred grass, the well-divine, with gods' — he directs without interruption. 5.20.2: He sacrifices as in the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) [rites]. 5.20.3: Between the eighth and ninth [<s>anuyājas</s>], [the following] enters. 5.20.4: 'The divine lord of the forest (<s>Vanaspati</s>), for the winning of wealth, may he approve of the wealth-offering. The divine sacred grass, of the <s>Vāritī</s>s, for the winning of wealth, may he approve of the wealth-offering.' 5.20.5: When told 'direct the hymn-recitation (<s>sūkta</s>),' he recites the <s>sūktavāka</s> directive: 'O <s>Agni</s>, today the <s>Hotṛ</s>.' 5.20.6: The <s>Saumika</s> (Soma-related) [one is used] in the <s>Savanīya</s> (pressing-day offering). 5.20.7: When the <s>Śamyorvāka</s> (benediction) has been spoken, having gone out as it comes, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest] is released. 5.20.8: The <s>Hotṛ</s>, having gone to the hall, concludes at night up to and including the <s>patnīsaṃyāja</s> (wife's offering).
