body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 8.24.1a: [The <s>nivid</s>:] 'May <s>Agni</s> <s>Jātavedas</s> be gladdened by the <s>Soma</s>. Of beautiful appearance, of varied splendor; not going away, the lord of the house; visible beyond the darkness; worthy of praise when ghee is offered; of many armors, the ever-sacrificing; who defeats enemies, the unconquered one. O <s>Agni</s> <s>Jātavedas</s>, bestow upon [us] splendor, bestow strength.'
ŚŚS 8.24.1b: 'Praised and unpraised — protect the kindler from distress! May <s>Agni</s> <s>Jātavedas</s> hear here, may he be gladdened by the <s>Soma</s> here! May the god...' — the rest is the same.
ŚŚS 8.24.2: Now the <s>ukthavīrya</s>.
ŚŚS 8.24.3: 'You are radiance; you are boldness; you are surpassing boldness; you are supreme boldness; you are the support; you are the foundation...'

body.translated_text:
8.25.1a: 'In the exhilaration of this [<s>Soma</s>], O singer, <s>Indra</s> was intoxicated by the <s>Soma</s>. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Ahi</s> (the serpent). In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> propped up the sky and spread out the earth. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> traversed the atmosphere and made the sun go with divine [rays]. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> raised up the <s>Ārya</s> color and struck down the <s>Dāsa</s> color.'
8.25.1b: 'In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> filled the waterless [rivers] and enlivened the lifeless. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> pacified the leaping, roaring, agitated mountains. In the exhilaration of this, O singer, <s>Indra</s> [performed all these feats].'

body.translated_text:
9.1.1: The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has been explained; it is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) for the twelve-day [<s>Soma</s> sacrifice] and the single-day rites.
9.1.2: We shall now explain its modifications (<s>vikāra</s>).
9.1.3: A known archetypal designation, [when applied] to a different material, reverts [the rite] to the archetype.
9.1.4: [This is] a prohibition.
9.1.5: [Or] a purpose.
9.1.6: [Or] an enumeration.
9.1.7: Or a supplement.
9.1.8: After the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [hymn], by the addition of three <s>śastras</s> (recitations), [the rite] becomes an <s>Ukthya</s>.
9.1.9: By the addition of one [more <s>śastra</s>] beyond the <s>Ukthyas</s>, [it becomes] a <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>.
9.1.10: By the addition of thirteen [more] beyond the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, [it becomes] an <s>Atirātra</s>.
9.1.11: Between the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [and the additional hymns, the procedure is as follows].

body.text:

ŚŚS_9.2.2: ehy.ū.ṣu.bravāṇi.iti.stotriya.anurūpau /
ŚŚS_9.2.3: carṣaṇī.dhṛtam.astabhnād.dyām.iti.tṛcau /
ŚŚS_9.2.4: indrā.varuṇā.yuvam.adhvarāya.naḥ /
ŚŚS_9.2.5: ā.vām.rājānau /
ŚŚS_9.2.6: indrā.varuṇā.madhumattamasya.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.2.1: The 'Together with the horse' [hymn is] for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest].
9.2.2: 'Come, now let me speak' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse).
9.2.3: 'Upholder of peoples,' 'He propped up the sky' — these are the <s>tṛcas</s> (triplets of verses).
9.2.4: 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, [come] to our sacrifice.'
9.2.5: 'Come to you, O two kings.'
9.2.6: 'O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, [give us] the sweetest' — with this he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.3.1: saubharam.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.3.2: vayam.u.tvām.apūrvya.yo.na.idam.idam.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.pragāthau /
ŚŚS_9.3.3: pra.manhiṣṭhāya.yo.adribhid.iti.tṛcau /
ŚŚS_9.3.4: astā.iva.su.prataram.ity.uttamām.uddhṛtya.udapruta.iti.śastvā.yā.pūrvasya.uddhṛtā.tayā.paridhāya.bṛhaspate.yuvam.indraś.ca.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.3.1: The <s>Saubhara</s> [hymn is] for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> [priest].
9.3.2: 'We indeed praise you, O primeval one,' 'He who for us this' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> <s>pragāthas</s> (chant-pairs).
9.3.3: 'For the most bountiful,' 'He who split the rock' — these are the <s>tṛcas</s>.
9.3.4: Having extracted the last [verse] of 'Like a good archer,' having recited 'He who burst forth,' and having concluded with the [verse] previously extracted, he offers with '<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, you and <s>Indra</s>.'

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.4.1: nārmedham.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_9.4.2: adhā.hi.indra.iti.stotriya.anurūpau /
ŚŚS_9.4.4: ṛtur.janitrī /
ŚŚS_9.4.4: viṣṇor.nu.kam /
ŚŚS_9.4.5: pra.vaḥ.pāntam.andhasaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.4.6: sam.vām.karmaṇā /
ŚŚS_9.4.7: indrā.viṣṇū.mada.patī.madānām.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.4.1: The <s>Nārmedha</s> [hymn is] for the <s>Acchāvāka</s> [priest].
9.4.2: 'For <s>Indra</s> indeed' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>.
9.4.4: 'The season, the progenitress.'
9.4.4: '[The strides] of <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed.'
9.4.5: 'Forth from your [pressed] juice.'
9.4.6: 'Together, your ritual action.'
9.4.7: '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lords of exhilaration, of exhilarations' — with this he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.5.1: ṣoḷaśine.stoṣyamāṇeṣu.|.yasmāj.jāto.na.paro.anyo.asti.ya.ā.babhūva.bhuvanāni.viśvā.|.prajāpatiḥ.prajayā.saṃrarāṇas.trīṇi.jyotīṃṣi.sacate.sa.ṣoḷaśī.|.iti.yajamānaḥ.ṣoḷaśi.graham.upatiṣṭhate /
ŚŚS_9.5.2a: indra.juṣasva.pra.vahā.yāhi.śūra.hariha.|.pibā.sutasya.matir.na.madhvaś.cakānaś.cārur.madāya /
ŚŚS_9.5.2b: indra.jaṭharam.navyam.na.pṛṇasva.madhor.divo.na.|.asya.sutasya.svarṇa.upa.tvā.madāḥ.suvāco.asthuḥ /
ŚŚS_9.5.2c: indras.turāṣāṇ.mitro.na.jaghāna.vṛtram.yatir.na.|.bibheda.valam.bhṛgur.na.sasāhe.śatrūn.made.somasya.|.iti.stotriyam.śastvā /
ŚŚS_9.5.3: tvāvataḥ.purūvaso.ity.ekā /
ŚŚS_9.5.4: ā.tvā.vahantu.harayaḥ.svādor.itthā.iti.gāyatram.tṛcam.pāṅktam.ca.viharati /
ŚŚS_9.5.5: prathamena.gāyatreṇa.pādena.prathamam.pāṅktām.pādam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.5.6: dvitīyena.gāyatreṇa.dvitīyam.saṃdhāya.praṇauti /
ŚŚS_9.5.7: tṛtīyena.gāyatreṇa.tṛtīyam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.5.8: dvau.paṅkteḥ.pariśiṣṭau.tābhyām.praṇauti /
ŚŚS_9.5.9: indrāya.sāma.gāyatā.mandrair.indra.haribhir.ity.auṣṇiham.tṛcam.bārhatam.ca.viharati /
ŚŚS_9.5.10: prathamena.auṣṇihena.pādena.prathamam.bārhatam.pādam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.5.11: dvitīyena.auṣṇihena.dvitīyam.saṃdhāya.praṇauti /
ŚŚS_9.5.12: aṣṭa.akṣaram.auṣṇihasya.pādasya.aṣṭa.akṣaram.bārhatasya.tābhyām.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.5.13: catur.akṣare.śiṣṭe.te.samasya.uttamam.bārhatam.pādam.saṃdhāya.praṇauti /
body.translated_text:
9.5.1: When [the <s>stotras</s> of] the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> [rite] are about to be chanted: 'Since being born, no other is beyond him who encompasses all beings — <s>Prajāpati</s>, delighting in progeny, attains the three lights; he is the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> (sixteenth)' — with this the sacrificer reverentially approaches the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> cup.
9.5.2a: 'O <s>Indra</s>, be pleased; come forth, go, O hero; drink the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], pleasant for intoxication, like sweet [honey], delighting.'
9.5.2b: 'O <s>Indra</s>, fill the belly anew, like honey, like heaven; of this pressed [<s>Soma</s>], like the sun, the sweet-voiced intoxications have approached you.'
9.5.2c: '<s>Indra</s> <s>Turāṣāh</s> (the mightily-conquering one), like <s>Mitra</s>, slew <s>Vṛtra</s>; striving, he split open <s>Vala</s> [the cave].'

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.6.1: ā.dhūrṣu.urum.na.iti.dvipadām.ca.viṃśaty.akṣarām.triṣṭubham.ca.viharati /
ŚŚS_9.6.2: prathamena.dvaipadena.pañca.akṣareṇa.prathamam.traiṣṭubham.pādam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.6.3: dvitīyena.pañca.akṣareṇa.dvitīyam.saṃdhāya.praṇauti /
ŚŚS_9.6.4: tṛtīyena.pañca.akṣareṇa.tṛtīyam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.6.5: caturthena.pañca.akṣareṇa.caturtham.saṃdhāya.praṇauti /
ŚŚS_9.6.6: eṣa.brahmā.ya.ṛtviya.indro.nāma.śruto.gṛṇe.|.viśrutayo.yathā.patha.indra.tvadyanti.rātayaḥ.|.tvām.icchavasaspate.yanti.giro.naḥ.samyataḥ.|.pra.te.maha.iti.dvaipadam.tṛcam.jāgatam.ca.viharati /
ŚŚS_9.6.7: prathamena.dvaipadena.catur.akṣareṇa.prathamam.jāgatam.pādam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.6.8: dvitīyena.catur.akṣareṇa.dvitīyam.saṃdhāya.praṇauti /
ŚŚS_9.6.9: tṛtīyena.catur.akṣareṇa.tṛtīyam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.6.10: caturthena.catur.akṣareṇa.caturtham.saṃdhāya.praṇauti /
ŚŚS_9.6.11: indro.dadhīca.iti.tisṛṇām.gāyatrīṇām.dvābhyām.avasāya.pādābhyām.dvābhyām.praṇauti.dvābhyām.avasāya.dvābhyām /
ŚŚS_9.6.12: uttamena.gāyatreṇa.pādena.pro.ṣv.asmai.puroratham.ity.etasyāḥ.pādam.saṃdhāya.avasyati /
ŚŚS_9.6.13: dvābhyām.praṇauti.dvābhyām.avasāya.dvābhyām /
ŚŚS_9.6.14: pra.pra.vas.triṣṭubhām.iti.tṛcam /
ŚŚS_9.6.15: ā.yat.patanti.ity.ekā /
ŚŚS_9.6.16: yo.vyatīṃr.iti.(?).tisṛṇām.uttamām.pariśiṣya.nividam /
ŚŚS_9.6.17: stotriye.ca.āhāvo.nivide.paridhānīyāyai.ca /
ŚŚS_9.6.18: yd.yad.bradhnasya.iti.paridhāya.uktha.vīryam.japitvā.apāḥ.pūrveṣām.iti.yajati /
ŚŚS_9.6.19: etasmin.stotriye.catvāriṃśat.sampada.ānuṣṭubhaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.6.20: vikriyamāṇe.yathā.samāmnātam /
ŚŚS_9.6.21: indraś.ca.saṃrāḍ.varuṇaś.ca.rājā.tau.te.bhakṣam.cakratur.agra.etam.|.tayor.aham.bhakṣam.anubhakṣayāmi.vāg.devī.juṣāṇā.somasya.tṛpyatu.|.iti.graham.bhakṣayati /
body.translated_text:
9.6.1: He distributes 'In the shafts, the wide one' — [alternating between] the <s>Dvipada</s> (two-footed) [verses] and the twenty-syllable <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
9.6.2: He joins the first five-syllable <s>Dvipada</s> half with the first <s>Triṣṭubh</s> foot and pauses.
9.6.3: He joins the second five-syllable [half] with the second [<s>Triṣṭubh</s> foot] and chants the <s>praṇava</s>.
9.6.4: He joins the third five-syllable [half] with the third [<s>Triṣṭubh</s> foot] and pauses.
9.6.5: He joins the fourth five-syllable [half] with the fourth [<s>Triṣṭubh</s> foot] and chants the <s>praṇava</s>.
9.6.6: 'This is the <s>Brahman</s> who at the proper season, <s>Indra</s> by name, is renowned; I praise. Like paths of renown, O <s>Indra</s>, treasures go to you. You, O Lord of wealth (<s>Vasaspati</s>), I seek.'

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.7.1: pāntam.ā.vo.andhasa.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.hotuḥ.prathameṣu.rātri.paryāyeṣu /
ŚŚS_9.7.2: na.prathamasya.prathamam.āṃreḷayāt /
ŚŚS_9.7.3: śeṣaḥ.sūktasya.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.7.4: abhi.tyam.meṣam.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.7.5: adhvaryavo.bharata.indrāya.iti.yajāt /
body.translated_text:
9.7.1: 'O purified one, from your juice' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> for the first night <s>paryāyas</s> (rounds).
9.7.2: The first [syllable] of the first [verse] should not be prolonged.
9.7.3: The remainder of the <s>sūkta</s> is the opening of the <s>uktha</s> (recitation).
9.7.4: 'That ram' — [this is] the <s>Jāgata</s> [section].
9.7.5: 'O <s>Adhvaryus</s>, bring to <s>Indra</s>' — with this he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.8.1: pra.va.indrāya.mādanam.prakṛtāni.iti.maitrāvaruṇasya /
ŚŚS_9.8.2: surūpa.kṛtnum.ity.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.8.3: tyam.su.meṣam.iti.jāgatasya.navamīm.ca.uttamām.ca.uddhṛtya.caturdaśīm.pūrvām.śastvā.trayodaśyā.paridhāya.pātā.sutām.indro.astu.somam.hantā.vṛtram.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.8.1: 'Forth for <s>Indra</s> the intoxicating [drink]' — these are the prescribed [hymns] for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest].
9.8.2: 'The maker of beautiful forms' — this is the opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.8.3: Having extracted the ninth and the last [verses] of 'That ram,' [which is] the <s>Jāgata</s> [section], having recited the fourteenth before [them], concluding with the thirteenth, he offers with 'May <s>Indra</s> be the drinker of the pressed <s>Soma</s>; may he be the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>.'

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.9.1: vayam.u.tvā.tad.id.arthā.vayam.u.tvā.divā.suta.iti.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.9.2: indra.tvā.vṛṣabham.ity.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.9.3: vārtrahatyāya.śavasa.iti.vā.uttamām.uddhṛtya /
ŚŚS_9.9.4: nyū.ṣu.vācam.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.9.5: vṛṣā.mada.indra.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.9.1: 'vayam u tvā' (We indeed thee), 'tad id arthā' (For that very purpose), 'vayam u tvā divā sute' (We indeed thee, at the day-pressing) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> priest.
9.9.2: 'indra tvā vṛṣabham' (O Indra, thee the bull) — this is the opening of the <s>uktha</s> (recitation).
9.9.3: Or [he recites] 'vārtrahatyāya śavase' (For the slaying of Vṛtra, for might), extracting the last [verse].
9.9.4: 'nyū ṣu vācam' (Down now, speech) — the <s>Jāgata</s> (in Jagatī meter) [verse].
9.9.5: 'vṛṣā mada indra' (The bull, the intoxicating, O Indra) — thus he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.10.1: indrāya.madvane.sutam.indram.id.gāthino.bṛhad.ity.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_9.10.2: śeṣaḥ.sūktasya.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.10.3: mā.no.asminn.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.10.4: idma.tyat.pātram.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.10.1: 'indrāya madvane sutam' (For Indra, pressed for exhilaration), 'indram id gāthinaḥ bṛhat' (Indra indeed, the singers, the great) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> priest.
9.10.2: The remainder of the hymn is the opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.10.3: 'mā no asmin' (Not us in this) — the <s>Jāgata</s> [verse].
9.10.4: 'idma tyat pātram' (We know that vessel) — thus he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.11.1: ayam.ta.indra.somo.ayam.te.mānuṣe.jana.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.hotur.madhyameṣu.rātri.paryāyeṣu /
ŚŚS_9.11.2: ud.ghed.abhi.ity.uktha.mukham.uttamām.uddhṛtya /
ŚŚS_9.11.3: aham.bhuvam.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.11.4: apāyy.asya.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.11.1: 'ayam ta indra somaḥ' (This thy Soma, O Indra) and 'ayam te mānuṣe jane' (This [is offered] among mankind for thee) — these are the <s>stotriya</s> (hymn verse) and <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse) of the <s>hotṛ</s> in the middle night-rounds.
9.11.2: 'ud ghed abhi' (Up indeed toward) — the opening of the <s>uktha</s>, extracting the last [verse].
9.11.3: 'aham bhuvam' (I have been) — the <s>Jāgata</s> [verse].
9.11.4: 'apāyy asya' (From this [Soma]) — thus he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.12.1: ā.tū.na.indra.kṣumantam.ā.tū.na.indra.vṛtrahann.iti.maitrāvaruṇasya /
ŚŚS_9.12.2: ā.indra.sānasim.ity.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.12.3: pra.vaḥ.satām.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.12.4: asya.made.puru.varpāṃsi.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.12.1: 'ā tū na indra kṣumantam' (Come to us, O Indra, with nourishment) and 'ā tū na indra vṛtrahan' (Come to us, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> priest.
9.12.2: 'ā indra sānasim' (Come, O Indra, the victorious) — the opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.12.3: 'pra vaḥ satām' (Forth for you, O true ones) — the <s>Jāgata</s> [verse].
9.12.4: 'asya made puruvarpāṃsi' (In the intoxication of this [Soma], many forms) — thus he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.13.1: abhi.tvā.vṛṣabha.abhi.pra.go.patim.iti.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.13.2: ā.tū.na.indra.madryag.ity.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.13.3: tad.asmai.navyam.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.13.4: yas.te.ratha.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.13.1: 'abhi tvā vṛṣabha' (Unto thee, O bull) and 'abhi pra gopatim' (Unto the lord of cows) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> priest.
9.13.2: 'ā tū na indra madryak' (Come to us, O Indra, intoxicatingly) — the opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.13.3: 'tad asmai navyam' (That new [praise] for him) — the <s>Jāgata</s> [verse].
9.13.4: 'yas te rathaḥ' (That chariot of thine) — thus he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.14.1: idam.vaso.sutam.indra.ihi.matsi.ity.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_9.14.2: śeṣaḥ.sūktasya.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.14.3: ajāta.śatrum.iti.jāgatasya.uttamām.uddhṛtya.ud.yat.saha.iti.paridhāya.idam.te.pātram.sanavittam.indra.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.14.1: 'idam vaso sutam' (This pressed [Soma], O Vasu) and 'indra ihi matsi' (O Indra, come, be gladdened) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> priest.
9.14.2: The remainder of the hymn is the opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.14.3: Extracting the last [verse] of the <s>Jāgata</s> [passage] 'ajātaśatrum' (O undefeated one), enclosing with 'ud yat sahaḥ' (Up, that which is might), he offers with 'idam te pātraṃ sanavittam indra' (This thy vessel, O Indra, won from old).

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.15.1: idam.hy.anv.ojasā.mahān.indro.ya.ojasā.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.hotur.uttameṣu.rātri.paryāyeṣu /
ŚŚS_9.15.2: śeṣaḥ.sūktasya.uktha.mukham.uttamās.tisra.uddhṛtya /
ŚŚS_9.15.3: viśvajita.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.15.4: tiṣṭhā.harī.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.15.1: 'idam hy anv ojasā' (This indeed with might) and 'mahān indro ya ojasā' (Great Indra who with might) — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> of the <s>hotṛ</s> in the last night-rounds.
9.15.2: The remainder of the hymn is the opening of the <s>uktha</s>, extracting the last three [verses].
9.15.3: 'viśvajitam' (The all-conquering) — the <s>Jāgata</s> [verse].
9.15.4: 'tiṣṭhā harī' (Stand firm, O two bay horses) — thus he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.16.1: ā.tv.etā.ni.ṣīdata.ā.tv.aśatravā.gahi.iti.maitrā.varuṇasya /
ŚŚS_9.16.2: yasya.saṃstha.iti.sapta.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.16.3: aham.dām.gṛṇata.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.16.4: pra.ghā.nv.asya.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.16.1: 'ā tv etā' (Come with these) and 'ni ṣīdata' (Sit down), 'ā tv aśatravā gahi' (Come, O foe-less one) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> priest.
9.16.2: 'yasya saṃsthaḥ' (Whose conclusion) — the seven [verses forming the] opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.16.3: 'aham dām gṛṇate' (I give to the singer) — the <s>Jāgata</s> [verse].
9.16.4: 'pra ghā nv asya' (Forth indeed now of this one) — thus he offers.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.17.1: yoge.yoge.yuñjanti.bradhnam.iti.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.17.2: śeṣaḥ.sūktasya.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.17.3: imām.te.dhiyam.iti.jāgatasya.uttamām.uddhṛtya.tad.asya.idam.paśyata.iti.paridhāya.pro.droṇa.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.17.1: 'yoge yoge yuñjanti bradhnam' (In every yoking they yoke the tawny one) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> priest.
9.17.2: The remainder of the hymn is the opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.17.3: Extracting the last [verse] of the <s>Jāgata</s> [passage] 'imāṃ te dhiyam' (This thought for thee), enclosing with 'tad asya idaṃ paśyata' (See this of his), he offers with 'pro droṇa' (Forth [from] the wooden vessel).

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.18.1: indraḥ.suteṣu.someṣv.indram.vardhantv.ity.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_9.18.2: uttamāni.catur.akṣarāṇy.abhyasyanti /
ŚŚS_9.18.3: upa.naḥ.sutam.ā.gahi.somam.indra.ity.uktha.mukham /
ŚŚS_9.18.4: pra.te.maha.iti.jāgatam /
ŚŚS_9.18.5: pra.ugrām.pītim.iti.yajati /
body.translated_text:
9.18.1: 'indraḥ suteṣu someṣu' (Indra, among the pressed Soma juices) and 'indraṃ vardhantv' (May they strengthen Indra) — [these are the verses] of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> priest.
9.18.2: They repeat the last four syllables [of each verse].
9.18.3: 'upa naḥ sutam ā gahi somam indra' (Come to us, to the pressed Soma, O Indra) — the opening of the <s>uktha</s>.
9.18.4: 'pra te mahaḥ' (Forth to thy greatness) — the <s>Jāgata</s> [verse].
9.18.5: 'pra ugrāṃ pītim' (Forth the mighty draught) — thus he offers.

body.translated_text:
9.19.1: Now the <s>Āhīnikī</s> (daily) [verses] of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> priest.
9.19.2: 'panyam panyam it sotāraḥ' (Wondrous, wondrous indeed, O pressers) and 'panya id upa gāyata' (Sing of the wondrous one indeed) — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> for the first [night-round].
9.19.3: 'ā tvā viśantv indavaḥ' (May the drops enter thee) and 'ā tvā viśantv āśavaḥ' (May the swift ones enter thee) — for the last [night-round].
9.20.1: Having concluded the night-rounds, when [the priests] are about to chant the <s>Āśvina</s> (hymn to the Aśvins), he offers the <s>pravṛta-āhutī</s> (initiating oblations).
9.20.2: He should recite in an even voice.
9.20.3: Or in a progressively rising [voice].
9.20.4: The morning <s>anuvāka</s> (recitation) — that is the <s>Āśvina</s> [portion].
9.20.5: We shall explain its modification.
9.20.6: The recitation [follows] the meters.
9.20.7: Of the <s>Bārhatī</s> (Bṛhatī-meter) opening [verses], [he takes] the first <s>pragātha</s> (paired verse) as the first, repeating it, in <s>Kakubh</s> form.
9.20.8: 'agnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ' (Agni the invoker, lord of the house)...

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.21.1: trivṛd.bahiṣ.pavamānaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.21.2: saṃdhi.ṣāma.ca /
ŚŚS_9.21.3: pañca.āditha.pañcadaśāni /
ŚŚS_9.21.4: rātriś.ca /
ŚŚS_9.21.5: pañca.saptadaśāni /
ŚŚS_9.21.6: pañca.ekaviṃśāni /
ŚŚS_9.21.7: iti.jyotiṣaḥ.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_9.21.8: eta.eva.abhiplavasya /
body.translated_text:
9.21.1: The external <s>Pavamāna</s> (purification chant) [is in] <s>Trivṛt</s> (nine-fold [stoma]).
9.21.2: And [there is] the <s>Sandhi-sāma</s> (junction-chant).
9.21.3: Five [chants are in] <s>Pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-fold) [stoma].
9.21.4: And [one for] the night.
9.21.5: Five [chants are in] <s>Saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-fold) [stoma].
9.21.6: Five [chants are in] <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold) [stoma].
9.21.7: These are the <s>stomas</s> (chant-structures) of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> (Light-sacrifice).
9.21.8: These same [apply to] the <s>Abhiplava</s> [day].

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.22.1: agnim.tu.ceṣyamāṇasya.adīkṣitasya.iṣṭiḥ /
ŚŚS_9.22.2: agnaye.brahmaṇvate.agnaye.kṣatravate.agnaye.kṣatrabhṛte /
ŚŚS_9.22.3: paurṇamāsī.vikāraḥ /
ŚŚS_9.22.4: brahma.prajāvad.ā.bhara.brahma.ca.te.jāta.veda.ity.agnaye.brahmaṇvate /
ŚŚS_9.22.5: arcantas.tvā.asmākam.agne.adhvaram.agne.dyumnena.svadasva.havya.ity.uttarayoḥ /
ŚŚS_9.22.6: bahūnām.ceṣyamāṇānām.samnivapanīyā /
ŚŚS_9.22.7: ekasya.ukhā.sambharaṇīyā /
body.translated_text:
9.22.1: For one who is about to build the fire-altar (<s>Agnicayana</s>) but is not yet consecrated, [there is] an <s>iṣṭi</s>.
9.22.2: To <s>Agni Brahmaṇvat</s> (Agni possessing sacred knowledge), to <s>Agni Kṣatravat</s> (Agni possessing warrior power), and to <s>Agni Kṣatrabhṛt</s> (Agni upholding warrior power).
9.22.3: [This is] a modification of the full-moon [sacrifice].
9.22.4: 'brahma prajāvad ā bhara' (Bring sacred knowledge rich in offspring) and 'brahma ca te jātaveda' (And sacred knowledge for thee, O Jātavedas) — for <s>Agni Brahmaṇvat</s>.
9.22.5: 'arcantas tvā' (Praising thee), 'asmākam agne' (O Agni, of ours), 'adhvaram' (The sacrifice), 'agne dyumnena' (O Agni, with splendor), 'svadasva havya' (Enjoy the oblation) — for the other two.
9.22.6: When many [sacrificers] are about to build, [they perform] the <s>samnivapanīyā</s> (joint pouring) [iṣṭi].
9.22.7: For a single [sacrificer], the <s>ukhā sambharaṇīyā</s> (pot-collecting) [iṣṭi].

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.23.1: prājāpatyaś.ca.paśu.bandhaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.23.2: vāyavyo.vā /

ŚŚS_9.23.8: vaiśvānarīyam.āgneye /

ŚŚS_9.23.10: upāṃśu /
ŚŚS_9.23.11: ekayā.ca.rāye.nu.kuvid.aṅga.iti.puronuvākyāḥ.pīvo.annān.pra.yābhir.yāsi.pravāyum.accha.iti.vāyavyasya /
ŚŚS_9.23.12: ā.te.vatso.mano.yamat.tubhyam.tā.aṅgirastama.agniḥ.pareṣu.dhāmasv.iti.puronuvākyā.vayam.te.adya.aśyāma.tam.īḷe.ca.tvā.ity.āgneyasya /
ŚŚS_9.23.13: bahuvat.paśu.nigamāḥ.pañcasu.kriyamāṇeṣu.pṛthivīm.śarīrāṇi.ity.ātaḥ.(.ataḥ.?) /
ŚŚS_9.23.14: ekavad.ata.ūrdhvam /
body.translated_text:
9.23.1: And [there is] the <s>Prājāpatya</s> (offering to Prajāpati) animal sacrifice.
9.23.2: Or one dedicated to <s>Vāyu</s>.
9.23.3: Or to <s>Agni</s>, for [fulfilling] a desire.
9.23.4: A man, a goat, a sheep, a cow, and a horse — these are the five [sacrificial] animals.
9.23.5: Or a goat or a hornless one.
9.23.6: And some make, for the <s>Prājāpatya</s>, an animal-cake (<s>paśu-puroḍāśa</s>) dedicated to <s>Vāyu</s>.
9.23.7: [Or] a <s>Prājāpatya</s> [cake] for the <s>Vāyavya</s> [rite].
9.23.8: A <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> [cake] for the <s>Āgneya</s> [rite].
9.23.9: 'hiraṇyagarbhaḥ' (The golden embryo) — three [verses as] <s>puronuvākyās</s>; the latter [three as] <s>yājyās</s> for the <s>Prājāpatya</s>.
9.23.10: [These are recited] in a low voice.
9.23.11: 'ekayā ca' (With one), 'rāye nu kuvid' (For wealth, surely), 'aṅga' (Indeed) — the <s>puronuvākyās</s>; 'pīvo annān' (Fat with food), 'pra yābhir yāsi' (Forth with which thou goest), 'pravāyum' (The impeller), 'accha' (Toward) — for the <s>Vāyavya</s>.
9.23.12: 'ā te vatso mano yamat' (May the calf direct thy mind), 'tubhyaṃ tā aṅgirastama' (For thee, O most Aṅgiras-like), 'agne'...

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.24.1: tri.haviś.ca.dīkṣaṇīyā /
ŚŚS_9.24.2: āgnāvaiṣṇavo.vaiśvānarīya.ādityebhyaś.ca /

ŚŚS_9.24.8: śucim.arkais.tam.śagmāsaḥ /
ŚŚS_9.24.9: citibhyaḥ.praṇīyamānābhya.ity.uktaḥ.purīṣyāsaḥ.(īi.22.4).pro.tye.agnayo.agniṣu.(v.6.6).viśvebhir.agne.agnibhir.(i.26.10).agne.viśvebhir.agnibhir.(īi.24.4).ity.upāṃśv.anubruvan.paścād.anusameti /
body.translated_text:
9.24.1: And the consecration (<s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>) [offering] has three oblations.
9.24.2: [They are] for <s>Agni</s>-<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, and the <s>Ādityas</s>.
9.24.3: Bearing those <s>Kṣatriyas</s> [warrior qualities].
9.24.4: Or five oblations.
9.24.5: The fourth for <s>Aditi</s>, the fifth for <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
9.24.6: Or the hospitality (<s>ātithya</s>) [offering] has five oblations.
9.24.7: [They are] for <s>Agni</s>, for <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Viśvedevas</s>, for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and for <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
9.24.8: [The verses are:] "<s>Śucim arkaiḥ</s>" (The pure one with songs) and "<s>Tam śagmāsaḥ</s>" (Him, the mighty ones).
9.24.9: When told "For the layers being carried forward," [he recites the verses:] "<s>Purīṣyāsaḥ</s>" (Borne by the filling, II.22.4), "<s>Pro tye agnayo agniṣu</s>" (Forward those fires among fires, V.6.6), "<s>Viśvebhir agne agnibhiḥ</s>" (With all fires, O <s>Agni</s>, I.26.10), "<s>Agne viśvebhir agnibhiḥ</s>" (O <s>Agni</s>, with all fires, II.24.4)" — softly repeating, he follows behind.

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.25.1: saṃcite.pariṣṭute.agny.uktham.anuśaṃsa.ity.uktaś.cityasya.paścād.upaviśya.ājyeyas.tūṣṇīm.śaṃsas.tena.anāhūya.sajapena.anuśaṃsati /
ŚŚS_9.25.2: vaiśvānarāya.ity.uktaḥ.puronuvākyām.anūcya.yājyayā.yajati.prayāja.anuyājān.vā.parihāpya /
body.translated_text:
9.25.1: When [the fire-altar] is piled up and praised around, being told "Recite the <s>agnyuktham</s> (fire-praise)," sitting behind the fire-altar, [reciting] the <s>Ājya</s> [portion] as a silent recitation, without calling with that, he recites as an accompaniment with murmuring.
9.25.2: Being told "For <s>Vaiśvānara</s>," having recited the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse), he offers with the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), omitting the <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings) and <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings).

body.text:
ŚŚS_9.26.1: agnīṣomīyasya.paśu.puroḷāśam.anvañci.devasūbhyo.havīṃṣi /
ŚŚS_9.26.2: agnaye.gṛha.pataye.somāya.vanaspataye.savitre.satya.prasavāya.rudrāya.paśu.pataye.bṛhaspataye.vācaspataya.indrāya.jyeṣṭhāya.mitrāya.satyāya.varuṇāya.dharma.pataye /
ŚŚS_9.26.3: agnir.hotā.gṛha.patir.havyavāḷ.agnir.ā.viśva.devam.na.pramiya.indram.vayam.mahā.dhana.urum.naḥ /
ŚŚS_9.26.4: sarva.pṛṣṭhā.havīṃṣi.ca /
body.translated_text:
9.26.1: The <s>puroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake) accompanies the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal [sacrifice], and the oblations for the <s>Devasūs</s> (divine impellers) follow.
9.26.2: [The oblations are] for <s>Agni</s> the householder, for <s>Soma</s> the lord of trees, for <s>Savitṛ</s> of true impulsion, for <s>Rudra</s> the lord of cattle, for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the lord of speech, for <s>Indra</s> the foremost, for <s>Mitra</s> the true, for <s>Varuṇa</s> the lord of <s>dharma</s>.
9.26.3: [The verses are:] "<s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s>, householder, bearer of oblations"; "O <s>Agni</s>, to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>"; "Not perishing"; "We [invoke] <s>Indra</s>"; "Of great wealth"; "Broad for us."
9.26.4: And the oblations [apply] to all the <s>Pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chants).

ŚŚS_9.27.7: śivas.tvaṣṭaḥ.prathama.bhājam /
body.translated_text:
9.27.1: [The seasonal oblations are:] For <s>Agni</s> of spring, of <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre, of the <s>Trivṛt</s> (nine-fold <s>stoma</s>), of the <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>sāman</s>]; for <s>Indra</s> of summer, of <s>Triṣṭubh</s> metre, of the fifteen-fold [<s>stoma</s>], of the <s>Bṛhat</s>; for the <s>Viśvedevas</s> of the rainy season, of <s>Jagatī</s> metre, of the seventeen-fold [<s>stoma</s>], of the <s>Vairūpa</s>; for <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> of autumn, of <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> metre, of the twenty-one-fold [<s>stoma</s>], of the <s>Vairāja</s>; for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> of early winter, of <s>Paṅkti</s> metre, of the <s>Triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold), of the <s>Śākvara</s>; for <s>Savitṛ</s> of late winter, of <s>Atichandas</s> (super-metre), of the thirty-three-fold, of the <s>Raivata</s>; for <s>Anumatī</s>; for <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>; for <s>Ka</s> [(<s>Prajāpati</s>)]; for <s>Aditi</s> the wife of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
9.27.2a: [The verses are:] "Praising you"; "Our <s>Agni</s>, in the sacrifice"; "By <s>ṛta</s>"; "You two who stretch forth your arms"; "O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, enjoy"; "Thus to the father, blameless"; "Wealth, today."
9.27.2: "May <s>Anumatī</s> today regard our sacrifice as [pleasing] among the gods. And may <s>Agni</s>, the bearer of oblations, be a delight to the worshipper. O <s>Anumatī</s>, may you think [favorably]; make welfare for us. Impel us to skill and dexterity; extend our lifespans."
9.27.3: The oblations that are directed in the animal ritual system do not obtain <s>nigama</s> (Vedic citation) [references].
9.27.4: Having concluded [the offering of] the omentum, they proceed with the <s>Anūbandhyā</s> (supplementary) cow, with the animal for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, softly, in the wife's chamber.
9.27.5: Having carried [the animal] around the fire, they release it; they do not bring it to conclusion.
9.27.6: Or they conclude [the rite] with ghee, following the animal procedure.
9.27.7: "Auspicious <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>" — [he recites this] receiving the first share.

body.translated_text:
9.28.1: And the oblations for the goddesses (<s>devikā havīṃṣi</s>) follow the <s>puroḍāśa</s> of the animal [sacrifice].
9.28.2: For <s>Anumatī</s>, for <s>Kuhū</s>, for <s>Rākā</s>, for <s>Sinīvālī</s>, and for <s>Dhātṛ</s>.
9.28.3a: [The verse for <s>Kuhū</s>:] "I invoke <s>Kuhū</s>, of good conduct, of known deeds, easy to invoke, at this sacrifice. May she grant us the fame of our forefathers; to you, O goddess, we worship with oblation."
9.28.3b: "<s>Kuhū</s>, wife of the immortality of the gods, may she make our oblation worthy. May she scatter abundant wealth for the worshipper; may she give increase of riches to the wise."
9.28.3c: "May <s>Dhātṛ</s> give to the worshipper an undecaying life extending eastward. May we enjoy the favor of the god of true law."
9.28.3d: "<s>Dhātṛ</s> rules over offspring and wealth. <s>Dhātṛ</s> generated this entire world. <s>Dhātṛ</s> shall give a son to the sacrificer. To him offer the ghee-rich oblation."
9.28.4: And the oblations for the goddesses.
9.28.5: For the waters, for herbs, for cattle, for dawn, for night, for <s>Sūryā</s> (the sun-goddess), for heaven, for earth, for speech, for the cow.
9.28.6: [The verses are:] "<s>Āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>" (You are indeed the waters); "<s>Yo vo vṛtābhyaḥ</s>" (He who from the enclosures).
9.28.7: "<s>Yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā</s>" (The herbs that are ancient); "<s>Ati viśvāḥ</s>" (Beyond all).
9.28.8: "<s>Yūyam gāvaḥ</s>" (You, O cattle); "<s>Na tā arvā</s>" (Not those horses).
9.28.9: "<s>Prati ṣyā sūnarī</s>" (This beautiful one); "<s>Satyā satyebhiḥ</s>" (True with the true).
9.28.10: "<s>Rātrī vyakhyat</s>" (Night has appeared); "Your observers, O Night, ninety-nine are yoked, eighty, and then your seventy-seven."
9.28.11: Two [verses beginning with] "<s>Dve te sukiṃśukam</s>."
9.28.12: "<s>Ā Indra yāhi haribhiḥ</s>" (Come, O <s>Indra</s>, with bay horses); "<s>Sakhe Viṣṇo</s>" (O friend <s>Viṣṇu</s>).
9.28.13: "<s>Syonā pṛthivi</s>" (O friendly earth); "<s>Balitthā parvatānām</s>" (By the might of the mountains).
9.28.14: "<s>Devīm vācam</s>" (Divine speech); "<s>Yad vāg vadantī</s>" (What speech speaking).
9.28.15: "<s>Mātā Rudrāṇām</s>" (Mother of the <s>Rudras</s>); "<s>Vacovidam</s>" (Knower of speech).
9.28.16: And the offerings for the directions.
9.28.17: For <s>Agni</s>, for <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>, for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, for the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, for <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
9.28.18: When [the rite] is completed, and at the concluding (<s>udavasānīyā</s>) [ceremony], with the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> milk offering, one who has constructed the fire-altar should not engage in sexual intercourse without having sacrificed.

body.translated_text:
10.1.1: On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, they consecrate themselves for the twelve-day [sacrifice].
10.1.2: Twelve <s>dīkṣās</s> (consecrations).
10.1.3: Twelve <s>upasads</s> (approach-offerings).
10.1.4: Twelve pressing days (<s>sutya</s>).
10.1.5: An <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite) is the first and last of the pressing days.
10.1.6: In the middle are ten nights.
10.1.7: A six-day <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant cycle).
10.1.8: Three <s>Chandoma</s> (metre-days).
10.1.9: [And] the tenth day.
10.1.10: "<s>Ayam yajñaḥ</s>" (This sacrifice) is the <s>yājyā</s> of the <s>Hāriyojana</s> [rite].
10.1.11: Without the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s>, without being directed, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest], having recited "<s>Parā yāhi maghavan</s>" (Go forth, O bountiful one), or "<s>Jāyed astam</s>" (Having conquered, homeward), pronounces the <s>atipraiṣa</s> (over-direction) "<s>Iha mada eva maghavan</s>" (Here indeed is the intoxication, O bountiful one) from the second day onward.
10.1.12: Or at the introductory [rite], as traditionally recorded.
10.1.13: "Tomorrow is the pressing day. O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, to you I declare [this] — to all the gods, to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, to those worthy of <s>Soma</s>, to the <s>Soma</s>-drinkers. O <s>Brahman</s>, grant speech" — thus the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> [priest], sitting behind his own <s>dhiṣṇya</s>.
10.1.14: This is constant before the last day.
10.1.15: [The rite] concludes with the wives' offerings (<s>patnīsaṃyāja</s>).
10.1.16: The blessings are not recited.
10.1.17: And the names are not taken.
10.1.18: At the introductory and concluding [rites], [the recitation] is <s>Sārasvata</s> [in form].
10.1.19: Or <s>Mādhucchandasa</s>.
10.1.20: In two-night [sacrifices] and above, in the day-combinations where the <s>Hotṛ</s> recites the <s>Āśvina</s> [<s>śastra</s>], there the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> should recite the morning <s>anuvāka</s> (recitation section).

body.translated_text: 10.2.1: With the <s>Trivṛt</s> (ninefold) <s>stoma</s> (chant-type), <s>Rathantara</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), [in the form of] an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> — the first day of the ten-day [rite] (<s>Daśarātrika</s>). 10.2.2: 'Approaching the sacrifice' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> [recitation] when [the cups are] distributed separately; 'forth for you, to the god' — when combined. 10.2.3: [The hymns] of <s>Madhucchandas</s> [form] the <s>prauga</s> (introductory recitation). 10.2.4: 'May <s>Indra</s> come with his help' — [this is] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 10.2.5: 'May <s>Indra</s> [come] to us from afar' — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. 10.2.6: 'O <s>Agni</s>, possessor of radiance — radiant are you among the gods; may I become radiant among humans' — he partakes of the <s>atigrāhya</s> (additional cup) [with this]. 10.2.7: 'They yoke the mind; here, here; your steed; the knowing one' — or excluding the last [verse] — this is the modification in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 10.2.8: The <s>Pañcajanīya</s> (five-people) [verse] is the concluding verse (<s>paridhānīyā</s>) everywhere for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 10.2.9: 'Forth, for the host' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. 10.2.10: Seven, from that onward, are <s>Ukthya</s> [days]. 10.2.11: The fourth [day] ends with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteenfold). 10.3.1: With the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold) <s>stoma</s>, <s>Bṛhat</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> — the second [day]. 10.3.2: 'We choose <s>Agni</s> as messenger' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> when distributed. 10.3.3: 'You indeed, like <s>Kṣaitava</s>' — when combined, everywhere excluding the last [verse]. 10.3.4: [The hymns] of <s>Gṛtsamada</s> [form] the <s>prauga</s>. 10.3.5: 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, those your thousandfold [gifts]' — two [verses]; 'the strong <s>Somas</s>, come' — one; 'of the bright one, the first' — one; 'both gods touching heaven' — two; 'this for you, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>' — four <s>tṛcas</s> (triplets); 'and she, our <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the terrible' — these are the <s>prauga</s> triplets. 10.3.6: 'Of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; indeed <s>Indra</s>; <s>Soma</s>-drinker' — the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 10.3.7: 'Arise, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>' — the <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> <s>pragātha</s> (paired verse). 10.3.8: 'O <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Soma</s>; O <s>Soma</s>-drinker' — [this is] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 10.3.9: 'Whatever your protection' — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. 10.3.10: 'O <s>Indra</s>, possessor of might — mighty are you among the gods; may I become mighty among humans' — he partakes of the <s>atigrāhya</s> [with this]. 10.3.11: 'Of the All-God (<s>Viśvadeva</s>)' — the opening [verse] of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 10.3.12: 'Of this, indeed, the most self-glorious' — the following [verses]. 10.3.13: 'To the All-God' — the accompanying [verse]. 10.3.14: 'That of the god; for you indeed, heaven and earth; of the sacrifice, you' — the modifications in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 10.3.15: 'Of <s>Pṛkṣa</s>; of the bull; for the bull-host; now indeed the mighty-born' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>.

body.translated_text: 10.4.1: With the <s>Saptadaśa</s> (seventeenfold) <s>stoma</s>, <s>Vairūpa</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> — the third [day]. 10.4.2: 'Yoke the most god-invoked ones' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> when distributed. 10.4.3: 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, [are lord of] the <s>Vasus</s>' — when combined, everywhere excluding the last [verse]. 10.4.4: The <s>Auṣṇiha-Ātreya</s> [hymns form] the <s>prauga</s>. 10.4.5: 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come for the enjoyment' — one [verse]; 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come, auspicious' — two; '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, of these pressed [<s>Somas</s>]' — two; 'this <s>Soma</s>, pressed in the bowl' — one; '<s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s> — come here; come with the pressing stones; with all the gods; and, O dear one' — these are the <s>prauga</s> triplets. 10.4.6: 'Him, that very; three; <s>Indra</s>'s <s>Soma</s>s' — the opening and following [verses] of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 10.4.7: 'May <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth' — the <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> <s>pragātha</s>. 10.4.8: 'Three; <s>Aryaman</s>' — [this is] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 10.4.9: 'When, O <s>Indra</s>, heaven; O <s>Indra</s>; O <s>Indra</s>, as great as' — the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> <s>pragātha</s>s of the <s>Vairūpa</s>. 10.4.10: 'O <s>Indra</s>, threefold' — the <s>sāma</s> <s>pragātha</s>. 10.4.11: 'I became; who born' — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. 10.4.12: 'O <s>Sūrya</s>, possessor of splendor — splendid are you among the gods; may I become splendid among humans' — he partakes of the <s>atigrāhya</s> [with this]. 10.4.13: 'To you, O god' — the accompanying [verse]. 10.4.14: 'Up, that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, golden; ghee-rich; of the worlds' — two triplets; 'the horseless one, born from afar' — the modifications in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 10.4.15: 'Of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; the flow-stream; you, O <s>Agni</s>, the first <s>Aṅgiras</s> <s>Ṛṣi</s>' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>.

body.translated_text: 10.5.1: With the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-onefold) <s>stoma</s>, <s>Vairāja</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> — the fourth [day]. 10.5.2: 'Like <s>Agni</s>, with your own [praises]' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> when distributed; '<s>Agni</s>, by men' — when combined. 10.5.3: The <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> (anuṣṭubh-metered hymns form) the <s>prauga</s>. 10.5.4: 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, the bright one, I come to you' — one [verse]; 'For the offering' — two; '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, of these <s>Somas</s>; who discerns; with all your helps; to you; food' — one; 'For you indeed' — two; 'She gave' — these are the <s>prauga</s> triplets. 10.5.5: 'May the goddess [come] forth for us' — when combined. 10.5.6: 'You, with sacrifices' — the opening [verse] of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 10.5.7: Those that are the [opening verses] of the first three-day [period] are the following [verses] of the next, together with the <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s>. 10.5.8: 'Hear the call, O <s>Indra</s>; O <s>Indra</s> accompanied by <s>Maruts</s>; this one, the crafty' — two triplets — [this is] the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. 10.5.9: 'Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; may it delight you' — the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> of the <s>Vairāja</s> [with the] <s>nyūṅkha</s> (insertion). 10.5.10: Of the middle foot, at the second and seventh syllables — twice the former, twice the latter — thus the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> [pattern]. 10.5.11: 'Whom [you pressed], O beloved <s>Hari</s>, the pressing stone' — thus. 10.5.12: At the second syllable, twelve times, one prolonged [syllable] each, with three short ones in between — thus the <s>Vairāja</s> [pattern]. 10.5.13: 'Whom you pressed' — thus. 10.5.14: At the second and fourth syllables of the response, the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> counter-insertion (<s>pratinyūṅkha</s>). 10.5.15: At the second, the <s>Vairāja</s> [pattern]. 10.5.16: 'And indeed, rejoicing, indeed' — thus. 10.5.17: 'And indeed, rejoicing' — thus. 10.5.18: '<s>Indra</s> indeed, at the worship of the gods' — the <s>sāma</s> <s>pragātha</s>. 10.5.19: 'For you this' — the <s>nyūṅkha</s> of the first two of three [verses]. 10.5.20: 'Where heard; of you the fighting; that one indeed; the all-conquering' — three [verses] — [this is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>. 10.5.21: The opening [verse] is from the second day. 10.5.22: 'Golden-handed' — the accompanying [verse]. 10.5.23: 'May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> come, of good treasures; forth, heaven and earth, with sacrifices and homages; forth for the <s>Ṛbhus</s>; forth may the bright goddess go' — the modifications in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 10.5.24: 'Forth the sovereign; who indeed; the manifest; I invoke you; the well-shining' — [this is] the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>.

body.translated_text:
10.6.1: The fifth [day has] the <s>Triṇava</s> (three-times-nine) <s>stoma</s> (praise-form) with the <s>Śākvara</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (backbone chant).
10.6.2: 'This one indeed' — nine verses [form] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee-hymn) when [the <s>stoma</s>] is distributed (<s>vyūḍha</s>); 'I think him as fire' when [it is] combined (<s>samūḍha</s>).
10.6.3: Of the first [verse], pausing foot by foot, then pausing after two [feet], he chants the <s>praṇava</s> with the [last] one.
10.6.4: The <s>Paṅkti</s> recitation [follows] after.
10.6.5: The <s>Prauga</s> (introductory hymn) is in <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter].
10.6.6: 'May our sacrifice reach the sky' — two [verses]; 'Come to us, O <s>Vāyu</s>' — one; 'We have a thousand' — three; 'Richly, thus' — two; 'Forth for <s>Mitra</s>' — one; 'These for you, O heavenly ones,' 'Come to us, all,' 'Well-invoked,' 'God by god for your aid,' 'God by god,' 'She has given' — these are the <s>Prauga</s> triplets.
10.6.7: 'And this our <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the fierce one' — when combined.
10.6.8: 'With the five peoples' — this is the opening verse (<s>pratipat</s>) of the <s>Marutvatīya</s> (hymn for <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>).
10.6.9: 'Thus indeed in the <s>Soma</s>, O helper,' 'O <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>, O bull,' 'This one by whom' — three [verses] — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
10.6.10: The <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> (Great Names) are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-verses).
10.6.11: As [there are] three <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [verses], so each one [is treated] separately.
10.6.12: The last [foot] of the last [verse is in] <s>Paṅkti</s> [meter].
10.6.13: And in the latter half, the five <s>padas</s> (feet) at the end — they call them 'filling' (<s>purīṣa</s>); that is the <s>nivid</s> (insertion) recitation.
10.6.14: 'To him who would be gratified,' 'He who is richest in riches,' 'That irresistible one of yours' — three triplets; 'To him, to him' — the tenth [verse]; 'Indeed you are the heroic one' — or this is the <s>anurūpa</s> (response-verse).
10.6.15: 'When <s>Indra</s> [is] among the <s>Nāhuṣīs</s>' — this is the <s>Sāma</s> <s>pragātha</s> (chant-pair).
10.6.16: '<s>Indra</s> for exhilaration,' 'Forth, this sacred utterance,' 'The one,' 'We urge <s>Indra</s> to strength' — three [verses] — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> (exclusive recitation).
10.6.17: 'That excellent [light] of <s>Savitṛ</s>' — this is the response-verse (<s>anucara</s>).
10.6.18: 'Up, that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, the home-maker' — three; 'Great heaven and earth' — four; '<s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Vibhvan</s>,' 'Who indeed for you, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,' 'Forth, O most praiseworthy' — or [this is] the modification for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [hymn].
10.6.19: 'The offering purified,' 'Form indeed,' '<s>Agni</s>, the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the house-lord' — three — this is the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> (for <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>).
10.6.20: 'The head,' 'O <s>Rudras</s>,' 'This one indeed' — nine — when combined.

body.translated_text:
10.7.1: The sixth [day has] the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-fold) <s>stoma</s> with the <s>Raivata</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s>.
10.7.2: They offer by joining the <s>Pārucchepa</s> [hymns] with the regular offering-verses (<s>yājyā</s>s).
10.7.3: 'Come to you, speeding,' 'Come to you, O thought' — these are the invitatory verses (<s>puronuvākyā</s>s) for the offering to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>.
10.7.4: 'The sacred grass is strewn,' 'Come, your chariot' — these are the <s>yājyā</s>s (offering verses).
10.7.5: 'Well-pressed' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; the next is the <s>yājyā</s>.
10.7.6: 'You two, with hymns of praise' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> for the <s>Āśvina</s> [offering]; the next is the <s>yājyā</s>.
10.7.7: 'O mighty <s>Indra</s>,' 'That cow of yours,' 'In all [rites] indeed you,' 'Do not from us,' 'Come to us,' 'May the wives,' 'May those grant us' — the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>'s <s>Dvipada</s> [verse] and <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; '<s>Agni</s> as <s>Hotṛ</s>,' '<s>Dadhyañc</s> indeed' — with these they offer the <s>prasthita</s> (extended) [offerings] at the morning pressing.
10.7.8: 'For you, O impeller' — one [verse] each from the two <s>sūktas</s>, beyond the seasonal directions (<s>ṛtu-praiṣa</s>s).
10.7.9: The <s>Adhvaryu</s> and the householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>) offer by themselves.
10.7.11: 'Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>,' 'Well-pressed,' 'For <s>Indra</s> indeed,' 'The sky,' 'With you, O <s>Maghavan</s> (bountiful one),' 'Protect us, O <s>Indra</s>,' 'Now, thus,' 'Your lesser,' 'Great,' '<s>Indra</s> wins by pressing' — this is the modification for the midday [pressing].
10.7.12: 'And the mother of the great heaven' — [this is] for the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> at the third pressing.
10.7.13: They offer without the [<s>Soma</s>-]carrying [hymns].
10.7.14: Or with the single-day [hymns].

body.translated_text:
10.8.1: 'This one was born' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s>.
10.8.2: The <s>Prauga</s> is in <s>Aticchanda</s>s (extended meters).
10.8.3: 'The grass is strewn,' 'Come, your chariot,' 'This for <s>Mitra</s>,' 'You two, with hymns,' 'O mighty <s>Indra</s>' — one [verse]; 'Your lesser, great <s>Indra</s>' — two; 'O now, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'She has given' — these are the <s>Prauga</s> triplets.
10.8.4: 'And our beloved' — when combined.
10.8.5: 'That ancient one' — [this is] the opening verse of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
10.8.6: 'Your chariot,' 'He who is the bull,' 'O <s>Indra</s> with <s>Maruts</s>, O liberal one' — three — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
10.8.7: 'O rich ones,' 'Rich indeed,' 'O wealthy one' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> of the <s>Raivata</s> [chant].
10.8.8: 'Let none other' — [this is] the <s>Sāma</s> <s>gātha</s> (chant-verse).
10.8.9: 'Come, O <s>Indra</s>,' 'Forth indeed of this,' 'To us with the bay horses' — three — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
10.8.10: 'That god' — [this is] the opening verse of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
10.8.11: Of that [verse], pausing after the sixteen-syllable [portion], chanting the <s>praṇava</s> after the eighteen-syllable [portion], pausing after the fifteen-syllable [portion], [and] after the fifteen-syllable [portion again].
10.8.12: 'Of him, the most self-glorious' — [these are] the subsequent [verses].
10.8.13: The response-verse is from the third day.
10.8.14: 'Up, that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, for impelling,' 'Which of the two is the first?' 'What is the best?' 'This thus' — having set aside the last [verses], having recited 'Those who by sacrifice,' he recites what was set aside — this is the modification for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
10.8.15: 'The day and the dark one,' 'O sacrificers,' 'This hymn of praise' — this is the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>.
10.8.16: From the middle three-day [period], he releases the final triplets of the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> and <s>Marutvatīya</s> [when they are] combined.
10.8.17: And he adds 'May she measure out well-being for us' — three [verses] — at the end of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>s.
10.8.18: 'That woven one for me' — [this is] the <s>Ārbhava</s> (hymn for the <s>Ṛbhus</s>) of the fourth [day].
10.8.19: 'Forth, may the prizes go' — three [verses] at the end of the <s>Māruta</s> (hymn for the <s>Maruts</s>).
10.8.20: 'The rich one of wondrous might' — [this is] the <s>Jātavedas</s> hymn.
10.8.21: [For the rites] having the <s>Parokṣa</s> (hidden), <s>Bṛhad-Rathantara</s>, <s>Upāṅkya</s>, <s>Apārkya</s>, <s>Tanū</s> as <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [chants], and the <s>Chandoruṭ</s> <s>stoma</s> — the <s>stotriya</s>s, <s>anurūpa</s>s, and <s>Sāma</s> <s>pragātha</s>s [follow] according to the <s>Chandoga</s> (chanter's) practice.
10.8.22: The rest is the same as with the combined [form].
10.8.23: Likewise in the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering sacrifice).

body.translated_text:
10.9.1: The seventh [day has] the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-four-fold) <s>stoma</s> with the <s>Bṛhat</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, [using] both <s>Sāmans</s> (chants).
10.9.2: 'Forth to you, the bright ones' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s>.
10.9.3: The <s>Prauga</s> is in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [meter].
10.9.4: 'Forth for the heroic,' 'By your truth,' 'Up, your eye,' 'Come, with cows,' 'O God,' 'Forth, at the sacrifices,' 'Forth, with the impelling [one]' — these are the <s>Prauga</s> triplets.
10.9.5: The opening and response verses of the first day of the three-day period, together with those belonging to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, are [used] in the <s>Chandomas</s> (meter-days), in the <s>Svara-Sāman</s>s (intonation-chants), and in the <s>Abhiplava</s> (six-day period).
10.9.6: From the first [day of the three-day period] come those of the first day of the <s>Chāndoma</s>.
10.9.7: From the second, those of the second.
10.9.8: From the third, those of the third.
10.9.9: Likewise for the earlier three-day period of the <s>Abhiplava</s>.
10.9.10: And likewise for the later [three-day period].
10.9.11: Likewise for the <s>Svara-Sāman</s>s.
10.9.12: 'With what beauty?' 'That good ram' — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
10.9.13: 'Praise him,' 'That ram' — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
10.9.14: One should not recite according to the <s>Kaṇva</s> <s>Rathantara</s> scheme.
10.9.15: The opening and response verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> from the first two days are [used] in the <s>Chandomas</s> and in the <s>Abhiplava</s>.
10.9.16: 'That excellent [light] of <s>Savitṛ</s>,' 'Go forth to the sacrifice,' 'This for the god' — triplets; 'Rightly led' — five; 'Go with food together,' '<s>Oma</s>,' 'Upholder of peoples' — three [verses] — [this is] the modification for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
10.9.17a: '<s>Vaiśvānara</s> for our aid'; '<s>Vaiśvānara</s> has come'; 'Accept this sacrifice together'; '<s>Agni</s> with the <s>uktha</s> (recitation) as vehicle.'
10.9.17b: '<s>Vaiśvānara</s> of the <s>Aṅgirasas</s> generated the hymn and the sacrifice'; 'In these, the glory going to the sun'; 'Forth to you, in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>' — fifteen or nine [verses]; 'Praising you' — this is the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 10.10.1: The forty-four-fold <s>stoma</s> (chant-type) with <s>Rathantara</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) — the eighth [day].
ŚŚS 10.10.2: 'O <s>Agni</s>, your god...' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee-offering hymn).
ŚŚS 10.10.3: The <s>prauga</s> (introductory litany) is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter.
ŚŚS 10.10.4: 'Kuvid aṅga' — the first [verse]; in the third [pressing], 'Ā Vāyo bhūṣa' and one more; as far as extended — 'Prati vām sūra udite,' 'Apa svasur,' 'Ayam somaḥ,' 'Pra brahmāṇa,' 'Uta syā naḥ Sarasvatī juṣāṇā' — these are the <s>prauga</s> triplets.
ŚŚS 10.10.5: 'Mahān Indraḥ,' 'Nṛvat,' 'Imā u tvā,' 'Purutamasya,' 'Kva sya vīra' — everywhere passing over the last four [verses] — 'Mahaś cit,' 'Tam asya,' 'Dyāvāpṛthivī' — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> (hymn associated with the <s>Maruts</s>).
ŚŚS 10.10.6: 'Tvam mahān Indra,' 'Tubhyam ha,' 'Tvam mahān Indra yo ha,' 'Apūrvyā,' 'Tām su te kīrtim,' 'Imām te dhiyam' — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> (the exclusive hymn).
ŚŚS 10.10.7: 'Hiraṇya-pāṇim ūtaye' — four [verses]; 'Mahī dyaur' [and] 'Yuvānā pitarā' — two triplets; 'Devānām it,' 'Imā nu kam,' 'Viśve devā ṛtāvṛdha' — three [verses] — this is the modification in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (hymn for All-Gods).
ŚŚS 10.10.8: 'Vaiśvānaro ajījanat'; '<s>Agni</s>, grant us a new thought; growing with the might of the earth; O purifying bull, shine forth; O <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, brilliantly; offered by the <s>Jamadagnis</s>'; '<s>Ṛtāvān</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s>'; 'Kad dha nūnam'; 'Kadha priyaḥ'; 'Your messenger, the all-knowing one' — this is [the hymn] for the <s>Āgni-Māruta</s> (associated with <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>).

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 10.11.1: The forty-eight-fold <s>stoma</s> with <s>Bṛhat</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> — the ninth [day].
ŚŚS 10.11.2: 'Aganma mahā,' 'Somasya,' 'Mā tavasam' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.11.3: Or the previous one.
ŚŚS 10.11.4: The <s>prauga</s> is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter.
ŚŚS 10.11.5: 'Ā Vāyo bhūṣa' — the first [verse] in the third [pressing]; and the last, and the second and fourth [verses]; 'Arvanto na śravase,' 'Divi kṣayantā,' 'Viśvavārā,' 'Indram nara,' 'Ūrdhvo agniḥ,' 'Pra kṣodasā' — these are the <s>prauga</s> triplets.
ŚŚS 10.11.6: 'Try aryamā,' 'Indro rathāya tiṣṭhā,' 'Harī gāyat sāma,' 'Pra mandinaḥ' — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.11.7: 'Ā satyo yātv,' 'Asmā id u,' 'Ya Indra tat,' 'Ta indriyam,' 'Aham bhuvam viśvajit' — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.11.8: 'Abhi tvā deva,' 'Pra vām,' 'Mahī dyavī' — two triplets; 'Indra iṣa' — one [verse]; 'Te no ratnāni' — two; 'Agnir uktha' and following — five hymns of <s>Manu</s>; extracting the penultimate [verse] 'Ye triṃśati'; 'Na hi vo asty arbhaka' — one; 'Aśarmā' — four [verses]; 'Babhrur eka' or 'Manu-pravalha'; 'Viśve devāsa ā gata' — a triplet; 'Bhāradvājam' — this is the modification in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
ŚŚS 10.11.9: 'On heaven's back he has shone — <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the great; with his light he drives away the darkness'; 'He has pervaded all; he who controls, releases the seasons at will; they have extended the warp of the sacrifice'; '<s>Agni</s> in the highest abodes'; '<s>Maruts</s>, whose <s>Agni</s> is the <s>Hotṛ</s> and the <s>Purohita</s>' — this is the <s>Āgni-Māruta</s>.
ŚŚS 10.11.10: The third-pressing [hymns] of the morning pressing of the first day of the three-day [cycle] are the same in the combined (<s>samūḍha</s>) [arrangement] of the <s>chandomas</s>.
ŚŚS 10.11.11: And in the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> and <s>Marutvatīya</s>, the <s>Jagatī</s> [verses] are released.
ŚŚS 10.11.12: 'Sa yo vṛṣā' [and] fifteen [verses] upward — one should chant with 'Kayā śubhā.'
ŚŚS 10.11.13: 'Yo jāta' — one should chant with 'Tam u ṣṭuhi.'
ŚŚS 10.11.14: On the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s> [days], all [hymns] have double <s>sūkta</s> [arrangement].

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 10.12.1: The <s>Avivákyā</s> (incontrovertible [day]) — the twenty-four-fold <s>stoma</s> — the tenth day.
ŚŚS 10.12.2: The thirty-three[-fold] is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>Sāman</s>.
ŚŚS 10.12.3: The <s>Trika</s> (triple) is the mental [chant].
ŚŚS 10.12.4: The <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> in the place of the <s>Vāmadevya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.12.5: When one fails to respond, another [recites] from his own Vedic study.
ŚŚS 10.12.6: Extracting [verses] in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meter], the completion of the other meters [is achieved] — fifteen thousand <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [syllables] in one pressing.
ŚŚS 10.12.7: Thirty-two <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses].
ŚŚS 10.12.8: 'Agnim naraḥ,' 'Prati,' 'Syā sūnaryā,' 'Śubhrā' — triplets in the place of the <s>Anuṣṭubhs</s>.
ŚŚS 10.12.9: Twenty-four <s>Triṣṭubh</s> [verses].
ŚŚS 10.12.10: Likewise <s>Jagatī</s> [verses].
ŚŚS 10.12.11: Fifteen <s>pragāthas</s> (paired verses).
ŚŚS 10.12.12: And fifteen triplets in <s>Uṣṇih</s> [meter].
ŚŚS 10.12.13: And [verses] in <s>Paṅkti</s> [meter].
ŚŚS 10.12.14: The morning litany (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>) of <s>Anuṣṭubhs</s> [consists of] fifteen hundred [verses].
ŚŚS 10.12.15: Having extracted the third and fourth of the <s>stokyas</s>, [he inserts] two [verses beginning with] 'Abhi pravanta.'
ŚŚS 10.12.16: 'Acchā naḥ śīra-śociṣam' — three [verses]; 'Acchā vo agnim avasā' — these [are placed] in their stead.
ŚŚS 10.12.17: 'Prati śrutāya' — three [verses]; 'Praty asmai pipīṣate' — these [are placed] in their stead.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 10.13.1: 'Agne tam adya' — [this is] the <s>ājya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.2: In its first [verse], having separated with a five-syllable [unit], concluding with two five-syllable [units], he chants with two [units].
ŚŚS 10.13.3: The <s>prauga</s> is of [the hymns of] <s>Madhucchandas</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.4: Twenty-two <s>Gāyatrī</s> [verses].
ŚŚS 10.13.5: 'Mṛjāno vāre pavamāno avyaye' — the <s>grāvastut</s> (praise of the pressing-stones), according to desire.
ŚŚS 10.13.6: 'Uttiṣṭhann ojasā' — one [verse], in the place of 'Uttiṣṭhata ava paśyata.'
ŚŚS 10.13.7: The <s>Trikadruka</s> [hymns] are the beginning of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.8: Of that [hymn], having separated with a sixteen-syllable [unit], chanting with a sixteen-syllable [unit], concluding with a sixteen-syllable [unit], [and proceeding] with a sixteen-syllable [unit].
ŚŚS 10.13.9: 'Tuviśuṣma' — the later [verses].
ŚŚS 10.13.10: From the hymn 'Bṛhad Indrāya,' the first two <s>pragāthas</s>; 'Pinvanty apīyayā' — he recites together — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.11: Having recited the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> [verses] of the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, then upward from the <s>Dhyāyyā</s>, the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>pragātha</s> and the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.12: 'Sakhāya ā śiṣāmahi' — nine [verses].
ŚŚS 10.13.13: 'Ā dhūrṣu,' 'Asmai vajram,' 'Eka' — and the two-footed [verse].
ŚŚS 10.13.14: And the <s>Hairaṇyastūpīya</s> [hymn].
ŚŚS 10.13.15: Before the <s>Hairaṇyastūpīya</s>, he recites together with a <s>pragātha</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.16: Thus [is] the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.17: From the sixth [day], the beginning and following [verses] of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.18: And before the <s>Ā no bhadrīya</s> [section], the <s>Pra śukrīya</s> — this is the modification in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.19: Having extracted 'Uru Viṣṇav,' he offers with 'Bhavā Mitra.'
ŚŚS 10.13.20: 'Agnim nara' — these are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>Sāman</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.21: 'Āyam gaur' [and] 'Mahī dyaur' — the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.22: 'Tam pratnathā' — thirteen [verses].
ŚŚS 10.13.23: 'Yajño babhūva' — having encircled [with this verse].
ŚŚS 10.13.23: He offers with 'Prajāpata.'
ŚŚS 10.13.24: The call (<s>āhāva</s>) with <s>ukthas</s> (praises) has been explained.
ŚŚS 10.13.25: Thus, in the combined [arrangement], the supplementary <s>uktha</s>.
ŚŚS 10.13.26: Having completed before the wife-offerings (<s>patnī-saṃyājas</s>), or having offered in the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, entering the <s>Sadas</s> through the eastern door, sitting behind his own fire-hearth, being praised with the mental [chant] — 'Āyam gaur' — the <s>Sārparājñī</s> [verses], silently beyond, without chanting.
ŚŚS 10.13.27: When addressed 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>!', he responds everywhere with 'Hoyi, O <s>Hotṛ</s>!'
ŚŚS 10.13.28: He responds 'Om, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, so be it, O <s>Hotṛ</s>' — when [the <s>Hotṛ</s>] is declaring.

body.translated_text:
10.14.1: [Saying] 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>!' — when about to recite the <s>Daśahotra</s> (ten-priest formula).
10.14.2: [The narrative:] '<s>Prajāpati</s> desired: "May I become many, may I procreate, may I pervade all this Veda, whatever there is [of gods, men, and so forth]." He perceived this <s>Daśahotra</s> sacrificial rite — the <s>Agnihotra</s>.'
10.14.3: Having said this, then [he recites] in a low voice:
10.14.4: 'Thought (<s>citti</s>) is the ladle; intention (<s>citta</s>) is the ghee; speech (<s>vāc</s>) is the altar; learning (<s>ādhīta</s>) is the sacred grass; perception (<s>keta</s>) is the fire; understanding (<s>vijñāta</s>) is the fire-kindler; the lord of speech (<s>Vācaspati</s>) is the <s>hotṛ</s>; mind (<s>manas</s>) is the prompter; breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is the oblation; <s>Sāma</s> is the <s>adhvaryu</s>' — these are the [ten] priests.
10.14.5: Then the cup [offering].
10.14.6: [The formula begins:] 'vācaspataye...' (To the lord of speech)...

body.translated_text:
10.15.1: [Saying] 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>!' — when about to recite the <s>Caturhotra</s> (four-priest formula).
10.15.2: [The narrative:] 'Only two [groups] remained with him — the gods and men. The <s>Asuras</s> were turned away from him. He desired: "May a hero be born to me, by whom I may overcome these <s>Asuras</s>." He perceived this <s>Caturhotra</s> sacrificial rite — the new-and-full-moon sacrifices.'
10.15.3: Having said this, then in a low voice:
10.15.4: '<s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) is the <s>hotṛ</s>; <s>Dyaus</s> (Heaven) is the <s>adhvaryu</s>; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is the fire-kindler; <s>Mitra</s> is the prompter' — these are the [four] priests.
10.15.5: Then the cup [offering].
10.15.6: [The formula:] 'vācaspate vāco vīryeṇa sambhṛtatamena āyacchase' (O lord of speech, thou drawest near with the most collected vigor of speech). 'For the lord of sacrifice...'

body.translated_text:
10.16.1: [Saying] 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>!' — when about to recite the <s>Pañcahotra</s> (five-priest formula).
10.16.2: [The narrative:] 'The deities did not submit to him, to <s>Indra</s>, for supremacy and preeminence. He perceived this <s>Pañcahotra</s> sacrificial rite — the <s>Cāturmāsyas</s> (four-monthly sacrifices).'
10.16.3: Having said this, then in a low voice:
10.16.4: '<s>Agni</s> is the <s>hotṛ</s>; the two <s>Aśvins</s> are the <s>adhvaryus</s>; <s>Rudra</s> is the fire-kindler; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the prompter' — these are the [five] priests.
10.16.5: Then the cup [offering].
10.16.6: [The formula:] 'vācaspate achidrayā vācā achidrayā juhvā | divi devā vṛdhan hotrām airayasva' (O lord of speech, with unbroken speech, with unbroken tongue; the gods grew strong in heaven — rouse up the invocation).
10.16.7: [This is recited] in a low voice.
10.16.8: Then [the narrative continues:] 'The deities then submitted to <s>Indra</s> for supremacy...'

body.translated_text:
10.17.1: [Saying] 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>!' — when about to recite the <s>Ṣaḍḍhotra</s> (six-priest formula).
10.17.2: [The narrative:] 'He desired: "May I be a food-eater, a lord of food." He perceived this <s>Ṣaḍḍhotra</s> sacrificial rite — the animal sacrifice (<s>paśubandha</s>).'
10.17.3: Having said this, then in a low voice:
10.17.4: 'The sun is thy eye; <s>Vāyu</s> is [thy] breath; the atmosphere is [thy] self; sacrifice is [thy] limbs; heaven is [thy] back; earth is [thy] body' — these are the [six] priests.
10.17.5: Then the cup [offering].
10.17.6: [The formula:] 'somaḥ somasya pibatu śukraḥ śukrasya pibatu | śrātās ta indra somā vātāpe havana śrutaḥ' (May Soma drink of Soma; may the bright one drink of the bright; the Soma juices are cooked for thee, O <s>Indra</s>; O <s>Vātāpi</s>, heard at the invocation).
10.17.7: [This is recited] in a low voice.
10.17.8: Then...

ŚŚS_10.18.8: tato.vai.tebhyo.akalpat.|.te.devāḥ.klṛptāḥ.klṛpteṣu.lokeṣv.āsan.|.apy.adya.klṛptāḥ.klṛpteṣu.|.sa.yeṣām.vā.evam.vidvān.hotā.bhavati.|.kalpate.vai.tasmai.hotre.yoga.kṣemahṇ.|.kalpate.tebhyo.yajamānebhyo.yoga.kṣemaḥ.|.abhi.vai.sa.hotā.svargam.lokam.aśnute.praty.asmiṃl.loke.pratitiṣṭhati.|.abhi.te.yajamānāḥ.svargam.lokam.aśnuvate.praty.asmiṃl.loke.pratitiṣṭhanti.yeṣām.evam.vidvān.hotā.bhavati.iti /
body.translated_text:
10.18.1: [Saying] 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>!' — when about to recite the <s>Saptahotra</s> (seven-priest formula).
10.18.2: [The narrative:] 'The gods desired: "May we be properly established in properly established worlds." They perceived this <s>Saptahotra</s> sacrificial rite — the Soma sacrifice (<s>Saumya adhvara</s>).'
10.18.3: Having said this, then in a low voice:
10.18.4: 'The great oblation (<s>Mahāhavis</s>) is the <s>hotṛ</s>; the true oblation (<s>Satyahavis</s>) is the <s>adhvaryu</s>; the unperceived protector (<s>Acittapāja</s>) is the fire-kindler; the unperceived mind (<s>Acittamanas</s>) is the prompter; the unassailable (<s>Anādhṛṣya</s>) and the irresistible (<s>Apratidhṛṣya</s>) are the two assistants; <s>Ayāsya</s> is the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanter)' — these are the [seven] priests.
10.18.5: Then the cup [offering].
10.18.6: [The formula:] 'vācaspate vidhe nāman vidhema te nāma | vidhes tvam asmākaṃ nāma' (O lord of speech, we would worship thy name, O [thou of] worship; do thou worship our name). 'mā...'

body.text:

ŚŚS_10.19.2f: adhvaryo.yeṣām.vā.anāptām.prajāpates.tanvam.vidvān.hotā.bhavaty.anāpto.vai.sa.hotā.bhavaty.anāptās.te.yajamānā.bhavanti /
ŚŚS_10.19.2g: adhvaryo.yeṣām.anāpyām.prajāpates.tanvam.vidvana.hotā.bhavaty.anāpyo.vai.sa.hotā.bhavaty.anāpyas.te.yajamānā.bhavanti /

ŚŚS_10.19.2i: adhvaryo.yeṣām.vā.anādhṛṣṭyām.prajāpates.tanvam.vidvān.hotā.bhavaty.anādhṛṣyo.vai.sa.hotā.bhavaty.anādhṛṣyās.te.yajamānā.bhavanti /
ŚŚS_10.19.2j: adhvaryo.yeṣām.vā.apūrvām.prajāpates.tanvam.vidvān.hotā.bhavati.na.vai.tasmādd.hotur.anyaḥ.pūrvo.bhavati.na.tebhyo.yajamānebhyo.anye.pūrve.bhavanti /
ŚŚS_10.19.2k: adhvaryo.yeṣām.vā.abhrātṛbhyām.prajāpates.tanvam.vidvān.hotā.bhavaty.abhrātṛvyo.vai.sa.hotā.bhavaty.abhrātṛvyās.te.yajamānā.bhavanti.yeṣām.evam.vidvān.hotā.bhavati.iti /
body.translated_text:
10.19.1: Then he recites the <s>Tanūḥ</s> (body) [section].
10.19.2a: 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he who, knowing the food-eating body of <s>Prajāpati</s>, becomes the <s>hotṛ</s> for those [sacrificers] — he indeed becomes a food-eating <s>hotṛ</s>, and those sacrificers become food-eaters. O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he who, knowing the food-ruling body of <s>Prajāpati</s>, becomes the <s>hotṛ</s> for those [sacrificers] — he indeed becomes a food-ruling <s>hotṛ</s>, and those sacrificers become food-rulers.'
10.19.2b: 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he who, knowing the auspicious body of <s>Prajāpati</s>, becomes the <s>hotṛ</s> for those [sacrificers] — auspiciousness indeed comes to that <s>hotṛ</s>, auspiciousness comes to those sacrificers.'
10.19.2c: 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he who, knowing the beautiful body of <s>Prajāpati</s>...'

body.text:
ŚŚS_10.20.1: gṛhapatir.ato.gṛhapati.vadanam /
ŚŚS_10.20.2a: adhvaryo.yeṣām.vai.gṛhapatir.gṛhapatim.vidvān.gṛhapatir.bhavati.rādhnoti.vai.sa.gṛhapatī.rādhnuvanti.te.yajamānāḥ /
ŚŚS_10.20.2b: adhvaryo.yeṣām.vā.apahata.pāpmānam.evam.vidvān.gṛhapatir.bhavaty.apa.vai.sa.gṛhapatiḥ.pāpmānam.hate.apa.te.yajamānāḥ.pāpmānam.ghnate.yeṣām.evam.vidvān.gṛhapatir.bhavati.iti /
body.translated_text:
10.20.1: The <s>gṛhapati</s> (householder) — hereafter [follows] the declaration of the <s>gṛhapati</s>.
10.20.2a: "O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he for whom a <s>gṛhapati</s> who knows the [nature of the] <s>gṛhapati</s> serves [as <s>gṛhapati</s>] — that <s>gṛhapati</s> indeed prospers, and those <s>yajamānas</s> prosper."
10.20.2b: "O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, he for whom one who knows thus, one who has destroyed sin, serves as <s>gṛhapati</s> — that <s>gṛhapati</s> indeed destroys sin, and those <s>yajamānas</s> destroy sin, for whom such a knowing one serves as <s>gṛhapati</s>."

body.text:
ŚŚS_10.21.1: prajāpata.iti.manasā.yajati /
ŚŚS_10.21.2: manasā.vaṣaṭ.karoti /

ŚŚS_10.21.4: manasā.bhakṣaḥ /
ŚŚS_10.21.4: manasā.uro.abhimarśanam /
ŚŚS_10.21.6: audumbarīm.anvārabhante.agreṇa.dhiṣṇyān.āsīnāḥ /

ŚŚS_10.21.8: uttamau.pāṇī.hotā.kurvīta /
ŚŚS_10.21.9: uttamo.asāni.iti /
ŚŚS_10.21.10: apidhāya.sadaso.dvārau.śālāyāś.ca.adhvaryur.vācam.upākaroti.|.vāg.yatāḥ.sammīlya.asata.ā.nakṣatrāṇām.darśanāt /
ŚŚS_10.21.11: nakṣatreṣu.dṛśyamāneṣu.mārjālīya.deśe.tac.cakṣur.iti.nakṣatreṣu.cakṣur.visṛjante /
ŚŚS_10.21.12: sarve.sāmno.nidhanam.upetya.uttarasya.havir.dhānasya.adho.akṣam.sarpanti /
ŚŚS_10.21.13: uttarasya.uttareṇa.vā /
ŚŚS_10.21.14: yuvam.tam.indra.aparvata.ity.akṣa.velāyām.japitvā.agreṇa.havir.dhāne.samupaviśya.kāmān.dhyāyante.yat.kāmā.bhavanti /
ŚŚS_10.21.15: ye.bahu.kāmā.bhūr.bhuvaḥ.svar.ity.etās.te.vyāhṛtīr.japeyuḥ /
ŚŚS_10.21.16: te.prāñca.udañca.utkramya.vācam.vihvayante.vāg.aitu.vāg.upaitu.vāg.upa.mā.etu.vāg.iti /
ŚŚS_10.21.17: subrahmaṇyā.pratīkam.trir.upāṃśv.abhivyāhṛtya.vācam.visṛjante /
ŚŚS_10.21.18: atra.dvādaśa.ahaḥ.saṃtiṣṭhate /
ŚŚS_10.21.19: kāla.vādo.vā.kāla.vādo.vā /
body.translated_text:
10.21.1: [For the offering] to <s>Prajāpati</s>, he offers mentally.
10.21.2: He pronounces the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> mentally.
10.21.3: He pronounces the <s>anuvaṣaṭ</s> mentally.
10.21.4: The partaking is mental.
10.21.4: The touching of the chest is mental.
10.21.6: They hold onto the <s>Audumbarī</s> (fig-wood post), sitting in front of the <s>dhiṣṇyas</s> (fire-seats).
10.21.7: [They hold] <s>palāśa</s> branches so that they would not step beyond.
10.21.8: The <s>Hotṛ</s> should make [his] hands the uppermost.
10.21.9: [Thinking:] "May I be the highest."
10.21.10: Having closed the doors of the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall) and of the <s>śālā</s> (hall), the <s>Adhvaryu</s> initiates the restriction of speech: "Restrained in speech, they should sit with eyes closed until the stars become visible."
10.21.11: When the stars become visible, at the place of the <s>Mārjālīya</s> [fire], [reciting] "<s>Tat cakṣuḥ</s>" (That eye), they release their sight upon the stars.
10.21.12: All, having reached the conclusion of the <s>sāman</s> (chant), crawl under the axle of the northern <s>havirdhāna</s> (oblation cart).
10.21.13: Or [they pass] to the north of the northern [cart].
10.21.14: Having murmured "<s>Yuvam tam Indra Aparvata</s>" (You two, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Aparvata</s>) at the time of the axle [passage], sitting together in front of the <s>havirdhāna</s> carts, they meditate on their desires — whatever desires they have.
10.21.15: Those who have many desires should murmur these <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>: "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>."
10.21.16: Going forth eastward and northward, they call forth speech: "May speech come; may speech approach; may speech come to me — speech!"
10.21.17: Having thrice softly pronounced the opening of the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> [litany], they release speech.
10.21.18: Here the twelve-day [sacrifice] is concluded.
10.21.19: [This is] a discussion of time, a discussion of time.

body.text:
ŚŚS_11.1.1: vyākhyāto.dvādaśa.ahaḥ.prakṛtiḥ.satra.ahīnānām /
ŚŚS_11.1.2: vacana.lakṣaṇo.vikāraḥ /
ŚŚS_11.1.3: dvirātra.prabhṛtayo.ahīnā.dvādaśa.aha.paryantāḥ /
ŚŚS_11.1.4: dvādaśa.aha.prabhṛtīni.satrāni /
ŚŚS_11.1.5: ahīneṣu.prāyaṇīyo.na.vidyate /
ŚŚS_11.1.6: satra.dharmāś.ca /
body.translated_text:
11.1.1: The twelve-day [sacrifice] has been explained; it is the archetype (<s>prakṛti</s>) of <s>Sattras</s> (communal sacrifices) and <s>Ahīnas</s> (multi-day sacrifices).
11.1.2: Modification [from the archetype] is indicated by [specific] statement.
11.1.3: <s>Ahīnas</s> begin from the two-night [sacrifice] up to the twelve-day limit.
11.1.4: <s>Sattras</s> begin from the twelve-day [sacrifice] [onward].
11.1.5: In <s>Ahīnas</s>, the introductory (<s>prāyaṇīya</s>) [rite] does not occur.
11.1.6: And [they follow] the rules of <s>Sattras</s>.

body.text:
ŚŚS_11.2.1: caturviṃśa.stomam.bṛhat.pṛṣṭham.ubhaya.sāma.agniṣṭoma.ukthyam.vā.ahaś.caturviṃśam.ity.ācakṣate /
ŚŚS_11.2.2: hotā.ajaniṣṭa.ity.ājyam /
ŚŚS_11.2.3: mādhucchandasaḥ.praugaḥ /
ŚŚS_11.2.4: kayā.śubhīyam.marutvatīyam /
ŚŚS_11.2.5: anuttamā.ta.iti.paridhānīya.uttarāḥ.pūrvāḥ.śastvā.yatra.asmin.dhīyate.nivit /
ŚŚS_11.2.6: tad.id.āsīyam.niṣkevalyam /
ŚŚS_11.2.7: dvitīyāt.sāvitra.dyāvā.pṛthivīye /
ŚŚS_11.2.8: vaiśvadeva.mārute.ca /
ŚŚS_11.2.9: ārbhavam.ṣaṣṭhāt /
ŚŚS_11.2.10: vaiśvānarīyam.tṛtīyāt /
ŚŚS_11.2.11: yajñena.vardhata.iti.jāta.vedasīyam /
ŚŚS_11.2.12: sāma.antar.ukthyaḥ /
ŚŚS_11.2.13: yajñāyajñīyasya.stotriyeṇa.ukthya.stotriyān.saṃśasya.|.anurūpeṇa.anurūpān.|.agne.marudbhir.ṛkvabhiḥ.pā.indrā.varuṇābhyām.matsva.indrā.bṛhaspatibhyām.indrā.viṣṇubhyām.sajūr.iti.śastvā.paridadhāti /
ŚŚS_11.2.14: graha.antar.ukthya.etayā.śastayā.yajet /
body.translated_text:
11.2.1: [The day] having the twenty-four-fold <s>stoma</s>, the <s>Bṛhat</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant), the <s>sāman</s> on both sides, [being either] an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> or <s>Ukthya</s> day — they call it the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-four) day.
11.2.2: "<s>Hotā ajaniṣṭa</s>" (The <s>Hotṛ</s> was born) is the <s>Ājya</s> [recitation].
11.2.3: The <s>Mādhucchandasa</s> [verses form] the <s>prauga</s> (introduction).
11.2.4: "<s>Kayā śubhā</s>" (By what splendor) is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation].
11.2.5: "<s>Anuttamā te</s>" (Unsurpassed are those) is the concluding (<s>paridhānīya</s>) [verse]; having recited the later [verses] before the earlier, where the <s>nivid</s> (insertion) is placed.
11.2.6: "<s>Tad id āsa</s>" (That indeed was) is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [recitation].
11.2.7: From the second [day onward], the <s>Sāvitra</s> and <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s> [recitations].
11.2.8: And the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and <s>Māruta</s> [recitations].
11.2.9: The <s>Ārbhava</s> [recitation] from the sixth [day].
11.2.10: The <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> [recitation] from the third.
11.2.11: "<s>Yajñena vardhata</s>" (Increase by sacrifice) is the <s>Jātavedasīya</s> [recitation].
11.2.12: The <s>Ukthya</s> [day has the <s>sāman</s> as] an interval.
11.2.13: Having combined the <s>Ukthya</s> <s>stotriyas</s> (chant-verses) with the <s>stotriya</s> of the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> [<s>sāman</s>], and the <s>anurūpas</s> (counterparts) with the <s>anurūpa</s>, having recited "O <s>Agni</s>, with the <s>Maruts</s>"; "<s>Ṛkvabhiḥ pā</s>" (drink with the <s>ṛcs</s>); "For <s>Indra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s>"; "Rejoice with <s>Indra</s>-<s>Bṛhaspati</s>"; "With <s>Indra</s>-<s>Viṣṇu</s> together" — he encloses.
11.2.14: The <s>Ukthya</s> [day] with the <s>graha</s> (cup) interval — one should sacrifice with this recitation.

body.text:
ŚŚS_11.3.1: ekatrike.tṛca.klṛptam.śastram /
ŚŚS_11.3.2: yathā.stutam.stotriyān.śastvā.tṛcān.vā.|.yathā.stotriyam.anurūpān.sāma.pragāthāṃś.ca.śastvā.|.paryāsānām.uttamāṃs.tṛcān.hotrakāḥ.śaṃsanti /
ŚŚS_11.3.3: nividdhānānām.hotā /
ŚŚS_11.3.4: sarvam.anyat.prakṛtyā /
body.translated_text:
11.3.1: In the <s>Ekatrika</s> [rite], the recitation is arranged in triplets.
11.3.2: Having recited the <s>stotriyas</s> as chanted, or the triplets, having recited the <s>anurūpas</s> according to the <s>stotriyas</s> and the <s>sāma-pragāthas</s> (chant strophes) — the <s>Hotraka</s> (assistant <s>Hotṛ</s>) priests recite the final triplets of the <s>paryāsas</s> (concluding sections).
11.3.3: The <s>Hotṛ</s> [recites] those containing the <s>nivid</s> (insertion).
11.3.4: Everything else is according to the archetype.

body.text:
ŚŚS_11.4.1: abhiplavaḥ.ṣaḷahaḥ.pṛṣṭhya.vikāraḥ /
ŚŚS_11.4.2: yāni.tryahasya.prathamasya.ājyāni.samūḷhe.tāni.pūrveṣām.ābhipravikānām /
ŚŚS_11.4.3: rathantaram.bṛhad.iti.pṛṣṭhe.viparyāsam /
ŚŚS_11.4.4: jyotir.agniṣṭomaḥ.prathamam.uttamam.ca /
ŚŚS_11.4.5: catvāry.ukthyāni.madhye /
ŚŚS_11.4.6: gām.dvitīyam.caturtham.ca /
ŚŚS_11.4.7: āyus.tṛtīyam.pañcamam.ca /
ŚŚS_11.4.8: indro.rathāya.iti.marutvatīyam /
ŚŚS_11.4.9: ā.yāhy.arvān.iti.niṣkevalyam /
ŚŚS_11.4.10: kathā.devānām.iti.vaiśvadevam /
ŚŚS_11.4.11: pañcame.ca /
ŚŚS_11.4.12: mārutam.eka.ahāt /
ŚŚS_11.4.13: ehi.pra.hotā.iti.jāta.vedasīyam /
ŚŚS_11.4.14: samānam.anyat.prathamena.ahnā /
body.translated_text:
11.4.1: The <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day [cycle] is a modification of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [six-day cycle].
11.4.2: The <s>Ājya</s> [recitations] of the first three-day period in the combined [version] are those of the former <s>Abhiplava</s> [days].
11.4.3: The <s>Rathantara</s> and <s>Bṛhat</s> [<s>sāmans</s>] alternate as <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants) in reversed order.
11.4.4: The <s>Jyotis</s> <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [is used for] the first and last [days].
11.4.5: Four <s>Ukthya</s> [days] in the middle.
11.4.6: The <s>Go</s> (cattle) [<s>stoma</s>] for the second and fourth [days].
11.4.7: The <s>Āyus</s> (life) [<s>stoma</s>] for the third and fifth.
11.4.8: "<s>Indro rathāya</s>" (<s>Indra</s> for the chariot) is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation].
11.4.9: "<s>Ā yāhy arvān</s>" (Come hither) is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
11.4.10: "<s>Kathā devānām</s>" (How of the gods) is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
11.4.11: And [also] on the fifth [day].
11.4.12: The <s>Māruta</s> [recitation is] from the single-day [archetype].
11.4.13: "<s>Ehi pra hotā</s>" (Come forth, <s>Hotṛ</s>) is the <s>Jātavedasīya</s>.
11.4.14: The rest is the same as the first day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_11.5.1: imām.u.tvā.iti.marutvatīyam.dvitīyam /

ŚŚS_11.5.6: devān.huva.iti.vaiśvadevam /
ŚŚS_11.5.7: caturviṃśāj.jāta.vedasīyam /
ŚŚS_11.5.8: samānam.anyad.dvitīyena.ahnā /
body.translated_text:
11.5.1: "<s>Imām u tvā</s>" (This you indeed) is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> for the second [day].
11.5.2: "<s>Suta it tvam nimiśla</s>" (Pressed indeed, you mingling) is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
11.5.3: The <s>Sāvitra</s> [recitation is] from the single-day [archetype].
11.5.4: "<s>Tatam me</s>" (Stretched for me) is the <s>Ārbhava</s>.
11.5.5: And [also] on the fifth [day].
11.5.6: "<s>Devān huva</s>" (I invoke the gods) is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
11.5.7: The <s>Jātavedasīya</s> [recitation is] from the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> [day archetype].
11.5.8: The rest is the same as the second day.

ŚŚS_11.6.8: ā.rudrāsas.tvām.agna.ṛtāyava.ity.āgni.mārutam /
body.translated_text:
11.6.1: The <s>Auṣṇiha Vaiśvamanasa</s> [verses form] the <s>prauga</s> (introduction) of the third [day].
11.6.2: [The <s>prauga</s> triplets are:] "<s>Vāyo yāhi</s>" (Come, O <s>Vāyu</s>); "<s>Śivā vām</s>" (Auspicious to you two); "<s>Sahasram</s>" (A thousand); "<s>Tā vām viśvasya</s>" (Both of you, of all); "<s>Ā vām vāhiṣṭhaḥ</s>" (The best bearer to you two); "<s>Sakhāya ā śiṣāmahy</s>" (O friends, let us invoke); "<s>Uta no devī Aditiḥ</s>" (And may the divine <s>Aditi</s> for us); "<s>Uta naḥ priya</s>" (And our dear one).
11.6.3: "<s>Tiṣṭhā harī</s>" (Stand, O bay horses) is the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
11.6.4: The <s>Niṣkevalya</s> is from the single-day [archetype].
11.6.5: "<s>Ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī</s>" (With ghee, heaven and earth) is the triplet.
11.6.6: And [also] on the sixth [day].
11.6.7: The <s>Ārbhava</s> and <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> are from the single-day [archetype].
11.6.8: "<s>Ā Rudrāsaḥ</s>"; "<s>Tvām Agna ṛtāyavaḥ</s>" (You, O <s>Agni</s>, seekers of <s>ṛta</s>) is the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [recitation].

body.text:
ŚŚS_11.7.1: hotā.ajaniṣṭa.ity.ājyam.caturthasya /
ŚŚS_11.7.2: maidhātithaḥ.praugaḥ /
