body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 14.42.1: The same procedure applies to the next [sacrifice].
ŚŚS 14.42.2: Only the <s>stomas</s> are different.
ŚŚS 14.42.3: The <s>Pavamāna</s> [chants] are <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-fourfold); the rest are <s>trivṛt</s> (ninefold).
ŚŚS 14.42.4: This is a contracted <s>Vājapeya</s> [sacrifice].
ŚŚS 14.42.5: For the attainment of both desires — that which one has in the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> and that in the <s>Vājapeya</s>.
ŚŚS 14.42.6: If his hostile kinsman performs a similar sacrifice, he should perform a surrounding sacrifice; if [the kinsman performs] a surrounding one, [he should perform] a surpassing one.
ŚŚS 14.42.7: One desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (splendor of sacred knowledge) should sacrifice with the one-three-three-one [arrangement].
ŚŚS 14.42.8: 'One in three' — thus are the <s>stotra</s>s of the first [day].
ŚŚS 14.42.9: 'Three in one' — thus of the latter [day].
ŚŚS 14.42.10: These [total] twenty-four <s>stotriya</s> [verses].
ŚŚS 14.42.11: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] has twenty-four syllables.
ŚŚS 14.42.12: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is spiritual radiance and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.
ŚŚS 14.42.13: Through these two [days], one attains spiritual radiance and <s>brahmavarcas</s>.
ŚŚS 14.42.14: The recitations (<s>śastra</s>s) of both [days] are arranged in <s>tṛca</s>s (triads).
ŚŚS 14.42.15: The <s>Abhijit</s> (conquest) [sacrifice is] for one wishing to conquer.
ŚŚS 14.42.16: The <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering) [sacrifice is] for one wishing to conquer everything.
ŚŚS 14.42.17: And those two have three possible conclusions.
ŚŚS 14.42.18: Having become <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>s, they find their conclusion in each other.
ŚŚS 14.42.19: Having become <s>Ukthya</s>s, [they find their conclusion] in each other.
ŚŚS 14.42.20: Having become <s>Atirātra</s>s, [they find their conclusion] in each other.

body.text: ŚŚS_14.43.1: indro.vai.vṝn.jigīṣaṃs.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyan.nṛjitam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.nṝn.ajayat.|.tena.nṝn.jigīṣan.yajeta /
body.translated_text: ŚŚS 14.43.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring to conquer men, having performed austerity (<s>tapas</s>), perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Nṛjit</s> (man-conquering). Having sacrificed with it, he conquered men. With it, one desiring to conquer men should sacrifice.

body.text: ŚŚS_14.44.1: indro.vai.pṛtanājam.jigīṣaṃs.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.pṛtanājitam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.pṛtanājam.ajayat.|.tena.pṛtanājam.jigīṣan.yajeta /
body.translated_text: ŚŚS 14.44.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring to conquer in battle, having performed austerity, perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Pṛtanājit</s> (battle-conquering). Having sacrificed with it, he conquered in battle. With it, one desiring to conquer in battle should sacrifice.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.45.1: indro.vai.satrājam.jigīṣaṃs.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.satrājitam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.satrājam.ajayat.|.tena.satrājam.jigīṣan.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.45.2: prathamāt.tryahān.madhyaṃdineṣu.nividdhānāni /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 14.45.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring to conquer completely, having performed austerity, perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Satrājit</s> (all-conquering). Having sacrificed with it, he conquered completely. With it, one desiring to conquer completely should sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.45.2: In the first three-day [period], <s>nivid</s> (invocatory formulas) are inserted at the midday [pressings].

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.46.1: indro.vai.dhanam.jigīṣaṃs.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyad.dhanajitam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.dhanam.ajayat.|.tena.dhanam.jigīṣan.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.46.2: caturviṃśam.ahaḥ /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 14.46.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring to conquer wealth, having performed austerity, perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Dhanajit</s> (wealth-conquering). Having sacrificed with it, he conquered wealth. With it, one desiring to conquer wealth should sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.46.2: [This takes] a twenty-four[-fold stoma] day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.47.1: indro.vai.svar.jigīṣaṃs.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.svar.jitam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.svar.ajayat.|.tena.svar.jigīṣan.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.47.2: utsanna.yajña.iva.vā.eṣa.yat.svarjit /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 14.47.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring to conquer heaven (<s>svar</s>), having performed austerity, perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Svarjit</s> (heaven-conquering). Having sacrificed with it, he conquered heaven. With it, one desiring to conquer heaven should sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.47.2: Or this <s>Svarjit</s> is like a sacrifice whose [normal form] has been abandoned.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.48.1: indro.vai.sarvam.jigīṣaṃs.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.sarvajitam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.sarvam.ajayat.|.tena.sarvam.jigīṣan.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.48.2: mahāvratīyam.ahaḥ /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 14.48.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring to conquer everything, having performed austerity, perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Sarvajit</s> (all-conquering). Having sacrificed with it, he conquered everything. With it, one desiring to conquer everything should sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.48.2: [It takes] a <s>Mahāvratīya</s> (great-vow) day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.49.1: indro.vai.sarvam.ujjigīṣaṃs.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyad.ujjitam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.sarvam.udajayat.|.tena.sarvam.ujjigīṣan.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.49.2: janiṣṭhā.ugraḥ.sahase.turāya.tam.u.ṣṭuhi.yo.abhibhūty.ojā.iti.nividdhāne /
ŚŚS_14.49.3: dhāntāt.prapitvād.udaranta.garbhā.utturvayāṇam.dhṛṣatā.ninetha.ity.udvatī.tad.etasya.ahno.rūpam /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 14.49.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring to win back everything, having performed austerity, perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Ujjit</s> (victorious recovery). Having sacrificed with it, he won back everything. With it, one desiring to win back everything should sacrifice.
ŚŚS 14.49.2: 'The mightiest born, the fierce one, for the power of conquest, praise him, who has overpowering might' — [these verses are recited] with <s>nivid</s> (invocatory formulas) inserted.
ŚŚS 14.49.3: 'From the blown-out evening, the embryos arose; with boldness you led forth the one who crosses over' — this upward [verse] is the characteristic form of that day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.50.1a: indro.vai.triśīrṣāṇam.tvāṣṭram.ahanat.|.arunmukhān.yatīn.sālāvṛkebhyaḥ.prāyacchat.|.tam.sarvāṇi.bhūtāny.abhyākrośan.|.sa.devebhyaḥ.pārśvata.iva.cacāra.|.te.devā.ūcuḥ.|.yadi.vā.ayam.evam.cariṣyaty.abhi.no.asurā.bhaviṣyanti /
ŚŚS_14.50.1b: upa.tam.yajña.kratum.jānīma.yena.enam.upāhvayemahi.iti.|.ta.etam.uaphavyam.yajña.kratum.apaśyan.|.tena.enam.upāhvayanta.|.tena.avaruddho.rājā.yajeta.rāṣṭram.avajigīṣan.|.aha.vā.eva.gacchati /
ŚŚS_14.50.2: imā.u.tvā.purutamasya.kāror.havyam.vīra.havyā.havante.ya.eka.iddhavyaś.carṣaṇīnām.iti.hūtavatī.nividdhāne.|.tad.etasya.ahno.rūpam /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 14.50.1a: <s>Indra</s> slew the three-headed [demon], the son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. He gave the <s>Yatis</s> (ascetics) with upturned faces to the wolves. All beings cried out against him. He moved as if aside from the gods. The gods said: 'If he continues thus, the <s>Asuras</s> will prevail over us.
ŚŚS 14.50.1b: Let us discover that sacrificial plan by which we may call him back.' They perceived this <s>Upahavya</s> (invocation) sacrificial plan. With it they called him back. With it, a king who has been exiled should sacrifice, desiring to reconquer his kingdom. He indeed attains [the kingdom].
ŚŚS 14.50.2: 'These, O most bountiful hero, the oblation-worthy ones invoke you with oblations, you who alone are to be invoked among the peoples' — [this is the verse] containing an invocation, with <s>nivid</s> inserted. That is the characteristic form of that day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.51.1a: tam.abhy.eva.ākrośann.anahar.jātatayā.vā.etat.pāpyā.vā.alakṣmyā.|.so.agnaye.sarvāṇi.savanāni.prāyacchat.|.tasya.agniḥ.sarvām.anahar.jātatām.sarvām.pāpīm.alakṣṇīm.niradahat /
ŚŚS_14.51.1b: sa.yo.anahar.jātaḥ.syād.yam.vā.pāpī.vāg.abhivadet.so.agni.ṣṭutā.yajeta.|.tasya.agniḥ.sarvām.anahar.jātatām.sarvām.pāpīm.alakṣmīm.nirdahati.ya.evam.veda.ya.u.ca.enena.yajate /
ŚŚS_14.51.2: trivṛt.stomena.triṣṭomena.vā.brahma.varcasa.kāmaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.51.3: catuṣṭomena.pratiṣṭhā.kāmaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.51.4: prātar.anuvāka.prabhṛti.hāriyojana.antam.sarvam.āgneyam /
ŚŚS_14.51.5: yathā.artham.ūhaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.51.6: vacanāt.pratyāmnāyaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.51.7: agnim.manye.pitaram.it.pratipat.prātar.anuvākasya /
ŚŚS_14.51.8: liṅga.īpsur.uttarayoḥ.kratvor.agni.śabdam.kurvīta /
ŚŚS_14.51.9: pra.devatra.ity.uddhṛtya.somasya.mā.iti.caturdaśa /
ŚŚS_14.51.10: tam.oṣadhīr.ity.avanīyamānāsu /
ŚŚS_14.51.11: aurvabhṛguvad.iti.tisro.ambaya.ity.uddhṛtya /
ŚŚS_14.51.12: upaprayantas.trīṇi.śata.iti.prathame.uttamā.ca.agni.manthanīyānām /
ŚŚS_14.51.13: agne.juṣasva.no.havir.iti.prathamā.caturthī.pañcamī.ca.savanīyānām /
ŚŚS_14.51.14: dūtam.vo.viśva.vedasam.iti.dvi.devatyānām /
body.translated_text:
14.51.1a: They reviled him on account of his being born on a non-day or on account of evil or ill-fortune. He offered all <s>savanas</s> (pressings) to <s>Agni</s>. <s>Agni</s> burned away all his non-day-born nature and all evil ill-fortune.
14.51.1b: He who is born on a non-day, or whom evil speech addresses, should sacrifice with the <s>Agniṣṭuta</s> (praise of Agni). <s>Agni</s> burns away all his non-day-born nature and all evil ill-fortune — for one who knows thus, and also for one who sacrifices with this rite.
14.51.2: One desiring <s>brahmavarcasa</s> (spiritual splendor) should use the <s>Trivṛt Stoma</s> (nine-versed hymn form) or the <s>Triṣṭoma</s>.
14.51.3: One desiring firm establishment should use the <s>Catuṣṭoma</s> (four-fold hymn form).
14.51.4: From the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> (morning litany) onwards up to the <s>hāriyojana</s> (yoking of the bay horses), everything is dedicated to <s>Agni</s>.
14.51.5: The substitution is according to the purpose.
14.51.6: The <s>pratyāmnāya</s> (counter-recitation) is based on the explicit statement.
14.51.7: "<s>Agnim manye pitaram</s>" (I consider Agni as father) is the opening verse of the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> (morning litany).
14.51.8: One desiring the characteristic mark should introduce the word "<s>Agni</s>" in the two subsequent rites.
14.51.9: Having extracted "<s>pra devatra</s>," fourteen verses beginning with "<s>somasya mā</s>."
14.51.10: "<s>Tam oṣadhīḥ</s>" is used during the pouring out.
14.51.11: Three verses like the <s>Aurva-Bhṛgu</s> formula; having extracted "<s>ambayaḥ</s>."
14.51.12: "<s>Upaprayantaḥ</s>" and "<s>trīṇi śatā</s>" are the first and last of the fire-churning hymns.
14.51.13: "<s>Agne juṣasva no haviḥ</s>" (O Agni, enjoy our offering) — the first, fourth, and fifth are of the <s>savanīya</s> (pressing-day) hymns.
14.51.14: "<s>Dūtam vo viśvavedasam</s>" (Your messenger, the all-knowing one) is for the two-deity hymns.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.52.1: agnim.īḷe.purohitam.ity.unnīyamānebhyaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.52.2: agnim.dūtam.iti.sapta.prasthitānām /
ŚŚS_14.52.3: uttarāś.carasro.acchāvāka.sūktasya.sthāne /
ŚŚS_14.52.4: agne.diva.iti.yājyā.ājyasya /
ŚŚS_14.52.5: upa.tvā.jāmaya.aibhir.agne.kas.te.jāmir.na.yor.upabdir.agnir.vṛtrāṇy.agne.sutasya.agne.dhṛta.vratāya.iti.prauga.tṛcāni /
ŚŚS_14.52.6: agne.viśvebhir.agnibhir.iti.yajati /
ŚŚS_14.52.7: kas.te.jāmiḥ.kayā.te.agne.aṅgira.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.maitrāvaruṇasya /
ŚŚS_14.52.8: viparyastau.tu.mādhyaṃdine /
ŚŚS_14.52.9: agnir.vṛtrāṇi.iti.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.52.10: agnir.mūrdhā.ity.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_14.52.11: arcantas.tvā.iti.maitrāvaruṇasya /
ŚŚS_14.52.12: uttaram.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.52.13: agne.dhṛta.vratāya.iti.ṣaḷ.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_14.52.14: uttamābhir.yajanti /
body.translated_text:
14.52.1: "<s>Agnim īḷe purohitam</s>" (I praise Agni, the foremost priest) is for those being drawn out.
14.52.2: Seven verses beginning with "<s>Agnim dūtam</s>" (Agni as messenger) are for those who have set forth.
14.52.3: The latter four are in place of the <s>Acchāvāka</s> hymn.
14.52.4: "<s>Agne divaḥ</s>" is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) for the <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter oblation).
14.52.5: "<s>Upa tvā jāmayaḥ</s>," "<s>Aibhir agne kas te jāmir</s>," "<s>Na yor upabdiḥ</s>," "<s>Agnir vṛtrāṇi</s>," "<s>Agne sutasya</s>," "<s>Agne dhṛtavratāya</s>" — these are the <s>prauga</s> (opening) <s>tṛcas</s> (three-verse groups).
14.52.6: He recites "<s>Agne viśvebhir agnibhiḥ</s>" (O Agni, with all fires).
14.52.7: "<s>Kas te jāmiḥ</s>" and "<s>Kayā te agne aṅgirā</s>" are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-linked) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response) verses of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> priest.
14.52.8: But in the midday pressing, they are reversed.
14.52.9: "<s>Agnir vṛtrāṇi</s>" belongs to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> priest.
14.52.10: "<s>Agnir mūrdhā</s>" belongs to the <s>Acchāvāka</s> priest.
14.52.11: "<s>Arcantas tvā</s>" belongs to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> priest.
14.52.12: The next one belongs to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> priest.
14.52.13: Six verses beginning with "<s>Agne dhṛtavratāya</s>" belong to the <s>Acchāvāka</s> priest.
14.52.14: They recite with the final verses.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.53.1: agnim.vo.devam.ity.unnīyamānebhyaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.53.2: pra.vaḥ.śukrāya.iti.sapta.prasthitānām /
ŚŚS_14.53.3: uttare.marutvatīya.grahasya /
ŚŚS_14.53.4: viśo.viśo.vas.tvam.agne.yajñānām.iti.pratipad.anucarau.marutvatīyasya /
ŚŚS_14.53.5: agna.ā.yāhy.agnibhiḥ.pra.vo.yahvam.iti.pragāthau /
ŚŚS_14.53.6: agnim.na.mā.mathitam.tvam.agne.prathamo.aṅgirā.ṛṣir.ity.eka.pātinīnām /
ŚŚS_14.53.7: agne.sa.kṣeṣad.iti.nividdhānam /
ŚŚS_14.53.8: uttamā.yājyā /
body.translated_text:
14.53.1: "<s>Agnim vo devam</s>" (Agni, your god) is for those being drawn out.
14.53.2: Seven verses beginning with "<s>Pra vaḥ śukrāya</s>" are for those who have set forth.
14.53.3: The latter ones are for the <s>Marutvatīya</s> cup.
14.53.4: "<s>Viśo viśaḥ</s>," "<s>Vas tvam agne</s>," "<s>Yajñānām</s>" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Marutvatīya</s> hymn.
14.53.5: "<s>Agna ā yāhy agnibhiḥ</s>" and "<s>Pra vo yahvam</s>" are the <s>pragāthas</s> (paired stanzas).
14.53.6: "<s>Agnim na mā mathitam</s>," "<s>Tvam agne prathamo aṅgirāḥ ṛṣiḥ</s>" are the <s>ekapātinī</s> (single-footed) verses.
14.53.7: "<s>Agne sa kṣeṣat</s>" is the <s>nividdhāna</s> (insertion verse).
14.53.8: The last verse is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse).

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.54.1: pāhi.no.agna.ekayā.pahai.no.agne.rakṣasa.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.pragāthau.niṣkevalyasya /
ŚŚS_14.54.2: pra.te.agne.haviṣmatīm.iti.dhāyyā /
ŚŚS_14.54.3: enā.vo.agnim.iti.pragāthaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.54.4: yathā.hotar.iti.nividdhānam /
ŚŚS_14.54.5: agnim.nara.iti.yājyā /
body.translated_text:
14.54.1: "<s>Pāhi no agna ekayā</s>" and "<s>Pāhi no agne rakṣasaḥ</s>" (Protect us, O Agni) are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-linked) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response) paired stanzas of the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> hymn.
14.54.2: "<s>Pra te agne haviṣmatīm</s>" is the <s>dhāyyā</s> (meditation verse).
14.54.3: "<s>Enā vo agnim</s>" is the <s>pragātha</s> (paired stanza).
14.54.4: "<s>Yathā hotaḥ</s>" is the <s>nividdhāna</s> (insertion verse).
14.54.5: "<s>Agnim naraḥ</s>" is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse).

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.55.1: agnim.agnim.vo.adhrigum.agne.jaritar.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.pragāthau.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.55.2: acchā.naḥ.śīra.śociṣam.ity.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_14.55.3: agne.vivasvat.tvam.agne.gṛhapatis.tvam.it.saprathā.ity.anupūrvam.pragāthāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.55.4: yajasva.hotar.iti.ca.sūktāni /
ŚŚS_14.55.5: uttamābhir.yajanti /
body.translated_text:
14.55.1: "<s>Agnim agnim</s>," "<s>Vo adhrigum</s>," "<s>Agne jaritaḥ</s>" are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-linked) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response) paired stanzas of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> priest.
14.55.2: "<s>Acchā naḥ śīraśociṣam</s>" belongs to the <s>Acchāvāka</s> priest.
14.55.3: "<s>Agne vivasvat</s>," "<s>Tvam agne gṛhapatiḥ</s>," "<s>Tvam it saprathāḥ</s>" — the <s>pragāthas</s> (paired stanzas) are in order.
14.55.4: "<s>Yajasva hotaḥ</s>" and the other complete hymns.
14.55.5: They recite with the final verses.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.56.1: aganma.mahā.ity.āditya.grahasya.puronuvākyā.uttarā.yājyā /
ŚŚS_14.56.2: ūrdhvam.ū.ṣu.ṇo.adhvarasya.hotar.iti.nava.unnīyamānebhyaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.56.3: uttare.hāriyojanasya /
ŚŚS_14.56.4: tvām.agna.ṛtāyava.iti.sapta.prasthitānām /
ŚŚS_14.56.5: eti.pra.hotā.iti.sāvitra.grahasya.puronuvākyā.uttarā.yājyā /
ŚŚS_14.56.6: iyam.te.navyasy.aśvam.na.tvā.iti.pratipad.anucarau.vaiśvadevasya /
ŚŚS_14.56.7: tvam.agne.draviṇodā.iti.tisraḥ.sāvitrasya /
ŚŚS_14.56.8: ārbhavasya.uttarās.tisraḥ /
ŚŚS_14.56.9: catasro.dyāvā.pṛthivīyasya /
ŚŚS_14.56.10: ṣaḷ.ādito.vaiśvadevasya /
ŚŚS_14.56.11: abodhi.jāra.iti.vāyavyāyāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.56.12: juṣasva.saprathastamam.iti.surūpa.kṛtnoḥ /
ŚŚS_14.56.13: samiddho.agnir.divi.iti.tisra.eka.pātinīnām /
ŚŚS_14.56.14: tad.adya.vāca.iti.pañca.janīyāyāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.56.15: yajñena.vardhata.iti.yājyā /
body.translated_text:
14.56.1: "<s>Aganma mahā</s>" — the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) for the <s>Āditya</s> cup, and the next one is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse).
14.56.2: Nine verses beginning with "<s>Ūrdhvam ū ṣu ṇaḥ</s>" and "<s>Adhvarasya hotaḥ</s>" are for those being drawn out.
14.56.3: The latter ones are for the <s>Hāriyojana</s> cup.
14.56.4: Seven verses beginning with "<s>Tvām agna ṛtāyavaḥ</s>" are for those who have set forth.
14.56.5: "<s>Eti pra hotā</s>" — the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) for the <s>Sāvitra</s> cup, and the next one is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse).
14.56.6: "<s>Iyam te navyasī</s>" and "<s>Aśvam na tvā</s>" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> hymn.
14.56.7: Three verses beginning with "<s>Tvam agne draviṇodāḥ</s>" are for the <s>Sāvitra</s> hymn.
14.56.8: The next three are for the <s>Ārbhava</s> hymn.
14.56.9: Four verses are for the <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s> (Heaven-and-Earth) hymn.
14.56.10: Six verses from the beginning are for the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> hymn.
14.56.11: "<s>Abodhi jāraḥ</s>" is for the <s>Vāyavyā</s> (wind-deity) hymn.
14.56.12: "<s>Juṣasva saprathaḥ tamam</s>" is for the <s>Surūpakṛtnū</s> hymn.
14.56.13: Three verses beginning with "<s>Samiddho agnir divi</s>" are the <s>ekapātinī</s> (single-footed) verses.
14.56.14: Five verses beginning with "<s>Tad adya vācaḥ</s>" are for the <s>Pañcajanīyā</s> hymn.
14.56.15: "<s>Yajñena vardhata</s>" is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse).

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.57.1: abhi.pravanta.iti.ghṛtasya /
ŚŚS_14.57.2: uttarā.saumyasya /
ŚŚS_14.57.3: ā.vo.rājānam.iti.raudryāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.57.4: vasum.na.citra.mahasam.iti.mārutasya /
ŚŚS_14.57.5: ā.no.yajñam.divi.spṛśam.ā.no.vāyav.ity.agniṣṭoma.sāmnaḥ.stotriya.anurūpau.pragāthau /
ŚŚS_14.57.6: nityau.vā /
ŚŚS_14.57.7: apsv.agna.ity.āpo.hi.ṣṭhīyānām /
ŚŚS_14.57.8: tam.devā.budhna.iti.vaiśvadevyāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.57.9: imam.ū.ṣu.vo.atithim.uṣar.budham.iti.catasro.devānām.patnīnām.rākāyāś.ca /
ŚŚS_14.57.10: huve.vaḥ.sudyotmānam.iti.tisro.akṣara.paṅktīnām /
ŚŚS_14.57.11: tri.mūrdhānam.iti.tisraḥ.paitrīṇām /
ŚŚS_14.57.12: kathā.te.agne.śucayanta.āyor.iti.tisro.yāmīnām /
ŚŚS_14.57.13: mathīd.yad.īm.iti.tisraḥ.svāduṣkilīyānām /
ŚŚS_14.57.14: uttarayor.uttare /
ŚŚS_14.57.15: evāgnir.gotamebhir.iti.paridhānīyā /
ŚŚS_14.57.16: graheṣv.avikṛteṣu.tiṣṭhā.harī.tam.u.ṣṭuhi.iti.nividdhāne /
ŚŚS_14.57.17: anaḍvān.hiraṇyam.vā.dakṣiṇā /
ŚŚS_14.57.18: etadd.hy.āgneyam.rūpam /
ŚŚS_14.57.19: utthāya.ca.agniṣṭomaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.57.20: ā.ha.vā.eṣa.sarvābhyo.devatābhyo.vṛścyate.yo.agni.ṣṭutā.yajate /
body.translated_text:
14.57.1: "<s>Abhi pravanta</s>" is for the <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) offering.
14.57.2: The next one is for the <s>Saumya</s> (Soma-related) offering.
14.57.3: "<s>Ā vo rājānam</s>" is for the <s>Raudrī</s> (Rudra-related) hymn.
14.57.4: "<s>Vasum na citramahasam</s>" is for the <s>Māruta</s> (Marut-related) hymn.
14.57.5: "<s>Ā no yajñam divispṛśam</s>" and "<s>Ā no Vāyo</s>" are the <s>stotriya</s> (chant-linked) and <s>anurūpa</s> (response) paired stanzas of the <s>Agniṣṭoma Sāman</s> (hymn of praise to Agni).
14.57.6: Or they are the regular ones.
14.57.7: "<s>Apsv agne</s>" is for the <s>Āpo hiṣṭhīya</s> (water-hymn) verses.
14.57.8: "<s>Tam devā budhne</s>" is for the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> (all-gods) hymn.
14.57.9: Four verses — "<s>Imam ū ṣu vaḥ atithim</s>" and "<s>Uṣarbudham</s>" — are for the <s>Devānām Patnī</s> (wives of the gods) and <s>Rākā</s> hymns.
14.57.10: Three verses beginning with "<s>Huve vaḥ sudyotmānam</s>" are for the <s>Akṣarapaṅkti</s> hymns.
14.57.11: Three verses beginning with "<s>Trimūrdhānam</s>" are for the <s>Paitrī</s> (ancestral) hymns.
14.57.12: Three verses beginning with "<s>Kathā te agne śucayanta āyoḥ</s>" are for the <s>Yāmī</s> hymns.
14.57.13: Three verses beginning with "<s>Mathīd yad īm</s>" are for the <s>Svāduṣkilīya</s> hymns.
14.57.14: For the latter two, the subsequent ones apply.
14.57.15: "<s>Evāgnir Gotamebhiḥ</s>" is the <s>paridhānīyā</s> (concluding verse).
14.57.16: When the cups are unmodified, "<s>Tiṣṭhā harī</s>" and "<s>Tam u ṣṭuhi</s>" are the <s>nividdhāna</s> (insertion verses).
14.57.17: A bull or gold is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee).
14.57.18: For this is the form pertaining to <s>Agni</s>.
14.57.19: And upon conclusion, the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> (rite) is complete.
14.57.20: Indeed, he who sacrifices with the <s>Agniṣṭuta</s> is cut off from all deities.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.58.1: indro.ha.bala.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyad.indra.stutam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.balam.āpnoti.|.tena.bala.kāmo.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.58.2: indra.abhivyāhāre.nividdhāne.tad.etasya.ahno.rūpam /
body.translated_text:
14.58.1: <s>Indra</s>, desiring strength, having performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity), beheld this sacrificial rite, the <s>Indrastuta</s> (praise of Indra). Having sacrificed with it, he obtained strength. Therefore, one desiring strength should sacrifice with it.
14.58.2: The <s>nividdhāna</s> (insertion verses) have the explicit mention of <s>Indra</s> — that is the characteristic form of this day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.59.1: sūryo.ha.tejas.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.sūrya.stutam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.teja.āpnot.|.tena.tejas.kāmo.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.59.2: sūrya.abhivyāhāre.nividdhāne.tad.etasya.ahno.rūpam /
body.translated_text:
14.59.1: <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), desiring splendor, having performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity), beheld this sacrificial rite, the <s>Sūryastuta</s> (praise of the Sun). Having sacrificed with it, he obtained splendor. Therefore, one desiring splendor should sacrifice with it.
14.59.2: The <s>nividdhāna</s> (insertion verses) have the explicit mention of <s>Sūrya</s> — that is the characteristic form of this day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.60.1: viśve.ha.devāḥ.prajāti.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyan.vaiśvadeva.stutam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.prājāyanta.|.tena.prajāti.kāmo.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.60.2: imā.u.tvā.purutamasya.vṛṣā.mada.indra.iti.nividdhāne /
ŚŚS_14.60.3: protaye.varuṇam.mitram.indram.mitro.no.atra.varuṇaś.ca.pūṣā.iti.vaiśva.deva.abhivyāhāre.tad.etasya.ahno.rūpam /
body.translated_text:
14.60.1: The <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods), desiring progeny, having performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity), beheld this sacrificial rite, the <s>Vaiśvadevastuta</s> (praise of the All-Gods). Having sacrificed with it, they begot offspring. Therefore, one desiring progeny should sacrifice with it.
14.60.2: "<s>Imā u tvā purutamasya</s>" and "<s>Vṛṣā mada Indra</s>" are the <s>nividdhāna</s> (insertion verses).
14.60.3: "<s>Protaye Varuṇam Mitram Indram</s>" and "<s>Mitro no atra Varuṇaś ca Pūṣā</s>" — the explicit mention of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (All-Gods) — that is the characteristic form of this day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.61.1: gotamo.ha.brahma.varcasa.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyad.gotamasya.catur.uttara.stomam.|.tena.iṣṭvā.brahma.varcasam.āpnot.|.tena.brahma.varcasa.kāmo.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.61.2: catasṛṣu.bahiṣ.pavamānaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.61.3: aṣṭāsv.aṣṭāsv.ājyāni /
ŚŚS_14.61.4: dvādaśasu.mādhyaṃdinaḥ.pavamānaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.61.5: ṣiḷaśasu.ṣiḷaśasu.pṛṣṭhāni /
ŚŚS_14.61.6: viṃśatyām.ārbhavaḥ.pavamānaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.61.7: catur.viṃśam.agniṣṭoma.sāma /
ŚŚS_14.61.8: sāma.antar.ukthyaḥ /
body.translated_text:
14.61.1: <s>Gotama</s>, desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavarcasa</s>), having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite — the <s>Caturuttara-stoma</s> (four-ascending praise) of <s>Gotama</s>. Having sacrificed with it, he attained sacred splendor. Therefore, one desiring sacred splendor should sacrifice with it.
14.61.2: The external <s>Pavamāna</s> [chant is] in four-fold [stoma].
14.61.3: The <s>Ājya</s> [hymns] are in groups of eight.
14.61.4: The midday <s>Pavamāna</s> is in twelve-fold [stoma].
14.61.5: The <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants) are in groups of sixteen.
14.61.6: The <s>Ārbhava Pavamāna</s> is in twenty-fold [stoma].
14.61.7: The <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāma</s> is in twenty-four-fold.
14.61.8: The <s>Ukthya</s> [is performed] between the <s>Sāman</s> chants.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.62.1: pañca.śāradīyaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.62.2: maruto.ha.agre.anapisoma.pīthā.āsuḥ.|.te.yatra.indram.marutaḥ.pupuvus.tad.enān.indraḥ.soma.pīthe.anvābheje.|.sa.yo.anapisoma.pīthaḥ.syād.yo.vā.marutām.salokatām.sāyujyam.īpseta.so.anena.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.62.3: pañca.ukṣāṇaḥ.pañca.śarado.marudbhyaḥ.prokṣitāś.caranti.|.te.savanīyasya.upālambhyāḥ /
body.translated_text:
14.62.1: The <s>Pañcaśāradīya</s> (five-autumn) [sacrifice].
14.62.2: The <s>Maruts</s> were originally without a share in the <s>Soma</s> drinking. When the <s>Maruts</s> purified <s>Indra</s>, then <s>Indra</s> admitted them to the <s>Soma</s> drinking. Therefore, one who is without a share in <s>Soma</s> drinking, or one desiring co-residence and union with the <s>Maruts</s>, should sacrifice with this.
14.62.3: Five bulls, dedicated to the <s>Maruts</s>, are set loose for five autumns. They are the slaughter-victims of the pressing-day offering.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.63.1: ṛṣi.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.63.2: gotamo.ha.brahma.varcasa.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.|.tena.iṣṭvā.brahma.varcasam.āpnot.|.tena.brahma.varcasa.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.63.1: The <s>Ṛṣi-stomas</s> (Sage-praises).
14.63.2: <s>Gotama</s>, desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite. Having sacrificed with it, he attained sacred splendor. Therefore, one desiring sacred splendor should sacrifice with it.

body.text: ŚŚS_14.64.1: bharadvājo.ha.bala.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.|.tena.iṣṭvā.balam.āpnot.|.tena.bala.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text: 14.64.1: <s>Bharadvāja</s>, desiring strength, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite. Having sacrificed with it, he attained strength. Therefore, one desiring strength should sacrifice with it.

body.text: ŚŚS_14.65.1: atrir.ha.prājāti.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.|.tena.iṣṭvā.prājāyata.|.tena.prajāti.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text: 14.65.1: <s>Atri</s>, desiring progeny, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite. Having sacrificed with it, he begot [progeny]. Therefore, one desiring progeny should sacrifice with it.

body.text: ŚŚS_14.66.1: vasiṣṭho.ha.anna.adya.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.|.tena.iṣṭvā.anna.adyam.āpnot.|.tena.anna.adya.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text: 14.66.1: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, desiring food-eating, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite. Having sacrificed with it, he attained food-eating. Therefore, one desiring food-eating should sacrifice with it.

body.text: ŚŚS_14.67.1: jamadagnir.ha.paśu.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.|.tena.iṣṭvā.paśūn.āpnot.|.tena.pauś.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text: 14.67.1: <s>Jamadagni</s>, desiring cattle, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite. Having sacrificed with it, he attained cattle. Therefore, one desiring cattle should sacrifice with it.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.68.1: prajāpatir.ha.prajāti.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyat.|.tena.iṣṭvā.prājāyata.|.tena.prajāti.kāmo.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.68.2: pṛṣṭhya.ahāny.anupūrvam /
body.translated_text:
14.68.1: <s>Prajāpati</s>, desiring progeny, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite. Having sacrificed with it, he begot [progeny]. Therefore, one desiring progeny should sacrifice with it.
14.68.2: The <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant) days [follow] in sequence.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.69.1: vrātya.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.69.2: vasavo.ha.svarga.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.vrātya.stomān.|.tair.iṣṭvā.svargam.āpuḥ.|.taiḥ.svarga.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.69.1: The <s>Vrātya-stomas</s> (Wanderer-praises).
14.69.2: The <s>Vasus</s>, desiring heaven, having practiced austerity, perceived these sacrificial rites — the <s>Vrātya-stomas</s>. Having sacrificed with them, they attained heaven. Therefore, one desiring heaven should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.70.1: mitrā.varuṇayor.aśvinor.vasūnām.marutām.viśveṣām.devānām /
ŚŚS_14.70.2: samūḷhāt.pṛṣṭhyāt.śastram /
body.translated_text:
14.70.1: [These are dedicated] to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, to the <s>Aśvins</s>, to the <s>Vasus</s>, to the <s>Maruts</s>, and to the <s>Viśve Devas</s> (all gods).
14.70.2: The recitation is from the combined <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [arrangement].

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.71.1: utkrāntir.atirātraḥ /
ŚŚS_14.71.2: indrā.viṣṇū.vai.svarga.kāmau.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyatām.utkrāntim.|.tena.iṣṭvā.svargam.lokam.udākrāmatām.|.tena.svarga.kāmo.yajeta /
ŚŚS_14.71.3: imā.u.tvā.purutamasya.dyaur.na.ya.indra.iti.nividdhāne /
ŚŚS_14.71.4: pra.pūṣaṇam.viṣṇum.agnim.puraṃdhim.hann.ṛjīṣin.viṣṇunā.sacāna.iti.viṣṇu.nyaṅge.tad.etasya.ahno.rūpam /
body.translated_text:
14.71.1: The <s>Utkrānti</s> (Ascent) is an <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight sacrifice).
14.71.2: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, desiring heaven, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite — the <s>Utkrānti</s>. Having sacrificed with it, they ascended to the heavenly world. Therefore, one desiring heaven should sacrifice with it.
14.71.3: 'imā u tvā purutamasya' (These for thee, O most manifold) and 'dyaur na ya indra' (Like heaven, O Indra) — [recited] with the <s>nivid</s>.
14.71.4: 'pra pūṣaṇam' (Forth Pūṣan), 'viṣṇum' (Viṣṇu), 'agnim puraṃdhim' (Agni the bountiful), 'hann ṛjīṣin viṣṇunā sacāna' (The smiter, the pressing-drinker, accompanied by Viṣṇu) — at the mention of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — that is the form of this [sacrifice] day.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.72.1: mitrā.varuṇayor.aśvinor.vasūnām.marutām.sādhyānām.āpyānām.viśvasṛjām.bhūtakṛtām.jyeṣṭhānām.madhyamānām.kaniṣṭhānām.ca /
ŚŚS_14.72.2: caturdaśaḥ.stomaḥ /
ŚŚS_14.72.3: vipṛthuḥ.sapratodaḥ.sa.iṣudhanvā.dakṣiṇā /
ŚŚS_14.72.4: eteṣām.deva.gaṇānām.samūḷhād.daśa.rātrāt.śastram /
body.translated_text:
14.72.1: [Dedicated] to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, to the <s>Aśvins</s>, to the <s>Vasus</s>, to the <s>Maruts</s>, to the <s>Sādhyas</s>, to the <s>Āpyas</s>, to the <s>Viśvasṛjas</s> (world-creators), to the <s>Bhūtakṛts</s> (creature-makers), and to the eldest, middle, and youngest [groups].
14.72.2: The <s>stoma</s> is fourteen-fold.
14.72.3: The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) is a broad [horse] with a goad, with a bow and arrows.
14.72.4: The recitation for these divine groups is from the combined ten-night [arrangement].

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.73.1: vrātya.stomānām /
ŚŚS_14.73.2: navānām.nākasadām.ca /
ŚŚS_14.73.3: caṣāla.mukha.tarasa.puroḷāśo.vaniṣṭu.sava.brahma.sava.kṣatra.sava.bhūmi.sava.oṣadhi.sava.odana.sava.vanaspati.savānām.ca /
body.translated_text:
14.73.1: [The recitations] of the <s>Vrātya-stomas</s>.
14.73.2: And of the nine <s>Nākasads</s> (heaven-dwellers).
14.73.3: And of the <s>Caṣāla</s> (turban), <s>Mukhataras</s> (face-crossing), rice-cake, <s>Vaniṣṭu</s>, <s>Sava</s> (quickening), <s>Brahma-sava</s> (priestly quickening), <s>Kṣatra-sava</s> (warrior quickening), <s>Bhūmi-sava</s> (earth quickening), <s>Oṣadhi-sava</s> (herb quickening), <s>Odana-sava</s> (rice-porridge quickening), and <s>Vanaspati-sava</s> (tree quickening) [rituals].

body.text: ŚŚS_14.74.1: prajāpatir.ha.parameṣṭhī.pratiṣṭhā.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyad.daśamam.ahaḥ.|.tena.iṣṭvā.pratyatiṣṭhata.|.tena.pratiṣṭhā.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text: 14.74.1: <s>Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme), desiring firm establishment, having practiced austerity, perceived this sacrificial rite — the tenth day. Having sacrificed with it, he became firmly established. Therefore, one desiring firm establishment should sacrifice with it.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.75.1: ṛtu.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.75.2: ṛtavo.ha.svarga.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.ṣaṭ.|.tair.iṣṭvā.svargam.āpuḥ.|.taiḥ.svarga.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.75.1: The <s>Ṛtu-stomas</s> (Season-praises).
14.75.2: The seasons, desiring heaven, having practiced austerity, perceived these six sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained heaven. Therefore, one desiring heaven should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.76.1: māsa.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.76.2: māsā.ha.anna.adya.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.dvādaśa.|.tair.iṣṭvā.anna.adyam.āpuḥ.|.tair.anna.adya.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.76.1: The <s>Māsa-stomas</s> (Month-praises).
14.76.2: The months, desiring food-eating, having practiced austerity, perceived these twelve sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained food-eating. Therefore, one desiring food-eating should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.77.1: ardha.māsa.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.77.2: ardha.māsā.ha.anna.adya.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyaṃś.caturviṃśatim.|.tair.iṣṭvā.anna.adyam.āpuḥ.|.tair.anna.adya.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.77.1: The <s>Ardhamāsa-stomas</s> (Half-month-praises).
14.77.2: The half-months, desiring food-eating, having practiced austerity, perceived these twenty-four sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained food-eating. Therefore, one desiring food-eating should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.78.1: nakṣatra.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.78.2: nakṣatrāṇi.ha.tejas.kāmāni.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.sapta.viṃśatim.|.tair.iṣṭvā.teja.āpuḥ.|.tais.tejas.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.78.1: The <s>Nakṣatra-stomas</s> (Lunar-mansion-praises).
14.78.2: The <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), desiring radiance, having practiced austerity, perceived these twenty-seven sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained radiance. Therefore, one desiring radiance should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.79.1: ahorātra.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.79.2: ahorātrā.ha.anna.adya.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.sapta.viṃśati.śatāni.|.tair.iṣṭvā.anna.adyam.āpuḥ.|.tair.anna.adya.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.79.1: The <s>Ahorātra-stomas</s> (Day-and-night-praises).
14.79.2: The day-and-nights, desiring food-eating, having practiced austerity, perceived these two hundred and seventy sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained food-eating. Therefore, one desiring food-eating should sacrifice with them.

body.text:

ŚŚS_14.80.2: muhūrtā.ha.anna.adya.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.daśa.sahasrāṇy.aṣṭau.ca.śatāni.|.tair.iṣṭvā.anna.adyam.āpuḥ.|.tair.anna.adya.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.80.1: The <s>Muhūrta-stomas</s> (Moment-praises).
14.80.2: The <s>muhūrtas</s> (moments), desiring food-eating, having practiced austerity, perceived these ten thousand eight hundred sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained food-eating. Therefore, one desiring food-eating should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.81.1: nimeṣa.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.81.2: nimeṣā.ha.akṣiti.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.daśa.ayutāny.aṣṭau.ca.sahasrāṇi.|.tair.iṣṭvā.akṣitim.āpuḥ.|.tair.akṣiti.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.81.1: The <s>Nimeṣa-stomas</s> (Eye-blink-praises).
14.81.2: The eye-blinks, desiring imperishability, having practiced austerity, perceived these one hundred and eight thousand sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained imperishability. Therefore, one desiring imperishability should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.82.1: dhvaṃsi.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.82.2: dhvaṃsayo.ha.ananta.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyan.daśa.prayutāny.aṣṭau.ca.ayutāni.|.tair.iṣṭvā.anantam.āpuḥ.|.tair.ananta.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.82.1: The <s>Dhvaṃsi-stomas</s> (Dust-particle-praises).
14.82.2: The dust-particles, desiring infinity, having practiced austerity, perceived these one million and eighty thousand sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained infinity. Therefore, one desiring infinity should sacrifice with them.

body.text:
ŚŚS_14.83.1: diśām.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_14.83.2: diśo.ha.ananta.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apaśyaṃś.caturaḥ.|.tair.iṣṭvā.anantam.āpuḥ.|.tair.ananta.kāmo.yajeta /
body.translated_text:
14.83.1: The <s>Diś-stomas</s> (Direction-praises).
14.83.2: The directions, desiring infinity, having practiced austerity, perceived these four sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained infinity. Therefore, one desiring infinity should sacrifice with them.

ŚŚS_14.84.2: avāntara.diśo.ha.ananta.kāmās.tapas.taptvā.etān.yajña.kratūn.apśyaṃś.caturaḥ.|.tair.iṣṭvā.anantam.āpuḥ.|.tair.ananta.kāmo.yajeta /

ŚŚS_14.84.6: dikṣu.diśām.stomā.avāntara.dikṣv.avāntara.diśām.avāntara.diśām /
body.translated_text:
14.84.1: The <s>Avāntaradiś-stomas</s> (Intermediate-direction-praises).
14.84.2: The intermediate directions, desiring infinity, having practiced austerity, perceived these four sacrificial rites. Having sacrificed with them, they attained infinity. Therefore, one desiring infinity should sacrifice with them.
14.84.3: These should have the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> as <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chants).
14.84.4: [With] single-day recitations.
14.84.5: 'kayā śubhīya' (Through what beauty) or 'tad id āsīye' — [recited] with the <s>nivid</s>.
14.84.6: The <s>Diś-stomas</s> [are performed] in the [cardinal] directions; the <s>Avāntaradiś-stomas</s> in the intermediate directions.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.1.1: In autumn, [one performs] the <s>Vājapeya</s> (drink of strength).
ŚŚS 15.1.2: [It is] for one who desires food.
ŚŚS 15.1.3: He who is about to sacrifice with the <s>Vāja</s> (strength) sacrifices for the preceding year with the <s>Peya</s> (drink) sacrificial designs.
ŚŚS 15.1.4: The <s>Peyas</s> are indeed drink; the <s>Vāja</s> is food.
ŚŚS 15.1.5: Drink indeed [comes] first, then food.
ŚŚS 15.1.6: For the attainment of both of these.
ŚŚS 15.1.7: Twelve <s>Agniṣṭomas</s>.
ŚŚS 15.1.8: Or [the arrangement] of <s>Gotama</s>, with the four ascending <s>stomas</s>, alternating with the basic [form].
ŚŚS 15.1.9: Some [say] without an enclosing sacrifice.
ŚŚS 15.1.10: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, having sacrificed with this sacrificial design, obtained food.
ŚŚS 15.1.11: Therefore, one who desires food should sacrifice with it.
ŚŚS 15.1.13: Moreover, by this [rite]: three consecrations (<s>dīkṣā</s>), <s>Upasad</s> rites, and the pressing day — the seventeenth day.
ŚŚS 15.1.14: The seventeenth indeed is <s>Prajāpati</s>; the <s>Vājapeya</s> [is <s>Prajāpati</s>].
ŚŚS 15.1.15: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.1.16: The sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) is four-cornered, of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) wood, with a cow-dung smoke-cap, seventeen cubits [high].
ŚŚS 15.1.17: The seventeenth indeed is <s>Prajāpati</s>; the <s>Vājapeya</s> [is <s>Prajāpati</s>].
ŚŚS 15.1.18: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.1.19: Seventeen <s>Āgnīṣomīya</s> [animal offerings].
ŚŚS 15.1.20: Their procedure is the same.
ŚŚS 15.1.21: Up to the <s>Aindrāgna</s> [offering]: an <s>Aindra</s> (for <s>Indra</s>) bull; a <s>Sārasvatī</s> (for <s>Sarasvatī</s>) ewe; for the <s>Maruts</s> of victory, a dappled barren cow — the fifth of the sacrificial animals.
ŚŚS 15.1.22: Seventeen dark, hornless <s>Prājāpatya</s> (for <s>Prajāpati</s>) [animals] to be sacrificed at the time of a <s>Lapsudina</s> [rite].
ŚŚS 15.1.23: The continuous [procedure] of the pressing offerings [extends] up to the circling with fire.
ŚŚS 15.1.24: They are consecrated with the <s>Brahma-sāman</s> (chant).
ŚŚS 15.1.25: The <s>Ādhrigu</s> [hymn] should be repeated, and the <s>stokyā</s> [verses] also.
ŚŚS 15.1.26: 'Bring <s>Agni</s> forth for him, O slayer of cows' — the continuous [rite]; the last <s>prayāja</s> (pre-offering); and the shavings.
ŚŚS 15.1.27: The giving [of dakṣiṇā] upward from the yoking of the bay horses.
ŚŚS 15.1.28: The subsidiary parts beginning with the tree [offering] should be drawn out.
ŚŚS 15.1.29: Or when the after-offerings have been offered.
ŚŚS 15.1.30: Or at their own proper times.
ŚŚS 15.1.31: The seventeen-fold <s>stoma</s>.
ŚŚS 15.1.32: The <s>Vairāja</s> [is] the <s>ājya</s> (ghee-hymn).
ŚŚS 15.1.33: Or the <s>Ghṛtastomīya</s>.
ŚŚS 15.1.34: The <s>prauga</s> is of <s>Madhucchandas</s>.
ŚŚS 15.1.35: Food indeed is <s>Virāṭ</s>; ghee is food.
ŚŚS 15.1.36: The essence [of the <s>prauga</s>] is of <s>Madhucchandas</s>.
ŚŚS 15.1.37: He places the essence with the food.
ŚŚS 15.1.38: Or the one-day [format].
ŚŚS 15.1.39: Or the one-day [sacrifice] is the foundation.
ŚŚS 15.1.40: For the sake of establishment itself.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.2.1: In the <s>Trikadruka</s> [hymns]: 'The buffalo [drinks] barley-mixed' [and] 'O mighty one' (<s>Tuviśuṣma</s>) — he begins the <s>Marutvatīya</s> with a hyper-metric (<s>atichandas</s>) [verse].
ŚŚS 15.2.2: The hyper-metric meter belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.3: The <s>Vājapeya</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.4: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.2.5: He should begin with 'Ā tvā ratham yathā ūtaye' (Come to your chariot for aid).
ŚŚS 15.2.6: The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.7: The <s>Vājapeya</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.8: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.2.9: 'Kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḍā' (With what beauty, companions of the same nest) — this is the <s>Marutvatīya</s>; the <s>Kadvat-kayā-śubhīya</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.10: 'Ka' (who) indeed is <s>Prajāpati</s>; the <s>Vājapeya</s> [is <s>Prajāpati</s>].
ŚŚS 15.2.11: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.2.12: A <s>Bārhaspatya</s> (for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>) [rice-cake] of wild rice, [prepared in] seventeen saucers.
ŚŚS 15.2.13: The seventeenth indeed is <s>Prajāpati</s>; the <s>Vājapeya</s> [is <s>Prajāpati</s>].
ŚŚS 15.2.14: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.2.15: That [offering takes place] between the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> and <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitations], and at the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s> (pressing for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>).
ŚŚS 15.2.16: There he is consecrated (anointed) — before the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> [offering].
ŚŚS 15.2.17: Its giving [of dakṣiṇā], the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, and the <s>Iḍā</s> [follow].
ŚŚS 15.2.18: 'Tad id āsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭham' (That indeed was the eldest in the worlds) — this is the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.19: The sacrifice indeed is the eldest in the worlds.
ŚŚS 15.2.20: The sacrifice indeed is <s>Prajāpati</s>; the <s>Vājapeya</s> [is <s>Prajāpati</s>].
ŚŚS 15.2.21: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.2.22: From the <s>Anucara</s> (attendant hymns) onward, from the sixth [day], the third pressing.
ŚŚS 15.2.23: The sixth day belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.24: The <s>Vājapeya</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.25: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.2.26: Or from the solstice (<s>viṣuvat</s>).
ŚŚS 15.2.27: Ascent (<s>roha</s>) indeed is the solstice.
ŚŚS 15.2.28: Ascent is the <s>Vājapeya</s>.
ŚŚS 15.2.29: Thus he fulfills it with its own nature.
ŚŚS 15.2.30: Or the one-day [format].
ŚŚS 15.2.31: Or the one-day [sacrifice] is the foundation.
ŚŚS 15.2.32: For the sake of establishment itself.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.3.1: There, before the <s>Ā no bhadrīya</s> [hymn], he should insert the <s>Madhunāḍī</s> (honey-tube hymns) — this is the [teaching] of <s>Paiṅgya</s>.
ŚŚS 15.3.2: 'Imam mahe vidathyāya' [and] 'Uṣasaḥ pūrvāḥ' — the verse [arrangement].
ŚŚS 15.3.3: If they were to perform the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>Sāman</s> with the <s>Citravatī</s> [verses] — 'Tvam naś citra ūtyā' [and] 'Agne vivasvat' — the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> <s>pragāthas</s>.
ŚŚS 15.3.4: Above the sixteen-fold [stoma], the supplementary <s>uktha</s> (praise).
ŚŚS 15.3.5: 'Pra tat te adya Śipiviṣṭa' [and] 'Pra tad Viṣṇuḥ' — the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s>.
ŚŚS 15.3.6: 'Brahma jajñānam prathamam purastāt' (The sacred word was born first, in the east) — two [verses].
ŚŚS 15.3.7: 'Those who led thought by thoughts, the foremost of speech, or who spoke truths by mind — agreeing with the third sacred utterance, they conceived the name of the milch cow by the fourth.'
ŚŚS 15.3.8: 'Venas tat paśyat' (Vena saw that) — five [verses].
ŚŚS 15.3.9: Or 'Ayam Venaḥ' (This Vena).
ŚŚS 15.3.11: Of 'Tam pratnathā' — thirteen [verses]; leaving out the last, having called, having encircled, he offers with 'Prajāpata.'
ŚŚS 15.3.12: He gives seventeen hundreds of cows.
ŚŚS 15.3.13: Seventeen [hundreds] of garments.
ŚŚS 15.3.14: Seventeen yoked vehicles — chariots, elephants, gold ornaments (<s>niṣkas</s>), and drums (<s>dundubhis</s>).
ŚŚS 15.3.15: These amount to seven sets of one hundred and seventeen.
ŚŚS 15.3.16: Thus is the fulfilled <s>Vājapeya</s>.
ŚŚS 15.3.17: 'Seventeen of each age group' — this is the <s>Kuru-Vājapeya</s>.

body.text:
ŚŚS_15.4.1: vāja.peyena.iṣṭvā.bṛhaspati.savaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.4.2: tejas.kāmasya.brahma.varcasa.kāmasya.ca /
ŚŚS_15.4.3: roho.vai.vāja.peyas.tejo.brahma.varcasam.bṛhaspati.savaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.4.4: tat.tejasi.brahma.varcase.pratitiṣṭhati /
ŚŚS_15.4.5: trivṛt.stomaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.4.6: rathantaram.pṛṣṭham /
ŚŚS_15.4.7: tṛca.klṛptam.śastram /
ŚŚS_15.4.8: agniṣṭomo.yajñaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.4.9: yas.tastambha.iti.catasro.anupūrvam.purastāt.sūktānām.eka.ekām.niṣkevalya.prabhṛtiṣu /
ŚŚS_15.4.10: trayastriṃśad.dakṣiṇā /
ŚŚS_15.4.11: anusavanam.ekādaśa.ekādaśa /
ŚŚS_15.4.12: anūbandhyasya.vapāyām.saṃsthitāyām.vaḍavām.brahmaṇe.anuśiśum /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.4.1: Having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, [one performs] the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s> (pressing for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>).
ŚŚS 15.4.2: [It is] for one who desires splendor (<s>tejas</s>) and sacred brilliance (<s>brahmavarcas</s>).
ŚŚS 15.4.3: Ascent (<s>roha</s>) indeed is the <s>Vājapeya</s>; splendor and sacred brilliance is the <s>Bṛhaspati-sava</s>.
ŚŚS 15.4.4: He thus becomes established in splendor and sacred brilliance.
ŚŚS 15.4.5: The nine-fold <s>stoma</s>.
ŚŚS 15.4.6: The <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
ŚŚS 15.4.7: The recitation is arranged in triplets.
ŚŚS 15.4.8: The sacrifice is an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
ŚŚS 15.4.9: 'Yas tastambha' — four [verses], one each in order, placed before the hymns, from the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> onward.
ŚŚS 15.4.10: Thirty-three [are] the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (priestly fees).
ŚŚS 15.4.11: Eleven for each pressing, [totaling] eleven [per pressing].
ŚŚS 15.4.12: When the omental offering of the <s>Anubandhya</s> (concluding animal) has been completed, [he gives] a mare with her foal to the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].

body.text:
ŚŚS_15.5.1: prajāpatir.ha.devān.sṛṣṭvā.tebhya.etad.anna.pānam.sasṛje.etān.yajñān.|.agniṣṭomam.prathamam.|.sa.enān.na.anvabhavat.|.atha.atyagniṣṭomam.|.sa.enān.na.anvabhavat.|.atha.ukthyam.|.sa.enān.na.anvabhavat.|.atha.ṣoḷaśinam.|.sa.enān.na.anvabhavat.|.atha.vājapeyam.|.sa.enān.na.anvabhavat.|.atha.atirātram.|.sa.enān.na.anvabhavat.|.atha.āptoryāmāṇam.|.sa.enān.anvabhavat /
ŚŚS_15.5.2: tasya.trayas.triṃśat.stotrāṇi /
ŚŚS_15.5.3: trayas.triṃśat.śastrāṇi /
ŚŚS_15.5.5: trayas.triṃśad.ukthya.āhutayaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.5.5: trayas.triṃśad.vai.sarve.devāḥ /
ŚŚS_15.5.6: tad.enān.stotraiḥ.śastrair.ukthya.āhutibhir.iti.pratyekam.sarvān.prīṇāti /
ŚŚS_15.5.7: tasya.nava.stomāḥ /
ŚŚS_15.5.8: nava.pṛṣṭhāni /
ŚŚS_15.5.9: ṣaṭ.saṃsthāḥ /
ŚŚS_15.5.10: parigraheṇa.tāni.catur.viṃśatiḥ /
ŚŚS_15.5.11: catur.viṃśatir.vai.saṃvatsarasya.ardha.māsāḥ /
ŚŚS_15.5.12: saṃvatsarasya.eva.āptyai /
ŚŚS_15.5.13: āpto.vai.ba.ayam.yāmo.yo.devāṃś.ca.saṃvatsaram.ca.anubhavati.iti.|.tasmād.āptoryāmaḥ /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.5.1: <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created the gods, produced for them this food and drink — these sacrifices. The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> was first. It did not satisfy them. Then the <s>Atyagniṣṭoma</s>. It did not satisfy them. Then the <s>Ukthya</s>. It did not satisfy them. Then the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>. It did not satisfy them. Then the <s>Vājapeya</s>. It did not satisfy them. Then the <s>Atirātra</s>. It did not satisfy them. Then the <s>Āptoryāma</s>. It satisfied them.
ŚŚS 15.5.2: It has thirty-three <s>stotra</s>s (chants).
ŚŚS 15.5.3: Thirty-three <s>śastra</s>s (recitations).
ŚŚS 15.5.5: Thirty-three <s>ukthya</s> oblations.
ŚŚS 15.5.5: Thirty-three indeed are all the gods.
ŚŚS 15.5.6: Thus with the <s>stotra</s>s, <s>śastra</s>s, and <s>ukthya</s> oblations respectively, he gratifies all [the gods] individually.
ŚŚS 15.5.7: It has nine <s>stomas</s> (chant-forms).
ŚŚS 15.5.8: Nine <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s (back-chants).
ŚŚS 15.5.9: Six conclusions (<s>saṃsthā</s>s).
ŚŚS 15.5.10: By inclusion, those total twenty-four.
ŚŚS 15.5.11: Twenty-four indeed are the half-months of the year.
ŚŚS 15.5.12: [This is] for the attainment of the year.
ŚŚS 15.5.13: 'Attained indeed is this course (<s>yāma</s>) which encompasses the gods and the year' — therefore [it is called] <s>Āptoryāma</s> (attainment of the course).

body.text:
ŚŚS_15.6.1: chandomāḥ.pavamānāḥ /
ŚŚS_15.6.2: trivṛt.pañcadaśe.saptadaśa.ekaviṃśe.ca.ājyāni /
ŚŚS_15.6.3: triṇavāni.pṛṣṭhāni /
ŚŚS_15.6.4: trayas.triṃśam.agniṣṭoma.sāma /
ŚŚS_15.6.5: ya.ājyānām.stomās.te.atirikta.ukthānām /
ŚŚS_15.6.6: etair.vai.prajāpatir.ubhayato.agniṣṭoma.stomaiḥ.sarvān.kāmān.anubhavataḥ.parigṛhya.ātmann.adhata /
ŚŚS_15.6.7: tatho.eva.etad.yajamāna.etair.eva.ubhayato.agniṣṭoma.stomaiḥ.sarvān.kāmān.ubhayataḥ.parigṛhya.ātman.dhatte /
ŚŚS_15.6.8: viśvajitaḥ.sarva.pṛṣṭhāt.sahautram.prātaḥ.savanam /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.6.1: The <s>Pavamāna</s> [chants follow the] <s>Chandoma</s> [pattern].
ŚŚS 15.6.2: The <s>ājya</s> (ghee-offering chants) are in the <s>trivṛt</s> (ninefold), <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteenfold), <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeenfold), and <s>ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-onefold) [stomas].
ŚŚS 15.6.3: The <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chants) are in the <s>triṇava</s> (twenty-sevenfold) [stoma].
ŚŚS 15.6.4: The <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s> is in the <s>trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-threefold) [stoma].
ŚŚS 15.6.5: The <s>stomas</s> of the <s>ājya</s> [chants] are [also used for] the additional <s>uktha</s> [recitations].
ŚŚS 15.6.6: With these <s>Agniṣṭoma stomas</s> on both sides, <s>Prajāpati</s> encompassed all desires and placed them in himself.
ŚŚS 15.6.7: Likewise, the sacrificer, with these very <s>Agniṣṭoma stomas</s> on both sides, encompasses all desires from both sides and places them in himself.
ŚŚS 15.6.8: The morning pressing follows the model of the <s>Viśvajit</s> with all <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s, with the <s>Sautra</s> [arrangement].

body.text:
ŚŚS_15.7.1: kayā.śubhīyam.cāturtha.āhnike.ca.aikāhikāt.pūrvāṇi.iti.marutvatīyam /
ŚŚS_15.7.2: bṛhad.vairāja.garbham.hotuḥ.pṛṣṭham.bhavati.rathantaram.vā /
ŚŚS_15.7.3: vāmadevyam.śākvara.garbham.maitrāvaruṇasya /
ŚŚS_15.7.4: śyaitam.vairūpa.garbham.brāhmaṇācchaṃsino.naudhasam.vā /
ŚŚS_15.7.5: kāleyam.raivata.garbham.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_15.7.6: garbham.pūrvam.śaṃsed.iti.ha.eka.āhur.atha.ātmānam.iti /
ŚŚS_15.7.7: ātmānam.tv.eva.pūrvam.śaṃset /
ŚŚS_15.7.8: ātmānam.vā.anū.garbhaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.7.9: aikāhikān.stotriyān.śastvā.viśvajitaḥ.sarva.pṛṣṭhāt.stotriyān.śaṃsanti /
ŚŚS_15.7.10: tathā.anurūpān /
ŚŚS_15.7.11: sāma.pragāthāṃś.ca /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.7.1: The <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> [hymn] and those before the <s>ekāhika</s> (one-day) [hymns] in the fourth-day [series are used] for the <s>Marutvatīya</s> [recitation].
ŚŚS 15.7.2: The <s>pṛṣṭha</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> is the <s>Bṛhad</s> with the <s>Vairāja</s> embedded, or the <s>Rathantara</s>.
ŚŚS 15.7.3: For the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> [priest], the <s>Vāmadevya</s> with the <s>Śākvara</s> embedded.
ŚŚS 15.7.4: For the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, the <s>Śyaita</s> with the <s>Vairūpa</s> embedded, or the <s>Naudhasa</s>.
ŚŚS 15.7.5: For the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, the <s>Kāleya</s> with the <s>Raivata</s> embedded.
ŚŚS 15.7.6: 'One should recite the embedded [chant] first,' say some; 'then the main one.'
ŚŚS 15.7.7: But one should recite the main one first.
ŚŚS 15.7.8: The embedded follows the main one.
ŚŚS 15.7.9: Having recited the <s>stotriya</s> [verses] of the one-day [rites], they recite the <s>stotriya</s>s from the <s>Viśvajit</s> with all <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s.
ŚŚS 15.7.10: Likewise the <s>anurūpa</s>s.
ŚŚS 15.7.11: And the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>s.

body.text:
ŚŚS_15.8.1: tad.id.āsīyam.cārutha.āhnike.ca.aikāhikāt.pūrvāṇi.iti.niṣkevalyam /
ŚŚS_15.8.2: yāni.pāñcama.āhnikāni.madhyatas.trīṇi.maitrāvaruṇasya.aikāhitābhyām.pūrvāṇi /
ŚŚS_15.8.3: tārtīya.āhnike.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.4: acchāvākasya.ṣaṣṭha.āhnike /
ŚŚS_15.8.5: anucara.prabhṛti.ṣaṣṭhāt.tṛtīya.savanam /
ŚŚS_15.8.6: āśvinād.ūrdhvam.atirikta.ukthāni /
ŚŚS_15.8.7: jarā.bodha.jaramāṇa.iti.stotriya.anurūpau.hotuḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.8: tyam.u.vaḥ.satrāsāham.iti.maitrāvaruṇasya /
ŚŚS_15.8.9: kam.te.dānā.asakṣata.yad.adya.kaś.ca.vṛtrahann.iti.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.10: tad.vo.gāya.stotram.indrāya.gāyata.iti.vā /
ŚŚS_15.8.11: idam.viṣṇur.ity.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_15.8.12: uttare.ca.pūrvā.ca.anurūpaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.13: eṣo.uṣā.dūrād.iha.eva.udīrāthām.ā.me.havam.ity.anupūrvam.navarcāni /
ŚŚS_15.8.14: ā.bhāti.iti.hotuḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.15: uttaram.maitrāvaruṇasya /
ŚŚS_15.8.16: ā.gomata.iti.brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.17: uttaram.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_15.8.18: kṣetrasya.patinā.iti.trayāṇām.tisraḥ.paridhānīyāḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.19: śam.no.devaḥ.savitā.trāyamāṇa.ity.acchāvākasya /
ŚŚS_15.8.20: ime.somāsa.ime.mandrāso.atyā.yātam.nivata.ā.no.gacchatam.havana.iti.yājyāḥ /
ŚŚS_15.8.21: purāṇam.okaḥ.sakyam.śivam.vām.iti.vā.anupūrvam.catasraḥ /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.8.1: 'Tad id āsa' and those before the <s>ekāhika</s> [hymns] in the fourth-day [series are used] for the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [recitation].
ŚŚS 15.8.2: The fifth-day [hymns] — the middle three for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, before the two one-day [hymns].
ŚŚS 15.8.3: Those of the third day for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.4: Those of the sixth day for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.5: The third pressing [begins] from the <s>Anucara</s> [hymn] onward, from the sixth [day series].
ŚŚS 15.8.6: After the <s>Āśvina</s> [pressing], the additional <s>uktha</s> [recitations follow].
ŚŚS 15.8.7: 'Jarābodha' [and] 'Jaramāṇa' are the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.8: 'Tyam u vaḥ satrāsāham' for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.9: 'Kam te dānā asakṣata' [and] 'Yad adya kaś ca vṛtrahan' for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.10: Or 'Tad vo gāya stotram indrāya gāyata.'
ŚŚS 15.8.11: 'Idam Viṣṇuḥ' for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.12: The latter [verse of each pair] and the former serve as the <s>anurūpa</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.13: 'Eṣo uṣā dūrāt,' 'Iha eva udīrāthām,' 'Ā me havam' — nine-versed [hymns] in order.
ŚŚS 15.8.14: 'Ā bhāti' for the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.15: The next one for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.16: 'Ā gomata' for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.17: The next one for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.18: 'Kṣetrasya patinā' — three closing verses (<s>paridhānīyā</s>s) for three [priests].
ŚŚS 15.8.19: 'Śam no devaḥ Savitā trāyamāṇaḥ' for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
ŚŚS 15.8.20: 'Ime somāsaḥ,' 'Ime mandrāsaḥ,' 'Atyā yātam nivatā,' 'Ā no gacchatam havanā' — the offering verses (<s>yājyā</s>s).
ŚŚS 15.8.21: Or 'Purāṇam okaḥ sakyam śivam vām' — four [verses] in sequence.

body.text:
ŚŚS_15.9.1: yama.stomaḥ /
ŚŚS_15.9.2: yoamo.ha.svarga.kāmas.tapas.taptvā.etam.yajña.kratum.apaśyad.yama.stomam.|.tam.āharat.|.tena.ayajata.|.tena.iṣṭvā.svargam.āpnot.|.tena.svarga.kāmo.yajeta /
ŚŚS_15.9.3: stotriya.anurūpān.śastrāṇām.uddhṛtya.sāma.ātānāṃś.ca /
ŚŚS_15.9.4: yāvatyas.tā.bhavanti.tāvatyas.tad.devatās.tat.chandasa.upajāyante /
ŚŚS_15.9.5: pareyivāṃsam.iti.pañcānām.purastāt.sūktānām.eka.ekām.madhyaṃdine /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.9.1: The <s>Yamastoma</s> (twin-chant).
ŚŚS 15.9.2: <s>Yama</s>, desiring heaven, having performed austerity (<s>tapas</s>), perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Yamastoma</s>. He obtained it. With it he sacrificed. Having sacrificed with it, he attained heaven. With it, one desiring heaven should sacrifice.
ŚŚS 15.9.3: Having extracted the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> [verses] from the recitations, and also the <s>sāma</s>-melodies.
ŚŚS 15.9.4: As many as those are, that many deities and meters are additionally generated.
ŚŚS 15.9.5: 'Pareyivāṃsam' (to the departed) — one [verse] from before each of the five hymns at the midday [pressing].

body.text:
ŚŚS_15.10.1: gāyatraḥ.sarva.svāro.maraṇa.kāmasya.svarga.kāmasya.ca /
ŚŚS_15.10.2: traiṣṭubhaḥ.sarva.nidhanaḥ.pratiṣṭhā.kāmasya /
ŚŚS_15.10.3: jāgataḥ.sarva.iḷaḥ.paśu.kāmasya.ca /
ŚŚS_15.10.4: ānuṣṭubhaḥ.sarva.vān.nidhanaḥ.śruta.kāmasya /
ŚŚS_15.10.5: pratyakṣam.sampadā.vā /
ŚŚS_15.10.6: nṛjit.prabhṛtibhyo.nividdhānāni /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.10.1: The <s>Gāyatra</s> [stoma] with all <s>svāra</s> (tonal) [endings is] for one desiring death [i.e., liberation] and one desiring heaven.
ŚŚS 15.10.2: The <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> [stoma] with all <s>nidhana</s> (concluding) [notes is] for one desiring a firm foundation.
ŚŚS 15.10.3: The <s>Jāgata</s> [stoma] with all <s>iḍā</s> (refreshment) [responses is] for one desiring cattle.
ŚŚS 15.10.4: The <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> [stoma] with all <s>vāṅnidhana</s> (speech-concluding) [notes is] for one desiring fame (<s>śruta</s>).
ŚŚS 15.10.5: Either directly or by equivalence.
ŚŚS 15.10.6: From the <s>Nṛjit</s> onward, <s>nivid</s> (invocatory formulas) are inserted.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 15.11.1: <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) desired: 'May I attain supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship over all beings.' She perceived this sacrificial plan — the <s>Vācaḥstoma</s> (praise of Speech). She obtained it. With it she sacrificed. Having sacrificed with it, she attained supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship over all beings. Likewise, when the sacrificer sacrifices with the <s>Vācaḥstoma</s>, he attains supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship over all beings.
ŚŚS 15.11.2: The <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> [is chanted] in hundreds.
ŚŚS 15.11.3: The <s>ājya</s> [chant is] in thousands.
ŚŚS 15.11.4: The <s>stotra</s>s [proceed in powers of ten]: ten thousand (<s>ayuta</s>), hundred thousand (<s>prayuta</s>), million (<s>niyuta</s>), ten million (<s>arbuda</s>), hundred million (<s>nyarbuda</s>), billion (<s>nikharva</s>), <s>samudra</s>, <s>salila</s>, <s>antya</s>, <s>anantya</s>.
ŚŚS 15.11.5: All the <s>ṛc</s> verses are employed, returning again and again, for the additional <s>stoma</s> recitations.
ŚŚS 15.11.6: Likewise the <s>sāmans</s> and <s>yajus</s> formulas.
ŚŚS 15.11.7: And having raised [the chant to conclusion], it becomes an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
ŚŚS 15.11.8: A thousand is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) for the <s>Vācaḥstoma</s>.
ŚŚS 15.11.9: In the great sacrifice:
ŚŚS 15.11.10: For the <s>Viutti</s> and <s>Anubhūti</s> [sacrifices].
ŚŚS 15.11.11: For the <s>Sarvajit</s> and <s>Dhanajit</s>.
ŚŚS 15.11.12: For the <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Abhijit</s>.
ŚŚS 15.11.13: For the <s>Sarvajit</s> and <s>Indravajra</s>.
ŚŚS 15.11.14: And in the <s>Āptoryāma</s>.
ŚŚS 15.11.15: When there is no specific instruction, the standard rule (<s>prakṛti</s>) applies for the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>s.

body.translated_text:
15.12.1: <s>Varuṇa</s> desired: "May I attain supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship over all kingdoms." He perceived this sacrificial rite — the <s>Rājasūya</s>. He brought it; he sacrificed with it. Having sacrificed with it, he attained supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship over all kingdoms. So too the sacrificer, when he sacrifices with the <s>Rājasūya</s>, attains supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship over all kingdoms.
15.12.2: A <s>Bhārgava</s> (descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>) is the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
15.12.3: Having offered a he-goat for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Pūṣan</s>, on the new-moon day of <s>Māgha</s>, the day after a one-day [<s>Soma</s> rite], he should be consecrated (<s>dīkṣā</s>) for the <s>Pavitra</s> [rite].
15.12.4: That is this same <s>Catuṣṭoma</s>, <s>Rathantara</s>-<s>pṛṣṭha</s>, <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
15.12.5: This is the <s>Pavitra</s> (purificatory rite). By it, being purified, one attains the pressing (<s>sava</s>).
15.12.6: The pressing day is on the eighth day.
15.12.7: With <s>iṣṭis</s> (oblations) for the remainder of the fortnight.
15.12.8: On the <s>Phālgunī</s> [full moon], having commenced the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly) rites.
15.12.9: For six months, the animal [sacrifice].
15.12.10: On the <s>Māghī</s> [full moon], the <s>Śunāsīrīya</s>.
15.12.11: For the following month, with <s>iṣṭis</s>.
15.12.12: On the <s>Phālgunī</s>, he is consecrated for the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> (consecration rite) and <s>Daśapeya</s> (ten-drinking rite).
15.12.13: Twelve consecrations (<s>dīkṣā</s>), three approach-offerings (<s>upasad</s>).
15.12.14: The pressing day is on the sixteenth day.
15.12.15: Or sixteen is the measure for all of this.
15.12.16: For the attainment of all this indeed.

body.translated_text:
15.13.1: They purchase both <s>Soma</s> [plants] together.
15.13.2: The ritual framework (<s>tantra</s>) of the <s>Daśapeya</s> extends up to the hospitality rite (<s>ātithya</s>) and beyond the concluding bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>).
15.13.3: "O <s>Agni</s>, you are <s>Varuṇa</s>" — the <s>Ājya</s> [recitation] is the <s>Varuṇa</s>-<s>nyaṅga</s>.
15.13.4: For they are consecrating <s>Varuṇa</s>.
15.13.5: The midday [pressing has] the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> [<s>stoma</s>].
15.13.6: With the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> [recitation] between the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> and <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
15.13.7: There the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) takes place before the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
15.13.8: The gift-giving (<s>pradāna</s>) and the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>-<s>Iḍā</s> belong to that [consecration].
15.13.9: The third pressing [follows the pattern] of the second day.
15.13.10: That is concluded as an <s>Ukthya</s>.
15.13.11: Or the <s>Ukthyas</s> [are substituted by] animals.
15.13.12: For the attainment of animals indeed.
15.13.13: They proceed to the concluding bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>).
15.13.14: The <s>avabhṛtha</s> ritual is performed, but he does not bathe.
15.13.15: Having placed the right forefoot of a black antelope skin in the water, they draw [the sacrificer] back, or [they immerse] a tenth [part] of his garment.

body.translated_text:
15.14.1: Then he proceeds to the northern sacrificial ground (<s>deva-yajana</s>).
15.14.2: He sacrifices there with the <s>iṣṭis</s> of the <s>Saṃsṛpas</s> (creeping rites).
15.14.3: Ten [<s>iṣṭis</s>] for ten days.
15.14.4: Then [the dedications are:] for <s>Savitṛ Prasavitṛ</s> (the Impeller), for <s>Savitṛ Āsavitṛ</s> (the Presser), for <s>Savitṛ Satya-prasava</s> (of True Impulsion), for <s>Sarasvatī Vāc</s> (Speech), for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> for forms, for <s>Pūṣan</s> for paths, for this <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> for brilliance, for <s>Soma</s> the king, for <s>Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa</s>.
15.14.5: On the tenth day, the <s>Daśapeya</s>.
15.14.6: Or with these ten deities they may proceed (<s>prasarpeyuḥ</s>) or distribute (<s>bhakṣayeyuḥ</s>).
15.14.7: "For <s>Savitṛ Prasavitṛ</s> I proceed" — or "For <s>Savitṛ Āsavitṛ</s> I distribute."
15.14.8: Those who have ten generations of Vedic scholars (<s>śrotriya</s>) on both sides should serve as officiating priests.
15.14.9: A hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s> partake of the <s>Soma</s>.
15.14.10: Ten [<s>brāhmaṇas</s>] from each cup, ten by ten.
15.14.11: Therefore [it is called] the <s>Daśapeya</s> ("ten-drinking").
15.14.12: Having risen, [he offers] a five-portion rice-offering.
15.14.13: At the conclusion, [two animals are offered] — a hawk-colored (<s>Śyenī</s>) and a spotted (<s>Pṛṣanī</s>) [cow], both having calves at foot, both pregnant — the first belonging to <s>Āditya</s> or <s>Vaiśvadevī</s>, the latter to <s>Mārutī</s>.

body.translated_text:
15.15.1: Now the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> [in the <s>Rājasūya</s> context].
15.15.2: For the <s>Aśvins</s>, a reddish he-goat.
15.15.3: For <s>Sarasvatī</s>, a ewe.
15.15.4: For <s>Indra Sutrāman</s> (the Good Protector), a bull.
15.15.5: When the circumambulations by fire have been performed, they proceed with <s>surā</s> (liquor) and <s>Soma</s>.
15.15.6: "Purify me by the purifier, shining brightly, O divine one" and "O <s>Agni</s>, flesh-eating, by [your] will" — with these they consecrate the flowing <s>surā</s>.
15.15.7: Or with [verses] having the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors) as deities.
15.15.8: "You two, the <s>surā</s>" — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse).
15.15.9: "May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer to the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and <s>Indra Sutrāman</s>" — this is the directive (<s>praiṣa</s>).
15.15.10: Some recite all the modifications (<s>vikṛtas</s>).
15.15.11: But one should not do so; that is demonic (<s>āsura</s>).
15.15.12: "Like a son" — this is the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse).
15.15.13: "What the <s>Aśvins</s> [gave] to <s>Namuci</s> the <s>Asura</s>, what <s>Sarasvatī</s> endowed for <s>Indra</s>'s power — this bright, honey-sweet moon, <s>Soma</s> the king, I here partake" — this is the partaking mantra for the <s>surā</s>.
15.15.14: "One should purchase a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>surā</s>-drinker" — thus it is prescribed for the partaking.

body.translated_text:
15.16.1: After this, the <s>Keśavapanīya</s> (hair-shaving rite).
15.16.2: The <s>Traidhātavī</s> [<s>iṣṭi</s>] is the <s>Udavasānīyā</s> (concluding offering).
15.16.3: [Dedicated] to <s>Agni</s>-<s>Viṣṇu</s> or to <s>Indra</s>-<s>Viṣṇu</s>.
15.16.4: The dispersal (<s>vyuṣṭi</s>) after that is a <s>Dvirātra</s> (two-night rite).
15.16.5: An <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and an <s>Atirātra</s>.
15.16.6: For the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who recites this [<s>Veda</s>], it dawns [with glory].
15.16.7: And for the <s>kṣatriya</s> who attains the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), it dawns.
15.16.8: Now, with this [rite called] <s>Kṣatrasya Dhṛti</s> ("Support of the Ruling Power"), he sacrifices.
15.16.9: With the <s>Catuṣṭoma</s>, <s>Rathantara</s>-<s>pṛṣṭha</s>, <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
15.16.10: But <s>Vṛddhadyumna Ābhipratāriṇa</s> sacrificed with that using the <s>Triṣṭoma</s>.
15.16.11: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> objected to him: "This is not the <s>Kṣatrasya Dhṛti</s>. In this very battle, the <s>Kurus</s> will be driven from <s>Kurukṣetra</s>."
15.16.12: And indeed it was just as he had told him.
15.16.13: Therefore one should sacrifice with the <s>Catuṣṭoma</s> only.
15.16.14: For the <s>Catuṣṭoma</s> is the foundation of sacrifices.
15.16.15: For the sake of foundation indeed.
15.16.16: Ten thousand (<s>ayuta</s>) is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee).
15.16.17: Neither kingdom nor people abandon him who gives ten thousand.
15.16.18: That is the "ten-thousand-ness" of the <s>ayuta</s>.
15.16.19: Or one hundred thousand.

body.translated_text:
15.17.1a: King <s>Hariścandra</s>, son of <s>Vidhasa</s>, of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> dynasty, was without a son. He had a hundred wives, but among them he did not obtain a son. <s>Parvata</s> and <s>Nārada</s> dwelt in his house. He asked <s>Nārada</s>:
15.17.1b: 'What indeed those desire who seek a son — both those who know [his value] and those who do not — what does one gain through a son? Tell us that, O <s>Nārada</s>.' Asked with one [verse], he replied with ten:
15.17.1c: 'He repays his debt through this [son], and attains immortality...'

body.translated_text:
15.18.1a: He [Nārada] said [to Hariścandra]: 'Approach King <s>Varuṇa</s> [saying]: "May a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to thee."' 'So be it.' He approached King <s>Varuṇa</s>.
15.18.1b: 'May a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to thee.' 'So be it.' A son was born to him, named <s>Rohita</s>. <s>Varuṇa</s> said to him: 'A son has been born to you indeed; sacrifice to me with him.' He replied:
15.18.1c: 'When indeed an animal becomes ten [days old], then it becomes fit for sacrifice...'

body.translated_text:
15.19.1a: 'There is no prosperity (<s>śrī</s>) for one who does not exert himself' — thus, O <s>Rohita</s>, we have heard. 'Sinful is the sedentary man; <s>Indra</s> is the companion of the one who wanders.'
15.19.1b: 'Wander, O <s>Rohita</s>!' — 'Wander indeed!' — thus a brahmin spoke to me. So he wandered in the forest for a second year. He came from the forest to the village. <s>Indra</s>, in the form of a man, approached him and said:
15.19.1c: 'Fortune (<s>bhaga</s>) sits with the one who sits; it rises with the one who stands; it lies down with the one who lies down; but fortune moves with the one who moves.'

body.translated_text:
15.20.1a: He [the sage Ajīgarta] had three sons — <s>Śunaḥpuccha</s> (Dog's Tail), <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> (Dog's Cord), and <s>Śunolāṅgūla</s> (Dog's Tail). He [Rohita] said to him: 'O sage, I shall purchase myself with one of these [sons]; I shall give thee a hundred cows.'
15.20.1b: The father, holding back [his] eldest, said: 'Not this one indeed.' 'Not this one either,' said the mother regarding the youngest. The two agreed upon the middle one — <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>.
15.20.1c: Having given a hundred [cows] and taken him, he came from the forest to the village. Going to [his] father...

body.translated_text:
15.21.1a: For his [sacrifice], <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), <s>Asāyāsya</s> (?) was the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest), <s>Jamadagni</s> was the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest), and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> was the <s>brahmā</s> (supervising priest). When [the victim] had been consecrated for him, they could not find a slaughterer. Then <s>Ajīgarta Sauyavasi</s> spoke:
15.21.1b: "Give me another hundred [cows], and I will bind him." They gave him another hundred. He bound him. When [the victim] had been consecrated, bound, and circumambulated with fire, they could not find a butcher.
15.21.1c: Then <s>Ajīgarta Sauyavasi</s> spoke: "Give me another hundred [cows], and I will slaughter him." They gave him another hundred. He came forward, sharpening his knife.
15.21.1d: Then <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> reflected: "They will slaughter me as if I were not a human being. Come, let me take refuge in the gods."

body.translated_text:
15.22.1a: He first approached <s>Prajāpati</s> among the gods, with this <s>ṛc</s> (verse): "To which one now, to which of the immortals?" <s>Prajāpati</s> said to him: "You are nearest to <s>Agni</s>; approach him."
15.22.1b: He approached <s>Agni</s> with this <s>ṛc</s>: "Of <s>Agni</s>, the first of the immortals, we..." <s>Agni</s> said to him: "<s>Savitṛ</s> rules over impulsions; approach him." He approached <s>Savitṛ</s> with this <s>tṛca</s> (group of three verses): "O god <s>Savitar</s>, unto you..."
15.22.1c: <s>Savitṛ</s> said to him: "You have been bound for king <s>Varuṇa</s>; approach him." <s>Savitṛ</s> said: "You have been bound for king <s>Varuṇa</s>; approach him."
15.22.1d: He approached king <s>Varuṇa</s> with the following thirty-one [verses]. <s>Varuṇa</s> said to him: "<s>Agni</s> is the mouth of the gods, the kind-hearted one; praise him, and then I will release you."
15.22.1e: He praised <s>Agni</s> with the following twenty-two [verses]. <s>Agni</s> said to him: "Praise all the gods, and then I will release you."
15.22.1f: He praised the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods) with this <s>ṛc</s>: "Homage to the great ones, homage to the small ones." The <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> said: "Praise <s>Indra</s>, and then we will release you." He praised <s>Indra</s> with the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) "If indeed, O true <s>Soma</s>-drinker" — with the fifteen [verses] of the latter [part].
15.22.1g: Being praised, <s>Indra</s> was pleased with him and gave him a golden chariot. He received it with this <s>ṛc</s>: "Ever, O <s>Indra</s>..." <s>Indra</s> said to him: "Praise the <s>Aśvins</s>, and then I will release you."
15.22.1h: He praised the <s>Aśvins</s> with the following <s>tṛca</s>. The <s>Aśvins</s> said: "Praise <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), and then we will release you." He praised <s>Uṣas</s> with the following <s>tṛca</s>.
15.22.1i: As each <s>ṛc</s> was recited, his bonds loosened progressively, and the belly of <s>Aikṣvāka</s> (Hariścandra) became smaller. When the last <s>ṛc</s> was recited, his bonds were completely released, and <s>Aikṣvāka</s> became free of disease. Then the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) said to him: "You yourself shall bring this day's [sacrifice] to completion."

body.translated_text:
15.23.1a: Then <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> perceived the direct <s>sava</s> (pressing). With these four [verses] beginning with "If indeed you, in house after house," having pressed [the <s>Soma</s>], he poured the remainder into the <s>droṇakalaśa</s> (wooden vat) [with the verse] "Bring [it] to the cups."
15.23.1b: Then, with [the priests] holding on to him, he offered oblations with the first four [verses] of that same <s>sūkta</s> (hymn).
15.23.1c: Then he led him to the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) with these two <s>ṛcs</s>: "You, O <s>Agni</s>, nearest to us" and "You, O <s>Agni</s>, knowing <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [laws]." Then he made him approach the fire with this <s>ṛc</s>: "<s>Śunaḥśepa</s>, bound a thousandfold."

body.translated_text:
15.24.1a: Then <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> took refuge in the lap of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. Then <s>Ajīgarta Sauyavasi</s> said to him: "Give me back my son." "No," said <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, "the gods have given him to me."
15.24.1b: He became known as <s>Devarāta</s> (god-given), a descendant of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. Then <s>Ajīgarta Sauyavasi</s> said to him: "Let us call him back together." "So be it," [said Ajīgarta].
15.24.1: "He is an <s>Āṅgirasa</s> by birth, <s>Ajīgarta</s>, the famed seer. O sage, from the lineage of the grandfather, do not depart — come back to me."
15.24.1c: Thus [Ajīgarta spoke]. Then <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> replied:
15.24.1d: "They saw you with knife in hand, what is not found even among <s>Śūdras</s>. You chose three hundred cows [over me], O son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>."
15.24.1e: Then <s>Ajīgarta Sauyavasi</s> said to him: "That evil deed done by me torments me, dear son. I renounce it before you — let the hundreds of cows be returned."
15.24.1f: <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> replied: "He who commits an evil act once would commit sin again thereafter. Do not depart from the way of a <s>Śūdra</s> — what you have done cannot be reconciled."
15.24.1g: "It cannot be reconciled" — thus he spoke, and <s>Viśvāmitra</s> approved.

body.translated_text:
15.25.1a: "Instruct us even as you would [instruct] the fearsome one, O prince, speak thus: how, being an <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, I may attain the status of your son." Thus [Śunaḥśepa spoke]. <s>Viśvāmitra</s> said to him:
15.25.1b: "You shall be the eldest of my sons, and yours shall be the foremost progeny. You shall attain the divine inheritance that is mine — with this I invite you."
15.25.1c: <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> replied: "You should speak with the consent [of your sons], for my friendship and for my glory, so that I, O bull of the <s>Bharatas</s>, may attain the status of your son."
15.25.1d: Then <s>Viśvāmitra</s> addressed his sons.

body.translated_text:
15.26.1a: "<s>Madhucchandas</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Reṇu</s>, <s>Aṣṭaka</s>, listen! Whoever among you are brothers, stand aside for his seniority."
15.26.1b: He had one hundred sons. Fifty were elder than <s>Madhucchandas</s>, and fifty were younger. The elder ones did not approve. He cursed them: "Your progeny shall inhabit the borderlands."
15.26.1c: They are these: the <s>Andhras</s>, <s>Puṇḍras</s>, <s>Śabaras</s>, and <s>Mūcīpas</s>. They say that the <s>Vaiśvāmitras</s> among the northern <s>Dasyus</s> (barbarians) are mostly descendants of <s>Dasyus</s>. But those who were younger, beginning with <s>Madhucchandas</s>, they approved. Then <s>Madhucchandas</s> sang:
15.26.1d: "That which our father agrees to, in that we stand. We all do this in your presence — we follow after you."
15.26.1e: Then <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, pleased, praised his sons.

body.translated_text:
15.27.1a: [Viśvāmitra said:] 'You sons shall become possessors of cattle and progeny, who honored my standing and made me heroic.'
15.27.1b: 'Formerly, heroic ones with the son of <s>Devarāta</s>, singers of songs — may all these sons be prosperous! This is their truthful declaration.'
15.27.1c: 'This hero of the <s>Kuśikas</s> is for you, <s>Devarāta</s>; follow him. May he obtain both you and the inheritance, and the knowledge that we know.'
15.27.1d: 'Those united <s>Vaiśvāmitras</s> (descendants of Viśvāmitra), all together, sharing the same gifts — to <s>Devarāta</s>...'

body.translated_text:
16.1.1a: <s>Prajāpati</s> desired: 'May I attain all desires; may I encompass all attainments.' He perceived this three-night sacrificial rite — the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (Horse Sacrifice). He obtained it.
16.1.1b: He sacrificed with it. Having sacrificed, he attained all desires and encompassed all attainments. Likewise, the sacrificer who sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> attains all desires and encompasses all attainments.
16.1.2: He offers portions to the chief priests (<s>mahā-ṛtvij</s>) — four vessels, handfuls, and measured portions.

body.translated_text:
16.2.1: '<s>Manu Vaivasvata</s>' (Manu, son of Vivasvat) — at the first [station].
16.2.2: 'His subjects were human beings; these sat here' — thus he instructs the householders.
16.2.3: He should recite the hymn: 'The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the Veda; this is that [Veda].'
16.2.4: '<s>Yama Vaivasvata</s>' (Yama, son of Vivasvat) — at the second [station].
16.2.5: 'His subjects were the ancestors; these sat here' — thus he instructs the elders.
16.2.6: He should recite the <s>Yajus</s> passage: 'The <s>Yajurveda</s> is the Veda; this is that [Veda].'
16.2.7: '<s>Varuṇa Āditya</s>' (Varuṇa, son of Aditi) — at the third [station].
