body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.3.1: There are twenty-one sacrificial posts (<s>yūpa</s>s), [each] twenty-one forearm-lengths [high].
ŚŚS 16.3.2: Eight are of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) wood, ten of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) wood.
ŚŚS 16.3.3: Two attendant posts are of <s>paitaudrava</s> (Himalayan pine) wood.
ŚŚS 16.3.4: The <s>agniṣṭha</s> (fire-seat) [post] is of <s>rājjudāla</s> wood.
ŚŚS 16.3.5: Twenty-one [victims are] for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>.
ŚŚS 16.3.6: Their ritual procedure is the same.
ŚŚS 16.3.7: The first pressing day follows <s>Gotama</s>'s <s>caturuttara</s> (progressively increasing by four) <s>stoma</s>.
ŚŚS 16.3.8: With it, one attains this world.
ŚŚS 16.3.9: The second [day] has the <s>ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-onefold) <s>stoma</s>.
ŚŚS 16.3.10: The twenty-onefold is that [sun] which shines there. Thus he brings [the sacrifice] into harmony with its own form.
ŚŚS 16.3.11: From him [the sun] the horse was fashioned.
ŚŚS 16.3.12: This is expressed by the <s>ṛc</s>: 'From the sun, the <s>Vasus</s> carved the horse.'
ŚŚS 16.3.13: The horse, cow, wild deer, goat, and <s>tūpara</s> (a type of bovine) — these are [victims] belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
ŚŚS 16.3.14: The <s>gaura</s> (wild ox), <s>gavaya</s> (gayal), <s>śarabha</s> (a mythical eight-legged beast), camel, <s>māyu</s> (barking deer), and <s>kiṃpuruṣa</s> — these are the animals spread [as covering for the horse].
ŚŚS 16.3.15: And the animals [total] twenty-one, twenty-one [offered] to the twenty-one <s>cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal sacrifice) deities.
ŚŚS 16.3.16: These <s>cāturmāsya</s> deities are indeed all the deities.
ŚŚS 16.3.17: [This is] for the gratification of all the deities.
ŚŚS 16.3.18: They make the adorned horse smell a post.
ŚŚS 16.3.19: He should have the sacrificer say: 'It smells well of cattle — it does not refuse to smell.'
ŚŚS 16.3.20: While [the horse] stands in front of the post, [they recite] 'Yad akranda' — eleven [verses] without the <s>praṇava</s> (<s>oṃ</s>).
ŚŚS 16.3.21: 'Samiddho añjan' — the <s>āprī</s> (propitiatory) [verses].
ŚŚS 16.3.22: Having concluded with 'Adhrigo,' [they recite] the hymn 'Mā no Mitra.'
ŚŚS 16.3.23: And at the end of the latter [hymn], without the <s>praṇava</s>.
ŚŚS 16.3.24: 'Thirty-four' — before the rib-portions.
ŚŚS 16.3.25: Then for the horse, they spread out a garment, a covering cloth, and gold.
ŚŚS 16.3.26: This is expressed by the <s>ṛc</s>: 'When they spread a garment for the horse, a covering cloth, the gold ornaments for him.'
ŚŚS 16.3.27: Then they sacrifice the consecrated horse.
ŚŚS 16.3.28: [They also sacrifice] many wild animals tied around [the posts].
ŚŚS 16.3.29: [The first portion goes] to <s>Pūṣan</s> at the forehead.
ŚŚS 16.3.30: This is expressed by the <s>ṛc</s>: 'Here the first portion goes to <s>Pūṣan</s>.'
ŚŚS 16.3.31: The dark-colored [victim] for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> [is offered] at the navel.
ŚŚS 16.3.34: They cover those two with the covering cloth.
ŚŚS 16.3.35: The sacrificer's wife lies down next to them.
ŚŚS 16.3.36: [She recites:] 'Between the thighs, down to the rectum, place [it]; bring forth the ointment — that which is the source of life for women.'
ŚŚS 16.3.37: No one speaks against that.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.4.1: 'Your mother and your father play at the top of the tree. I give you forth,' said your father, thrusting his fist into the womb.' — With this the <s>Hotṛ</s> addresses [the queen in the ritual dialogue].
ŚŚS 16.4.2: 'Raise her up, as one carrying a load up a mountain. Then her middle quivers, as one fanning in the cold wind.' — The <s>Brahman</s> priest [addresses] the dismissed woman.
ŚŚS 16.4.3: 'What is narrow and to be split' — the <s>Udgātṛ</s> [addresses] the rejected woman.
ŚŚS 16.4.4: 'When the deer eats barley, he does not consider it nourishing. When a <s>śūdra</s> woman has a noble lover, she does not prosper for wealth.' — The <s>Adhvaryu</s> [addresses] the <s>pālāgalī</s> (servant woman).
ŚŚS 16.4.5: A hundred attendant women of the same caste as the horse-keepers — they respond [with counter-verses].
ŚŚS 16.4.6: 'Your mind seems to desire, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, do not speak so much. Raise him up.' 'When the gods licked.' 'When a <s>śūdra</s> man is the husband of a noble woman' — these are the variations of the counter-responses.
ŚŚS 16.4.7: In the <s>sadas</s> (shed), ritual theological debate (<s>brahma-vadya</s>) [takes place].
ŚŚS 16.4.8: The <s>Hotṛ</s> asks the <s>Adhvaryu</s>. He replies with the second [verse]. He asks with the third. He replies with the fourth.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.5.1: [The <s>Hotṛ</s> asks:] 'What light is equal to the sun? What lake is equal to the ocean? What is greater than the earth? What has no measure?'
ŚŚS 16.5.2: [The <s>Adhvaryu</s> replies:] '<s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) is a light equal to the sun. Heaven is a lake equal to the ocean. <s>Indra</s> is greater than the earth. The cow has no measure.'
ŚŚS 16.5.3: [The <s>Hotṛ</s> asks:] 'Who walks alone? Who is born again? What is the remedy for cold? What is the great sowing ground?'
ŚŚS 16.5.4: [The <s>Adhvaryu</s> replies:] 'The sun walks alone. The moon is born again. Fire is the remedy for cold. The earth is the great sowing ground.'
ŚŚS 16.5.5: The <s>Brahman</s> priest asks the <s>Udgātṛ</s>. He replies with the second [verse]. He asks with the third. He replies with the fourth.
ŚŚS 16.6.1: [The <s>Brahman</s> asks:] 'I ask you for understanding, O friend of the gods, if you have comprehended this with your mind: in which three strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s> was the offering placed? In which did the entire world enter?'
ŚŚS 16.6.2: [The <s>Udgātṛ</s> replies:] 'I am indeed in those three strides in which the entire world entered. Instantly I traverse the earth and heaven, with one limb [I reach] the ridge of the sky.'
ŚŚS 16.6.3: [The <s>Brahman</s> asks:] 'Into what did the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) enter? What is placed within the <s>puruṣa</s>? This, O <s>Brahman</s> priest, we ask of you — what will you answer us here?'
ŚŚS 16.6.4: [The <s>Udgātṛ</s> replies:] 'Into five [elements] the <s>puruṣa</s> entered; those are placed within the <s>puruṣa</s>. Thus I reckon this against you — you are not superior to me by illusion.'
ŚŚS 16.6.2: [Then] 'I ask you the farthest end of the earth' — the sacrificer asks.
ŚŚS 16.6.3: He replies with the next [verse].

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.7.1: '<s>Subhū</s>, the self-existent one, first [placed himself] within the great ocean; he bore the seasonal embryo, from whom the one who shines was born' — this is the <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse) of the <s>mahiman</s> (greatness offering).
ŚŚS 16.7.2: 'Let the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Prajāpati</s>' — this is the bidding formula (<s>praiṣa</s>).
ŚŚS 16.7.3: 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you' — this is the offering verse (<s>yājyā</s>).
ŚŚS 16.7.4: Having performed [the rite] with the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) of the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [victim], they should then offer the other <s>vapā</s>s following that — [say] some. Or since <s>Prajāpati</s>'s deities follow this [order], he thus gratifies each one accordingly.
ŚŚS 16.7.5: Or [the first vapā is] of the one for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
ŚŚS 16.7.6: Or of the one for the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (all-gods).
ŚŚS 16.7.7: 'Why should they hurry?' — thus <s>Indrota Śaunaka</s> used to say.
ŚŚS 16.7.8: They should proceed separately for separate deities.
ŚŚS 16.7.9: Together for deities of the same [class], when unspecified.
ŚŚS 16.7.10: Separately when the order is specified.
ŚŚS 16.7.11: Thus he gratifies each one accordingly.
ŚŚS 16.7.12: For the latter <s>mahiman</s> offering, the <s>yājyā</s> and <s>puronuvākyā</s> should be reversed.
ŚŚS 16.7.13: He should recite together both the <s>ekāhika</s> (one-day) and the <s>pāṅkta</s> (fivefold) [hymns] in the <s>ājya</s> [recitation].
ŚŚS 16.7.14: For the attainment of both desires — that in the <s>ekāhika</s> and that in the <s>pāṅkta ājya</s>.
ŚŚS 16.7.15: He should introduce both the <s>ekāhika</s> and <s>bārhata</s> (pertaining to the <s>Bṛhat</s>) openings (<s>prauga</s>) together.
ŚŚS 16.7.16: For the attainment of both desires — that in the <s>ekāhika</s> and that in the <s>bārhata prauga</s>.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.8.1: The <s>Mahānāmnī</s> [verses] are the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
ŚŚS 16.8.2: The <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> indeed are everything.
ŚŚS 16.8.3: The <s>Aśvamedha</s> is everything.
ŚŚS 16.8.4: 'By the whole, may I attain the whole.'
ŚŚS 16.8.5: Whatever hymns belong to the fifth-day [series] in the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> and <s>Marutvatīya</s>, having recited those first, he places the <s>nivids</s> (litanies) of the one-day [sacrifice].
ŚŚS 16.8.6: The one-day [sacrifice] is indeed the foundation.
ŚŚS 16.8.7: For the sake of establishment itself.
ŚŚS 16.8.8: Or a thousand [verses] at the midday [pressing].
ŚŚS 16.8.9: Forty of each meter in the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
ŚŚS 16.8.10: Those make eight hundred and two.
ŚŚS 16.8.11: Seven hundred and twenty-seven in the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
ŚŚS 16.8.12: That [makes] a thousand.
ŚŚS 16.8.13: A thousand indeed is everything.
ŚŚS 16.8.14: The <s>Aśvamedha</s> is everything.
ŚŚS 16.8.15: 'By the whole, may I attain the whole.'
ŚŚS 16.8.16: Whatever hymns belong to the fifth-day [series] in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and <s>Āgni-Māruta</s>, having recited those first, he places the <s>nivids</s> in the one-day [portions].
ŚŚS 16.8.17: The one-day [sacrifice] is indeed the foundation.
ŚŚS 16.8.18: For the sake of establishment itself.
ŚŚS 16.8.19: It concludes as an <s>Ukthya</s> (praise-sacrifice).
ŚŚS 16.8.20: By that, he attains the atmospheric world.
ŚŚS 16.8.21: The <s>Sarva-stoma Atirātra</s> (overnight pressing with all chant-types) is the last day.
ŚŚS 16.8.22: The <s>Sarva-stoma Atirātra</s> indeed is everything.
ŚŚS 16.8.23: The <s>Aśvamedha</s> is everything.
ŚŚS 16.8.24: 'By the whole, may I attain the whole.'
ŚŚS 16.8.25: By that, he attains the yonder world.
ŚŚS 16.8.26: The recitation [follows that] of the second <s>Ābhiplava</s> [six-day cycle].
ŚŚS 16.8.27: With this [rite], <s>Indrotaḥ Śaunaka</s> caused <s>Janamejaya Pārikṣita</s> to sacrifice.
ŚŚS 16.8.28: And thereupon this sacrificial song (<s>yajña-gāthā</s>) is sung:

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.9.1: '<s>Janamejaya</s> bound a dappled horse for the gods — grain-eating, with a golden ornament (<s>rukmin</s>), wearing green garlands, [placed] upon the throne (<s>āsandī</s>).'
ŚŚS 16.9.2: These same are the first two days. The <s>Jyotir-Atirātra</s> — by that, [he sacrificed for] <s>Agrasena</s>.
ŚŚS 16.9.3: The <s>Gaus</s> [Atirātra] — by that, [for] <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
ŚŚS 16.9.4: The <s>Āyus</s> [Atirātra] — by that, [for] <s>Śrutasena</s>.
ŚŚS 16.9.5: All are descendants of <s>Parikṣit</s>.
ŚŚS 16.9.6: And thereupon this sacrificial song is sung:
ŚŚS 16.9.7: 'The <s>Pārikṣitas</s>, sacrificing with <s>Aśvamedhas</s>, one after another, abandoned sinful deeds — the meritorious ones, by meritorious deeds.'
ŚŚS 16.9.8: The <s>Abhijit</s> [Atirātra] — by that, <s>Ṛṣabha Yājñatura</s> sacrificed.
ŚŚS 16.9.9: And thereupon this sacrificial song is sung:
ŚŚS 16.9.10: 'When King <s>Ṛṣabha Yājñatura</s> formerly sacrificed with the horse, <s>Indra</s> became intoxicated with <s>Soma</s>, and the Brahmins [were satisfied] with desired wealth.'
ŚŚS 16.9.11: The <s>Viśvajit</s> — by that, <s>Parāhṇāra Vaideha</s> sacrificed.
ŚŚS 16.9.12: And thereupon this sacrificial song is sung:
ŚŚS 16.9.13: 'They bound the sacrificial horse of <s>Parāhṇāra</s> yonder — the <s>Kauśalya</s> of the golden navel distributed [gifts] to fill the quarters.'
ŚŚS 16.9.14: The <s>Mahāvrata-Atirātra</s> — by that, <s>Marutta Āvikṣita</s> sacrificed.
ŚŚS 16.9.15: And thereupon this sacrificial song is sung:
ŚŚS 16.9.16: 'The <s>Maruts</s> were the attendants, dwelling in the house of <s>Marutta Āvikṣita</s>; <s>Agni</s> was the chamberlain, and the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-Gods) were the courtiers.'
ŚŚS 16.9.17: Then indeed the deities became his courtiers.
ŚŚS 16.9.18: The eastern direction [belongs to] the <s>Hotṛ</s>.
ŚŚS 16.9.19: The southern [direction belongs to] the <s>Brahman</s> [priest].
ŚŚS 16.9.20: The western [direction belongs to] the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.
ŚŚS 16.9.21: The northern [direction belongs to] the <s>Udgātṛ</s>.
ŚŚS 16.9.22: Whatever else [belongs to] the earth and to non-Brahmin people is their own.
ŚŚS 16.9.23: Here also [is the share] of the assistant priests (<s>hotrakās</s>).
ŚŚS 16.9.24: But he should sacrifice in the middle.
ŚŚS 16.9.25: Five animals [bound to] a forked sacrificial post (<s>viśākha-yūpa</s>).
ŚŚS 16.9.26: For a year, seasonal animals [are offered].
ŚŚS 16.9.27: Six for <s>Agni</s> in spring.
ŚŚS 16.9.28: [Those] for <s>Indra</s> in summer.
ŚŚS 16.9.29: [Those] for the <s>Maruts</s>, or for <s>Parjanya</s>, in the rains.
ŚŚS 16.9.30: [Those] for <s>Mitra</s>-<s>Varuṇa</s> in autumn.
ŚŚS 16.9.31: [Those] for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> in winter.
ŚŚS 16.9.32: [Those] for <s>Indra</s>-<s>Viṣṇu</s> in the cool season.

ŚŚS_16.10.1: prajāpatir.aśvamedhena.iṣṭvā.puruṣamedham.apaśyat.|.tasya.yad.anāptam.aśvamedhena.āsīt.tat.sarvam.puruṣamedhena.āpnot.|.tatho.eva.etad.yajamāno.yat.puruṣamedhena.yajate.yad.asya.anāptam.aśvamedhena.bhavati.tat.sarvam.puruṣamedhena.āpnoti /

ŚŚS_16.10.16: iyam.vā.aditiḥ.pratiṣṭhā.vā.aditir.asyām.eva.enam.tad.adīnāyām.antataḥ.pratiṣṭhāpayanti /
body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.10.1: <s>Prajāpati</s>, having sacrificed with the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, perceived the <s>Puruṣamedha</s> (human sacrifice). Whatever had not been attained by the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, all that he attained by the <s>Puruṣamedha</s>. Likewise indeed, the sacrificer who sacrifices with the <s>Puruṣamedha</s> — whatever has not been attained by the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, all that he attains by the <s>Puruṣamedha</s>.
ŚŚS 16.10.2: Everything [follows] the procedure of the <s>Aśvamedha</s>.
ŚŚS 16.10.3: And also the attendants (<s>upajana</s>).
ŚŚS 16.10.4: Then [there are] offerings to <s>Agni</s> as the Desire (<s>Kāma</s>), the Giver (<s>Dātṛ</s>), and the Path-maker (<s>Pathikṛt</s>).
ŚŚS 16.10.5: <s>Agni</s> as Desire is indeed the lord of the gods.
ŚŚS 16.10.6: For the satisfaction of all the gods.
ŚŚS 16.10.7: <s>Agni</s> as the Giver — he indeed gives the sacrifice to him.
ŚŚS 16.10.8: <s>Agni</s> as the Path-maker — he indeed causes him to walk the path of sacrifice again.
ŚŚS 16.10.9: Having purchased a Brahmin or a Kṣatriya for a thousand [cows] with a hundred horses, they release him for a year, [allowing him to fulfill] all desires except celibacy-breaking.
ŚŚS 16.10.10: And they guard him in just that way.
ŚŚS 16.10.11: Then, offerings to <s>Anumati</s> (Approval), <s>Pathyā Svasti</s> (Auspicious Path), and <s>Aditi</s> (Boundlessness) throughout the year.
ŚŚS 16.10.12: With <s>Sāvitrī</s> [verses] in reverse order.
ŚŚS 16.10.13: The <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> [verses] with the <s>Pāriplavīya</s> [narratives].
ŚŚS 16.10.14: 'With the approval of <s>Anumati</s>, approved, may I sacrifice with this sacrifice.'
ŚŚS 16.10.15: Speech indeed is <s>Pathyā Svasti</s> — she thus creates a path of well-being for the sacrificer in the sacrifice.
ŚŚS 16.10.16: This [earth] indeed is <s>Aditi</s>; <s>Aditi</s> is the foundation — in her, the unbounded one, they finally establish him.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.11.1: The <s>Śaunahśepa</s> [narrative is] the first.
ŚŚS 16.11.2: How <s>Śunahśepa</s>, son of <s>Ajīgarta</s>, bound to the sacrificial post, freed himself.
ŚŚS 16.11.3: And he should recite in the first hymn.
ŚŚS 16.11.4: The <s>Kākṣīvata</s> [narrative is] the second.
ŚŚS 16.11.5: How <s>Kakṣīvān Auśija</s> obtained a reward from <s>Svanaya Bhāvayavya</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.6: And he should recite in the last hymn.
ŚŚS 16.11.7: The <s>Śyāvāśva</s> [narrative is] the third.
ŚŚS 16.11.8: How <s>Śyāvāśva Ārcanānasa Vaidadaśva</s> obtained a reward.
ŚŚS 16.11.9: And [he should recite] the hymn 'Ke ṣṭhā nara.'
ŚŚS 16.11.10: The <s>Bhāradvāja</s> [narrative is] the fourth.
ŚŚS 16.11.11: How <s>Bharadvāja</s> obtained a reward from <s>Bṛbu Takṣan</s> and <s>Prastoka Sārñjaya</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.12: 'Adhi Bṛbuḥ' [and] 'Prastoka' — four [verses].
ŚŚS 16.11.13: The <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> [narrative is] the fifth.
ŚŚS 16.11.14: How <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> became the <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) of <s>Sudāsa Paijavana</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.15: And [he should recite] the hymn 'Dve naptur.'
ŚŚS 16.11.16: The <s>Maidhātitha</s> [narrative is] the sixth.
ŚŚS 16.11.17: How <s>Āsaṅga Plāyogi</s>, being a woman, became a man.
ŚŚS 16.11.18: And [he should recite] the hymn 'Stuhi stuhi.'
ŚŚS 16.11.19: The <s>Vātsya</s> [narrative is] the seventh.
ŚŚS 16.11.20: How <s>Vatsa Kāṇva</s> obtained a reward from <s>Tirindira Pāraśavya</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.21: And [he should recite] the hymn 'Śatam aham Tirindira.'
ŚŚS 16.11.22: The <s>Vāśa</s> [narrative is] the eighth.
ŚŚS 16.11.23: How <s>Vaśa Aśvya</s> obtained a reward from <s>Pṛthuśravasa Kānīta</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.24: And [he should recite] the hymn 'Ā sa etu ya īvadā.'
ŚŚS 16.11.25: The <s>Prāskaṇva</s> [narrative is] the ninth.
ŚŚS 16.11.26: How <s>Praskaṇva</s> obtained a reward from <s>Pṛṣadhra Medhya Mātariśvan</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.27: And [he should recite] the hymns 'Bhūri id Indrasya.'
ŚŚS 16.11.28: The <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> [narrative is] the tenth.
ŚŚS 16.11.26: How <s>Nābhānediṣṭha Mānava</s> obtained a great reward from the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.30: And [he should recite] the hymn 'Ye yajñena.'
ŚŚS 16.11.31: These are the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> (praise-of-men) [narratives].
ŚŚS 16.11.32: A man (<s>puruṣa</s>) indeed is <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s>.
ŚŚS 16.11.33: Thus he fulfills [the sacrifice] with its own nature.

body.translated_text:
16.12.1: Twenty-five <s>yūpas</s> (sacrificial posts).
16.12.2: Twenty-five <s>aratnis</s> (cubits) [in height].
16.12.3: Ten of <s>bilva</s> wood, twelve of <s>khadira</s> wood.
16.12.4: The two attendant posts are of <s>paitaudrava</s> (Himalayan cedar) wood.
16.12.5: Or the <s>agniṣṭha</s> (fire-nearest post) is of <s>rājjudāla</s> or <s>sārala</s> (pine) wood.
16.12.6: Twenty-five <s>Agniṣomīya</s> (Agni-and-Soma) [rites are performed].
16.12.7: The procedure for them is the same.
16.12.8: On the first and the last of the <s>Āśvamedhika</s> (horse sacrifice) pressing days,
16.12.9: the second [day] has the <s>pañcaviṃśa-stoma</s> (twenty-five-fold chant).
16.12.10: The <s>puruṣa</s> (man) is indeed twenty-five-fold.
16.12.11: Thus he fulfills him with his own form.
16.12.12: A man, a cow, a deer, a goat, and a <s>tūpara</s> (horse of a particular breed) — these are sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
16.12.13: A <s>gaura</s> (white ox), a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox), a <s>śarabha</s> (eight-legged beast), a camel, a <s>māyu</s> (type of deer), and a <s>kimpuruṣa</s> (a mythical being) — these are the <s>anustaraṇa</s> (covering) animals.
16.12.14: And the sacrificial animals are twenty-five each, twenty-five for each of the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal) deities.
16.12.15: For indeed all these deities are the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> deities.
16.12.16: For the gratification of all the deities.
16.12.17: Having caused the adorned <s>puruṣa</s> (man), who is lying down, to smell [the offerings], [they recite] "<s>udīratām avara</s>" with eleven [verses] without the <s>praṇava</s> (syllable Om).
16.12.18: "<s>Agnir mṛtyuḥ</s>" (Agni is death) are the <s>āprī</s> (propitiatory) verses.
16.12.19: "<s>Mā enam agna</s>" — at the two <s>adhrigu</s> [verses], likewise.
16.12.20: Then they spread out for the <s>puruṣa</s> (man) [garments of] <s>kauśa</s> (silk), <s>tārpya</s> (linen), <s>āruṇa</s> (reddish cloth), and <s>āṃśava</s> (flaxen cloth).
16.12.21: When [the victim] has been suffocated, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter) attends upon it with the <s>Yāma</s> <s>Sāman</s> (chant).

body.translated_text:
16.13.1: The <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker) [recites] with the <s>Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa</s> [hymn].
16.13.2: Then the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) attend upon the departed one — with two [verses] each: the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, and the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, [reciting] "<s>pareyivāṃsam</s>" (the one who has passed away).
16.13.3: After that, they heal the sacrificer.
16.13.4: [With the hymns beginning] "<s>uta devā avahitam</s>" (O gods, the one who is cast down), "<s>muñcāmi tvā haviṣā jīvanāya kam</s>" (I release you with an oblation for life), "<s>akṣībhyāṃ te nāsikābhyām vāta ā vātu bheṣajam</s>" (may the wind blow medicine through your eyes and nostrils) — with these hymns in sequence.
16.13.5: "<s>Pra tāry āyuḥ</s>" — one [verse] each from the <s>Nairṛta</s> (relating to Nirṛti) [hymns].
16.13.6: Three each from the <s>Śaṃtātīya</s> [hymns].
16.13.7: They cause the chief queen (<s>mahiṣī</s>) to lie down beside the suffocated [victim].
16.13.8: The two are covered together with an upper cloth.
16.13.9: The sacrificer addresses them thus [with ritual dialogue].
16.13.10: [The verses beginning] "<s>parivṛktā</s>" (the discarded one), "<s>aprapāṇā</s>" (the one without a drinking place), "<s>yo anākta akṣo na seśe</s>" (the unanointed axle that does not rest), "<s>yasya romaśam</s>" (whose hairy one) — these are the <s>abhimethinī</s> (reviling) verses.
16.13.11: With the subsequent [verses], they revile back in turn.
16.13.12: The <s>Adhvaryu</s> [reviles] with the first one.
16.13.13: "<s>Udīrṣva nāri</s>" (rise up, O woman), "<s>udīrṣva ataḥ pativati</s>" (rise up from here, O wife), "<s>udīrṣva ato Viśvāvaso</s>" (rise up from here, O <s>Viśvāvasu</s>), "<s>aśmanvatī</s>" (stony one) — these are the <s>utthāpinī</s> (raising-up) verses.
16.13.14: He consecrates with the <s>tṛcas</s> (verse-triads) [beginning] "<s>mano nv asunīte</s>," "<s>yat te yamam</s>," "<s>yathā yugam</s>."
16.13.15: The <s>Brahman</s> (priest) causes [the verses] to be recited.
16.13.16: In the <s>sadas</s> (assembly hall) there is theological discourse (<s>brahma-vadya</s>).
16.13.17: "<s>Gāvo yavam</s>" (cows [eat] barley) — the <s>Hotṛ</s> asks the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; with the second [verse] he replies; with the third he asks; with the fourth he replies.
16.13.18: "<s>Dve srutī aśṛṇavam pitṝṇām</s>" (I have heard of two paths of the fathers) — the <s>Brahman</s> asks the <s>Udgātṛ</s>; with the second [verse] he replies; with the one in between he asks; with the last he replies.

body.translated_text:
16.14.1: The <s>Āśvamedhika</s> (horse sacrifice) [litany begins] from the <s>ājya</s> (ghee offering).
16.14.2: Both the <s>Ekāhika</s> (one-day rite) and the <s>Māhāvratika</s> (great vow rite) [recitations] should be combined in the <s>ājya</s> [litany].
16.14.3: Whatever purpose is in both the <s>Ekāhika</s> and <s>Māhāvratika</s> <s>ājya</s> [litanies], for the attainment of both.
16.14.4: Both the <s>Ekāhika</s> and <s>Māhāvratika</s> <s>praüga</s> (introductory litany) recitations should be combined.
16.14.5: Whatever purpose is in both the <s>Ekāhika</s> and <s>Māhāvratika</s> <s>praüga</s>, for the attainment of both.
16.14.6: The <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great vow) [chants are used] at the midday [pressing].
16.14.7: The <s>Rājana</s> becomes the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant).
16.14.8: This is indeed the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) that has the form of the <s>puruṣa</s> (man), namely the <s>Rājana</s>; thus he fulfills him with his own <s>Sāman</s>.
16.14.9: The third pressing [begins] from the <s>Anucara</s> onward, being the sixth [day].
16.14.10: The sixth day is indeed the <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> (relating to man).
16.14.11: The <s>puruṣa</s> (man) is indeed <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s>.
16.14.12: Thus he fulfills him with his own form.
16.14.13: The <s>Mahādivākīrtya</s> becomes the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s> (Agni-praise chant).
16.14.14: This is indeed the <s>Sāman</s> that has the form of the <s>puruṣa</s>, namely the <s>Mahādivākīrtya</s>; thus he fulfills him with his own <s>Sāman</s>.
16.14.15: It concludes with the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> (sixteen-fold [chant]).
16.14.16: The <s>puruṣa</s> is indeed sixteen-parted; thus he fulfills him with his own form.
16.14.17: The fourth day of the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-chant cycle) [is] the fifth [day overall].
16.14.18: Together with the <s>puruṣa</s> (human victim), [the fee] is given.
16.14.19: Ten animals [are offered] at a forked <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post).
16.14.20: Twelve [animals] each are the <s>ṛtu-paśus</s> (seasonal victims).

body.translated_text:
16.15.1a: <s>Brahman</s> (the Absolute), the self-existent, performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity). Having performed that <s>tapas</s>, he considered: "There is no infinity in <s>tapas</s>; let me offer myself in all beings." Having offered himself in all beings, he offered all beings in the <s>Sarvamedha</s> (all-sacrifice). Thereupon he attained the supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship of all beings.
16.15.1: Thus indeed the sacrificer, when he sacrifices with the <s>Sarvamedha</s>, having offered himself in all beings, offers all beings in the <s>Sarvamedha</s>. Thereupon he attains the supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship of all beings.
16.15.2: The <s>Puruṣamedha</s> (human sacrifice) ritual [constitutes] the preliminary rites.
16.15.3: After the <s>Agniṣṭut</s>, <s>Indraṣṭut</s>, <s>Vaiśvadevaṣṭut</s>, and <s>Sūryaṣṭuti</s> [days], they immolate the horse.
16.15.4: The <s>Puruṣamedha</s> [rites constitute] the fifth day.
16.15.5: There they immolate the <s>puruṣa</s> (human victim).
16.15.6: The <s>Vājapeya</s> (drink of strength) is the sixth [day].
16.15.7: The <s>Āptoryāma</s> (complete course) is the seventh [day].
16.15.8: There they immolate all sacrificial victims — whatever beings have breath.
16.15.9: They offer the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) of those that have omentum.
16.15.10: The skins of those that lack omentum.
16.15.11: They scatter the cut portions of herbs and trees.
16.15.12: The <s>Triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-fold) and <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-fold) [<s>stomas</s>] are for the eighth and ninth days.
16.15.13: The <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering) with all <s>stomas</s> (chant-forms) and all <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> (back-chants), an <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite), is the last day.
16.15.13: The <s>Viśvajit</s> with all <s>stomas</s> and all <s>pṛṣṭhas</s>, an <s>Atirātra</s>, is the last day.
16.15.14: The <s>Viśvajit</s> with all <s>stomas</s> and all <s>pṛṣṭhas</s> is indeed an <s>Atirātra</s>.
16.15.15: The <s>Sarvamedha</s> (all-sacrifice) is everything.
16.15.16: "May I attain everything through everything."
16.15.17: Twenty animals [are offered] at a forked <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post).
16.15.18: Twenty-four [animals] each are the <s>ṛtu-paśus</s> (seasonal victims).
16.15.19: Here the <s>Sarvamedha</s> (all-sacrifice) is concluded.
16.15.20: Together with the earth, [the fee] is given.

body.text:
ŚŚS_16.16.1: gārhapatye.adhara.araṇim.anuprahṛtya.|.āhavanīya.uttara.araṇim.|.ātmany.agnīn.samāropya.|.araṇyam.pravrajet /

body.translated_text:
16.16.1: Having placed the lower <s>araṇi</s> (fire-churning stick) on the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire) and the upper <s>araṇi</s> on the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), having gathered up the fires into himself, he should go forth into the forest as a renunciant.
16.16.2: <s>Viśvakarman Bhauvana</s> performed the final sacrifice.
16.16.3: The Earth spoke to him: "No mortal is worthy to give me away. O <s>Viśvakarman Bhauvana</s>, you would give me away! I shall sink into the midst of the waters; your contract with <s>Kaśyapa</s> is in vain."
16.16.4: <s>Kaśyapa</s> raised her up.

body.translated_text:
16.17.1: In the <s>Vājapeya</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> (priest) ascends an <s>udumbara</s> (fig-wood) chariot-wheel [saying]: "May I, through <s>Vāja</s> (prize), through the impulsion of <s>Savitṛ</s>, of true impulsion, of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, ascend to the highest vault of heaven."
16.17.2: "Of <s>Indra</s>" — when the sacrificer is a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
16.17.3: "Of the <s>Maruts</s>" — when a <s>vaiśya</s>.
16.17.4: Having seated himself on that turning chariot-wheel, without being urged, he sings the <s>Sāman</s> three times.
16.17.5: And he should also mutter [the mantra] three times.
16.17.6: "The youths have appeared; the swift ones have come for the prize. In the impulsion of divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, let the steeds conquer the heavenly [realm]" — and [this verse].
16.17.7: With that same mantra he descends.
16.17.8: "I ascended" (<s>aruham</s>) — the modification [is used] in the descent (<s>pratyavarohaṇa</s>).
16.17.9: Having partaken of the breath-portion (<s>prāṇa-bhakṣa</s>) of the <s>madhu-graha</s> (honey cup) in a golden vessel, he offers the vessel.
16.17.10: "This sacrificer ascends to heaven; this sacrificer ascends to the heavenly world" — or [this is said].
16.17.11: They mark the one climbing the sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) with thorns (<s>ūṣa-puṭa</s>).

body.translated_text:
16.18.1: In the <s>Rājasūya</s>, the consecrated sacrificer addresses the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] five times [saying:] "O <s>Brahman</s>!"
16.18.2: "You are <s>Brahman</s>" — thus he responds in every case.
16.18.3: "You are <s>Savitṛ</s> of true impulsion" — at the first [address].
16.18.4: "You are <s>Indra</s>, of universal power" — at the second.
16.18.5: "You are <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of <s>dharma</s>" — at the third.
16.18.6: "You are <s>Rudra</s>, the benevolent" — at the fourth.
16.18.7: "You are <s>Brahman</s>" — again at the fifth.
16.18.8: He gives him mentally two golden ornaments.
16.18.9: He accepts them mentally.
16.18.10: The <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice) priests, holding the horse with reins, bathe it at the confluence of two streams flowing into lakes.
16.18.11: "By this sacrificial horse, may this king, having sacrificed, conquer; may he dispel all that is not <s>brāhmaṇya</s> (unrighteous)."
16.18.12: And if they should touch him [the horse] together with the sacrificer, he should mutter: "I and you."
16.18.13: At the conclusion, on the middle day, they construct pavilions (<s>prāsāda</s>) in the directions around the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
16.18.14: They surround them from above with solid wall-barriers having holes.
16.18.15: The priests offer an all-herb [oblation] during the night.
16.18.16: At the time of the morning litany (<s>prātaranuvāka</s>), they descend.
16.18.17: The attendants (<s>parikarmiṇaḥ</s>) ascend; they make offerings until sunrise.
16.18.18: Here they purchase an <s>Ātreya</s> (descendant of <s>Atri</s>) for a thousand — one who is fair-complexioned, tawny-eyed, wrinkled, having a mole-mark, maimed, impotent, bald — taking him, they go to the river.
16.18.19: Then having made him wade into the water, when the water flows over his mouth, the <s>Adhvaryu</s> then offers on his head: "For [the expiation of] embryo-killing (<s>bhrūṇahatyā</s>), <s>svāhā</s>."
16.18.20: Then they send him away.
16.18.21: "Those whose sins have been sent away become free from the village" — thus [it is said].

body.translated_text:
16.20.1: Now what is of two kinds, that [one attains] by the <s>Dvirātra</s> (two-night rite).
16.20.2: Two are the day-and-night pair, two are heaven and earth, two are these foundations. Whatever is of two kinds, relating to the deities (<s>adhidaivatam</s>) or to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), all that one attains by this.
16.20.3: If the day-combination is undefined, one should extend to a ten-night [rite].
16.20.4: The curtailment is from the beginning.
16.20.5: The last [day] becomes an <s>Atirātra</s>.
16.20.6: The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) is [given] day by day.
16.20.7: The unconsecrated ones have the consecrated one perform the sacrifice.
16.20.8: The <s>Ahīnas</s> have a maximum duration of one month.
16.20.9: When pressing days decrease, they should increase the consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) [days].
16.20.10: The <s>Mahāvrata</s> should not be chanted for one not consecrated for a full year.
16.20.11: Nor for one whose fire-pot (<s>ukhā</s>) has not been maintained for a year.
16.20.13: The chief of sacrificial rites is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
16.20.14: So that the face of sacrifice be not diminished.
16.20.15: But the <s>Sampātas</s> (coincidences) are [placed] at the <s>Nivid</s> insertions.
16.20.16: "May my sacrifice, stretched out, be increased" — in the <s>Ārbhava-Jātavedaseya</s> [recitation] of the second [day].
16.20.17: And in the <s>Trirātra</s> (three-night rite).
16.20.18: The <s>Abhijit</s> and <s>Viśvajit</s> [are performed] at the <s>Caturviṃśa</s> or <s>Mahāvrata</s>, or the <s>Go-Āyuṣī</s> [rites].
16.20.19: What is of two kinds, that one attains by the <s>Dvirātra</s>.

body.translated_text:
16.21.1: Now what is of three kinds, [one attains] by the <s>Trirātra</s> (three-night rite).
16.21.2: Three are these worlds, three are the luminaries, threefold is the sacrifice [with three pressings]. Whatever is of three kinds, relating to the deities (<s>adhidaivatam</s>) or to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), all that one attains by this.
16.21.3: The three <s>stomas</s> of the first day begin with the <s>Trivṛt</s> (nine-fold).
16.21.4: Those of the second begin with the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-fold).
16.21.5: The <s>Ājya</s> of the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] has sixteen [verses].
16.21.6: Those of the third begin with the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-fold).
16.21.7: The first day is an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.
16.21.8: The second is an <s>Ukthya</s>.
16.21.9: The third is an <s>Atirātra</s>.
16.21.10: The <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-chant) of the first.
16.21.11: The <s>Vāmadevya</s> of the second.
16.21.12: The <s>Bṛhat</s> of the third.
16.21.13: This world is the <s>Rathantara</s>.
16.21.14: The atmospheric world is the <s>Vāmadevya</s>.
16.21.15: The yonder world is the <s>Bṛhat</s>.
16.21.16: For the attainment of these worlds indeed.
16.21.17: The <s>Ājya</s> [recitations come] from the <s>Samūḷha</s> (collection).
16.21.18: From the middle <s>Chandoma</s>, the <s>Traiṣṭubha Prauga</s> of the second day.
16.21.19: "<s>Aryamā</s>" — thus the <s>Marutvatīya</s>.
16.21.21a: What is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> of the second day, that he performs on the third day.
16.21.21b: That makes these worlds sharers [of one another]; for indeed these worlds enjoy one another.
16.21.22: Or one may transpose the days.
16.21.23: "<s>Kas tam Indra</s>" — the <s>Sāma-pragātha</s> of the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>.
16.21.24: "<s>Mo ṣu tvā vāghataś cana</s>" — the <s>stotriya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> <s>pragāthas</s> of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, extracting the two-footed [verses].
16.21.25: "<s>Kam navya</s>" — the <s>Kadvān</s>.
16.21.26: From the hymns of the second day.
16.21.27: "<s>Astāvi manma ubhayaṃ śṛṇavad</s>" — of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>.
16.21.28: "<s>Kad ū nv asya</s>" — the <s>Kadvān</s>.
16.21.29: "<s>Śrāyanta iva sūryam</s>" and "<s>Śagdhy ū ṣu Śacīpata</s>" — of the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.
16.21.30: "<s>Yad Indra prāg apāg udag</s>" — the <s>Kadvān</s>.
16.21.31: "<s>Kayā śubhīya</s>" and "<s>Tad id āsīya</s>" — at the non-<s>Nivid</s> insertions of the second [day].
16.21.32: From the <s>Anucara</s> onward, the sixth [recitation]; the third pressing.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.22.1: This indeed is the thousand-<s>stotra</s> (hymn of praise) with which <s>Prajāpati</s> sacrificed.
ŚŚS 16.22.2: This same rite they call the '<s>Garga</s> three-night' (<s>trirātra</s>).
ŚŚS 16.22.3: The second is the <s>Aśvi</s> (relating to the Aśvins) three-night.
ŚŚS 16.22.4: On the middle day, they sacrifice the horse.
ŚŚS 16.22.5: The <s>aghri</s> cow [is used for] the <s>aśva-stomīya</s> (horse-praise hymn).
ŚŚS 16.22.6: The third [day follows] the <s>chandoma</s> (metre-hymn) and <s>pavamāna</s> (purificatory hymn) [pattern].
ŚŚS 16.22.7: The <s>parāka</s> (distant rite) is the fourth.
ŚŚS 16.22.8: With <s>pṛṣṭhya</s> (back-praise) <s>stomas</s> (hymn-forms), three <s>triṣṭoma</s> (triple-praise) [days].
ŚŚS 16.22.9: This is indeed the <s>parāka</s>.
ŚŚS 16.22.10: One desiring to depart from this world should sacrifice with this.
ŚŚS 16.22.11: They say the <s>dvaiparāka</s> (double parāka) is for one desiring a firm foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>).
ŚŚS 16.22.12: For one [verse] is <s>Jagatī</s> (metre), and those two are <s>Gāyatrī</s> (metre).
ŚŚS 16.22.13: This world has the <s>Gāyatrī</s> form; thereby one becomes established in this world — [it is] for establishment and non-falling.
ŚŚS 16.22.14: 'Light, cow, life' — this is the <s>Kusuru-bindu</s> three-night.
ŚŚS 16.22.15: On the first day he gives three hundred [cows as gifts].
ŚŚS 16.22.16: Thirty-three and five parts.
ŚŚS 16.22.17: Likewise on the second, likewise on the third.
ŚŚS 16.22.18: Then the thousandth part — a cow — remains.
ŚŚS 16.22.19: That [remaining cow] should be redeemed by exchanging it with another cow.
ŚŚS 16.22.22: They say it should be prepared at home, for it belongs to the sacrificer's own abundance.
ŚŚS 16.22.22: They say that among those [cows] being led away, whichever first stops — that should be [the one selected].
ŚŚS 16.22.22: That is the form for non-falling.
ŚŚS 16.22.25: They say that among those standing, whichever first sits down — that should be [the one].
ŚŚS 16.22.26: That is the form for progeny.
ŚŚS 16.22.27: They say whichever is the best — that should be [the one].
ŚŚS 16.22.28: 'The best one was prepared at home.'
ŚŚS 16.22.29: In the all-<s>Veda</s> three-night, the <s>Brahman</s> priest should be a <s>triśukri</s> (thrice-purified one), with <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Veda-learned ones) on both sides for three generations.
ŚŚS 16.22.30: Whatever is threefold, that one attains by the three-night rite.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.23.1: Now, whatever is fourfold, that [one attains] by the four-night rite (<s>catūrātra</s>).
ŚŚS 16.23.2: For cattle are indeed fourfold.
ŚŚS 16.23.3: And also four-footed.
ŚŚS 16.23.4: Whatever is fourfold — pertaining to the deities or to the self — all that one attains by this.
ŚŚS 16.23.5: <s>Trivṛt</s> (nine-versed) on the first day, <s>pañcadaśa</s> (fifteen-versed) on the second, <s>saptadaśa</s> (seventeen-versed) on the third, <s>ekaviṃśa</s> (twenty-one-versed) on the fourth.
ŚŚS 16.23.6: These four <s>stomas</s> (hymn-forms) are of diverse powers, [being] ritual structures of the sacrifice. Therefore, four heroes of diverse powers are born in the progeny of one who knows thus.
ŚŚS 16.23.7: This indeed is the four-night rite of <s>Jamadagni</s>.
ŚŚS 16.23.8: And likewise that of <s>Atri</s> is the <s>caturvīra</s> (four-hero rite).
ŚŚS 16.23.9: <s>Trivṛt</s> is the morning pressing of the first day, <s>pañcadaśa</s> the midday [pressing], <s>saptadaśa</s> the third pressing.
ŚŚS 16.23.10: <s>Pañcadaśa</s> is the morning pressing of the second day, <s>saptadaśa</s> the midday, <s>ekaviṃśa</s> the third pressing.
ŚŚS 16.23.11: <s>Saptadaśa</s> is the morning pressing of the third day, <s>ekaviṃśa</s> the midday, <s>triṇava</s> (twenty-seven-versed) the third pressing.
ŚŚS 16.23.12: <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> is the morning pressing of the fourth day, <s>triṇava</s> the midday, <s>trayastriṃśa</s> (thirty-three-versed) the third pressing.
ŚŚS 16.23.13: They proceed, releasing one <s>stoma</s> at a time and generating one at a time.
ŚŚS 16.23.14: Therefore, four heroes of diverse powers are born in the progeny [of the sacrificer]. For the <s>stoma</s> is indeed a hero.
ŚŚS 16.23.15: Its <s>śastra</s> (recitation) [is as follows].
ŚŚS 16.23.16: The <s>Rathantara</s> is the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> (back-praise) of the first [day].
ŚŚS 16.23.17: The <s>Sajanīya</s> [sāman is] the <s>niṣkevalya</s> (independent recitation).
ŚŚS 16.23.18: The '<s>Kayā śubhīya</s>' and 'That indeed I sat' — these are the <s>nivid</s>-containing [hymns] of the second [day].
ŚŚS 16.23.19: On the third [day], with <s>Vairūpa</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, [and] from the <s>Vairāja</s> [comes] the third pressing.
ŚŚS 16.23.20: On the fourth [day], with <s>Vairāja</s> as the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, from the <s>Vairūpa</s> [comes] the third pressing.
ŚŚS 16.23.21: Or the standard <s>Atirātra</s> (overnight rite).
ŚŚS 16.23.22: That they call the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (pertaining to all men).
ŚŚS 16.23.23: The <s>Abhijit</s> (victory rite) is the fourth among the <s>Ābhiplavika</s> (flood-rites).
ŚŚS 16.23.24: The <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering rite) among the others.
ŚŚS 16.23.25: The <s>Vaiśvānara</s> or the <s>Mahāvrata</s> (great observance).
ŚŚS 16.23.26: Whatever is fourfold, that one attains by the four-night rite.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.24.1: Now, whatever is fivefold, that [one attains] by the five-night rite (<s>pañcarātra</s>).
ŚŚS 16.24.2: The <s>Paṅkti</s> (metre) has five feet; the sacrifice is of <s>Paṅkti</s> nature. Whatever is fivefold — pertaining to the deities or to the self — all that one attains by this.
ŚŚS 16.24.3: <s>Trivṛt</s> on the first day, <s>pañcadaśa</s> on the second, <s>ekaviṃśa</s> on the third, <s>saptadaśa</s> on the fourth, and the <s>catuṣṭoma</s> (four-hymned) <s>Atirātra</s> on the last day.
ŚŚS 16.24.4: That [arrangement] is indeed in the form of these [fingers].
ŚŚS 16.24.5: This one [finger] has the form of the <s>trivṛt</s>.
ŚŚS 16.24.6: This one of the <s>pañcadaśa</s>.
ŚŚS 16.24.7: This one of the <s>ekaviṃśa</s>.
ŚŚS 16.24.8: This one of the <s>saptadaśa</s>.
ŚŚS 16.24.9: This one [the thumb] of the <s>catuṣṭoma Atirātra</s>.
ŚŚS 16.24.10: Since the <s>ekaviṃśa</s> is the greatest among the <s>stomas</s>, therefore this one [the middle finger] is the greatest among these [fingers].
ŚŚS 16.24.11: And since the <s>catuṣṭoma Atirātra</s> is the last day, therefore this thumb opposes all fingers.
ŚŚS 16.24.12: Its <s>śastra</s> (recitation) [is as follows].
ŚŚS 16.24.13: A three-day [set] and a fourth <s>Ābhiplavika</s> [day].
ŚŚS 16.24.14: And two pressings of the fifth [day], with the third pressing from the sixth <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [day] on the fifth.
ŚŚS 16.24.15: Or five <s>Ābhiplavika</s> [days].
ŚŚS 16.24.16: The third pressing of the last [day] from the fifth.
ŚŚS 16.24.17: The <s>Abhijit</s> is the fourth among the <s>Ābhiplavika</s> [days].
ŚŚS 16.24.18: The <s>Viśvajit</s> among the others.
ŚŚS 16.24.19: The <s>Vaiśvānara</s> or the <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
ŚŚS 16.24.20: Or for both, <s>Abhijit</s> is the fourth and <s>Viśvajit</s> the fifth.
ŚŚS 16.24.21: Whatever is fivefold, that one attains by the five-night rite.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.25.1: Now, whatever is sixfold, that [one attains] by the six-night rite (<s>ṣaḍrātra</s>).
ŚŚS 16.25.2: There are six seasons, six <s>stomas</s>. Whatever is sixfold — pertaining to the deities or to the self — all that one attains by this.
ŚŚS 16.25.3: A three-day [set], <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Viśvajit</s>, and the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> or <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
ŚŚS 16.25.4: Or the <s>Mahāvrata</s> follows immediately after the <s>Abhijit</s>.
ŚŚS 16.25.5: The <s>Viśvajit</s> is the sixth.
ŚŚS 16.25.6: Or [with] a <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> [day] or an <s>Ābhiplava</s> [day].
ŚŚS 16.25.7: Whatever is sixfold, that one attains by the six-night rite.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.26.1: Now, whatever is sevenfold, that [one attains] by the seven-night rite (<s>saptarātra</s>).
ŚŚS 16.26.2: There are seven vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>), seven metres (<s>chandas</s>). Whatever is sevenfold — pertaining to the deities or to the self — all that one attains by this.
ŚŚS 16.26.3: A three-day [set], <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Viśvajit</s>, <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
ŚŚS 16.26.4: Now [this is] the extension (<s>pravalha</s>) of the year-long [rite].
ŚŚS 16.26.5: The standard <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>caturviṃśa</s> (twenty-four-versed), <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Viṣuvān</s> (solstice day), <s>Viśvajit</s>, <s>Mahāvrata</s>, and <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
ŚŚS 16.26.6: This indeed is the seven-night rite of the seven <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers).
ŚŚS 16.26.7: This same they call the '<s>Janaka</s> seven-night.'
ŚŚS 16.26.8: The <s>Abhijit</s> is the seventh among the <s>Ābhiplavika</s> [days].
ŚŚS 16.26.9: The <s>Viśvajit</s> among the others.
ŚŚS 16.26.10: The <s>Vaiśvānara</s> or <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
ŚŚS 16.26.11: Whatever is sevenfold, that one attains by the seven-night rite.

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.27.1: Now, whatever is eightfold, that [one attains] by the eight-night rite (<s>aṣṭarātra</s>).
ŚŚS 16.27.1: Eight are the <s>Vasus</s>, eight syllables has the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Whatever is eightfold — pertaining to the deities or to the self — all that one attains by this.
ŚŚS 16.27.3: The <s>Abhijit</s> is the seventh among the <s>Ābhiplavika</s> [days].
ŚŚS 16.27.4: The <s>Viśvajit</s> among the others.
ŚŚS 16.27.5: The <s>Vaiśvānara</s> or <s>Mahāvrata</s>.
ŚŚS 16.27.6: Or for both, <s>Abhijit</s> is the seventh and <s>Viśvajit</s> the eighth.
ŚŚS 16.27.7: Whatever is eightfold, that one attains by the eight-night rite.

body.text:
ŚŚS_16.28.1: atha.yan.nava.vidham.tan.nava.rātreṇa /
ŚŚS_16.28.2: catasro.diśaś.catasro.avāntara.diśa.ūrdhvā.iyam.navamī.din.nava.akṣarā.bṛhatī.tad.yat.kim.ca.navavidham.adhidaivatam.adhyātmam.tat.sarvam.anena.āpnoti /
ŚŚS_16.28.3: ṣaḷ.aho.abhijid.viśvajitau.vaiśvānaraś.ca.mahā.vratam.vā.anantaram.vā.abhijito.mahā.vratam.viśvajin.navamaḥ /
ŚŚS_16.28.4: jyotir.agniṣṭomo.gaur.ukthya.āyur.atirātras.trir.etam.upayanti.śalalī.piśaṅga.ity.ācakṣate /

body.translated_text:
ŚŚS 16.28.1: Now that which is ninefold — that [is attained] by the nine-night [session].
ŚŚS 16.28.2: Four cardinal directions, four intermediate directions, and the upward [direction] as the ninth — the <s>Bṛhatī</s> meter has nine syllables. Whatever is ninefold, whether cosmological (<s>adhidaivatam</s>) or pertaining to the self (<s>adhyātmam</s>) — all that one attains by this [session].
ŚŚS 16.28.3: Six days, the <s>Abhijit</s> and <s>Viśvajit</s> [days], and the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [day] — or the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, or the [day] immediately after the <s>Abhijit</s>, with the <s>Mahāvrata</s>, the <s>Viśvajit</s> as the ninth.
ŚŚS 16.28.4: <s>Jyotis</s> (light) as the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Go</s> (cow) as the <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Āyus</s> (life) as the <s>Atirātra</s> — they approach this [sequence] three times. They call it the <s>Śalalī-piśaṅga</s> (tawny-feathered).
ŚŚS 16.28.5: That which is ninefold — that one attains by the nine-night [session].
